# Iron Sights: fork change inventory

This is the maintained inventory of additions and modifications made by this
fork. Update it whenever repository work changes an entry or introduces a new
area, following [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Comparison baseline and scope

- **Upstream project:** [murkantor/Project-Midas](https://github.com/murkantor/Project-Midas).
- **Current inherited baseline:** Project Midas 1.0.2b,
  [`9062f9f120b7f64d39e5db59500ed50e8e7a6686`](https://github.com/murkantor/Project-Midas/commit/9062f9f120b7f64d39e5db59500ed50e8e7a6686).
- **Previous baseline:** Project Midas 1.0.1,
  [`6be5920beed453b6a81fdf9935fb9851928b718d`](https://github.com/murkantor/Project-Midas/commit/6be5920beed453b6a81fdf9935fb9851928b718d).
- **Initial inventory:** 2026-10-22, covering the fork commits after that baseline
  and the working tree at initialization. At that point, several HUD/rendering/
  icon changes were uncommitted; inclusion here does not imply a release, commit,
  or push.

The baseline advances deliberately from 1.0.1 to 1.0.2b with FORK-026 on
2026-10-25. Earlier entries retain their implementation history; imported 1.0.2b
work belongs to upstream. FORK-026 records overlaps and fork-specific resolutions.
This describes our differences from the inherited baseline, rather than a live
comparison with upstream's latest branch. The original PC port, its existing
menus, multiplayer features, ROM loaders and other inherited functionality are
not claimed as additions by this fork.

Keep this as a current feature map: update an entry when its implementation
changes, retain useful replacement/history notes, and add separate entries for
new areas. Status describes implementation state, not Git publication state.

## Inventory

### FORK-095 — In-game updater

**Status:** UPD-001 (package identity) is done on `main` (0f82e0d, every CI
job passed; release `build-453.1-0f82e0da71ea` is the first with
`package.txt`). UPD-002 (the updater core) is built and waiting on CI: a
release package updates itself only when its `midas.ini` sets
`[updates] mode=automatic` or it is launched with `--update-now`, since the
default stays `off` until UPD-003 adds the screens. UPD-003 and UPD-004 are
not started. The plan
was drafted on 2026-11-27 and the owner accepted it
the same day with five decisions. Every CI release counts as an update, with
checks at most twice a day. Automatic mode holds the launch with an indicator
while it downloads and installs, then restarts into the new build. There is
no manifest signing yet. Automatic is the default with no consent screen,
because the player already downloaded the game from GitHub; System > Updates
turns checks off. The held launch allows 5 s for the check and gives up on a
download after 15 s without progress. `AGENTS.md`'s Repo-Local Guidance
points to the plan.

**What it is.** [The in-game update plan](scripts/port/self_update_plan.md)
proposes an **Updates: Off / Notify / Automatic** setting under Iron Sights >
System in both menus. Desktop packages would find newer GitHub releases
through each flavor's existing `build-info.json` asset and check the package
against its `SHA256SUMS` file. They would replace only the allowlisted program
files, with a rename-first swap and a journal, and restart with the same
arguments through FORK-034's restart helper. `Data/`, `midas.ini` and the ROM
stay untouched. A new build that fails to reach the legal screen puts the old
files back by itself. Local, dirty and comparison builds never update. The web
build and macOS are out of scope. The plan has four milestones (UPD-001 to
UPD-004) and a status table.

**UPD-001: package identity.** Every player package now has `package.txt`
beside its executable (`schema=1`, `flavor=`, one of `windows-x86-zip`,
`windows-x64-zip`, `linux-{i686,x86_64}-tar`, `linux-{i686,x86_64}-appimage`,
`steamdeck-{i686,x86_64}`). [`package_identity.py`](scripts/port/package_identity.py)
writes it, maps each flavor to the release package, checksum file and
build-info file it updates from (`FLAVORS`), and checks a package
(`check`): `package.txt` names the expected flavor, and the package's own
`SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every other file with the right hash and nothing
else. That file existed before; the updater will use it as its list of
program files, so the plan's proposed `package-files.txt` was not added.
[`package_windows.py`](scripts/port/package_windows.py) adds `package.txt`
to the zip and builds the sums through the module (same format as before).
[`package_linux.py`](scripts/port/package_linux.py) builds the tarball,
Steam Deck ZIP and AppImage from one AppDir; `write_identity` now rewrites
its `package.txt` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` before each of the three, and
`checksums` writes LF line endings on every host.
[`test_sentry_linux.py`](scripts/port/test_sentry_linux.py) runs `check` on
the built tarball, Steam Deck ZIP and extracted AppImage in CI. Player data
under `Data/` is unchanged; the package's own `Data/README.txt` and
`Data/shaders_base.txt` count as program files.

**UPD-002: the updater core.** `portUpdateStartup` (`main.c`, before the
arenas are pinned) first recovers. It undoes a swap that a crash
interrupted, counts a new build's starts, and after a third start that never
reached the legal screen it restores the previous files, records the build
as bad and restarts. Then it checks when `[updates] mode=automatic` (read
from `midas.ini` directly) or `--update-now` asks, at most every 12 hours
unless forced. The check fetches the flavor's `build-info.json` from
`releases/latest/download/`, offers only a clean CI build with a larger
`build_number` whose `release_url` names this repository and a valid tag,
then fetches that tag's `SHA256SUMS` file and the package. The package is
streamed to `Data/Updates/<tag>/` and checked, and a zip or tarball is
unpacked into `staged/`. Every file must be listed in the package's own
`SHA256SUMS.txt` with its hash, every listed file must be present,
`package.txt` must name the installed flavor, and no entry may be unsafe or
player data (`midas.ini`, or `Data/` beyond its README and shader list). The
swap renames each current file to `.old` before moving the new one in (a
running Windows executable can be renamed but not overwritten), moves aside
files only the old package listed, and journals each step so a failure
undoes all of it. A file the player edited is kept as `NAME.edited`. An
AppImage is one file renamed over `$APPIMAGE`. The game then restarts with
its own command line (`CreateProcessW`, or `execv` on Linux). The legal
screen's first frame (`portUpdateLegalScreen`, `port_startup.c`) confirms
the build and deletes the `.old` files. A second copy of the game cannot
install at the same time (`Data/Updates/lock`). Local, dirty and comparison
builds never update, and only Windows and Linux desktop builds with video
compile the updater. The updater's lines also go to `Data/Updates/log.txt`,
which outlives the restart. Downloads use the Enhanced Fonts and HD textures
stream transport through `port/src/port_update_http.cpp`, which enforces the
owner's 5 s check and 15 s stall limits from a worker thread. libcurl
already followed redirects, so no `port/fast3d/` file changed and the
gallery is not involved. [`AppRun`](scripts/port/linux/AppRun) now refreshes
`midas_ini_help.txt` and `Data/shaders_base.txt` in the AppImage's data
folder when they differ, so an updated AppImage's own copies reach it; the
controller files are still seeded only when missing, because players edit
them. `tools/midas_ini_help.txt` documents `[updates] mode`. The key is read
by the updater rather than registered as an option, so it is in neither
menu until UPD-003, which adds the rows and makes Automatic the default.
Sources: [`port_update.h`](port/include/port_update.h),
`port/src/port_update*.c`, `port_update_files.h`, `port_update_http.cpp`,
the hooks in `main.c` and `port_startup.c`, and `CMakeLists.txt`
(`GE_UPDATER` only on those two files; `GE_UPDATE_TEST`, never shipped,
only on `port_update_startup.c`). The game's own `isdigit` (`src/str.c`) and
`string.h` (no `strncmp`, `strcpy` or `strcat`) shadow the C library's, so
the updater uses neither.

**Why it differs from upstream.** Upstream has no updater. This fork
publishes a release on every push to `main`, and updating by hand means
replacing program files while keeping `Data` and `midas.ini`
([releases.md](scripts/port/releases.md)).

**Validation.** The plan commits were documentation only and ran the
standards checks. For UPD-001, `test_distribution.py`'s new
`PackageIdentity` tests (each Windows zip's flavor and full sums, the Steam
Deck ZIP after the tarball's identity, every flavor against the packagers'
asset names, refused packages, unknown flavors and schemas) pass on Windows
and in the `midas-linux-release-x86_64` image. The suite's other failures
are the same before the change: on Windows,
`test_bundling_copies_strips_and_relinks_every_library`, and in that image the
two tests that need a 32-bit compiler. The zips packaged from the local
`build_win` and `build_win64` trees (21 files each) pass
`package_identity.check`. No game code changed, so no game build, gallery
or benchmark is needed. In CI on 0f82e0d both Linux jobs' `test_sentry_linux.py`
ran `check` on the built tarballs, Steam Deck ZIPs and extracted AppImages,
and `test_distribution.py` ran its 36 tests; every job passed.

UPD-002, locally: [`test_update.sh`](scripts/port/test_update.sh) passes at
64 bits (in the `midas-linux-release-x86_64` image) and at 32 bits (in
`midas-lp64-i686-video`). It covers SHA-256 vectors, settings, tags, paths,
the flavor table against `package_identity.py`'s, a zip install and its
confirmation (edited file kept, obsolete file removed, player data
untouched), the throttle (a failed check counts), a rollback after three
starts, a failure mid-swap that undoes every earlier step, refused releases
(tampered file, unsafe path, player-data path, other flavor, not CI,
missing, corrupt download), an interrupted swap, a tarball install with a
pax long name, and an AppImage install, all against fake releases from
[`update_fixture.py`](scripts/port/update_fixture.py). CI's tests job runs
it. [`update_e2e.py`](scripts/port/update_e2e.py) passes all eleven of its
checks on a 32-bit Windows `GE_UPDATE_TEST` build with the local ROM: the
installed build found the release on 127.0.0.1, downloaded, unpacked and
swapped its own files while running, restarted, and the new process counted
its first start and confirmed at the legal screen, with player data and
`midas.ini` untouched, about a second after launch. `build_win`,
`build_win64` and the test tree build and link. `lp64_diagnostics.py gate`
compiles a 64-bit Linux video tree (402 files, 0 failures); `narrowing
--check` finds no narrowing, and `unprototyped --check` passes after the
updater stopped using the C library's string functions that the game's
`string.h` lacks. A MinGW x64 gate tree in this container lacked SDL headers
for 11 renderer and input files, none of them the updater's, so CI's tree is
the check there. `lp64_casts.py check` and `lp64_overlays.py check
--no-defects` pass, after the updater dropped nine casts the overlay review
flagged. `test_linux_launcher.py` passes with a new case for the AppImage
refresh. A 64-bit Linux video link and the Linux packages are first built by
CI. CI's first run on 87c8d4a failed two jobs. GCC 13 at 64 bits
flagged a 16-byte buffer for a `long` (`port_update_swap.c`; the local GCC
11 image had not). And `port_update_swap.c` was missing from CMake's updater
list, so the macOS headless build, which has no updater, kept it and left 17
references undefined. Both were fixed in the next commit; `test_update.sh`
then passed at both widths under GCC 13, and a 64-bit Linux headless tree
linked. No benchmark or late-load audit was run: nothing is drawn or computed
per frame, and the stage loads are unchanged. The work happens at boot
before the window opens; the legal screen's first frame does one journal
read, plus about twenty deletes on the start after an install.

### FORK-094 — Native Windows x64 build

**Status:** WIN64-001 (build and boot) is done on `main` (4fde028, CI
passed); WIN64-002 (plays and matches) is done on `main` (1f3ea6f, CI
passed); WIN64-003 (crash reporting and tooling) is done on `main`
(7ca2347, CI passed, its `sentry-sdk` job building the x64 runtime);
WIN64-004 (package, release and hand-over) is done: the first x64 zip was
published in release `build-442.1-9352f2162b26` (9352f21), and every push
since publishes one beside the x86 zip; the owner closed the milestone
after their session, leaving its gamepad, windowed and HDR-on parts
untested. The Windows x64 plan is done. No x64 zip is released yet. The plan was drafted on
2026-11-27 at the owner's request and accepted the same day with all five
recommendations; [WIN64-001's plan](scripts/port/windows_x64_win64_001.md)
and [WIN64-002's](scripts/port/windows_x64_win64_002.md) were accepted under
the owner's standing instruction to take sensible recommendations;
[WIN64-003's](scripts/port/windows_x64_win64_003.md) and
[WIN64-004's](scripts/port/windows_x64_win64_004.md) when they asked to start
each, WIN64-004 after being told its push publishes the zip.

**What it is.** [The Windows x64 plan](scripts/port/windows_x64_plan.md)
proposes a native 64-bit Windows executable from the 64-bit source that
already ships for x86_64 Linux (FORK-089), ending with
`Iron-Sights-windows-x64.zip` beside the 32-bit zip. It follows the 64-bit
and macOS plans' form: why, goals, non-goals, anti-goals, constraints, what
was measured, approaches, design, verification, four milestones (WIN64-001
to WIN64-004), the owner's decisions and a status table. `AGENTS.md`'s
Repo-Local Guidance points to it, and the 64-bit plan's "Windows x64 is out
of scope" call now notes that the owner lifted it for this plan.

**WIN64-001: build and boot (current behavior).**

- *Build.* `cmake/mingw-x86_64.cmake` builds `GE_POINTER_BITS=64` for
  Windows into `build_win64` (README step 6). The old refusal of Windows x64
  is replaced by a width check: CMake refuses `GE_POINTER_BITS=64` with the
  i686 toolchain and 32 with the x86_64 one (`test_pointer_bits.sh` case 5a
  to 5c). At 64 bits the Windows link drops `-m32`, the fixed 0x10000000
  image base and `--disable-dynamicbase`, so MinGW links a dynamic-base,
  high-entropy image; the 32-bit line is unchanged. The SDL2 MinGW default
  folder follows the width (`GE_MINGW_TRIPLE`). On Windows, include
  directories go on the command line instead of `@` response files, so the
  compile gate can read them. The manifest's `processorArchitecture` is
  `*`, which Windows resolves to the process's own architecture; with
  `x86` the 64-bit exe stopped before `main` with `0xC000007B`. The
  `goldeneye` image (`Dockerfile`) gains the x86_64 MinGW packages, in a
  layer that refreshes the package lists first, because the cached lists
  named archives the mirror had dropped.
- *Addresses.* `port_lp64.c` takes the executable's range from its PE
  headers (`GetModuleHandleW`, `SizeOfImage`) on Windows. In `pcsched.c`,
  64-bit Windows allocations use `VirtualAlloc` with no hint and refuse a
  mapping below 4 GB, and the memp arena takes its fixed 0x20000000 hint
  only at 32 bits, so at 64 bits it goes through `portAllocHighOrExit` and
  the address check lists it.
- *Crash handler.* `port/include/port_win_context.h` names the registers,
  the address type and print format, the stack walk's machine and the PE
  offsets by width, so `main.c`'s SEH dump, first-chance reporter, stall
  watchdog and watchpoints serve both widths. At 64 bits the frame walks
  use the unwind tables (`RtlLookupFunctionEntry`, `RtlVirtualUnwind`),
  because MinGW x64's RBP points into its frame, not at the saved RBP, and
  system DLLs keep no frame pointer; the SEH dump prints all 16 integer
  registers. At 64 bits `main` installs no `SIGSEGV`, `SIGILL` or `SIGFPE`
  handler: MinGW-w64's x64 start-up runs `main` inside an SEH scope whose
  filter calls such a handler before Windows reaches the unhandled-exception
  filter, so `portCrashHandler`'s `_exit(139)` pre-empted the dump (and
  would pre-empt Sentry, WIN64-003).
- *Profiler.* At 64 bits `port_profile.c` compiles a stand-in that says
  `GE_PROFILE` is not available yet (WIN64-003); it tests `_WIN64`, since
  `bench/stock.py` compiles the file into stock trees.
- *Gates.* CI's tests job installs the x86_64 MinGW compilers
  (`ci_dependencies.py`'s tests profile, with their win32 alternatives) and
  the SDL2 MinGW package, configures `build/lp64/gate-mingw` and runs the
  three `lp64_diagnostics.py` checks over it with the Linux gate trees.
  `test_abi_probe.sh` compiles and links the layout probe with the x86_64
  MinGW compiler (its static assertions; the run-time checks need Windows).
  The overlay review (`lp64_overlays_source.py`) no longer treats `_WIN32`
  as undefined at 64 bits; its 15 newly visible sites have verdicts
  (13 `typed`, 2 `dead` in the 32-bit profiler).
- *Windows ABI findings.* MinGW lays bitfields out by Microsoft's rules at
  both widths, so `struct image_entry` and `Gsetcolor` are 12 bytes on
  Windows, not 8 (the shipped 32-bit exe included). `Gsetcolor` is unused on
  a PC. `chrprop.c`'s guard-shot impact check stepped `g_Textures` by 8
  bytes, so on Windows it read another texture's `hitSound` and could
  spark on water or snow or skip the effect elsewhere; it now reads the
  field, which on Linux is the same byte and nibble, and its two reviewed
  overlay lines are gone. The probe asserts 12 bytes under `_WIN32` and 8
  elsewhere. The N64 read this nibble as `hitTexture` (IDO packs bitfields
  from the top bit, as `chrprop.c`'s impact-sound comment says, and
  `romdataImageTableApply` takes `hitTexture` from bits 24 to 27 of an
  entry's first word); every PC build read `hitSound` there. A follow-up
  change makes the check read `hitTexture`, with a PORT comment. A scan of
  the stock ROM's table (cdata+0x28570, 2,698 entries; output kept out of
  Git) found the two fields differ only for textures 653 to 655 (`hitSound`
  HIT_GLASS, `hitTexture` HIT_GLASS_XLU), and none is HIT_WATER or HIT_SNOW
  in one field but not the other (8 entries are in both), so the check's
  result is unchanged for every stock texture: no stock gameplay, picture
  or comparison stream changes, and the pins in
  `lp64_equiv_expected.txt` stand. Only a modded table whose two fields
  disagree on water or snow sees the N64's behaviour now. The probe's
  run-time `hitSound` nibble check stays, its comment saying no site
  depends on it.
- *Smaller fixes for the MinGW tree.* `include/string.h`'s PC block
  prototypes `strcmp` (and `_stricmp` on Windows), which also removes the
  `port_build_time.c` line from `lp64_unprototyped_allowed.txt`;
  `audio_pc.c` prototypes `memmove`, which MinGW's SDL headers do not
  declare. `lp64_boot.py` copies `SDL2.dll` beside the executable it runs.
  The 64-bit warning comment in `CMakeLists.txt` lists the MinGW tree's two
  extra macro-redefinition warnings, which have no option.

**WIN64-002: plays and matches.**

- *The run tools on Windows.* `lp64_play.py run --video`, `lp64_equiv.py
  run --video` and `audit_buffers.py --mission-smoke --video` run natively
  from Windows' Python. SDL's offscreen driver cannot make a GL context on
  Windows ("Could not initialize OpenGL / GLES library"), so
  `lp64_play_run.py` sets `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=windows` there
  (`host_video_driver`) and each case opens a real 640x480 window on the
  desktop, input off; elsewhere it stays `offscreen`. `run_copies.py`'s one
  executable copy carries `SDL2.dll` and links it beside each case's copy.
  Windows runs are video runs: the 64-bit headless tree does not link on
  Windows.
- *Windows logs in order.* The Windows C runtime buffers a redirected
  stderr, unlike glibc, so a harness run's `ge:` lines (stderr) came out
  late, out of order with stdout's `load_bg_file` lines and once split
  mid-line by the frame-limit line; `lp64_play.py peaks` then put 27 of 341
  pool and stage pairs in the wrong level. `portDirectLaunchLog`
  (`port/src/main.c`) now makes a redirected stderr unbuffered on Windows,
  as the direct-launch log already was. A pool use is printed at a stage
  unload and at exit, never per frame.
- *Streams byte for byte.* The simulation trace (`port_simtrace.c`) and
  the picture digest (`port_gfx_digest.cpp`) open their files `"wb"`: in
  text mode a Windows build wrote CRLF lines, which the stream readers
  refused (`rooms=0:811c9dc5` with a trailing CR). Linux is unchanged.
- *Maths.* `lp64_libm_sweep.c` built with MinGW x64 and the comparison
  build's three maths files prints the six pinned hashes (`sinf cc151db4`,
  `cosf 4c162bf1`, `tanf e3ccc704`, `atanf f160154d`, `expf 8be3a4cd`,
  `powf 648805d1`). With MinGW's own C library, `tanf` and `atanf` match
  and four differ: `sinf 902caeb5`, `cosf e4754375`, `expf 30a1a4f5`,
  `powf 1c4c5c98`. Shipped builds keep their C library's maths (the plan's
  anti-goal), so a shipped 64-bit Windows build computes those four
  otherwise than a shipped Linux build, as the 32-bit Windows build always
  has. `test_compare_math.c` fails under MinGW only in its reference:
  MinGW's double `sin` is far off for huge arguments
  (`sinf(0x1.59d074p+67)`); it is not one of the gates.

- *WIN64-002 evidence* (2026-11-27, on the owner's laptop with its RTX 3070
  Laptop GPU, Windows 11; the tree is 4fde028 with this change):
  - The play sets `demos,stages,stops,menus,tours,attract,sound` on
    `build_win64/IronSights.exe`, natively with `--video`: `OK: 119 of 119
    cases` (about 45 minutes at 7 jobs), and `lp64_play.py peaks --budget
    scripts/port/lp64_budgets.txt` over their logs: `OK: 320 pool and stage
    pairs within budget`. The two sound recordings are 22,050 Hz stereo,
    30 s, peaks 15,027 and 22,392. Before the stderr change the same sets
    also passed 119 of 119 but the budget check failed 27 of 341 pairs.
  - `audit_buffers.py --mission-smoke --video --frames 1800 --jobs 4`: 20 of
    20 missions pass.
  - The comparison (verification 4 and 5): `build/lp64/cmp-win64-video`
    (MinGW x64) and the Linux `build/lp64/cmp-x64-video`, each `lp64_equiv.py
    run --video --repeat 2` over the 38 cases: both `OK: 38 of 38 cases ran`

    changes, neither of which changes a Linux build's behaviour.
  - Drawn pixels: `--draw --shots 1800` on six cases (Dam, Facility,

    Side by side, Cradle and Temple 4-player show the same geometry,

  - `bench.py run --smoke` (32-bit `build_win/IronSights.exe` as w32 and

**WIN64-003: crash reporting and tooling.**

- *Sentry x64.* `sentry_tools.py build` and `stage` take `--arch x86` (the
  default, so the 32-bit CI job is unchanged) or `--arch x64` (`-A x64`, its
  own build folder); `sentry-build.json` records the architecture and
  `stage` refuses a runtime of another one. CI's `sentry-sdk` job builds and
  caches both, the x64 runtime as the `sentry-msvc-x64` artifact, which
  WIN64-004's job will package. `reporting_win.c` needed no width change (it
  loads `sentry.dll` from the exe's folder by name); it now sets the
  `architecture` tag from `portBuildArchitecture()` (`i686` or `x86_64`), as
  `reporting_linux.c` does, so the 32-bit exe's events gain it too.
  `test_sentry_windows.py` expects the image `arch` and tag the exe's PE
  machine implies.
- *Profiler at 64 bits.* `port_profile.c` samples a 64-bit exe again
  (WIN64-001 had a stand-in). Sample words are pointer-sized at 64 bits
  (96 MB of samples) and stay 32-bit at 32 bits. The walk unwinds with
  `RtlVirtualUnwind`, finding each function's unwind entry by a binary
  search of its module's own exception directory, from a module list the
  sampler refreshes while no thread is suspended; `RtlLookupFunctionEntry`
  is not called there, since it takes the loader's function-table lock,
  which a suspended thread loading a DLL may hold, and the sampler starts
  while DLLs load. A function without an entry is a leaf, its return
  address on top of the stack. The file stays `# ge-profile 1`.
  `bench_profile.py` reads the exe's PE header for its machine and
  preferred image base, rebases each address in the exe from its `M` line
  to that base, names symbols with the matching container `nm`, drops the
  i686 compiler's leading underscore so 32-bit and 64-bit runs compare row
  by row, and sets the pump aside under either spelling.
- *Tooling.* `audit_mission_cheats.ps1` copies `SDL2.dll` from the exe's own
  folder. `audit_states.ps1` and `audit_state_effects.ps1` read the exe's PE
  machine and refuse a 64-bit exe by name (no suspend points at 64 bits)
  before making any folder. `hand_gallery.py generate --executable`
  refuses a 64-bit Windows exe by name: the references are the 32-bit
  exe's pictures. That check lives in the new `scripts/port/pe_machine.py`
  (tested by `test_pe_machine.py`, run in CI's tests job), so the gallery
  tool stays within its recorded length baseline with one import line. `bench/stock.py --arch x64 --ref <commit>` builds a
  64-bit ref with the x86_64 toolchain and SDL, and refuses `--arch x64`
  for the stock 1.0.2b baseline. `late_load_audit.py`, `soak.py` and
  `bench.py` already took `build_win64` (WIN64-002 ran two of them).

  MSVC 19.40 from Visual Studio 2022 Community):

### FORK-093 — Native macOS build plan

**Status:** MAC-001 is done (2026-11-27, its eleven tasks below): the
headless 64-bit game builds with Apple clang, boots, plays its 20 missions
and its play sets, runs them under the sanitizers, and its simulation is
identical to the aarch64 Linux build's in all 38 comparison cases. It has
no window, picture, sound or input, and nothing on macOS is shipped.
MAC-002 is planned and not yet accepted
([its plan](scripts/port/macos_mac_002.md), 2026-11-27, five decisions
for the owner); none of it is built. MAC-003 to MAC-006 are not started.
The owner chose the
audience, the graphics path and the outline on 2026-11-26, approved the
design on 2026-11-27 and accepted MAC-001's plan the same day.

**What it is.** [The macOS plan](scripts/port/macos_plan.md) is the
project after the 64-bit port (FORK-089): a native Apple Silicon macOS build
that ends as a Developer ID signed, notarized download. It follows the
64-bit plan's form: why, goals, non-goals, anti-goals, constraints, what was
measured, approaches, design, verification, six milestones (MAC-001 to
MAC-006), decisions and a status table. `AGENTS.md` ("Repo-Local Guidance")
points to it, and `scripts/port/linux_64bit.md`'s last section now names it
instead of calling macOS a later milestone of the 64-bit plan.

**Why it differs from upstream.** The inherited baseline has no macOS
build. Upstream's open pull requests #42 and #95 add one and ship an ad-hoc
signed zip. Under the 64-bit plan's decision to write our own, they were
read for approach only and no code was taken.

**The owner's decisions.** A notarized download rather than self-build only
or an ad-hoc signed zip; OpenGL 4.1 core as the renderer already has it,
with ANGLE over Metal as the recorded fallback and a new backend rejected;
six milestones, Apple Silicon only. The plan's "Decisions" lists the calls
made in drafting that the owner accepted with the design.

**What was measured** (2026-11-26, `main` at 843c143, macOS 27.2.1, Apple M4
Max, Apple clang 21.0.0, in scratch trees outside the repository). The plan
gives each with its file reference or command:

- Apple clang configures the 64-bit headless tree as it is and fails 61 of
  361 compile steps, from six causes: `include/PR/os.h:1019-1033`'s libc
  redeclarations, the ELF section names of `port/include/asmsym.h`, the
  `#error` in `port/src/port_lp64.c`, `clock_nanosleep` in
  `port/src/pcsched.c`, `__errno_location` in `port/src/romdata.c`, and two
  redeclarations in `src/game/lv.c` and `src/game/spectrum.c`. A video tree
  fails 75 of 393: the same `os.h` lines in seven more C files, and seven
  renderer files where the game's headers come before libc++'s.
- An SDL2 probe on the Mac got an OpenGL "4.1 Metal" core context and none
  for 3.0 compatibility, which the renderer asks for first; its context list
  (`port/fast3d/gfx_sdl2.cpp:404-415`) then asks for 4.1 core. No shipped
  build has yet run that path.
- With no macOS code in the tree, save transfer would stop the game at
  startup (`port/fast3d/save_transfer.cpp:141-146` reads `/proc/self/exe`),
  and crash reporting, the downloads, the weapon icon worker and the file
  pickers exist only for Windows and Linux.
- SDL's offscreen driver cannot make a GL window on the Mac, so picture
  checks there need a real window.

**Constraints the plan carries.** Every edit under `port/fast3d/` is strict
tier: it is committed on a branch and reaches `main` through a gallery
regeneration on the owner's Windows laptop. A headless build compiles none
of those files, so MAC-001 lands on `main` from the Mac. The plan needs from
the owner an Apple Developer Program membership, a bundle identifier, a
Developer ID certificate and a notarization key.

**MAC-001's plan (2026-11-27).** [macos_mac_001.md](scripts/port/macos_mac_001.md)
plans the first milestone in eleven tasks. The owner accepted it on
2026-11-27 with all seven of its recommendations: how its done condition
is read; which of clang's undefined-behaviour checks a sanitizer build
runs; Arm's MIT-licensed `sinf`, `expf` and `powf` for comparison builds
only; a macOS build-and-test job in CI from this milestone; clang's
narrowings read and listed; dynamic lookup with a link check for the weak
references; and no 32-bit harness half on macOS. Nothing was built when it
was accepted; "MAC-001 as built" below records its execution. It was
measured in a copy of the tree (`git archive` of 990f991) edited and built
outside the repository, then discarded:

- Seven guarded edits (a seventh site, `include/bstring.h:28`, appeared once
  `os.h` compiled) and two host functions (the executable's range from
  dyld, a sleep to an absolute time) build the headless game. The link also
  needs `-Wl,-map,` and `-Wl,-undefined,dynamic_lookup`: 705 weak
  references are undefined, which ELF resolves to null and Mach-O does not.
- That executable ran `lp64_boot.py --expect-run --frames 600` (`OK`), the
  mission smoke (20 of 20) and the headless play sets (`OK: 117 of 117
  cases`, 292 pool and stage pairs within budget).
- Clang prints 9,706 warnings in 19 classes where GCC's log is clean.
- `lp64_diagnostics.py narrowing --check` printed `OK` on the clang tree
  without reading it (it knows only GCC's wording); clang itself reports 33
  implicit narrowings of pointer-sized integers that GCC's check cannot
  see. `unprototyped` needs GCC's `-aux-info`.
- The sanitizer build boots; AddressSanitizer reported nothing; clang's
  undefined-behaviour checks report 43 source lines of six kinds that
  GCC's build never did, three of them in strict-tier files.
- 7 of the 46 harnesses pass as they are; Apple clang's acceptance of
  `-m32` is the main cause, and with the 32-bit half off 21 pass.
- macOS's `sinf`, `expf` and `powf` differ from glibc's (`3990ade5`,
  `027eb54f`, `e758d294` against `cc151db4`, `8be3a4cd`, `648805d1`). A
  macOS comparison build agreed with itself in 38 of 38 cases and with the
  aarch64 Linux build in 33; the other five matched once both builds were
  given one `sinf`, `expf` and `powf`.

**MAC-001 as built.** One paragraph a task, each with what ran on the
owner's Mac (macOS 27.2.1, Apple M4 Max, Apple clang 21.0.0) and in the
Linux containers of `scripts/port/lp64_env.py`.

- **Task 1, the harness helper and the two host functions.**
  `harness_widths` (`scripts/port/harness_widths.sh`) never offers 32 on an
  Apple compiler (`harness_apple_compiler`: its `-dumpmachine` names
  `-apple-`), because Apple clang accepts `-m32` for arm64 and can then
  build nothing with it; `test_harness_widths.sh` has the two cases, which
  printed `32 64` and `32` before the fix. `port/src/port_macos.c`
  (`port/include/port_macos.h`) holds `portMacImageRange`, the main
  executable's span from dyld's `LC_SEGMENT_64` commands with the slide
  applied and `__PAGEZERO` left out, and `portMacSleepUntil`, a sleep to an
  absolute `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` time that returns 0 or `EINTR` as Linux's
  `clock_nanosleep(..., TIMER_ABSTIME, ...)` does. It sleeps with
  `nanosleep` and reads the clock again until the target is reached, since
  `nanosleep` counts on another clock. Nothing calls them yet (Task 2).
  `CMakeLists.txt` globs `port/src/*.c`, so the same change keeps the file
  out of every build that is not macOS (it includes dyld's headers) and
  compiles it there with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`; the plan had those lines
  in Task 2. `scripts/port/test_macos_host.sh` (driver
  `test_macos_host.c`, no game header) checks five things: the range holds
  `main` and a file-scope variable, it starts at or above 4 GB, a sleep
  reaches a future time, returns at once for a past one, and says `EINTR`
  when `SIGALRM` interrupts it and then finishes on retry. Off macOS it
  prints `test_macos_host: SKIP (not macOS)`. It is on
  `HARNESS_WORKFLOW_EXEMPT` until Task 10's macOS job names it.
  *Ran:* on macOS `test_macos_host: PASS (64-bit)` (it failed to link
  before `port_macos.c` existed) and `test_harness_widths: PASS`; in the
  x86_64 container the `SKIP` line, `test_harness_widths: PASS`, the gate
  on `build/lp64/gate` and `gate-video` (361 and 394 files compiled, 0 failed), `narrowing --check` and
  `unprototyped --check` `OK`; in the aarch64 container `OK: ran 600
  frames`; `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` printed `identical in loaded code
  and data`.

- **Task 2, the headless game builds, links and boots.** `CMakeLists.txt`
  refuses a macOS configure that is not 64-bit ("macOS builds are 64-bit
  only: configure with -DGE_POINTER_BITS=64") or not arm64 ("macOS builds
  are Apple Silicon only"), links with `-Wl,-map,` in place of GNU ld's
  `-Wl,-Map=` and with `-Wl,-undefined,dynamic_lookup`, and runs
  `scripts/port/macos_link_check.py` on the executable after every link.
  The compile causes are fixed behind `__APPLE__`, so every other compiler
  sees the tokens it saw: `include/PR/os.h` and `include/bstring.h` take
  `<strings.h>` there, and `os.h` and `src/game/image.c` skip their
  `sprintf` declaration where macOS's `<stdio.h>` has made it a macro;
  `port/include/asmsym.h` has Mach-O section names (`__DATA,__data`,
  `__DATA,__const`); `src/game/lv.c` and `src/game/spectrum.c` share the
  browser build's `#define` in place of `#pragma weak A = B`, which Mach-O
  lacks; `port/src/romdata.c` reads `errno` through `__error()`;
  `port/src/port_lp64.c` fills its range from `portMacImageRange` and
  keeps its `#error` for any other platform; `port/src/pcsched.c`'s two
  `clock_nanosleep` calls have a `portMacSleepUntil` twin. Two things the
  plan did not foresee: `port_macos.c` compiled under the game's include
  path sees the game's short `include/string.h`, so it compares the
  segment name with `memcmp`; and clang's unknown `-Wno-discarded-qualifiers`
  is an error under that file's `-Werror`, so the flag became GCC-only in
  this task rather than the next (GCC's command lines are unchanged).
  *Why dynamic lookup.* A 64-bit build has no compiled-in assets, so 705
  weak references are undefined: 702 file symbols of
  `assets/obseg/obseg.h` and `portHealthWide`, `portMpHudWide` and
  `portInputPadDigMoveP1`, video-only functions the headless build tests
  for. ELF makes such a reference null at link time; Mach-O does so only
  with dynamic lookup, which would also let a strong undefined symbol
  through. `macos_link_check.py` reads `nm -m` and fails the build naming
  any strong one (`strong_lookups`, tested on any host by
  `test_macos_link_check.py`, which CI's tests step runs); a line it
  cannot classify counts as strong. The link prints one warning, `reducing
  alignment of section __DATA,__common from 0x8000 to 0x4000`: two common
  symbols of 0x8000 bytes (`sp_main`, `decompressdata.s_huftWorkspace`)
  whose alignment no source asks for.
  `scripts/port/test_pointer_bits.sh` gained case 0 for macOS (the refusal,
  the link line, the link check, `port_macos.c` compiled) and, since a Mac
  can no longer configure the default 32-bit tree, skips by name there the
  cases that read one (1, 1b, 6, 7's video half, 7b, 7d, 8d and the 32-bit
  halves of 7e); its Linux run is unchanged. Its canary cases still fail on
  macOS on clang's wording, which is Task 4's.

  `empty-body` 217, `comment` 81, `pragma-pack` 46, `parentheses` 9. Every
  site of the other twelve was read before its class was switched off:
  - `macro-redefined` 82: idiom. `src/bondconstants.h:4764-4765` defines

    (text-bank indices returned as a `LEVELID`) and 2 in `propobj.c`.
  - `implicit-const-int-float-conversion` 29: idiom. `1.0f / UINT_MAX`
    and its macro forms, where 4294967295 becomes 4294967296.0f on every
    compiler.
  - `pointer-bool-conversion` 23: idiom. Decompiled `if (&x);` and
    `if (array)` statements with no effect; `initpathtablelinks.c:187,190`
    test `!(&g_CurrentSetup)`, always false, as decompiled.
  - `unused-value` 21: idiom. Decompiled `(0, x)` comma expressions and

  - `switch` 13: idiom. Switches over an enumeration that name some of
    its values.
  - `format-security` 12: idiom. `sprintf(buffer, langGet(...))` in
    `mpmenu.c`, `options.c` and `gunfire.c`: the game's own text as the

  - `tautological-constant-out-of-range-compare` 5: **two defects, in
    debug traces on every build, recorded and not fixed here.**
    `src/game/lightfixture.c:160-161` compares a `u8` opcode with
    `G_SETOTHERMODE_L`, `G_SETOTHERMODE_H`, `G_SETGEOMETRYMODE` and
    `G_CLEARGEOMETRYMODE`, which are negative constants (-71, -70, -73,
    -74), so the `lightdbg` dump never prints those four commands.
    `src/game/prop.c:839` writes `!isNotBoundPad(arg1->lookpad)`, which
    expands to `!arg1->lookpad < 10000` and is always true, so the
    `cctvprobe` trace reads `boundpads[lookpad - 10000]` for a pad that is
    not a bound pad. Neither fix is a macOS-only line.
  - `logical-not-parentheses` 2: `prop.c:839` again, and `src/joy.c:259`,
    `!(g_ControllerStates) & (1 << i)`, which the source's own comment
    calls a typo in the original game; kept as the original has it.
  - `non-literal-null-conversion` 2: idiom. `RMON_THREAD_ID` (0) passed as
    a thread pointer in `src/init.c`.
  - `shift-op-parentheses` 2: idiom. `x + width << 2` in
    `textrelated.c:800,816`, where the addition first is what is meant.
  - `parentheses-equality` 1: idiom. `if ((a == b))` in `propobj.c:8215`.

- **Task 5, the static checks on clang.** `lp64_diagnostics.py narrowing
  --check` printed `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files` on a clang tree without
  reading a line of it: its pattern knew only GCC's wording. Both static
  checks now ask the trees' compiler which it is first
  (`lp64_static_checks.tree_family`, by `--version`, clang before GCC
  because Apple's `cc` and `gcc` are clang). `narrowing` compiles a clang
  tree with `-Wshorten-64-to-32` and reads clang's line, "implicit
  conversion loses integer precision: 'SRC' (aka 'X') to 'DST'"; a GCC
  tree is run and read as before. A compiler that is neither exits 2
  ("neither GCC nor clang by its --version"), and so do GCC and clang
  trees given together: an `OK` never means that nothing was read.
  `unprototyped` exits 2 on a clang tree ("needs GCC's -aux-info: run it
  in the x86_64 or aarch64 container"); `port_macos.c`, the one file only
  clang compiles, is covered by its own `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`.
  `narrowing --check` compares a clang tree with
  `scripts/port/lp64_narrowing_clang.txt` (`path<TAB>count<TAB>reason`,
  exact match) and never with GCC's list: clang keeps a typedef's name
  through arithmetic and so lists places GCC's run shows only as `long
  unsigned int`. On `build/mac/headless` it lists 33 places in 19 files
  (the plan counted 18 files). Each was read: 26 are a difference of two
  addresses in one object, segment or table; 3 (`front.c`) a file size
  rounded up through `ALIGN64_V2`'s `uintptr_t` cast; 2 (`prop.c`) an AI
  list ID read in place from a pointer-sized field; 1 (`stan.c:2801`) a
  flag kept in one; 1 (`resample.c:132`) a float's bits passed through a
  pointer-typed parameter. **None carries a host address into 32 bits**,
  so nothing was fixed and nothing goes to the owner. The Linux check is
  no stricter than before: GCC still cannot see these 33.
  Tests (`test_lp64_static_checks.py`, where these checks' tests live; its
  stand-in compiler now answers `--version` and refuses the other
  compiler's flags): clang's wording is listed; `unsigned long` only with
  `--all`; `--check` reads the clang list and fails a place only GCC's
  list allows; `unprototyped` refuses a clang tree; an unknown compiler and
  mixed trees exit 2. All eight failed before the change.
  *Ran:* `test_lp64_static_checks.py` 34 tests and
  `test_lp64_diagnostics.py` 44 tests `OK` on macOS; `narrowing --check

- **Task 6, the sanitizers under clang** (the owner's decision 2). A
  `-DGE_SANITIZE=ON` tree builds and boots under Apple clang, and before
  this task its mission smoke failed 20 of 20, each log's first report at
  `src/game/stan.c:782`. Clang's undefined-behaviour checks are stricter
  than GCC's: with reports made non-fatal in a scratch tree, the 20

  reported, and AddressSanitizer reported nothing. Two of them were the
  fork's own and are fixed: `stan.c:3472-3473`, a debug trace that took a
  member's offset through a null pointer, uses `offsetof` on macOS, behind
  `__APPLE__`; every other build compiles the lines it compiled before
  (the correction below says why the guard). The other 41 are decompiled idioms in
  upstream-owned or strict-tier lines, so with `GE_SANITIZE` on a clang
  compiler `CMakeLists.txt` adds
  `-fno-sanitize=array-bounds,object-size,float-cast-overflow`, and
  `-fno-sanitize=pointer-overflow` for `src/game/model.c` alone; the
  comment beside the options has the sites. GCC's options do not change,
  and no AddressSanitizer report is switched off. The 41, re-measured
  after the fix:
  - `array-bounds`, 38 lines: 37 index past `struct coord2d[4]` where
    `rect4f.points` is used as a longer polygon (`stan.c` 18, `chrprop.c`
    10, `propobj.c` 9), and `gunfire.c:5455` (the compiler's numbering: the file has `#line`
    directives) indexes past `struct hand[2]`;
  - `object-size`, 1: `stan.c:782` reads a record wider than the object it
    is read through (`prefix = &stan_prefix`, as decompiled);
  - `float-cast-overflow`, 1: `bondview2.c:5505`, `(s8)(frac * 255)` with
    246.5 (GCC's `-fsanitize=undefined` has no such check);
  - `pointer-overflow`, 1: `model.c:5959`, `+= 1` on a null
    `uselessPointer`.

  **Correction (same day).** This task first committed the `offsetof` form
  for every build (2af7d4b), as its plan said, and that broke CI's Linux
  tests job: `lp64_pointer_types.py check` reported `no longer
  pointer-only: StandTile` (and the two records it embeds). GCC prints
  `<stddef.h>`'s `offsetof` macro with each piece on its own indented
  line, the tool looks only 40 characters behind a type name, so it missed
  `__builtin_offsetof (` and took the type for an object held by value.
  The tests job failed on the runs of 2af7d4b, 6b6c49d and 844f7de, and
  their `publish` job was skipped; the task check here had run the gate,
  the two static checks and the harness lines of that CI step, not its
  other lines. The fix guards the `offsetof` form with `__APPLE__`, so the
  trees that tool reads hold the original lines again. Before it was
  pushed, every line of CI's tests step ran in the x86_64 container on a
  snapshot (105 of 108 passed; the other three read Git's file list, which
  a snapshot lacks, and pass in the checkout: `lp64_casts.py check`,
  `test_lp64_overlays.py`, `lp64_overlays.py check --no-defects`), and
  `lp64_pointer_types.py check` printed `OK: 121 pointer-only types, as
  pinned`. Two ways not taken, for the record: taking the offsets from the
  trace's own pointers adds a `(StandTile *)` cast, a new site for
  `lp64_overlays.py`; widening the tool's look-behind fixes its reading of
  `offsetof` but also changes how it counts `ALBank_s` and `ALInstrument`,
  which needs FORK-089's R11 judgement. **That tool defect stands and is
  for the owner:** an `offsetof` of a pointer-only type from a system
  header's macro is misread on a GCC tree.

  **For MAC-002:** three of those sites are in strict-tier files and were

  `deprecated-declarations` warnings, all `sprintf`: AddressSanitizer

- **The final review and its fix pass.** One fresh reviewer read the
  eleven commits against the plan, its Review Focus and the executor's
  rulings: nothing critical, three important findings, each fixed with a
  test that failed first, and one question that a measurement answered.
  1. *`src/game/stan.c` had lost its line endings.* Task 6's two-line edit
     went through a tool that rewrites the whole file, and the commit
     turned 3,747 of its lines from CRLF to LF: a reformatting of an
     upstream-owned file that hid the edit in the diff, which neither the
     commit nor this entry said, and which Task 6's correction left in
     place. The file has its own endings again, written to the index
     unfiltered (`.gitattributes` would otherwise normalise it once more);
     against the commit before Task 6 it now differs by the five guarded
     lines and nothing else. `scripts/port/test_line_endings.py` (new, in
     CI's tests step) pins the 17 tracked files Git stores with CRLF or
     mixed endings and fails when one loses them or another gains them; it
     failed on `stan.c` first. No compiled byte depends on it (the Windows
     comparison below).

     Task 4's `harness_skip_unless_tool` skipped wherever `emcc` was
     missing, so CI's browser job (`web-pages.yml`), which runs that
     harness in the SDK image, would have printed `SKIP` and passed if the

     Task 4 (`a missing tool is not skipped off macOS`, in
     `test_harness_widths.sh`, failed first).

     `NAME: SKIP (`, so the partial skips of four harnesses were held by
     nothing, and a harness that printed nothing passed. It now treats
     every line that speaks of skipping ("skip", "skipped", "SKIP", "did
     not run"; a line starting `ok: ` is a check's own name) as a skip

     `test_macos_harnesses.sh` gained seven checks, which failed first.
     This supersedes Task 10's "list of two": two harnesses still skip

  *The question: are Task 8's three functions glibc's bits?* The plan's
  test was the sweep's 1,048,576 inputs, which passed. Compared in the
  containers with the C library itself, in scratch (a NaN counted as one
  value): against aarch64 glibc 2.39, `expf` is equal on all
  4,294,967,296 floats, `sinf` differs on 12 (six values and their
  negatives, |x| between 53 and 117, each by one unit in the last place),
  and `powf` is equal on 300,000,000 scrambled pairs and differs on 19 of
  about 940 million pairs chosen at its range edges. Against x86_64 glibc
  on a processor with FMA (the container's, under Rosetta 2): the same 12
  `sinf` inputs, 2 `expf` inputs and the same kind of `powf` pairs.
  Against i686 glibc: equal on all 14 of the differing inputs listed and
  on 20,000,000 scrambled pairs (not run over every float: 32-bit code is
  emulated here). The cause is fused multiply-adds: Arm's originals built
  with `-ffp-contract=fast` and their default aarch64 configuration equal
  aarch64 glibc on every float for `sinf` and `expf` and on all the `powf`
  pairs above, and built without fusing they equal this port. So glibc's
  hosts never agreed with each other on every input, only on those the
  sweep and the cases reach; the port, which must not fuse, follows the
  i686 results, and every comparison build now agrees on all of them. The
  Linux comparison streams did not move (Task 8's before-and-after run),
  and no line of the expected file was exercised again at i686: the
  reviewer advised an i686 `stage-jungle` run against its pins, which the
  plan leaves out and this session did not make. `port_compare_math_arm.c`
  and the guide say what was found. This went to the owner against
  decision 3, whose wording was "reproduce glibc's bits". **The owner
  accepted the functions as built (2026-11-27, "Accept as built"):** the
  comparison build's `sinf`, `expf` and `powf` are Arm's without fused
  multiply-adds, equal to glibc's on the sweep and on every input the 38
  cases reach, and not glibc's bits on the inputs counted above. The
  i686 `stage-jungle` run was still not made.
  *Left as the reviewer's minor notes, not acted on:* a NaN's sign is the
  host's in these functions; no `#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF` in the Arm
  files (flags alone prevent fusing); the Apple-Silicon-only refusal reads
  `CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR`; clang's narrowing warning misses narrowings to
  16 or 8 bits, and `__APPLE__` branches are outside `unprototyped`;
  `macos_no_rom.sh` and `macos_harnesses.sh` have no deadline of their

  aarch64: `OK: ran 600 frames`. `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`:
  `identical in loaded code and data`. CI on the closing commit
  (`9a1e389`, run 46082375237) passed in every job, `tests`,
  `macos-arm64-tests` and `publish` among them, so the five MinGW x64
  lines ran there.

**MAC-002's plan (2026-11-27, documentation only).**
[`scripts/port/macos_mac_002.md`](scripts/port/macos_mac_002.md) plans the
window, picture, sound and input in 13 tasks. It was measured on a scratch
copy of `main` at 567251f outside the repository; no source, tool or
workflow file changed, and nothing it describes is built. What the
measurements found, each with its command or file reference in the plan:

- The macOS video tree fails 7 of 396 steps, all C++ under `port/fast3d/`,
  because libc++'s `<cmath>` finds the game's `include/math.h`. Three
  lines in that header clear six; the seventh needs one cast in
  `hd_textures.cpp`, a strict-tier file. With a link line of SDL2 alone it
  links (`OK: 702 weak references, 0 strong`), and the gate compiles its
  393 files.
- With the executable's path taken from dyld instead of `/proc/self/exe`
  the game starts, gets Apple's OpenGL 4.1 core context and draws Dam
  correctly. The log holds three faults the Linux logs do not: the two sky
  programs' retained twins fail to link under the core profile, glad's
  loader logs 36 functions the context does not export, and a 3.0 request
  fails before the 4.1 one.
- A window created and never shown is drawn by the GPU on macOS. With a
  variable that keeps the game's window hidden and `cocoa` as the tools'
  video driver: 119 of 119 video play cases (the two sound cases among
  them), 318 pool and stage pairs within budget, 20 of 20 missions.
- A macOS video comparison build against the aarch64 Linux one, both at
  567251f: 38 of 38 simulation streams, 38 of 38 picture digests and 24 of
  24 sound streams identical.
- A sanitizer video build ran Dam with no report. The late-load audit and
  the smoke benchmark run on macOS as they are.
- Retina needs two edits, not one: `gfx_sdl2.cpp:396` tests an SDL
  enumerator with `#ifdef`, so no build has ever asked for a HiDPI window.
  With both, Dam is drawn at 3,456x2,234 and holds 120 pictures a second.
- At the tools' 60 Hz tick a shown window on the 120 Hz panel logs frames
  of 25 ms; at the shipped 120 Hz it does not.
- A defect in every build, read and not run: `gfx_sdl2.cpp:827` copies a
  screenshot row into a 4,096-pixel stack buffer whatever the drawable's
  width.

The plan's five decisions (hidden windows for automated runs; the strict
branch `macos/strict` kept current by merging, never rebased; Retina on
without a new setting; the screenshot row fixed for every build; the cost
figures as a first macOS baseline) wait for the owner. The scratch copy
and its run folders were deleted; the aarch64 reference run stayed under
`build/lp64/` until the same cleanup.

**Validation.** Through the plans' acceptance this entry was documentation
only, and the measurements above it were taken on scratch copies outside
the repository: they are the plans' inputs, not checks of a change. From
MAC-001 Task 1 each task's paragraph above names what ran for it. The
pre-commit hook's standards and settings placement checks ran on each
commit.

### FORK-092 — Linux weapon icons, icon cache and save transfer dialogs

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-25 at the owner's request, during LP64-007
Task 10's hardware session, after the owner played the x86_64 Linux package in
WSLg on the laptop (RTX 3070 through Mesa's d3d12 driver; Ubuntu 24.04, Mesa
25.2.8, zenity 4.0.1, GTK 4.14.5). Five faults; each fix below (the fifth
found on CI's `f069653` package and fixed after it).

**1. Weapon icons drew nothing under Mesa.** The weapon strip showed its cards,
the active bar and the caption, but no picture, on the RTX 3070 (Mesa d3d12)
and under llvmpipe. Task 8 Step 5 saw the same blank cards offscreen (FORK-089)
and left it to this session. The Windows game draws them on the same GPU,
with default settings: a scripted Dam start (`GE_STAGE=dam GE_CHEATS=guns`,
screenshots) showed every icon on Windows and none in WSL. The cache was
sound: its 38 images decode as weapon renders. A debug build in the x86_64
container (offscreen llvmpipe) showed the vertices, UVs and the uploaded
512x160 texture correct and bound to unit 0, with no GL error. The fragment
shader was the fault: `texel = vec4(texVal0.rgb, mix(texel.a, texVal0.a,
vInput1.a))` reads `texel` before it is set.

The icon draw (`gfx_ge_vector_overlay`, shape 4, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`,
FORK-011) asked for `alpha_comb(G_ACMUX_TEXEL0, 0, G_ACMUX_SHADE, 0)`. In the
N64 combiner, 0 in the B and D slots is COMBINED, the previous cycle's output,
not zero (`G_ACMUX_COMBINED` is 0, `G_ACMUX_0` is 7). In a one-cycle draw that
is undefined. NVIDIA's own driver happened to start it at zero, giving TEXEL0
times SHADE; Mesa does not. Both icon passes (the rim and the picture) now use
`alpha_comb(G_ACMUX_TEXEL0, G_ACMUX_0, G_ACMUX_SHADE, G_ACMUX_0)`, which is
TEXEL0 times SHADE in any driver. The new shader is
`texel = vec4(texVal0.rgb, texVal0.a * vInput1.a)`. The other overlay draws
use `(0, 0, 0, D)`, where COMBINED cancels; a scan of the run's 180 compiled
programs found no other read of `texel` before it is set.

The two programs' ids change: the rim pass now maps to
`0000000001081000 10000001`, already in `tools/shaders_base.txt`, and the
picture to `0000000001088000 10000001`, added there. The old
`00000000d1d81000` and `00000000d1d88000` lines are removed, so the strip's
shaders still compile while loading (`web_target_progress.md`'s 2026-11-07
note added the old two for the same reason).

**2. A first launch on NVIDIA's WSL driver kept weapon names.** The icon worker
(`port/fast3d/weapon_worker.cpp`) wrote a valid cache, then crashed at exit in
NVIDIA's driver (`ge: icons: worker exited 139`; the game itself does the
same at every quit, FORK-089's Task 10 record). The game read the exit status
as a failure and showed names until the next launch. `prepare`
(`port/fast3d/weapon_cache.cpp`) now accepts the cache when it validates after
the worker ran, whatever the exit status: the file is replaced atomically and
checked against its CRC and the ROM fingerprint, and the cache did not
validate before the worker started. It logs `ge: icons: the worker failed
after writing a valid cache; using it`. Checked in the x86_64 container with a
fresh cache folder and an `LD_PRELOAD` library raising SIGSEGV from a
destructor at exit: the run logged `worker exited 139`, then that line and
`background preparation ready`. On the laptop the owner's first launch showed
icons from the next mission.

**3. The save transfer dialogs on Linux.** Export and Import (Files screen,
`port/fast3d/save_transfer.cpp`) failed in WSLg in several ways, each found in
the owner's runs:
- **No click reached the picker.** zenity's dialog took typing but no click.
  zenity alone took clicks, so the game was the cause. While the picker was
  open the game thread blocked in `read()`, so requests SDL had queued in
  Xlib's buffer were never sent, and XWayland kept the pointer lock it makes
  from a warped hidden cursor (FORK-091). The game now shows the cursor and
  leaves relative mode before a dialog, then waits with `poll()` and pumps
  SDL's events every 50 ms. That sends the requests and keeps the window
  answering; the events it queues reach the game after the dialog closes.
  Taking the game out of fullscreen while the dialog was open was tried and
  proved unnecessary: with pumping, a fullscreen game worked too, so that
  change was removed.
- **A chosen file was lost.** GTK 4 zenity inherited the game's
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12` and segfaulted at exit in NVIDIA's driver (a
  self-closing `zenity --info --timeout=2` exits 139 with those variables), so
  the game read the exit as Cancel. Dialogs now run with GTK's GL off
  (`GDK_DEBUG=gl-disable` for GTK 4.14, `GDK_DISABLE=gl` for 4.16 and later):
  the same test then exits cleanly (5, its timeout), and `GSK_RENDERER=cairo`
  alone does not help. The picker also keeps a path it printed with its
  newline even if it then fails; both tools print that only on a confirmed
  choice.
- **No message, and Import could not be confirmed.** SDL could not open its
  message box under WSLg (`No message system available`), so the result
  message never showed and Import's confirmation always read as Cancel. When
  SDL's box fails, both use zenity (`--info`, `--error`, `--question`) or
  kdialog. Only a clean exit 0 confirms an import; a failed or crashed dialog
  is Cancel.
- **Where the files go.** An exported name without an extension gets `.json`,
  as the Windows picker's default extension does; Import lists only `*.json`,
  so the owner's backup saved as `aab` could not be found. Both pickers start
  in the folder of the last export, remembered in `.save-transfer-folder`
  beside the data (not a setting, so not on the Iron Sights page or in
  `midas.ini`; outside `save_backup.cpp`'s backup allowlist), else in the home
  folder. Import passes a file in that folder, since zenity 4 opened a
  folder's parent with the folder selected. The Windows dialog remembers its
  own folder and is unchanged.
- The game window is passed as the dialog's parent (zenity `--attach`,
  kdialog `--attach`) when SDL's X11 driver gives its id. zenity 4 ignores it
  ("DEPRECATED; does nothing") and still prints a warning; zenity 3 and kdialog
  honour it.
- Known limit: zenity 4.0.1 opens the suggested folder but leaves Export's
  name field empty, so the player types a name.

The runner is `port/fast3d/posix_dialog.{h,cpp}`: it finds zenity, else
kdialog, on `PATH`, builds the argument and environment lists before `fork`,
`execve`s without a shell, and reports the output and exit status. CMake adds
it to `ge_save_transfer` on non-Windows builds only. Mouse, keyboard and pad
reach the dialogs as the desktop gives them; browser touch has its own picker
(`portWebFileMenuRequest`), unchanged.

**4. Mouse-look under WSLg: not fixable here.** Turning stops at the screen
edge and runs backwards. That is WSLg's relative motion (FORK-091's last
paragraph, corrected today); no change was made.

**5. The menus lost the mouse after a mission.** On CI's `f069653` package the
owner paused, quit a mission and found the menu cursor would not follow the
mouse (keyboard only); the log read `mouse 0/s` from the release on. Leaving
relative mode, SDL warps the hidden cursor back, and XWayland turns a warp
under a hidden cursor into the pointer lock FORK-091 resets on focus; under
WSLg it then gets no motion. The day's first probe showed it too: no motion
for nine seconds after relative mode was switched off. `portMouseApplyCapture`
(`port/src/input_pc.c`) now calls `portXwaylandPointerReleased` after
releasing the mouse, which applies FORK-091's reset (show, then hide, the
cursor; X11 under a Wayland display, cursor hidden) and logs
`ge: input: XWayland pointer reset on release`. Linux native builds only.
`test_xwayland_pointer.sh` runs its seven cases through both resets
(`14 cases passed` at 32 and 64 bits). A local release package with it, on
the laptop: after a pause and quit the menu cursor followed the mouse.
`compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (this change against `f069653`):
`identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`.

**Sources:** `port/src/port_xwayland_pointer.c` and its header
(`portXwaylandPointerReleased`), `port/src/input_pc.c` (`portMouseApplyCapture`),
`scripts/port/test_xwayland_pointer.c`, `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` (the icon combiner),
`tools/shaders_base.txt`, `port/fast3d/weapon_cache.cpp` (`prepare`),
`port/fast3d/save_transfer.cpp`, `port/fast3d/posix_dialog.h`,
`port/fast3d/posix_dialog.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` (`ge_save_transfer`),
`scripts/port/save_transfer.md`.

**Checks:**
- [ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_posix_dialog.cpp) and its
  [runner](scripts/port/test_posix_dialog.sh), in the workflow's tests step,
  against fake zenity and kdialog scripts: a chosen file with an argument
  holding a space and a quote, a tool that prints and then dies of SIGSEGV,
  Cancel, the kdialog fallback, no tool, and the GL switches (an existing
  `GDK_DEBUG` keeps its flags). `PASS (32-bit): 7 cases`, `PASS (64-bit): 7
  cases` in the x86_64 container; `test_harness_widths.sh` passes.
- CI's 64-bit gate lines on task-owned trees in the x86_64 container
  (`lp64_diagnostics.py gate`, `narrowing --check`, `unprototyped --check`,
  `lp64_pointer_types.py check`, `lp64_lto.py check`, `lp64_overlays.py check
  --no-defects`, `lp64_casts.py check`): all passed.
- Offscreen llvmpipe in the x86_64 container, Dam: the strip draws every
  card's weapon, pairs included, where it drew none before.
- Laptop, a local x86_64 release package of `9d4e0cb` plus this change: the
  owner saw the strip's icons, the first-launch icons, Export writing the
  file, the result message, Import opening in the export's folder and its
  confirmation.
- Smoke benchmark, Windows, RTX 3070 (`bench.py run --smoke`, `before` built
  from `HEAD` by `stock.py`, three repeats). Average fps before and after:
  default cradle-fight 567 and 566, dam-walk 907 and 897, temple-4p 658 and
  664; matched 717 and 718, 1182 and 1175, 809 and 836. Run-to-run ranges
  1-7%; every difference is inside them except matched temple-4p's median
  frame, 2% faster. One profiled matched dam-walk run of each:
  `bench_profile.py`'s largest differences are all under 0.1 ms a frame, the
  renderer's `gfx_run_dl` 0.697 and 0.663 ms. The browser runner was not run
  (two more browser builds); the picture pass's shader drops one `mix`.
- `late_load_audit.py --stage dam --keep` with both builds, then `--compare`:
  the only difference is the old build compiling the two old icon programs
  during play (the audit installs this checkout's shader list); the new build
  compiles no shader during play.
- `hand_gallery.py generate`: 0 image cells changed; `verify` passes.
- The 32-bit Windows program changes, as LP64-007 decision 13 allows when
  every changed function is named. `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`
  reports `different` (sections moved). Only three objects differ
  (`gfx_pc.cpp`, `weapon_cache.cpp`, `save_transfer.cpp`). Disassembled in the
  `goldeneye` container and compared function by function, with addresses and
  relocated immediates masked, the changed functions are
  `gfx_ge_vector_overlay` (the icon combiner), `prepare`'s locked callback in
  `weapon_cache.cpp`, and `portSaveTransferRequest` (with `message` and

### FORK-091 — XWayland pointer reset on focus

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-25 at the owner's request, during LP64-007
Task 10's hardware session, after the owner found the x86_64 Linux package's
menus soft-locked under WSLg on the laptop (Windows 11, WSL 2.1.5, Ubuntu
24.04) after an alt-tab.

**The fault.** After the owner alt-tabbed out of the fullscreen game and back,
the window still got key presses and clicks but no pointer motion. The red
menu cursor stayed where it was, and each click pressed whatever lay under it.
The game logged `mouse 0/s` from then on. F1 (take and release the mouse) did
not bring motion back. A minimal SDL window built on the package's own
`libSDL2`, with the same X11 driver and desktop fullscreen, reproduced it.
With the cursor hidden it recovered from every alt-tab until it warped the
pointer once. After that warp it still moved while focused, but after the next
focus change it got no motion until the cursor was shown again. Showing the
cursor brought motion back at once.

XWayland emulates a pointer warp under a hidden cursor with a Wayland pointer
lock. Under WSLg the emulation survives the focus change without receiving
motion, and showing the cursor ends it. The same session showed the Windows
arrow over the game: WSLg does not honour the hidden cursor either.

Inherited behaviour: upstream's menus warp the real pointer to re-seat their
cursor (`mouseWarpFree`, `port/src/input_pc.c`), and the game hides the
system cursor for as long as mouse control is on. Upstream has no reset.

**The fix.** On `SDL_WINDOWEVENT_FOCUS_GAINED`, a Linux native build shows the
system cursor and hides it again, when SDL's video driver is `x11`,
`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set (so X11 is XWayland) and the cursor is hidden.
Nothing else changes: no setting, no new input, no change to the warp or to
the mouse lock. Plain X11, SDL's Wayland driver, offscreen runs and a cursor
the player has shown are left alone. The call sits behind
`#if defined(__linux__) && !defined(__EMSCRIPTEN__)`, and the module compiles
to nothing elsewhere, so the Windows and browser builds are unchanged. It runs
once per focus gain, never per frame, so it needs no benchmark. It logs
`ge: input: XWayland pointer reset on focus` each time.

Keyboard, pads and browser touch are unaffected. Real Linux Wayland desktops
(GNOME, KDE) were not tried. Their compositors may not show the fault, and the
reset there costs one cursor change per focus gain.

**Sources:** [interface](port/include/port_xwayland_pointer.h),
[module](port/src/port_xwayland_pointer.c), with the hook in
`port/src/input_pc.c`'s window-event case. FORK-092 adds the same reset after
the game releases the mouse (`portXwaylandPointerReleased`).

**Checks:** [ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_xwayland_pointer.c) and its
[runner](scripts/port/test_xwayland_pointer.sh), in the workflow's tests step.
It covers seven cases: XWayland with the cursor hidden and shown, plain X11,
an empty Wayland display, SDL's Wayland and offscreen drivers, and no driver.
A reset must show, then hide, the cursor, and leave it hidden. It passes at 32
and 64 bits in the x86_64 container. A copy of the module without the show
call fails it. The module compares names with `SDL_strcmp`: the game's include
path puts the N64 SDK's `string.h` first, which declares no `strcmp`. CI's
`lp64_diagnostics.py unprototyped --check` failed the first push, `97ddab2`,
on it.

On the laptop, the minimal SDL window, given the same reset, recovered pointer
motion after a warp and an alt-tab twice (524 and 71 events a second, against
0 without it). An x86_64 package built with the fix in the release image
(`linux-release-x86_64.Dockerfile`) was played in WSLg. After each alt-tab
the menu cursor followed the mouse again, and the log showed one reset line
for each return.

`compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` prints `identical in loaded code and
data; .buildid differs`. CMake keeps the module out of every build but Linux
video builds, as it does for `input_pc.c`. On Windows its empty object would
still add a compiler identification string. A configure of 64-bit headless
and video trees confirmed which builds compile it.

The first comparisons on the laptop differed for an unrelated reason. The
checkout held 34 files with CRLF line endings that Git stores with LF.
`WORKTREE` exports files from disk, so `hd_texture_scope_embed.cmake`
embedded `hd_level_native_aliases.json` with 2,114 extra bytes. Restoring the
files' LF endings from Git made the two builds identical.

Two other WSLg faults stay as they were; this fix does not reach them. WSLg
still draws the Windows arrow over the game. In relative mode, which gameplay
uses for mouse-look, WSLg hands SDL the Windows cursor's own motion with its
sign flipped, at full scale: the minimal window logged `xrel` −54 while the X
pointer moved 55 to the right, and `yrel` +26 for a move of 27 up. That cursor
is never recentred, so turning stops at the edge of the screen. A warp moves
only the X server's pointer (to the window's centre, 506,427), never the
Windows cursor, and the next motion puts it back where the Windows cursor is.
SDL's warp-based relative mode therefore piles up phantom motion (+11,462 in
five seconds). Nothing inside Linux can recentre the Windows cursor, so
mouse-look cannot be played under WSL; the menus read absolute positions and
are unaffected. Corrected 2026-11-25 from probes in LP64-007 Task 10's session
(the first reading had the motion as one count an event).

### FORK-090 — Load before play: late-load audit, HD prefetch, warm-up frames

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-15 at the owner's request, after the owner
reported frames skipped when the shutter opens at the start of Runway. Built
and measured for Windows (RTX 3070 Laptop GPU, NVIDIA driver). The owner
play-tested the Windows build and confirmed the Runway hitch is gone. The
browser, Linux and Steam Deck builds were not built or run.

**The Runway hitch.** Opening the shutter makes the outdoor rooms visible for
the first time. With the HD texture pack on, the renderer then read 60 HD
images from the pack in that one frame, on the render thread, inflating each
PNG with the vendored reference decompressor `puff`: a 330-365 ms frame
(uploads 285-315 ms) against 25 ms with original textures. A profile of the
frame put 98% of the render thread in `import_texture` -> `hd_textures::lookup`
-> `Pack::read` -> `png_decode::rgba`: 69% inflating PNG data in `puff`, 16%
unfiltering rows, 6% creating and uploading GL textures, 3% inflating the ZIP
entry. FORK-053 had kept the download's images on that immediate read on
purpose, so they never showed their originals first.

Inherited behaviour: upstream loads everything on first use, as the N64 did.
The fork's HD packs (FORK-053), shader prewarm (FORK-057) and room-cache and
level-cube passes (FORK-058, FORK-066) added first-use work of their own.

**The rule.** A slightly longer load is better than a stall during play:
`AGENTS.md` ("Load before play") and
[the guide](scripts/port/late_loads.md). First-use work belongs to the stage
load or the boot, is recorded so later runs load it ahead, or runs in the
background; leaving it on first use needs a reason here.

**What changed:**

- **Late-load reporting** ([port_late_loads.c](port/src/port_late_loads.c)).
  A stage's load ends with its first frame shown. Every timed load event after
  that is late: `ge: late load:` lines in the log for events of
  `GE_LATEWARNMS` (default 3) ms or more, at most 20 a stage, and every event
  in `GE_LATELOG=<file>`. The existing timing sites now name what they loaded
  (`portHitchNoteItem`: room number, model file, texture number, shader ids,
  the upload's format, size, GL-name wait and HD read). Uploads now include
  the wait for a new GL texture name, and room-cache twin programs are timed
  as shaders.
- **Room tour** ([port_load_tour.c](port/src/port_load_tour.c)).
  `GE_LOADTOUR=<ticks>[,<settle>]` puts Bond on one pad of every room and turns
  him a full circle there, for audits; it ends the run after the last room or
  when a room finishes the mission (`portLoadTourMissionEnded`, file.c), and
  `portBenchRequestEnd` (port_bench.c) writes the frame log then.
- **Audit** ([late_load_audit.py](scripts/port/late_load_audit.py),
  [late_load_report.py](scripts/port/late_load_report.py)): every mission and
  multiplayer-only arena, toured with an isolated copy of the executable, the
  HD pack linked in and the shipped shader list; a report per stage, the
  costliest late events, shaders compiled during play, `--check`,
  `--env GE_LOAD_AHEAD=0` for the old behaviour, and `--learn-prefetch`.
- **HD prefetch** ([hd_texture_prefetch.cpp](port/fast3d/hd_texture_prefetch.cpp)).
  As a stage starts loading (`boss.c`, `portHdPrefetchStage`) the download's
  images for it are read on 2-8 worker threads: its mission folder in the
  scope (`group_of_path`, `Entry::group`), the in-game effects, and the other
  folders' textures it was seen to draw,
  [hd_stage_prefetch.json](port/fast3d/texture_packs/hd_stage_prefetch.json)
  (788 native keys for 26 stages, written by `--learn-prefetch`; Runway draws
  about 40 of Dam's). The title gets the gunbarrel. `boss.c` waits for them
  after `lvlStageLoad` (`portHdPrefetchWait`, at most 20 s). A lookup takes the
  image (moved, not copied); in play, a download image not prefetched is read
  on the custom-pack workers and swapped in when ready instead of stalling the
  frame. Images are dropped at the next stage.
- **Shader prewarm at load** (gfx_pc.cpp). While a stage (the title at boot
  included) loads, the prewarm compiles every listed program instead of 3 ms a
  frame; in play, after a filter change, it keeps 3 ms a frame. A combiner
  program made while loading builds its room-cache twin too (gfx_opengl.cpp).
  The browser keeps its own pace.
- **GL texture names ahead** (gfx_opengl.cpp): 64 at a time, stocked to 512
  while loading. On Runway one `glGenTextures` waited up to 5.9 ms behind the
  driver's queue.
- **Warm-up frames** (port_late_loads.c, gfx_sdl2.cpp, gfx_opengl.cpp). A
  stage's first three frames are drawn in full and presented black
  (`gfx_sdl_blank_back_buffer`), and every loading frame ends in `glFinish`.
  The frame after Runway's load had waited 185-290 ms for the driver when the
  level cube was first built; that wait now falls in a black frame. Presenting
  matters: with the frames drawn but not presented, the first real present
  waited 180 ms instead.
- `GE_LOAD_AHEAD=0` restores first-use loading in all of the above, for
  before/after audits and benchmarks of one executable; a mask keeps parts
  (1 HD prefetch, 2 prewarm at load and twins, 4 names, 8 warm-up frames).

Tried and not kept: drawing every room during the warm-up frames (through
closed portals; `bg.c` already has `GE_ALLROOMS`) did not help, because the
game unloads rooms it has not seen for a while and the room cache forgets them
with it; making the level cube's storage at load did not help, the wait was
not the allocation; neither building the level cube in each warm-up frame nor
a no-pixel draw with each prewarmed program changed the driver stall below.

**Measured:**

- **The Runway shutter**, with the owner's settings and HD pack (fixed
  tick, walking into the shutter; one executable, `GE_LOAD_AHEAD=0` against
  the default): the shutter frame 326.6 ms (uploads 312.0) to 34.5 ms
  (uploads 13.0). The stage's frames before play, 1,462 ms to 745 ms: the
  images are decoded on several threads instead of one.
- **Every stage**, audited on 2026-11-15 (20 missions and 6 multiplayer-only
  arenas, HD pack, room tour of 24 ticks a room, the shipped shader list, one
  executable, before = `GE_LOAD_AHEAD=0`): late load work summed over the
  stages 15,850 ms to 2,068 ms; frames of play that loaded 4 ms or more, 505
  to 73; shaders compiled during play 881 to 0; frames before play
  summed 11,418 ms to 6,491 ms. Per stage, late ms before/after: Dam 941/140,
  Facility 735/113, Runway 1,264/46, Surface 1,840/57, Bunker 1,115/86, Silo
  556/85, Frigate 440/61, Surface II 543/18, Bunker II 901/81, Statue 405/50,
  Archives 1,118/268, Streets 1,014/95, Depot 634/119, Train 920/63, Jungle
  462/75, Control 541/263, Caverns 650/76, Cradle 357/108, Aztec 597/84,
  Egyptian 473/29, the arenas 18-124 to 12-41.
- **Original textures** (Runway and Frigate): late load work 180/216 ms to
  22/30 ms, mostly the GL texture-name waits (2-4 ms for each new texture
  before); the worst frame of play 12/16 ms to 9/14 ms.
- Bisected with `GE_LOAD_AHEAD` masks on Runway and Frigate: the prefetch
  (bit 1) removes the HD reads, the prewarm at load (bit 2) the shader
  compiles, the names (bit 4) the name waits.

**Known remaining first-use costs:** With the HD pack, a frame that first draws several newly
uploaded large textures can wait 100-250 ms in the NVIDIA driver with nothing
timed: on Dam when the gun first shows after the intro (tick 545, 185 ms), and
in about half the audited stages where the tour jumps into a large new area.
With original textures it did not show, nor on Runway and Frigate with only
the prefetch off (`GE_LOAD_AHEAD=14`), where the same places stalled about as
long decoding instead (Runway 156 ms). Ruled out: the uploads (a `glFinish`
after each took at most 3.5 ms), address space (a large-address-aware copy
stalls the same), program first draws, the level cube's storage, and building
the level cube during the warm-up frames. Suspected, not confirmed without GPU
tools: the driver making the new textures resident on their first draw; the
next thing to try is uploading and drawing each prefetched image while the
stage loads. Also remaining: the room cache's capture and level-cube draws of
a room seen for the first time (about 17 ms of Runway's shutter frame, the
same with original textures), prefetched images' GL uploads (1-13 ms for the
largest), and models read from the ROM when first spawned (1-3 ms each, as
the original game does).

**Not covered:** the watch and pause menus (the tour does not open them), MP
with more than two players, weapons other than those a stage starts with,
explosions, non-default display modes. Custom HD packs keep their background
reads (FORK-053). The browser does not prefetch HD textures (it has no HD
packs) and keeps its own prewarm pace; its warm-up frames and loading
`glFinish` were not measured there.
