Inherited behaviour: upstream builds only as a 32-bit program (`-m32`, and
32-bit WebAssembly), by design, and this fork inherited that. FORK-031 recorded
a native x86_64 port as assessed and deferred. Upstream has open, unmerged
64-bit macOS pull requests (murkantor/Project-Midas 42 and its rebase 95).

**What was decided** ([plan](scripts/port/native_64bit_plan.md)):

- **Why.** The owner wants the game on their own Apple TV, buildable by other
  developers for theirs, and native macOS and 64-bit Linux builds. Apple TV and
  Apple Silicon run only 64-bit ARM code. Three projects follow in order: the
  64-bit engine port (this plan), a macOS build, an Apple TV build. The last
  two get their own plans.
- **Approach.** Widen: 8-byte pointers, 16-byte display-list commands, ROM data
  converted to the wider layout at load. The fork writes its own
  implementation, following the Perfect Dark port's mechanisms, and does not
  adopt upstream's open pull requests. If upstream merges its own 64-bit work,
  the next upstream merge will conflict widely with this one; the owner
  accepted that.
- **Scope.** Linux x86_64 is the first shipped 64-bit build, compared with
  Linux i686 in one container; a Linux aarch64 build is a development and
  verification target only. The 32-bit Windows, Linux and web builds keep
  their current loaders and keep shipping. Windows x64, macOS, Apple TV and
  64-bit WebAssembly are outside this plan.
- **Suspend points.** Planned as unavailable on 64-bit builds, because they
  restore raw memory to fixed addresses. Campaign saves are unaffected.
- **Where the work runs.** The owner's Apple Silicon Mac, with the US ROM in
  that checkout's root, ignored by Git.
- **Review gallery rule, two tiers (built in LP64-001 Task 1).** The owner
  chose to loosen the gallery requirement to two tiers: a strict list (the
  fork's hand, arm and wardrobe code, the game files the arm contracts name,
  the renderer, the weapon icons, the capture path and the tool) keeps today's
  rule; every other rendering input may leave the gallery pending, opt-in per
  clone (`midas.galleryDefer`), cleared on the development laptop at each
  milestone's end at the latest. Commits 2a3101e and 2c4d7f1 built it; the
  gallery was regenerated on the owner's Windows laptop in 8d6760d on
  2026-11-15 (only `manifest.json` and `index.html` changed, no image), and
  again there at LP64-001's end, also on 2026-11-15, in the commit
  "Regenerate the review gallery and close LP64-001" (no image changed). The rule is in `AGENTS.md` ("Render
  review gallery") and [the gallery guide](scripts/port/hand_gallery.md).

**Measured while planning** (2026-11-15, not a check of any build):

- A syntax-only 64-bit compile of the 161 game and engine C files reported
  about 1,600 distinct places in 70 files that mix pointers with 32-bit
  integers, and 40 hard errors. The port layer and renderer were not compiled.
- On macOS 27.2 on Apple Silicon, a 64-bit program could not map memory below
  4 GB, and one linked with a smaller zero page was killed at launch.
- A dry-run merge of upstream pull request 95 into this fork conflicted in 24
  of its 200 files. It was not merged.

**Milestone LP64-001 (scaffolding), planned on 2026-11-15, done on 2026-11-15:**
[its implementation plan](scripts/port/native_64bit_lp64_001.md) lists eight
tasks: the two-tier gallery rule, a container runner for the Mac, a layout
probe, a 64-bit diagnostics ratchet, a 32-bit executable comparison, a repair
of the headless build (Task 5b), a `GE_POINTER_BITS` build option, and CI
wiring. All eight have been built (below): Task 1 (the two-tier rule) in 2a3101e and
2c4d7f1, Task 2 in 54b1209, 857398a, a0ed9b2 and 8167b54, Task 3 in 803e4c6,
Task 4 in 59d1755 and 02e7c35, Task 5 in ebf3912 and c7f9701, Task 5b in
be840ef and 36d7ed2, Task 6 in 72064fe and f126afc, and Task 7 in 364fb13 and
f4c2c10. Each task extended this entry with what it built and ran; the fix wave
after the whole-milestone review extended the notes of the tasks it changed.

*LP64-001 task 2, the container runner (built 2026-11-15 on the owner's Apple
Silicon Mac, Docker 29.9.2):* `scripts/port/lp64_env.py` runs a command in the
right container (`build-images`; `run --arch i686|x86_64|aarch64 -- COMMAND...`).
i686 and x86_64 use the root `Dockerfile`'s `goldeneye` image under
`linux/amd64`; aarch64 uses `scripts/port/lp64-arm64.Dockerfile`
(`midas-lp64-arm64`, `linux/arm64`, Ubuntu 24.04 with build-essential, cmake,
ninja, python3, git). The checkout mounts at `/home/dev/project`, and the ROM
read-only at `/rom/baserom.u.z64` with `GE_ROM` set. Docker gets an argument
list, never a shell. `scripts/port/test_lp64_env.py` (11 ROM-free tests) was run
and passes. *Fix wave after the milestone review (the commit "Refuse a GE_ROM
that is not an existing file"):* `GE_ROM` is resolved to an absolute path and
must be an existing file; otherwise `run` prints an error naming the path and
exits 2 before Docker is called (a relative path used to reach Docker as a
named volume, and a mistyped absolute one could be created as a host
directory). Two `*.z64` files in the root now also exit 2 with a message rather
than a traceback. The file has 15 tests; the four new ones (a relative path
becomes absolute, a missing path and a directory are refused naming the path,
`run` exits 2 without calling Docker) were seen failing before the change. Run on the Mac: `build-images` succeeded (3 min 58 s);
`gcc -dumpmachine` printed `aarch64-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-linux-gnu` in the
two images; a `gcc -m32` program ran in the i686 container, so 32-bit x86 runs
under Docker Desktop here. **Reference run (found two workarounds, repaired in task 5b):** the stock headless build had defects. (1) `cmake ... -DGE_HEADLESS=ON` (with or without `-DGE_VIDEO=OFF`) failed to compile `port/src/port_baked_trace.c` (`SDL.h: No such file or directory`; headless builds do not exclude that SDL-using file). (2) Past that, linking failed with `port_bench.c:110: undefined reference to portRenderAsyncActive` (`s32 portRenderAsyncActive(void)`, defined only in `port/src/video.c`, which the headless list removes; also called from `hitchlog.c` and `pcsched.c`). Task 2 ran the reference with `-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-I/home/dev/project/scripts/port/sdl_shim` and a scratch object for that one symbol, and the 20-mission smoke (`audit_buffers.py --mission-smoke ... --frames 600 --jobs 2`, i686 container) exited 0 in 184 s with all 20 `PASS`.

*LP64-001 task 5b, the headless build repair (2026-11-15):* the headless build now configures, compiles and links with no extra flags, and the flag and scratch object are no longer needed. `CMakeLists.txt` gives `port/src/port_baked_trace.c` the include directory `scripts/port/sdl_shim` under `GE_HEADLESS` only (a source-file `INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES` property), so the bake uses its time-sliced, thread-free path (FORK-082); `port_baked_trace.c` is unchanged and a `GE_VIDEO=ON` build's compile and link commands are unchanged. `port/src/headless_stubs.c` (compiled only in headless builds) gained two stubs: `portRenderAsyncActive` returning 0 (no render thread without video) and `portRequestQuit` calling `exit(0)` (no window or event loop receives a close request, so it ends the process as `front.c`'s Exit Game does without video; the commit 3ef28aa load tour and `save_transfer.cpp` reference it; the first version did nothing, which would have left a headless load tour with no bench end running forever). `scripts/port/test_headless_configure.sh` configures a headless build into a temporary directory with `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON` and compiles `port_baked_trace.c` from its recorded command; before the repair it failed in the i686 container with `fatal error: SDL.h: No such file or directory`, after it prints `Headless configure OK`. In the i686 container the stock configuration (`cmake -S . -B build/lp64/ref-i686-stock -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DGE_HEADLESS=ON`, no other flags) built and linked, and `audit_buffers.py --mission-smoke build/lp64/ref-i686-stock/IronSights --rom /rom/baserom.u.z64 --frames 600 --jobs 2` exited 0 with all 20 missions `PASS` in 3 min 4 s (Task 2's flagged run: 184 s). A stock x86_64 configure into a fresh directory followed by `lp64_diagnostics.py check` printed `OK: 1432 diagnostics, baseline 1432`, so the baseline (recorded with the old flag) is unchanged. `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` built the Windows executable twice (56 s each) and exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data`. The one port source this task changed is `port/src/headless_stubs.c`, compiled only in `GE_HEADLESS` builds, so no shipped build's sources changed; no game, engine or renderer source was changed. *Which builds compile the two changes* (established by reading `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/emscripten.cmake`, `scripts/port/web_build.py` and `.github/workflows/web-pages.yml`; not built): the `GE_HEADLESS` block in `CMakeLists.txt` also applies to the Emscripten build, so the web `core` configuration (`python3 scripts/port/web_build.py core`, which configures `emcmake cmake -S . -B build/web/core -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK=OFF -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON -DGE_WEB_LINK_OPT=2 -DGE_VIDEO=OFF -DGE_HEADLESS=ON`, and `web_spike.py`'s audit) compiles `port/src/headless_stubs.c` and gives `port_baked_trace.c` the `sdl_shim` include; `port/web` defines neither new stub, so no duplicate symbol was seen by reading. CI does not build that configuration: `web-pages.yml` builds `web_build.py video` (`GE_HEADLESS=OFF`) and `files`, and no job builds `core`. The web `core` build with these changes has not been run.

*LP64-001 task 3, the layout probe:* `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` holds
compile-time `_Static_assert`s on the structs the renderer and ROM loader depend
on; it includes `<ultra64.h>`, `<PR/abi.h>`, `"ob.h"` and `"platform_info.h"`,
and all of them compile at 64-bit with GCC. At every width `s32`/`u32` are 4
bytes, `Vtx` 16, `Mtx` 64, `Vp` 16 and `Acmd` 8; `IS_64_BIT` matches
`sizeof(void *)`; `Gfx` is two pointer words with `words.w1` at one pointer
width. Under 32-bit only, `Gfx` is 8 bytes, `fileentry` 12 and
`resource_lookup_data_entry` 20. `scripts/port/test_abi_probe.sh` compiles it
at the host's native width and again with `-m32 -msse2 -mfpmath=sse`, runs
each, and prints `ABI probe OK (N-bit)`; it skips the `-m32` pass, announcing
it, when `-m32` does not compile. Flags follow `test_states.sh`. LP64-004 is to
add each file layout's assertions here. No game, engine, port or renderer
source was changed. *Fix wave after the milestone review (the commit "Assert
the light structs in the layout probe and the 32-bit link options"):* the probe
also asserts the renderer's light formats at every width: `Light_t` 12, `Light`
16, `Ambient_t` and `Ambient` 8, `Lights0` and `Lights1` 24, `Lights2` to
`Lights7` 40 to 120 in steps of 16, `Lightsn` 120, `LookAt` 32 and `Hilite_t`
16. `Hilite` is asserted at 16 bytes under 32-bit only: its alignment member is
`long int[4]` (`include/PR/gbi.h`), so it is 32 bytes on LP64. Each size was
measured first with a scratch program in the x86_64 container at both widths
(64-bit: `Hilite` 32, `Gsetcolor` 16, `TexRect` 32; 32-bit: 16, 8 and 16; the
light structs equal at both), and the 32-bit `Hilite` assertion without its
guard failed at 64-bit with `static assertion failed: "32-bit highlight
layout"`. `test_abi_probe.sh` now passes every definition `CMakeLists.txt` gives
all builds (`VERSION_US LANG_US REFRESH_NTSC LEFTOVERDEBUG LEFTOVERSPECTRUM
BUGFIX_R0 NONMATCHING AVOID_UB _LANGUAGE_C`; before, the five from
`LEFTOVERDEBUG` to `AVOID_UB` were missing, and `bondview.h` has a typedef under
`BUGFIX_R0`), so the layouts it asserts are the build's. In the x86_64
container it printed `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` and `ABI probe OK (32-bit)`.

*LP64-001 task 4, the 64-bit diagnostics ratchet (removed by LP64-002 task 10, which replaced it with the compile gate; see that note):* `scripts/port/lp64_diagnostics.py`
compiles every C file in a `compile_commands.json` syntax-only with 64-bit
pointers (it drops `-m32`, `-msse2`, `-mfpmath=sse`, `-w`, `-c`, `-o`, the
dependency flags and `-fsanitize...`, and adds `-fsyntax-only` with
`-Wint-conversion`, `-Wpointer-to-int-cast`, `-Wint-to-pointer-cast`), in
parallel (at most 8 workers, 60 s per compile; a compile that cannot start,
times out, or fails with no recognised diagnostic aborts the run). It counts
distinct (file, line, column, kind) places, where kind is one of the three
tracked flags (whether GCC reports it as a warning or an error) or `error` (any
other compile error). `count` prints the tally as JSON,
`update` rewrites `scripts/port/lp64_diagnostics_baseline.json` (sorted, trailing
newline, so an unchanged tree gives an empty `git diff`), and `check` exits 1
naming every file whose count rose above the baseline (a new file counts from
zero), refuses to compare across compilers (the baseline records `gcc-13`), and
prints `Baseline can be lowered: run update.` only when the total fell and nothing regressed. The baseline also records `errors_by_file`, and `check` fails when a file's compile-error count rises even if its total falls, since a hard error such as a missing header can hide the file's other diagnostics. A `compile_commands.json` with no C entries is an error, never a zero. Default input
is `build/lp64/diag/compile_commands.json`, resolved against the repository root
(before the fix wave, against the working directory). Task 7 ran `check` in CI until LP64-002 task 10; the
pre-commit hook never ran it. No game, engine, port or renderer source was changed.
*Coverage:* the count covers exactly the C files of the headless configuration
(329 entries in its `compile_commands.json`, all C). It does not cover the video, input
and audio platform files that configuration removes (`port/src/video.c`,
`input_pc.c`, `audio_pc.c`, `raphnet.c`), the vendored C (`glad.c`, `puff.c`),
any C++ (the renderer in `port/fast3d` included), or `port/web`. Widening it to
the video configuration and C++ is LP64-002's (recorded in the plan's status
table; widened by LP64-002 Task 1, see the note after the milestone
paragraph below). *Fix wave after the milestone review (the commit "Build the headless tree
before counting 64-bit diagnostics"):* the procedure is now configure, build the
whole headless tree, then count. Three files include `port_buildinfo.h`, which
the `ge_buildinfo` build target writes, and the old configure-only procedure
stopped them at `fatal error: port_buildinfo.h: No such file or directory`, so
they were never measured: `port/crash/reporting_linux.c`,
`port/src/port_startup.c` and `port/src/sysstubs.c`, exactly the three files
with one "error" each. A `fatal error:` in any file now makes `count`, `check`,
`update` and `sites` exit 2 naming the files, before anything is written. A
failing compile whose error lines are not all located diagnostics (a driver
error such as `gcc: error: unrecognized command-line option`) is refused even
when tracked warnings were also found; the fatal-error rule did not cover that
case, so it is a separate rule. An error line whose flag is one of the three
kinds counts under that kind (GCC 14 makes `int-conversion` an error by
default). A new `sites [FILE...]` subcommand prints every diagnostic as
`file:line: kind`, and a failing `check` prints the sites of each file whose
count rose. `check` still passes below the baseline, so a file can regain what
it lost until the baseline is lowered: when fixes lower the count, run `update`
in the same change so the ratchet tightens. `scripts/port/test_lp64_diagnostics.py`
has 23 tests: the pure functions, and `main` run on a `compile_commands.json`
whose compiler is a stand-in Python script (no real compiler); each new test
was seen failing before the change. *Re-recorded baseline,* in the x86_64
container from a wiped `build/lp64/diag`: the configure-only tree made `count`
exit 2 naming the three files; `cmake --build build/lp64/diag -j"$(nproc)"`
built and linked the headless game in 19 s (16 cores; Rosetta 2 translates the container's 64-bit tools); `check` against
the old baseline then exited 1 with `port/src/port_startup.c: 2 diagnostics,
baseline 1` and its two sites (`port/src/port_startup.c:19:
pointer-to-int-cast`, the `(s32)` casts of the font pointers), the false rise
the reviewer predicted. `update` recorded the new baseline, a second `update`
was byte-identical and `check` printed `OK: 1432 diagnostics, baseline 1432`.
Old: 1,432 in 93 files, 709 `int-conversion`, 432 `pointer-to-int-cast`, 229
`int-to-pointer-cast`, 62 `error` (`src/game/propobj.c` 59 and the three files
above with one each). New: 1,432 in 92 files, 710 `int-conversion`, 434
`pointer-to-int-cast`, 229 `int-to-pointer-cast`, 59 `error` (all in
`src/game/propobj.c`). The three missing-header errors went; once measured,
`port_startup.c` shows its two casts, `reporting_linux.c` one `int-conversion`
(line 179) and `sysstubs.c` none. The total is unchanged by coincidence.

*LP64-001 task 5, the unchanged-32-bit comparison:* `scripts/port/compare_win32.py`
proves a change leaves the 32-bit Windows program unchanged. `commits REF_A REF_B`
(either may be `WORKTREE`: the files on disk now, tracked files with
uncommitted edits plus untracked files Git does not ignore, because the build
globs `src/game/*.c`, `src/*.c` and `port/src/*.c` and a new file is compared
before it is added; ignored files such as the ROM and `build/` stay out) exports
each state into `build/lp64/compare/a` and `b` (`git archive`, or a copy of
`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`),
builds each in the `goldeneye` container through `lp64_env.docker_command`
mounted at the same `/home/dev/project` path (the compiler embeds source paths),
one after the other, with the README's Windows configuration (Debug, `GE_VIDEO=ON`,
the i686 MinGW toolchain) under a per-build `timeout` (default 180 s,
`--deadline`; a timeout names the build and prints the log's tail), and
compares the executables. `compare EXE_A EXE_B` compares two existing files.
The comparison parses the PE with `struct` and compares: every loaded section's
bytes, VirtualSize, VirtualAddress and Characteristics (a `.bss` with no raw data
included; a section in only one file is a difference, and one named twice in a
file is an error); the COFF Machine and Characteristics; an explicit list of
optional-header fields (`HEADER_FIELDS`: Magic, AddressOfEntryPoint, ImageBase,
SectionAlignment, FileAlignment, the operating-system, image and subsystem
versions, Subsystem, DllCharacteristics, SizeOfStackReserve and Commit,
SizeOfHeapReserve and Commit, LoaderFlags, BaseOfCode, BaseOfData, SizeOfCode,
SizeOfInitializedData and SizeOfUninitializedData; these carry what
`CMakeLists.txt` sets with `--stack`, `--disable-dynamicbase` and
`--subsystem`); and every data directory's address and size except Debug and
Security. A list rather than "everything but the stamps", because some header
fields describe the file, which debug information also fills. Not compared,
deliberately: debug sections, meaning a section whose name marks it as debug
(`.debug*` or a `/N` long name) and whose flags carry
`IMAGE_SCN_MEM_DISCARDABLE` (a long-named section the loader keeps is compared;
the flag alone sets nothing aside, since `.reloc` is discardable and matters at
load); `.buildid`'s bytes (an identifier derived from the whole file, debug
information included; a `.buildid` in only one file is a difference); the COFF
TimeDateStamp and the optional header CheckSum (build stamps); SizeOfImage,
SizeOfHeaders, NumberOfSections, the linker version, the COFF symbol-table
pointer and count, and section file offsets (they describe the file rather than
what is loaded); the Debug directory (it points into debug information) and the
Security directory (a file offset to data that is not loaded). When everything
compared is identical but `.buildid` differs, the tool prints `identical in
loaded code and data; .buildid differs` and exits 0; exit 1 means a compared
difference, and exit 2 means it could not compare (a build, Git or Docker
failure, or an input that is not a PE file, named on stderr). The comparison
build configures without `MIDAS_SENTRY_INCLUDE_DIR`, unlike the release
workflow, so its `port/crash/reporting_win.c` compiles without
`MIDAS_SENTRY_ENABLED`; that file is compared as the comparison build compiles
it, not as the release does. Both builds run with
`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1700000000` exported: the build already honours it for the
About-page build time (`scripts/port/build_info.py`), and GCC and the linker
honour it for `__DATE__`/`__TIME__` and the PE export-directory stamp. The
exports have no `.git`, so both builds report the commit as unknown. Logs stay in
`build/lp64/compare/`, ignored by Git. `scripts/port/test_compare_win32.py` (36
tests, synthetic PE files and temporary Git repositories, no Docker or compiler)
passes. No game, engine, port, renderer or CMake source was changed.
*Fix wave after the milestone review (the commit "Compare the Windows
executable's load header and new untracked files"):* `WORKTREE` gained untracked
unignored files (before, a new `port/src` file was absent from the "after"
build and the tool said identical), the header fields above beyond the entry
point, image base and section alignment, the discardable-flag condition for
debug sections, the one-sided `.buildid` difference and exit status 2. Tests,
each seen failing before the change: an untracked unignored file is exported
and an ignored one is not; one test per header field group (COFF Machine and
Characteristics; Magic; BaseOfCode, BaseOfData and FileAlignment; the six
version fields; Subsystem and DllCharacteristics; stack, heap and LoaderFlags;
the three size totals), each a synthetic PE differing in that field alone;
a non-discardable `/4` is compared; a `.buildid` in one file is a difference;
a non-PE input exits 2. The debug-only experiment was repeated with the new
field list (working tree only, `src/game/bg.c` line 1504 in
`addToByteSetMaxSize15`, `s32 i = 0;` to `int i = 0;`, then restored with `git
checkout -- src/game/bg.c`, never committed): `commits HEAD WORKTREE` built
twice (55 s each) and exited 0 with `identical in loaded code and data;
.buildid differs`. Read directly from those two executables (35,176,161 bytes
each), every listed header field was equal, so none is derived from debug data
and none was dropped; only 16 bytes of `.buildid` and 2 bytes of the debug
section `/29` (`.debug_info`) differed. `SizeOfInitializedData` (5,819,392)
equals the raw size of the non-debug initialised-data sections; the debug
sections (27,488,768 more bytes) are not in it. That build has one long-named
section that is not discardable, `/4`, which the string table names
`.eh_frame` (unwind data, flags 0x40000040); the old name-only rule had left it
out of every comparison, and it is now compared.

*LP64-001 task 6, the pointer-width build option (built 2026-11-15, commits 72064fe and f126afc):*
`CMakeLists.txt` gains the cache variable `GE_POINTER_BITS` (string, `32` or
`64`, default `32`; code never reads it and no compile definition carries it).
Its checks run first, right after `project()`, which is early enough because
`WIN32` and `EMSCRIPTEN` come from the toolchain file, so a missing SDL2 under
the MinGW toolchain cannot pre-empt them. Any other value stops with
`GE_POINTER_BITS must be 32 or 64`; `64` with Emscripten stops with `The web
build is 32-bit; GE_POINTER_BITS=64 is not supported`; with `WIN32`, `Windows
x64 is outside the 64-bit plan; see scripts/port/native_64bit_plan.md`; with
`GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK=ON`, `GE_POINTER_BITS=64 requires runtime ROM loading
(GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK=OFF)`. At `32` every flag is as before. At `64` the build
drops `-m32`, `-msse2`, `-mfpmath=sse` and `-no-pie`, adds `-ffp-contract=off`,
omits the `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS`/`_TIME_BITS` definitions on `ge_hd_textures` and
`ge_save_transfer`, and links SDL2 by name from `${SDL2_LINUX_ROOT}/lib` (or the
system) instead of the i386 library directory. The compiled-in asset objects are
untouched, and they do not reach a 64-bit build: `PORT_ASSET_KEEP_SYMS` is set
empty (`CMakeLists.txt`, above `port_asset_record`, whose comment says that with
`GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK=OFF` all generated asset objects are dropped), so the keep
list is empty and with the fallback off no asset object is built or linked; a
default configure's `CMakeFiles/ge.dir/link.txt` and `build.make` name none
(checked in the x86_64 container, headless and default configurations, by the
fix wave). `ASSET_C_FLAGS` still carries `-m32`, but it is reached only with
`GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK=ON`, which `GE_POINTER_BITS=64` refuses. An earlier version
of this entry (commit f126afc) said the keep set was built `-m32` and linked into
every build so that a 64-bit build could not link; that was wrong, from a
misreading of the empty list. The 64-bit `SDL2_LINUX_ROOT` link
(`${root}/lib`) is unverified: untested, it ignores multiarch directories such
as `lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`, and it sets no build rpath. Under `EMSCRIPTEN` the first
branch is still `include(cmake/emscripten.cmake)` and every later guard keeps its
`32` behaviour, so no line reached by the web build changes at the default
value. `scripts/port/test_pointer_bits.sh` configures into temporary
directories and checks five cases (default has `-m32`, and its link command,
read from `CMakeFiles/ge.dir/link.txt` without building, has `-m32` and
`-no-pie` as whole words; `64` has none of `-m32`/`-msse2`/`-mfpmath=sse` and
has `-ffp-contract=off`, and its link command has neither `-m32` nor `-no-pie`; `48` is refused;
`64` with the fallback is refused; `64` with `cmake/mingw-i686.cmake` is refused,
skipped with a message when `i686-w64-mingw32-gcc` is absent). Only configuring
is tested; a 64-bit compile is not expected to work until LP64-002. Run in the
x86_64 container: before the change the script stopped at case 2
(`64-bit build still uses -m32`); after, all five cases passed. The link checks
were added by the fix wave after the milestone review; run against an export of
the working tree whose `CMakeLists.txt` had `-no-pie` removed from the 32-bit
link, the script failed with `FAIL: default link lacks -no-pie`, and against the
tree as committed it printed `ok 1b` and `ok 2b` with the five cases passing. A default
headless configure's `compile_commands.json` (build directory name
normalised) is identical to the one captured before the edit
(`commands-identical`), and `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` exited 0,
`identical in loaded code and data`. The Emscripten case was not run (no emsdk
here); the web build is shown unchanged by reading the diff only. Task 7 runs
`test_pointer_bits.sh` in CI, where the Emscripten case is not run either. This
task changed no game, engine, port or renderer source.

**Milestone LP64-002 (type hygiene), planned and done on 2026-11-16; all eleven tasks are on `main`:**
[the milestone's plan](scripts/port/native_64bit_lp64_002.md) lists eleven
tasks. The task notes below were written as each commit was made, so they say
"not pushed", "local" or "on the branch `lp64/types-strict`"; every commit
they name is on `main` since 9fdb6ec (the task 11 note, before the hand-off
list). This paragraph records the plan and
the measurements it rests on (no source, build file or tool had changed for it then), taken on `main` at ce60a74 in the Mac's
containers. *Root causes:* each of the 1,432 recorded places was attributed
from its compiler message and source line: 1,384 to 66 declarations or idioms
(the largest: `frontPrintText`'s two font parameters typed `s32`, 252 places;
the monitor animation script tables and their jump macros, 121, which include
all 59 hard errors; font locals in `options.c`, 102; calls to pointer-returning
functions with no prototype in scope, 102; the image bank's relocation offset,
87) and 48 to one-off sites. 167 places are in the gallery's strict-tier files
(`bondview2.c` 82, `model.c` 47, `gunfire.c` 38). *A real 64-bit compile:*
with `-DGE_POINTER_BITS=64 -DGE_HEADLESS=ON`, 328 of 329 translation units
compiled in both the aarch64 and the x86_64 container; only
`src/game/propobj.c` failed, on those 59 errors. With `GE_VIDEO=ON` and the
distribution's `libsdl2-dev` installed in a throwaway container (neither image
has a 64-bit SDL2), 356 of 360 compiled; the other three failures are C++
files under `port/fast3d/` and none is an int/pointer conversion
(`gfx_pc.cpp` and `gfx_opengl.cpp` on `system.h`'s `s64` typedef, which
conflicts with the game's at 64 bits; `gfx_shiny.cpp` on six C-linkage
conflicts that also occur at 32 bits in that container). Linking was not
tried. *Found on the way:* the build's `-w` also switches off
`-Werror=int-conversion` and its siblings, so the 64-bit gate cannot keep
`-w`; `src/game/gunfire.c`, `gun.c`, `lv.c` and `src/libultrare/audio/env.c`
use `#line`, so compiler line numbers for them are not file lines; the
pre-commit hook refuses a strict-tier change on the Mac on any branch, which
the plan's Task 2 puts to the owner. Not covered by the planned gate and
recorded for later milestones: about 527 calls to functions without a
prototype, of which the pointer-returning ones are in the plan, and about
1,780 incompatible-pointer-type places, both present at 32 bits too. (The 527
were the `implicit-function-declaration` warnings of the 64-bit headless tree
at ce60a74, pointer-returning functions included; the final review fix wave
re-measured what is left, in the "LP64-002 hand-off" list.)

*LP64-002 task 1, tooling (2026-11-16, local commit "Count the video configuration and guard against
truncating casts"; not pushed):* no game, engine, port or renderer source changed. (1) Both
toolchain images gain the distribution's 64-bit `libsdl2-dev`
(`--no-install-recommends`): one added `RUN` in the root `Dockerfile` (the
image the owner's Windows laptop also builds; nothing else in it changed) and
the package on the existing install line of `scripts/port/lp64-arm64.Dockerfile`.
The i686 SDL2 under `/home/dev/sdl2-linux-i686` is untouched. (2)
`scripts/port/lp64_diagnostics.py`: `--compile-commands` may be repeated;
the entries are merged and a source file several trees list is compiled once,
with the first tree's command. `sites --messages [FILE...]` prints
`file:line: kind: message | source text` (GCC's message without its `[-W...]`
flag, and the source line GCC quotes under the diagnostic, stripped). *Fix
round, `#line` files:* `src/game/gunfire.c`, `gun.c`, `lv.c` and
`src/libultrare/audio/env.c` use bare `#line N` directives, so the compiler's
line numbers for them are not the file's lines and the text it quotes is the
wrong line. For a source file that contains such a directive, `sites` (with and
without `--messages`) now reports the physical line and quotes the file's text
there: the tool compiles a second copy of the file with the directive lines
emptied (same line count), in a temporary folder outside the source tree, with
the original's folder searched first for quoted includes, and takes that
file's diagnostics from the copy (other files' diagnostics from the same
compile are unchanged). `count`, `check` and `update` still use the
compiler's own numbering, so the baseline is unaffected. `update` exits 2
and writes nothing when the new total exceeds the recorded one, unless
`--allow-rise REASON` is given; the reason is printed only when the total did
rise. A baseline that is unreadable or lacks `total`, `compiler` or `by_file`
makes `check` and `update` exit 2 naming the file. The default input is still
`build/lp64/diag/compile_commands.json`. (3) `scripts/port/lp64_casts.py`
(new): `find_casts(text)` returns the lines of a truncating round trip, an
`(u32|s32|int|unsigned|unsigned int|u16|s16)` cast applied directly to a
`(uintptr_t|intptr_t)` cast; `check` scans the tracked `*.c`, `*.h`, `*.cpp`
and `*.inl` files under `src/`, `port/` and `include/` (`git ls-files`, so
never build output or the ROM), exits 1 listing every site of a file whose
count exceeds `scripts/port/lp64_casts_allowed.txt` (`path<TAB>count<TAB>reason`;
a file not listed is allowed none) and 0 otherwise; `list` prints every site.
*Fix round, exact match:* `check` now requires each file's count to equal its
allowlist line. A file below its line (or at zero), or a listed file that is no
longer tracked, fails with `lower the allowlist line to N` or `remove the
allowlist line`, so the allowlist tightens as casts are removed and a freed
allowance cannot be reused; `violations` returns each path with its message.
`test_lp64_casts.py` has 16 tests after this round.
The comment text is not excluded: a cast written inside a comment counts. The
allowlist starts with today's 23 casts in 9 files (`port/src/port_arm_mesh.c`
3, `port_grip_mesh.c` 1, `port_textures.c` 1, `romdata.c` 2,
`romfile_model.c` 1, `romfile_setup.c` 7, `romfile_stan.c` 4, `src/game/bg.c` 3,
`src/game/propobj.c` 1), each with the reason `existing before LP64-002`. CI
(`windows-release.yml`) runs `test_lp64_casts.py` and `lp64_casts.py check`
after `test_lp64_diagnostics.py`; its diagnostics lines are unchanged and still
count the headless tree only, so against the wider baseline its count can only
read lower, never raise a false failure. *Tests* (each written first and seen
failing): `test_lp64_diagnostics.py` went from 23 to 33 tests (10 failing
before the change: the message and source parse, the merge, the rise refusal,
and the command-line cases for two trees, `sites --messages` and `update`
with and without `--allow-rise`); `test_lp64_casts.py` has 12 tests (it failed
to load before `lp64_casts.py` existed). *Re-recorded baseline,* from the
x86_64 container over both configurations (`build/lp64/diag`, headless, and
`build/lp64/diag-video`, `GE_VIDEO=ON`): `update` without `--allow-rise`
exited 2 with `the total would rise from 1432 to 1441` and wrote nothing;
with `--allow-rise "video configuration added"` it recorded 1,441 diagnostics

on the port hold absolute 32-bit addresses (`romdata.c` rebases ROM banks
into them, through the allowlisted `(u32)(uintptr_t)` cast; the compiled-in
`char *LxE[]` banks are read through the same `u32 *`). A wider
`output_slot` would only widen a value that was read from a 4-byte slot: it
would silence the warning while the 64-bit read stays wrong. They are the two
of the plan's 12 `g_LangBanks` places not removed here, hence 427 rather than
429. `language.c:427`, `textbank_ptr = g_LangBanks[bank_id]`, is now a
`u8 *` to `u32 *` conversion that the three counted kinds do not report; it
belongs to the same text bank converter question. *Windows comparison:* `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`
exited 1 in 112 s (`.text` 0xB0 bytes longer, VirtualSize 0x335874 to
0x335924; `.CRT`, `.data`, `.rdata`, `.reloc` and the debug section `/4`
differ). Disassembled by symbol with addresses normalised, seven functions
differ, all in files this task edited: `_portOskDraw`,
`_constructor_menu1C_portsheet`, `_constructor_menu08_difficulty`,
`_portPpoDraw` (`front.c`), `_langGet` (`language.c`), `_mpCalculateAwards`,
`_mp_watch_menu_display` (`mpmenu.c`); the `.ctors` lists differ only in the
constructor addresses they hold, and every differing 32-bit word in
`.rdata` (7,026), `.data` (175) and `.CRT` (3) is an address inside the
image in both builds. Recompiling the four game files and the four port files
at both refs with the Windows flags gave the same seven at `-O2`, and nothing
in `options.c` or the port files. In each of the seven, the optimised GIMPLE
calls the same functions with the same arguments as before, except
`_constructor_menu08_difficulty` (below). `_langGet`: the same loads, tests
and strings; GCC now predicts the `NULL` test of a pointer bank at 18 % where
it predicted the `int` test at 34 %, so the "bank not loaded" return moved out
of line and `eax`/`edx` swapped roles (block order and registers).
`_mp_watch_menu_display`: the first award's `textMeasure`/`textRender`
block, now behind a pointer test predicted non-null, moved inline with the
branch inverted (`jne` to `je`), its instructions unchanged but for the
temporary register. `_portPpoDraw`, `_constructor_menu1C_portsheet`:
register and stack-slot choice. `_mpCalculateAwards`: register and
stack-slot choice (the `% 17` magic multiplier and the constant 1 swap
`ebx` and `esi`), and at both award stores (`mpmenu.c:647` and `:666`,
`g_playerPointers[i]->ptr_text_*_mp_award = langGet(...)`) the load of
`g_playerPointers[i]` (`0x113273c4(,%esi,4)`) now happens before the
`langGet` call and is spilled to `0x34(%esp)`, where before it was loaded
after the call. That is equivalent: C leaves the two sides of `=`
unsequenced, and `langGet` stores nothing (`language.c:413-450` only reads
the bank table), so the pointer read is the same on either side of the call.
(The first version of this note called the whole difference register and
stack-slot choice; the GIMPLE check compared only call statements, so it
missed a load moving across a call. Correction round below.) `_portOskDraw`:
as well as registers, `cmpl $0x4, port_osk_row` became
`cmp port_osk_row, r` at two sites, each on a path where `r == 4` is already
known (two equivalent comparisons). `_constructor_menu08_difficulty`
is more than that: from GCC's `dom2` pass on (identical, conversions aside,
up to `thread1`), the jump threader specialised the difficulty loop's last
iteration: on the path where `i == 3`, the second `frontPrintText` of the
row, the loop exit and, when `hasCheatInfo` is 0, the tail
(`frontAddPreviousTabText`, `portMissionBestTimesDraw`) are copied, so the
function has one more `frontPrintText`, `viGetX`, `viGetY`,
`frontAddPreviousTabText` and `portMissionBestTimesDraw` call site; every
path still makes the same calls in the same order with the same arguments.
The likely trigger is that the dropped `(int)` conversions of the two font
pointers brought the copied block under the threader's statement limit.
This is tail duplication rather than block order; the requirement for
pointer parameters leaves no type that keeps this function identical. The
review traced every path of this function and of `_langGet` in both
executables and found the behaviour unchanged, and the controller accepted the
jump threading as an equivalent difference. *What ran:* the plan's task
check. Step 1 exited 0 in 22 s; `update` recorded 945 in 80 files without
`--allow-rise`. Step 2: the i686 headless build exited 0 (10 s, incremental)
and the 20-mission smoke exited 0 with 20 of 20 `PASS` (188 s). Step 3 as

*Task 5 review fix round (local commit "Sign-extend signed monitor script
operands and assert the table element width"; not pushed):* (1) A 64-bit bug
the retyping introduced: the tables write negative operands as unsigned hex
literals (`MONHORZSCROLL(0xFFFFE000, 120)`, `MONVERTSCROLL(0xFFFFFE00, 80)`;
eight commands, `propobj.c` lines 2620, 2653, 2655, 2657, 2659, 2661, 2727,
2778 at b4e409a), which zero-extended into a 64-bit `uintptr_t` element, so
`intptr_t time` read 4294966784 instead of -512 and those scrolls moved about
4 million units the wrong way (the 32-bit build was unaffected). *A general
hazard for the rest of the milestone:* a `u32` table element that holds a
negative value written as an unsigned hex literal zero-extends when the
element is widened to `uintptr_t`, so each widened table must have its signed
values sign-extended. Fix: `chrai.h` defines
`MONSIGNED(v) ((uintptr_t) (intptr_t) (s32) (v))`, which sign-extends at 64
bits and keeps the same bytes at 32 bits, and each macro operand is typed by
how the interpreter reads it. Signed (read as `tvcmd.time` into a float, a
signed `s16` or a rotation), now through `MONSIGNED`: the offset of
`MONHORZSCROLL`, `MONVERTSCROLL`, `MONHORZSCROLLNA` and `MONVERTSCROLLNA`; the
zoom factor of `MONZOOMWIDTH` and `MONZOOMHEIGHT` (so `MONZOOMSQUARE`); the
count of `MONHOLDTIME` (`pause60 = m->time`, `assert(m->time > 0)`); the angle
of `MONSETROTATION` and `MONROTATEIMAGE`. Unchanged: every duration `t` in
`arg2` (used as `1.0f / m->arg2`, unsigned), the `MONJUMPCHANCE` chance in
`arg2` (compared unsigned with `randomGetNext() >> 16`), the `MONUSEIMAGE`
image number (stored as `tconfig`, compared unsigned `< 100`), the `MONRGBA`
colour (masked or cast to `u32` at `propobj.c:7492-7501`), and the
`MONJUMPTO`/`MONJUMPCHANCE` targets (addresses, `(uintptr_t)`). `lp64_casts.py
check` does not flag the `MONSIGNED` form (it widens; the checker's pattern is
a narrowing cast applied to a `uintptr_t`/`intptr_t` cast). (2)
`test_monitor_script.c` now has four commands: after the rotation, a
`MONHORZSCROLL(0xFFFFFE00, 20)` whose operand must read back as -512 through
`monitorScriptCommand`, stepped past with `offset += 3`, then the jump to the
stop at `&script[7]`. Before the macro fix it failed in the x86_64 container
with `monitor script: scroll operand is 4294966784, expected -512` and passed
at `-m32`; after it, it printed `OK (64-bit)` and `OK (32-bit)` in the x86_64
and i686 containers. (3) `propobj.c` asserts beside the tables that a script
element is pointer-sized (`_Static_assert(sizeof(monAnim00Bond[0]) ==
sizeof(void *), ...)`), so reverting the tables to `u32` breaks the 64-bit
compile; the test builds its own script and would not notice. (4) The
reader count above was corrected (five readers, four casts added). (5) The
plan now shows `initanitable.c:249` moving to Task 9: the Cluster table's
animation pointer tables row says 1 of its 11 places moves, and Task 9's
Interfaces widen `ModelAnimation.address` together with its reader
`loadAnimationFrame` (`model.c:5915-5927`). *What ran:* step 1 of the task
check exited 0 in 22 s and `update` recorded 711 in 76 files (unchanged; the
count did not rise); the i686 headless build exited 0 (11 s);
`compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` against b4e409a exited 0,
`identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs` (112 s), so the
mission smoke was not repeated; `lp64_casts.py check` passed (23 casts,
unchanged).

*LP64-002 task 6, image bank, textures and model-file relocation (2026-11-16,
local commit "Type the image bank delta, texture slots and model relocation";
not pushed):* *Declarations:* `globalbank_rdram_offset` (`src/game/image_bank.c`
and its `extern` in `image_bank.h`) went from `s32` to `intptr_t`;
`sImageTableEntry.index` (`src/bondtypes.h`) from `u32` to `uintptr_t`;
`ModelFileTextures.TextureID` (`src/bondtypes.h`) from `u32` to `uintptr_t`,
because `texLoad` overwrites it with a data pointer exactly as it does `index`,
and the two audits that read it back (`gun.c`'s `portGunTexAudit`,
`objecthandler_2.c`'s hardware-pace loop) need the whole value; their local
`u32 id` became `uintptr_t id`. `texSetBitstring` takes `u8 *` (definition and
`image_bank.h`); its third caller passes `rzipGetSomething()`, which returned
`s32` while returning `rz_inbuf + rz_inptr`, so it now returns `u8 *`
(`src/game/decompress.c` and `.h`; this also removes the one-off at
`decompress.c:85`). `vtxstore_allocate` (`src/game/vtxstore.c` and `.h`) returns
`Vertex *` and its third parameter, which `objDeform` passes `model->obj` and
`chrCreateBloodStain` passes 0, is `void *`; the record field it is stored in,
`unk04` of `vtxstore.c`'s local `struct unk_09B7A0_struct_parent`, is `void *`
(only compared for equality). `chr.c` called `vtxstore_allocate` without a
prototype (harmless while it returned `s32`), so it now includes `vtxstore.h`.
In `bloodImgTranspose` (`blood_decrypt.c`), `rowend`, `var_t2` and `t1` are
`u8 *` and the two loop tests compare pointers. In
`sub_GAME_7F0762E0` (`objecthandler_2.c`), `filedata` is `u8 *`,
`replacementgdl` `uintptr_t` and `delta` `intptr_t`. `propobj.c`'s monitor test
reads `(uintptr_t)screen->tconfig < 100` (unsigned, as the `(u32)` was) and
indexes `monitorimages[(intptr_t)screen->tconfig]` (signed, as the `(s32)`
was). *The offset arithmetic:* every use was `(void *)(globalbank_rdram_offset +
(u32)&sym)`, 32 image table pointers and 17 `texLoadFromDisplayList`
arguments, all in `texReset`. Each is now `(u8 *)&sym +
globalbank_rdram_offset` (the display-list ones cast to `Gfx *`, the type the
web build's generated prototype declares): the symbol's address as a byte
pointer plus a signed byte count, so the result is the same number of bytes
from the symbol whatever its type, and at 32 bits the same sum modulo 2^32 as
the old `u32` addition. The only writes are `= 0` (port) and, under
`TARGET_N64` only, `(u32)pGlobalimagetable + 0xFE000000`, left as it was. The
other readers, in strict `gunfire.c`, are all under `TARGET_N64` and add it to
`u32` icon offsets; that file is not edited. *Model relocation:* the casts
inside `sub_GAME_7F0762E0`'s N64 path became `(intptr_t)` (for the `(s32)`
casts) and `(uintptr_t)` (for the `(u32)` casts), types identical to the old
ones at 32 bits, so every sum and difference keeps its expression; with
`filedata` a byte pointer, `(romremaining + filedata) - (intptr_t) name` is
byte pointer arithmetic, and the final size is the byte difference
`(Switches + (replacementgdl & 0x00ffffff)) - filedata`. The matching hack
`(u32)*(s32 *)&gdl` reads `gdl` through an `intptr_t` lvalue instead, so it
reads the whole pointer at 64 bits. On the PC this path is never reached: the
function returns after its port block, and `modelNodeReplaceGdl`'s first
argument and `sub_GAME_7F075A90` stay for Task 9. *Widened fields checked:*
`uintptr_t` and `u32` are both `unsigned int` on i686 Linux and i686 MinGW
(and `unsigned long`, also 4 bytes, on wasm32), so at 32 bits
`sImageTableEntry` stays 12 bytes (4 + eight `u8`) and `ModelFileTextures`
12 (4 + seven `u8`, padded to 4); at 64 bits they become 16 and 16. Every
initialiser of `index` (the 32 tables in `assets/oddtextures.c`) is an
`IMAGE_*` texture number, none with its top bit set; at run time `texLoad`
replaces it with a pointer and `port_textures.c` stores one
(`(u32)(uintptr_t) px`, its allowlisted cast, behind a 64-bit refusal). Every
comparison stays unsigned: `index < (u32)(MAX_TEXTURES - 1)` in `front.c`,
`(u32) tconfig->index < NUM_TEXTURES` in `othermodemicrocode.c`,
`ent->index >= 0x10000000u` in `sky.c`, `TextureID < (u32)MAX_TEXTURES` in
`image.c` (the signed N64 test is under `TARGET_N64`), and the two `id >=
(u32)MAX_TEXTURES` audits. Noted for LP64-003, not changed: the `(u32)`
truncations in `othermodemicrocode.c:362` and `port_textures.c:82` would let a
64-bit pointer whose low word is small pass as a texture number, and
`port_textures.c`'s cast and refusal can go now that `index` is pointer-sized;
`texLoad` still writes through `s32 *updateword` (the 64-bit plan's texture
item), and `ModelFileTextures` is a ROM record read in place as 12 bytes
(`romfile_model.c`), LP64-004's converter question. `vtxstore.c` allocates its
records with a literal 0x14 stride (`tmp = 0x14`), right at 32 bits and short at
64 bits, where the record (with its existing `Vertex *` and the new `void *`)
is 32 bytes. *Files touched:* `src/bondtypes.h`; in `src/game/`:
`image_bank.c`, `image_bank.h`, `decompress.c`, `decompress.h`, `vtxstore.c`,

(`rowend - v1` when `rowend >= v1 + 1`, else 1) with one `cmovb` where it used
`setae` and two `cmove`s, then advances the source, `var_t2` and destination by
`n`, `n` and `n * srcheight - pixelcount + 1` as before (an equivalent
comparison, and register choice). `_vtxstore_allocate`: `esi` and `edi` swap
roles throughout, and the successful return duplicates the four-instruction
epilogue instead of jumping to the shared one; every path stores the same
fields and returns `var_t0[var_a1].unk00`. `_objDeform` (`propobj.c`) and
`_chrCreateBloodStain` (`chr.c`), the two callers that copy vertices into the
buffer `vtxstore_allocate` returns: the copy loop addresses destination
`Vertex` `j` as base plus `j * 16` instead of a pointer stepped by 16 (the same
16-byte loads from `Vertices[j]`, reloaded each iteration in both, and the same
stores), with block order, branch direction (`jne` to `je` for the second
allocation in `chrCreateBloodStain`) and register and stack-slot choice; in
`_objDeform` the float block computing `(x - 60) / x` and the two constant
stores moved, unchanged. *What ran:* the plan's task check. Step 1 exited 0: both trees

*Task 8, review fix (local commit "Clear the bg stride casts and keep debug
traces' 32-bit output"; not pushed):* the first commit's message did not name
its changed functions; this commit's message does: `romCopyAligned` (a pure
`ebx`/`esi` swap), `init` (one displacement moved with the code) and
`replay_recorded_ramrom_at_address` (register choice, the header swap loop
stepping one pointer over the same addresses, and loads moved ahead of stores
to other, non-overlapping fields of the same buffer, every address keeping its
read-before-write order). The LP64-002 plan's list of accepted differences now
includes that last kind. *Stride places:* the ten `(s32)` casts on `bg.c`'s
four `bg_room_data` stride lines (4455 and 4659: three `vtxbase` and one
`ptr_bgdata_room_fileposition_list` each; 6394 and 6427: one each) are
`(intptr_t)`, and each line carries `/* LP64-004: bg_room_data stride */`; the
literals `24` and `+ 12` are unchanged, so the 32-bit arithmetic is the same.
This clears 20 places; the plan's Task 7 sentence that kept the lines for
LP64-004 now says the casts were retyped here. *Debug traces:* the
`GE_DUMP_BOND` cursor trace (`front.c`) and the five `GE_ROOM_AUDIT` `mema.c`
traces print addresses with `%08" PRIxPTR "` and a `(uintptr_t)` argument
(`<inttypes.h>`, which resolved in the Windows, i686 headless and x86_64 count
builds). On MinGW i686 and glibc i386 `PRIxPTR` is `"x"`, so the strings are
byte-identical to the originals; at 64 bits the traces now print the whole
address, where the `(unsigned)` casts of the first commit truncated it.
*`os.h` places:* GCC reports a macro argument at the macro's definition, and
the count records each header line and kind once. `os.h:877`
(`OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL`, int-conversion) is reached from `bondview2.c` 5014 and
5031 (`sub_GAME_7F0A3B40(Gfx *, s32 *)`, `glass2.c`), from six `options.c`
calls of the same function (4650 to 4708) and from `title.c:156`
(`titleRenderFolderMenuBackgroundLines`' `u8 *image`, `title2.h:9`); the
`options.c` and `title.c` calls now cast to the parameter type, and the place
stays until `bondview2.c`'s two calls are fixed in Task 9. `os.h:880`
(`OS_PHYSICAL_TO_K0`) int-conversion comes from `bondview2.c` 12259 and 12270
(`buildGaugeBarDL`'s integer parameter), and its int-to-pointer-cast from
`bondview2.c:12087` (`(u32) perspmtx`). *Other changes:* `resample.c` stores
`(intptr_t) param` in one line instead of a braced local (the cast checker
does not flag it, and the Windows functions are unchanged); the `mema` test
adds the trace's overlap compare (old line 211: at 32 bits a free at
0x7FFFF800 inside a space ending at 0x80001000 is not reported because the
end reads negative; at 64 bits it is). Retyping that compare `uintptr_t` made
the 32-bit run fail ("the overlap check's end compare changed signedness") in

as the game does, because `_memaFree`'s slot index wraps at 32 bits for these
addresses. The N64-only branch at `title.c:537` now adds to a `void *`
(`barrelDisplayListPtr`), a GNU extension. *Windows comparison of the whole
task* (`compare_win32.py commits c6a5a69 WORKTREE`, exit 1, 112 s): the same

constructor addresses; every differing word in `.data` (175), `.rdata`
(5,543) and `.CRT` (3) is an image address in both builds, with no other

*LP64-002 task 9, on the branch `lp64/types-strict` (written as local commits;
the branch was pushed with Task 10 at dd408f1 and CI ran on it, see Task 10;
the strict-tier gallery is regenerated on a machine that can render before the

*Declarations* (old type to new): in `src/bondtypes.h`, `ModelAnimation.address`

`uintptr_t` (element 15 is promoted in place to a pointer; nothing else reads

`& 0x80000000` RAM test reads `intptr_t address`, which at 32 bits is the same
`int` (the literal is unsigned, so the test is unchanged); the offset sums keep
their old signedness (`intptr_t` for former `s32`, `uintptr_t` for former
`u32`). No unsigned hex literal initialises a widened field: `address` and
`unk0c` are filled at run time, and the model files are served from the ROM or

*Fourth commit, the three C++ items:* `port/fast3d/system.h` declares
`typedef long long s64`, the game's type (`PR/ultratypes.h`), instead of
`int64_t`: on i686 (glibc and MinGW) and wasm32 `int64_t` is already
`long long`, so nothing changes at 32 bits, while at 64 bits on Linux it is
`long`, and `gfx_pc.cpp` and `gfx_opengl.cpp`, which see both headers, stopped
on the conflicting typedef; `sysSleep`, the one declaration using it, has C
linkage. `gfx_pc.cpp`'s DL jump ring (`struct DlJumpEntry`) stores the two
`Gfx` words as `uintptr_t` instead of `uint32_t`, so the brace initialiser at
line 8558 copies them at their own width and the 64-bit narrowing is gone
without a conversion; the brief asked for an explicit conversion that states
the width, but the only width that keeps `w1` (a display-list pointer at 64
bits) is the word's own, and a cast to 32 bits would be a truncating cast this
task does not add. The fatal-error dump prints the two words with
`"%08" PRIxPTR` (`<cinttypes>` replaces `<cstdint>` on the same line, so no
line number and therefore no `assert` line constant moves; `PRIxPTR` is `"x"`
on i686, so the format string is byte-identical). `gfx_shiny.cpp`: in the
containers (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13) C++20 `<chrono>` includes `<sstream>`, whose
`<ios>` reaches libstdc++'s `gthr-default.h`, which includes `<pthread.h>`, which
includes `<sched.h>`; with `-I src` ahead of the system folders that resolves
to the game's `src/sched.h`, which pulls in `ultra64.h` and the repository's C
`stdio.h`/`math.h` stand-ins inside libstdc++ and gives six C-linkage
conflicts (`sprintf`, `cos`, `sin`, `cosf`, `sinf`, `sqrtf`). Compiling the
same command with `-std=gnu++17` succeeds, and GCC 13's `<chrono>` includes
`<sstream>` only under `__cplusplus >= 202002L`. CI's `linux` job builds in
`scripts/port/linux-release.Dockerfile`, Ubuntu 22.04 with GCC 11; that image was
not built for this commit, so that GCC 11's `<chrono>` stops short of `<pthread.h>`
is inferred, not reproduced. Later, during the final review, that image
(GCC 11.4.0, linux/amd64 on the Mac, not real x86 hardware; the translator was not recorded then, and on 2026-11-19 it was Rosetta 2) built commit 79138e5 with
`linux_build.py` to a linked `IronSights`; packaging and the Sentry smoke were
not run. That shows GCC 11 compiles the 32-bit renderer with the game folders
on its include path without the conflict; it does not show which header chain
GCC 11 takes, so the cause stays inferred. `gfx_pc.cpp` also reaches `src/sched.h` this way
in the containers and compiled only because it includes the game headers
itself. The fix is in the 64-bit include order: `CMakeLists.txt` gathers
`src src/game src/inflate` in `PORT_GAME_INCLUDE` and, only when

`include`; no C++ file includes a header from them (every quoted include of
`port/fast3d` and `port/include` resolves elsewhere). The source is unchanged.

*LP64-002 task 10, the gate (2026-11-16, on the branch `lp64/types-strict`,

*Flags:* `CMakeLists.txt` keeps its warning options in `GE_WARNING_OPTIONS`:

class (`chraidata.c:50`) and a pointer mismatch in a conditional
(`language.c:447`); only `-w` or a source edit removes them, and neither was

*LP64-003 task 1, tooling (2026-11-16, commits 9a36c51 "See narrowed pointer-sized integers and unprototyped pointer calls at 64 bits" and 15df016 "Narrow the cast pattern's difference exclusion and correct the LP64-003 row", pushed):* no game, engine, port or renderer source and no build file changed; the 32-bit program is not touched. (1) `scripts/port/lp64_casts.py` `find_casts` also finds a truncating cast applied to a parenthesised pointer-width cast, `(u32)((uintptr_t)p)`, and the types `uint32_t`, `int32_t`, `uint16_t` and `int16_t`; it leaves out a cast of a difference of two addresses, `(s32)((uintptr_t)a - (uintptr_t)b)`, only when a top-level minus inside the wrapping parentheses is followed by a second `(uintptr_t)` or `(intptr_t)` cast; `(u32)((uintptr_t)p - 4)` is still found (the first version of the exclusion skipped any top-level subtraction, which the review caught; the count was 28 in 13 files before and after the fix). `lp64_casts.py check` still prints `OK: 28 truncating casts in 13 files, all allowed`, so `lp64_casts_allowed.txt` is unchanged (the planning run's widened pattern found 29, one being the difference at `src/init.c:129`, which this pattern excludes). (2) `lp64_diagnostics.py gate` also refuses, before compiling anything, an entry carrying `-Wno-error`, `-Wno-error=KIND` or `-Wno-KIND` for a kind that entry's language gates (all three in C, `int-to-pointer-cast` in C++), or an argument starting with `@` (a response file could hide a flag from the check); each refusal names its reason. (3) New commands `lp64_diagnostics.py narrowing [--check] [--all] BUILD_DIR...` and `unprototyped [--check] BUILD_DIR...`, kept in a new module beside it, `scripts/port/lp64_static_checks.py`, because `lp64_diagnostics.py` would otherwise pass 500 lines (it is 422 lines with the dispatch; the module is 182); the diagnostics file loads the module by path and passes it each tree's syntax-only commands. `narrowing` compiles every C and C++ entry with `-Wconversion -Wno-sign-conversion -Wno-float-conversion -Wno-error` under `LC_ALL=C` and lists each implicit conversion whose source type is `uintptr_t`, `intptr_t` or `romptr_t` as `file:line:column: SOURCE -> TARGET | source text`; `--all` adds the other 64-bit source types (`long`, `unsigned long`, `long long`, `size_t`, `ptrdiff_t`, `ssize_t`, `u64`, `s64`, `uint64_t`, `int64_t`) as a report that `--check` never counts. GCC drops the typedef name after arithmetic, so `(uintptr_t) a + b` narrowed to `u32` shows as `long unsigned int` and is found only by `--all`; the command's help and the module's docstring say so, and that a file with `#line` directives (`gunfire.c`, `gun.c`, `lv.c`, `env.c`) is listed at the compiler's line numbers. `unprototyped` compiles every C entry with `-Wimplicit-function-declaration` restored and `-aux-info`, and lists each call without a prototype, as `file:line:column: NAME | PROTOTYPE`, to a function whose definition (an `NF` or `OF` line of any file's aux-info) takes or returns a pointer or a 64-bit type; a name with no definition in the tree (a library function or a macro) is not listed. Both exit 2 when a tree is not a configured 64-bit tree, when no entry of the right language exists, or when any compile fails (such a file was not measured). `--check` compares each file's count with its line in `lp64_narrowing_allowed.txt` or `lp64_unprototyped_allowed.txt` (`path<TAB>count<TAB>reason`, exact match: more or fewer fails, the latter saying to lower or remove the line). (4) Both allowlists were written from this run, every line with the reason `existing before LP64-003`. (5) CI's tests step runs the two `--check` lines after `gate`, and the new test file after the diagnostics tests; `AGENTS.md`'s 64-bit paragraph and the LP64-003 row of the plan describe them. *Counts* (GCC 13.3, x86_64 container, both 64-bit trees): `narrowing` lists 112 places in 19 files and `unprototyped` 159 calls in 75 files, against the planning figures of 111 in 18 and 157 in 73. The headless tree alone gives 89 in 16 and 152 in 70, the video tree alone the same as both together. All the difference is video-only code in files both trees compile: the planning script compiled each file once, with the first tree's command, so it missed `port/src/port_state_effects_audit.c:31` (`uintptr_t` to `u32`, video-only code, the file the gate's task 10 found), and `strcmp` at `port/src/port_music_export.c:48` and `portDisplayCrosshairImage` at `src/game/options.c:2255` (unprototyped). Neither figure moves a Global Constraint. *What ran:* the new and extended tests (`test_lp64_casts.py` 23 tests, `test_lp64_diagnostics.py` 39, `test_lp64_static_checks.py` 22; each new test was seen to fail first: the cast tests on the missing pattern, the gate tests on the missing refusal, the new file's tests on the missing commands) pass with plain `python3`; task check step 1 in the x86_64 container (`329 files compiled, 0 failed` and `360 files compiled, 0 failed`); step 4 in the x86_64 container (`OK: 112 narrowings in 19 files, all allowed`, `OK: 159 unprototyped calls in 75 files, all allowed`); `lp64_casts.py check`, `test_lp64_env.py`, `test_compare_win32.py`, `test_settings_placement.py`, `settings_placement.py`, `test_hand_gallery.py`, `test_ci_dependencies.py`, `hand_gallery.py verify --allow-pending` (strict inputs fresh, deferred pending) and `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts all` (0 findings). (2) New `port/include/port_lp64.h` and `port/src/port_lp64.c` (175 lines): `portLp64RegionIsHigh(start, size)` is true when the region starts at or above `0x100000000` and does not wrap; `portLp64CheckRegion(name, start, size)` prints `ge: lp64: NAME at ADDRESS is below 4 GB; a 64-bit build needs every game address above 4 GB (scripts/port/native_64bit_plan.md, "Addresses")` and exits with status 4 for a low region, and otherwise remembers its name and start (16 entries for the report; a later name for the same start replaces the earlier, so the ROM's mapping is listed as `ROM image`, not `high allocation`; regions past 16 are still checked and counted as "and N more"); `portLp64CheckAddressSpace()` checks the main executable's loaded segments (the span of the `PT_LOAD` segments of the first object `dl_iterate_phdr` reports), a 64-byte `malloc` block and a stack address, then logs `ge: lp64: address space OK:` with each remembered region's name and start. The executable-image check is Linux-only (`#if defined(__linux__)`); a 64-bit build on any other system stops at an `#error` saying that platform's port must supply the main executable's loaded address range (the macOS project fills it in). At 32 bits the three are macros that generate no code (`1`, `((void) 0)`, `((void) 0)`), and `CMakeLists.txt` removes `port_lp64.c` from the source list unless `GE_POINTER_BITS` is 64: with the file in the 32-bit list, its empty object still grew the Windows executable's `.rdata` by 20 bytes (0xf526c to 0xf5280, at the end, where the objects' compiler idents sit) and changed 14 bytes of `.text` (`compare_win32.py` exit 1, with every change of this task except the `port_memp.c` message), and without it the comparison was identical. The 32-bit paths, the hint ladders (`0x20000000`, `0x30000000`, `0x50000000` and up), the Windows scan and the 32-bit messages are untouched; each 64-bit branch sits behind `IS_64_BIT`. No hint, fixed base or `-no-pie` link is added at 64 bits. (4) `port/src/romdata.c`: the "keeping the heap copy" fallback is inside `#if !IS_64_BIT` (at 64 bits `portAllocHighDedicated` stops the game instead of returning `NULL`), and `portLp64CheckRegion("ROM image", sRom, sRomSize)` runs once the image is copied. (5) `port/src/main.c` calls `portLp64CheckAddressSpace()` right after `romdataInit` returns, before `osInitialize` and `portAnimDataInit`: the arenas are reserved (`main.c:853`) and the ROM image is in place, and no ROM data is converted yet. (6) `port/src/port_memp.c`: the memory-bank exhaustion message names the bank as well as its number, at both widths: `Memory bank exhausted (bank %u "%s", request %u bytes)`, with the names of `enum MEMPOOL` (`total`, `mf`, `2`, `ml`, `stage`, `me`, `permanent`). (8) `scripts/port/test_high_alloc.c` (run by `test_buffers.sh`) expects the 64-bit fatal exit for oversized requests (below). ROM image 0x7ffff5cbb000, executable image 0x555555554000, malloc block 0x555556553490, stack 0x7ffffffc572c`. Both runs then end with signal 11 (exit 139) in `modelAnimReadRootMotionValue` (`src/game/model.c:941`) from `initResolveAnimGroups` in `bossInitMainthreadData` (`src/boss.c:284`), the crash the plan measured, which Task 4 turns into a named stop. The sanitizer build (`-DGE_SANITIZE=ON`, aarch64) passes the check too (its `malloc` block is at `0x506000000020`, still above 4 GB) and stops at its first report, `src/game/initanitable.c:241`, as measured. *The other pools' behaviour on exhaustion*, read from the code at this commit, for LP64-005 (none is resized or changed here):

| Pool | Where it is made | What happens when it is full |
|---|---|---|
| Memory banks (`stage`, `permanent` and the others) | `port/src/port_memp.c` `portMempAllocate`, in the 64 MB memp arena | Falls back to the `permanent` bank; when that is full too, `sysFatalError("Memory bank exhausted (bank N \"name\", request N bytes)")`. Named and fatal. Setup files, model slots, the graphics and frame buffers, the stage texture pool and the music heap are all carved from these banks, so their own allocation at stage load stops here. |
| Graphics buffer (the master display list, `g_GfxBuffers`) | `src/game/dyn.c` `dynInitMemory`, `-mgfx` KB per stage, doubled on PC, from the `stage` bank | Not checked: display-list writers run past the end into the next allocation. Only `GE_ROOM_AUDIT` notices, after the frame (`portDynAuditFrameEnd`: `roomaudit: *** DYN POOL OVERFLOW`). Silent otherwise. |
| Frame data (vertices, matrices, lights; `g_VtxBuffers`) | same place, `-mvtx` KB, doubled and sized by `portDynVertexCapacity` | `port/src/port_dyn.c` `portDynAllocate`: `sysFatalError("Frame data buffer exhausted (request ..., remaining ... bytes)")`. Named and fatal. |
| Room display lists and vertices | `src/game/bg.c` `bgLoadRoom`, one block per room from the `mema` heap (`-ma` KB, `src/mema.c` `memaAlloc`) | `memaAlloc` returns `NULL` after eight defragmentation passes and the room is not loaded, so it is not drawn; a block too small for the expanded display list makes the loader return -1 and the room is freed and not drawn. A message only with `GE_ROOM_AUDIT` (`roomaudit: *** MEMA ALLOC FAILED`). |
| Model slots (`g_ModelSlots`, `g_AnimModelSlots`) | `src/game/initunk_005520.c`, a fixed count from the `stage` bank | `modelmgrInstantiateModel` and `modelmgrInstantiateModelWithAnim` (`src/game/model.c`) return `NULL` to their caller, with no message. |
| Model display-list copies and the model texture pool | `src/game/objecthandler_2.c` through `portAllocHigh` (the 4 MB pool is `portModelTexPool`) | At 32 bits a `NULL` from `portAllocHigh` leaves the model node unconverted; at 64 bits, after this task, a request the high arena cannot hold gets its own mapping, and only a failed mapping stops the game (`ge: high allocation: could not map N bytes above 4 GB`). |
| Texture pools (the stage pool, `-mt` KB doubled, `src/game/initmttex.c`; the model pool above) | loaded by `texLoad` (`src/game/image.c`) | When fewer than `0x10CC` bytes (uncompressed) or `0xA28` (zlib) are free, the texture is pointed at the pool's start and draws as garbage; the PC build prints `ge: TEXOOM: texnum N cannot fit ...` for the first 12. The test is a fixed minimum, not the texture's size. Named, not fatal. |
| Music heap | `src/music.c`, `4 * 0x2E000` bytes from the `permanent` bank | `alHeapAlloc` (`src/libultra/audio/heapalloc.c`) returns `NULL` with no message (its `_DEBUG` report is compiled out), and `musicSeqPlayerInit` copies into the result unchecked, so the game crashes unnamed. (The comment in `music.c` says the allocator has no bounds check; it has one, and returns `NULL`.) |

A per-function comparison of the two executables' disassembly, with addresses blanked, shows `_portMempAllocate` as the only changed function (the remaining entries it lists are the `.ctors` pointer tables, data disassembled as code, whose function addresses moved). *LP64-003 task 4, a named stop at each unconverted asset class, and the boot check (2026-11-16). Task 4 built: commit "Stop a 64-bit boot at the first asset class without a converter".* (1) `port/include/port_lp64.h` gains `enum PortLp64Asset` (`PORT_LP64_TEXT_BANKS`, `_FONTS`, `_TEXTURES`, `_ANIMATIONS`, `_MODELS`, `_COLLISION`, `_SETUPS`, `_BACKGROUNDS`, `_AUDIO_BANKS`, `_MUSIC`, `PORT_LP64_ASSET_COUNT`: the design's ten classes in the design's order), declared at both widths (an enum makes no code), and at 64 bits `portLp64AssetName` (`text banks`, `fonts`, `textures`, `animation tables`, `models`, `collision tiles`, `setup files`, `backgrounds`, `audio banks`, `music sequences`; `unknown asset class` outside the enum), `portLp64AssetConverted` and `portLp64RequireConverter`, which for an unconverted class logs `ge: lp64: stopping: asset class "NAME" has no 64-bit converter yet (LP64-004)` and exits with status 5. `port/src/port_lp64.c` (237 lines) holds the names and the converted table, all ten entries 0; LP64-004 sets a class's entry in the commit that lands its converter. (2) The guards. A guard is the first statement of the code that reads or rewrites a class's ROM bytes (or the compiled-in copy) in place, after declarations whose initializers only look a segment up (`romdataSeg`). Where a class has a compiled-in path that the ROM path's guard does not cover, that path has its own guard. Line numbers are at this commit:

| Class | Guarded function | Place | Compiled-in path |
|---|---|---|---|
| text banks | `romdataTextPreprocess` (rewrites the bank's 4-byte offsets as 4-byte pointers) | `port/src/romdata.c:899` | None to guard: the compiled-in banks are C pointer arrays, used as they are, and at 64 bits they are not linked (`GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK` is refused); this ROM serves every bank |
| fonts | `portFontBuildSegments` (fontchar tables and `fontdl` written as 4-byte words) | `port/src/segments.c:348` | Covered by the same guard: it precedes the choice between the ROM and the compiled-in composition; the fix-up in `load_font_tables` (`src/game/textrelated.c`) runs after it |
| textures | `texLoad` (writes a texture's data address into a 4-byte slot of a display list, a model file's `ModelFileTextures` record or an image table entry) | `src/game/image.c:2541` | Covered: every caller goes through `texLoad`, including the compiled-in global image bank (`texReset`, `assets/oddtextures.c`) and the room lists (`texLoadFromGdl` through `texLoadFromTextureNum`) |
| animation tables | `portAnimDataInit` (`ModelAnimation`'s 0x14-byte file header read through 8-byte address fields) | `port/src/animdata.c:248` | Covered by the same guard (before the ROM or compiled-in choice); `expand_ani_table_entries`' relocation (`boss.c:282`) runs after it |
| models | `romfileModelConvert` | `port/src/romfile_model.c:412` | Guarded: the compiled-in branch of `load_object_fill_header`, `src/game/objecthandler_2.c:372` (not linked at 64 bits; this ROM serves every model) |
| collision tiles | `romfileStanConvert` (4-byte room pointer slots) | `port/src/romfile_stan.c:65` | Guarded: `portStanPack`, `src/game/stan.c:603` (4-byte room slots), which builds every compiled-in stan; eight stans are missing from this ROM |
| setup files | `romfileSetupConvert` | `port/src/romfile_setup.c:501` | Guarded: the compiled-in setup's restore and word walk in `proplvreset2`, `src/game/prop.c:1979`, the first layout-dependent step on that path (the `SETUP_PROMOTE` before it passes the typed struct's own pointers through); not linked at 64 bits, and this ROM serves every setup |
| backgrounds | `romfileBgConvert` (4-byte offset words of the front matter) | `port/src/romfile_bg.c:68` | Guarded: a new `else` of the served test in `load_bg_file`, `src/game/bg.c:1098`, before the header is read as `s32` words; eleven bg files are missing from this ROM |
| audio banks | `alBnkfNew` (relocated in place through 8-byte pointer slots over 4-byte file offsets) | `port/src/audio_stubs.c:238` | None: the banks come only from the ROM segments, and it is the only bank conversion (`src/libultra/audio/bnkf.c` is not compiled) |
| music sequences | `musicSeqPlayerInit`, before the sequence table is read (`RareALSeqData`'s address slot over a 4-byte file offset) | `src/music.c:798` | None: the table comes only from the ROM segment |

The 19 files this ROM lacks, from the 32-bit smoke's log (`not in this ROM's directory - keeping the compiled-in copy`): the bg files of `sho`, `eld`, `imp`, `ash`, `lue`, `rit`, `ear`, `lee`, `lip`, `wax` and `pam`, and the stans of `ear`, `eld`, `lee`, `lip`, `lue`, `pam`, `rit` and `wax`. At 64 bits their compiled-in copies are not linked. A stage that needs one stops at the bg guard in `load_bg_file`, which runs before the stan is loaded; every missing stan belongs to a missing bg file. (A null stan on its own would be read in `stanDetermineEOF` before `portStanPack` is reached.)

The texture class needs no guard where its directory is installed. `romdataImageTableApply` (`port/src/romdata.c`, inside `romdataInit`, before the address line; the log line `romdata: texture table`) reads the ROM table with `be32` and stores each value into `g_Textures` by field name, and takes the image bank's base from the file table: nothing in it depends on pointer size. The pointer-sized work of the class is `texLoad`'s store into a 4-byte slot, so the guard is there, and it is reached only at the first texture load, after the animation guard. The guard covers `texLoad` as a whole, including `texLoadFromTextureNum` with a stack copy, because the pool record `struct tex` it builds is in the design's texture class too. Edits in upstream-owned files are one include and one call each: `src/game/image.c` (the call inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`, like the include), `src/music.c`, `src/game/stan.c`, `src/game/objecthandler_2.c` and `src/game/prop.c`; `src/game/bg.c` also gains the two-line `else`. `stan.c` and `objecthandler_2.c` keep their CRLF line endings. (3) New `scripts/port/lp64_boot.py` (Python standard library): `parse_log(text) -> BootResult` (`address_ok`, `stop_class`, `fatal_signal`, `sanitizer_errors`), and `lp64_boot.py --rom ROM --expect-stop NAME [--stage NAME] EXECUTABLE...`, which copies each executable into its own directory under the system temp folder and runs it there with `GE_ROM`, `GE_FRAMES=120`, `GE_SEED=1`, `GE_NOINISAVE=1`, `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0` (a mid-boot stop leaves the game's allocations unfreed by design), `GE_STAGE` with `--stage`, every other `GE_` variable of the caller dropped, and a 120 s timeout. It exits 0 only if every run exited with status 5, logged `ge: lp64: address space OK`, stopped at NAME, and logged no `ge: fatal signal` and no sanitizer line (`runtime error:`, `ERROR: AddressSanitizer`, `ERROR: LeakSanitizer`, `ERROR: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer`); it prints `OK: stopped at "NAME" (EXECUTABLE)` or `FAIL:` with every difference and the last 20 log lines.
