*LP64-003 task 6, host pointers told from numbers and segment words at full width (2026-11-16). Task 6 built: commit "Classify command words and texture slots at pointer width".* The game told a host pointer from a small number or an N64 segment word by looking at a 32-bit copy of the value; at 64 bits that drops the upper half, so a real pointer could pass as a texture number or a segment word. (1) `port/include/port_hostptr.h` gains three predicates beside `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR`, each with a 32-bit form that is the expression its sites had and a 64-bit form that reads the whole word: `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST(w)` is `((u32) (w) >= 0x10000000u)` at 32 bits (under `GE_XBOX` too, whose `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR` differs; the user supplies `u32`) and `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(w)` at 64; `PORT_WORD_HAS_SEGMENT(w, seg)` is `(((uintptr_t) (w) & 0xFF000000) == ((uintptr_t) (seg) << 24))` at 32 bits and `(((uintptr_t) (w) >> 24) == (uintptr_t) (seg))` at 64; `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(w, limit)` is `((uintptr_t) (w) < (uintptr_t) (limit))` at both. The header now includes `platform_info.h` outside the `GE_XBOX` branch as well (a second, guarded include on the other branch); `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR` is unchanged, and `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, the strict-tier file that includes the header, uses none of the new names. (2) The sites (line numbers at this commit):

| Site | Before | Now | At 64 bits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `propobj.c:9168-9170` (`bgTestHitOnObj`, `G_VTX`) | `u32 vaddr = gdl->words.w1;` and `vaddr >= 0x10000000u` | `uintptr_t vaddr`, `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST(vaddr)` | a host vertex pointer is used whole; only a word with the upper 32 bits clear is resolved as segment-relative |
| `propobj.c:9293-9295` and `:9477-9479` (`G_TRI1`/`G_TRI2` texture lookups) | `u32 timg = tcmd->words.w1;` and `timg >= 0x10000000u && (timg >> 16) != 0xABCDu` | `uintptr_t timg`, `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST(timg) && (timg >> 16) != 0xABCDu` | the texture number is read at `timg - 8` from the whole pointer; the `0xABCD` IMAGESEG marker test keeps its tokens, so it reads the whole word: an IMAGESEG word (`0xABCD0000 \| id`) has its upper half clear and is already rejected by the host test, and a host pointer whose bits 16-31 are `0xABCD` still counts as a pointer |
| `bg.c:4517-4519` and `:4718-4720` (`bgTestRayIntersectionInRoom`) | as the `propobj.c` texture lookups | as the `propobj.c` texture lookups | as the `propobj.c` texture lookups |
| `lightfixture.c:296` (`lightFindVertexBaseForTri`) | `((uintptr_t) ret & 0xFF000000) == 0x0E000000` | `PORT_WORD_HAS_SEGMENT(ret, 0x0E)` | a host pointer whose bits 24-31 are `0x0E` is no longer rebased onto the room's vertices |
| `othermodemicrocode.c:363` | `(u32) tconfig->index < NUM_TEXTURES` | `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(tconfig->index, NUM_TEXTURES)` | a pixel pointer with a small low word is not taken for a texture number |
| `port_textures.c:83` (`texCrosshairNum`) | `(u32) crosshairimage->index < 0x1000u` | `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(crosshairimage->index, 0x1000u)` | as above, for the crosshair's slot |
| `port_textures.c:348` (`texLoadSlot`) | `t->entry.index = (u32) (uintptr_t) px;` | `t->entry.index = (uintptr_t) px;` | the external texture's slot holds the whole pixel address |

Each `src/game` file gains one `#include "port_hostptr.h"` (inside the existing `#ifndef TARGET_N64` include block in `propobj.c` and `bg.c`, beside the other includes in `lightfixture.c`, whose function is also compiled for the N64, and `othermodemicrocode.c`); the lines that rebuild the pointers (`(u8 *) (uintptr_t) vaddr`, `(u16 *) (uintptr_t) (timg - 8)`) are unchanged and now take the whole word. (3) The two refusals of external textures at 64 bits in `port/src/port_textures.c` are removed, as the design says (`native_64bit_plan.md`, "External textures stop being refused on 64-bit once their address slot is..."). Behind the first (`portTexExternal`) the slot loader reads a BMP through `stdio`, allocates the blob with `portAllocHigh` into a `u8 *`, writes the pixels through a `u16 *` and stores the address in `entry.index`, now whole; behind the second (`portTexReplaceRom`, called from `texLoad`) the code copies and re-encodes pool bytes through `u8 *` buffers and a `struct tex *`, keyed by the `s32` texture number. Neither path truncates a pointer or assumes 4-byte pointers once the slot is whole. At 64 bits `texLoad` itself is behind Task 4's `textures` guard, so the second path is not reached until LP64-004. `docs/port/abi-and-portability.md` no longer says the file truncates the slot and refuses external textures. (4) The slot loader can be driven ROM-free, so its first run is here rather than in LP64-005: new `scripts/port/test_lp64_textures.c` (173 lines) links `port_textures.c` with stubs (`portRootPath` into a scratch root, `portAllocHigh` from a static array, which is above 4 GB in a position-independent 64-bit executable, and empty stand-ins for the ROM-texture and crosshair paths), writes a 4x4 24-bit BMP it draws itself (no game data) as `Data/Textures/Base/option.bmp`, calls `portTexExternal("option")` and checks that `entry.index` equals the address of the pixels (16 bytes into the allocation); at 64 bits it first checks that the array is above 4 GB. `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.sh` builds and runs it at each width (`-Iinclude` puts the game's `string.h` first, as in the game build, so it adds `-Wno-builtin-declaration-mismatch`), and now passes `-D_LANGUAGE_C` so `test_lp64_address.c` can include `PR/ultratypes.h`. Seen to fail first: at 6def5b4 (in an ignored scratch directory) the driver printed `ge: textures: external textures need the 32-bit build` and `FAIL: the external texture's index is the whole address of its pixels`; with the refusals removed and `(u32) (uintptr_t) px` restored in a scratch edit (reverted) the 64-bit half printed the same `FAIL` line after `option.bmp 4x4 loaded`. (5) `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.c` gains one truth table per predicate. `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST`: `0x0E001234` false at both widths; at 32 bits `0x0FFFFFFF` false and `0x10000000` true (the non-Xbox `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR` line); at 64 bits `0xFFFFFFFF` false and `0x0000AAAA0E001234` true. `PORT_WORD_HAS_SEGMENT(w, 0x0E)`: `0x0E001234` true and `0x0F001234` false at both; `0x0000AAAA0E001234` false at 64 bits. `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(w, 0x1000)`: `0xFFF` true and `0x1000` false at both; `0x0000AAAA00000123` false at 64 bits (the old `(u32)` test said true). Seen to fail first: before the predicates existed both containers stopped on `error: implicit declaration of function 'PORT_WORD_IS_HOST'` (and the other two names). With each 64-bit form replaced by its 32-bit form in a scratch edit (reverted), the 64-bit half printed four failures: `0xFFFFFFFF is not a host word at 64 bits`, `0x0000AAAA0E001234 is a host word although its low word looks like a segment-14 word`, `0x0000AAAA0E001234 is not a segment-14 word at 64 bits` and `0x0000AAAA00000123 is not an index below 0x1000 at 64 bits`. (6) `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts that `ModelFileTextures.TextureID`, `sImageTableEntry.index` and `Gfx.words.w1` are unsigned (`UNSIGNED_FIELD`, `(__typeof__(field)) -1 > 0`), beside the existing pointer-sized assertions, so the full-width sentinel comparisons that the check found correct (`gun.c`, `objecthandler_2.c`, `image.c`, `front.c` and the others in the plan's list) stay unsigned; those sites are not edited. The same macro on a signed `int` field fails to compile (checked in a scratch file). *LP64-003 task 7, display-list words and other pointer-sized integers (2026-11-16). Task 7 built, first of two commits: "Store whole texture pointers through texLoad".* `texLoad` replaces a texture number in a slot with the address of the texture's data. Its parameter was `s32 *`, so at 64 bits it read and wrote 4 of the slot's 8 bytes, while every slot it is given is pointer-sized since LP64-002 (`Gfx.words.w1`, `ModelFileTextures.TextureID`, `sImageTableEntry.index`). (1) `texLoad(uintptr_t *updateword, struct texpool *pool)` (`src/game/image.c`, `image.h`). Its callers pass the field itself instead of a cast pointer to the record: `texLoadFromDisplayList` `&cmd->words.w1` (was `(s32 *)&cmd->words.w1`), `texLoadFromModelFileHeader` `&textures[i].TextureID` (was `&textures[i]`), `texReset` (`src/game/image_bank.c`) `&genericimage->index`, `&explosion_smokeimages[i].index` and `&scattered_explosions[i].index` (were the records), and `texSelect` (`src/game/othermodemicrocode.c`) `&tconfig->index` (was `(s32 *)tconfig`); the field is each record's first, so at 32 bits the address passed is the same. `texLoadFromTextureNum`'s stack copy `texturenumcopy` is `uintptr_t` (was `u32`). The two web-only traces in `texLoad` print the slot with `"%08" PRIxPTR` and the slot's address through `(void *)` (`<inttypes.h>` joins the file's `#ifndef TARGET_N64` include block). Task 4's `portLp64RequireConverter(PORT_LP64_TEXTURES)` stays `texLoad`'s first statement; its comment, which gave the 4-byte slot as the reason, now names what is still unconverted, the pool's `struct tex` records. The one other call, `texLoad((u32 *)((s32)bytes + 4), arg1)` in `texLoadFromDisplayList`, is inside `#ifdef TARGET_N64` (the N64 byte-walk; the PC branch is the `cmd->words` loop above), so it is not compiled on PC and its text is unchanged. No strict-tier file calls `texLoad`. At 64 bits `texLoad` is still behind the `textures` guard, so the whole store is not reached in a running game until LP64-004. (2) Test: `scripts/port/test_lp64_textures.c` (built at each width by `test_lp64_address.sh`; it already includes `image.h`) declares a stand-in with `static __typeof__(texLoad) stubTexLoad;` and defines it with a `uintptr_t *` parameter that stores `0x0000AAAA12345678`; the slot keeps all 8 bytes at 64 bits and `0x12345678` at 32. The case is in the textures driver rather than `test_lp64_address.c` (where the plan put it) because only that driver includes `image.h`, and the declaration through `__typeof__` is what ties the stand-in to `texLoad`'s real parameter. Seen to fail first, before the parameter changed, in the x86_64 container at both widths: `error: conflicting types for 'stubTexLoad'; have 'void(uintptr_t *, struct texpool *)'` with the note `previous declaration of 'stubTexLoad' with type 'void(s32 *, struct texpool *)'`. The CI tests step's 43 harness lines (every line but the configure, build, gate and static-check lines) ran in the i686 container and all exited 0, `test_buffers.sh` without `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1` (it hangs under i686 emulation); `test_lp64_address.sh` also passed in the x86_64 (`PASS (32-bit)`, `PASS (64-bit)`) and aarch64 (`PASS (64-bit)`) containers. *Not run:* the x86_64 boot check, the sanitizer variant of `test_buffers.sh`, the browser build (no emscripten here; the two changed traces are web-only), any 64-bit stage load, anything in CI.

*LP64-003 task 7, second commit: "Read and write display-list words at their own width".* A `Gfx` word is 8 bytes at 64 bits; code that copies one into a 32-bit integer, or reads half of it, either narrows silently or reads the wrong half. (1) New `port/include/port_gfxwords.h` (30 lines) holds four accessors and nothing else: `GFX_W0(g)` is `((u32) (g)->words.w0)`, the N64 command word; `GFX_OP(g)` is `(GFX_W0(g) >> 24)`; `GFX_W1_DATA(g)` is `((u32) (g)->words.w1)`, for a second word that holds data; `GFX_W1_ADDR(g)` is `((g)->words.w1)`, pointer-sized. At 32 bits each is the plain member access with a cast that changes nothing. They are used only where they replace an implicit narrowing; other `words.w0` reads in the tree are not rewritten, and no reader masks (the plan's "A command word's upper half is zero"). `GFX_OP` and `GFX_W1_ADDR` have no game site yet (`GFX_OP` is used by the test); the plan gives the strict-tier places to Task 11, which uses the same accessors. The header is included unconditionally where a use sits in code shared with the N64 build (`src/game/bg.c`, `src/game/tex.c`, as Task 6 did in `lightfixture.c`), inside the existing `#ifndef TARGET_N64` block in `src/game/propobj.c`, and beside the other includes in the three `port/src` files. (2) `bgTestRayIntersectionInRoom` (`src/game/bg.c:4383`) read the vertex offset as `((u32 *) gdl)[1]`, the second 4-byte half of the command; at 64 bits that is the upper half of `w0` (zero), not `w1`, so every vertex base was the room's first vertex. It now reads `gdl->words.w1 & 0x00ffffff`, and the comment above, which named the old expression, names the field. At 32 bits both load the word at offset 4. The other seven `((u32 *) gdl)[1]` reads are N64-only and unchanged. (3) `bgTestBulletHitBackground`'s tile size (`bg.c:4903`), `(w0 << 11) >> 30`, kept bits 19 to 52 at 64 bits instead of bits 19 and 20; it now shifts `GFX_W0`. (4) The assignments to `words.w0`, each read; none can put a nonzero value in the upper half, so no writer is edited. The census is by text search at this commit (assignments and compound assignments to `words.w0` outside `PR/gbi.h` and `PR/abi.h`, whose macros build words with `_SHIFTL`; `abi.h`'s 16 build `Acmd` words, which are LP64-004's): 37 sites in 20 source files plus 5 macros in `include/gbi_extension.h`. *LP64-003 task 8, structures the game builds at run time (2026-11-16). Task 8 built: commit "Size and access run-time structures by their types".* Some structures the game allocates and fills itself were sized or written as if a pointer were 4 bytes, so at 64 bits they overran or put a flag in the wrong half of a pointer. Each is now sized or written through its type. (1) `vtxstore.c`'s two slot arrays were allocated at the literal stride `0x14`; `struct unk_09B7A0_struct_parent` is 32 bytes at 64 bits, so each array was indexed at 32 bytes a slot in an allocation of 20, and its later slots lay past the allocation. `sub_GAME_7F09B820` now sets `tmp = sizeof(struct unk_09B7A0_struct_parent)` (20 at 32 bits, the same constant). The struct moved verbatim, with its comment, from `src/game/vtxstore.c` into `src/game/vtxstore.h` so that the layout probe can name it: the one moved block of this task, eight lines, made because the plan puts the assertion in the probe, which links nothing from the game. The same function allocates its `Vertex` arrays at `0x10` a slot; `Vertex` is 24 bytes at 64 bits until Task 11 makes it 16, so those lines are Task 11's and unchanged. (2) `StandTileLocusCallbackRecord` (`rooms` pointer, then `count`, `bufMax`, `nearEdgeCount`): `stanCheckLinkedSpecialTile` (`src/game/stan.c`) wrote its crouch and ladder flags as `((s32 *) record)[0]` and `[1]`; at 64 bits word 1 is the upper half of `rooms`, so the ladder never reached `count` and `stanGetLocusCount` returned 0. It now writes `record->rooms = (s32 *) (intptr_t) 1` and `record->count = 1`, which at 32 bits store the same four bytes at offsets 0 and 4. `stanTileDistanceRelated`'s clear, four `((s32 *) arg4)[n] = 0`, is `*arg4 = (struct StandTileLocusCallbackRecord) {0};`: the brief asked for the four fields set by name, and that form changed the 32-bit executable (see the comparison below), while the compound literal sets the same four fields through the type and compiles to the old instructions. `stanGetLocusField0` keeps its `s32` result and its body. (3) `bondview2.c`'s `move_bond_temp_struct curLocus` (strict tier, not edited) is the record those functions clear and write: 16 bytes and 4-byte aligned, while the record is 24 bytes and 8-byte aligned at 64 bits, so the typed clear would have written past it. Its definition in `src/game/bondview.h` (not strict tier) is `struct StandTileLocusCallbackRecord record;` under `#if IS_64_BIT`, and the old fields, token for token, under `#else`; no code names its members. *LP64-003 task 10, `long` in data layouts (2026-11-16). Task 10 built: commit "Keep long-typed data layouts at their N64 size on 64-bit builds".* `long` is 4 bytes on the N64 and on every 32-bit build, and 8 on 64-bit Linux and macOS, so a `long` field doubles at 64 bits and moves what follows it. *Layouts fixed:* `include/PR/gbi.h` gains `gbi_long` and `gbi_ulong`, defined once before `Hilite`: `long` and `unsigned long` unless `__SIZEOF_LONG__` is defined and above 4, `int` and `unsigned int` there. The test is the size of `long`, not `IS_64_BIT`, because the renderer includes `<PR/gbi.h>` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp:29`, `gfx_pc.h:11`, `gfx_opengl.cpp:20`) before anything defines `IS_64_BIT`, where an `#if IS_64_BIT` would read 0 and give the C++ files the other layout; compilers that do not predefine `__SIZEOF_LONG__` (IDO, MSVC) have a 4-byte `long`, as has 64-bit Windows, so the `long` branch is right for them. `Hilite`'s `force_structure_alignment[4]`, `Gsetcolor`'s `color` and `TexRect`'s `w0` to `w3` use them, so at 32 bits the declarations are the same `long` types as before, and at 64 bits the structures are 16, 8 and 16 bytes instead of 32, 16 and 32. The renderer has no copy of these structures (`gbiex_compat.h` has no `long`) and uses none of them; in the game no code reads the changed members (`Gsetcolor` is a `Gfx` member only on 32-bit big-endian builds, `TexRect` has no user, `guLookAtHilite`'s source is not compiled), so no user of a changed field needed a change. *Arithmetic fixed, because a 64-bit `long` changed a result:* (1) `src/str.c`'s `ULONG_MAX` (`(unsigned long)(~0L)`) is the overflow bound of the game's `strtol`, which accumulates in `unsigned int` and stores `ULONG_MAX / base` and `ULONG_MAX % base` in `unsigned int`. At 64 bits the quotient was cut to 32 bits (base 10: `0x99999999` where 32 bits give `0x19999999`; base 8 and 16: `0xFFFFFFFF`), so overflow went undetected and the accumulator wrapped: `strtol("4294967296")` returned 0 instead of -1. Where `long` is wider than 32 bits it is now `0xFFFFFFFFu`; the 32-bit definition is unchanged. (2) The same function returns `neg ? -accum : accum`, an `unsigned int`, as `long`: at 32 bits the conversion gives back the sign, at 64 bits it does not, so `strtol("-5")` returned 4294967291. It now returns through `(int)`, the same value at 32 bits. On native builds the game's `strtol` is the one every caller links to, port code and the renderer's `gfx_shiny.cpp` included (the browser build renames it `ge_strtol`); the callers that store the result in a 32-bit type saw no difference, and the two that keep a `long` (`video.c`'s `GE_AUTOBTN` mask, used as `u16`, and `gfx_shiny.cpp`'s `glint_skip` id, which rejects anything outside 0 to 31) saw none in practice, but the function's result now matches 32 bits. The prototypes (`str.h:12`, `memp.c:42`, `frametiming.c:145`) keep `long`, the C library's return type. (3) `include/PR/gu.h`'s `FTOFIX32(x)` is `(long)((x) * 65536.0f)`, stored by `guMtxF2L` (`src/libultra/gu/mtxutil.c`, compiled on PC; it builds the projection, look-at, rotation, scale and translation matrices, and strict `bondview2.c` (twice) and `gunfire.c` call it) into an `int`. For values below 32768.0 in magnitude both widths agree. Past it the 32-bit conversion is out of range: x86 gives `INT_MIN` (what the shipped Windows and Linux builds do) and Arm saturates; through a 64-bit `long` the value is exact and the store to `int` keeps its low 32 bits, so 40000.0 became -25536.0. Where `long` is wider than 32 bits `FTOFIX32` now converts to `int`. `gbi.h`'s `G_DEPTOZSrg` uses it too and has no user. *Tests, written first:* `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts `sizeof(Hilite) == 16`, `sizeof(Gsetcolor) == 8` and `sizeof(TexRect) == 16` at every width (the earlier 32-bit-only `Hilite` assertion moved there). Before the fix, `test_abi_probe.sh` failed at 64 bits in the x86_64-hosted i686 container and in the aarch64 container with `static assertion failed: "Highlight layout"`, `"Set-colour command layout"` and `"Textured rectangle layout"`, and the same probe built with `-m32 -msse2 -mfpmath=sse` printed `ABI probe OK (32-bit)`. `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.c` gains `testStrtolOverflowIsMinusOne`, `testStrtolNegativeKeepsSign` and `testFixedPointConversionDoesNotWrap` (40000.0 through a `volatile float` must give `INT_MIN` or `INT_MAX`); `test_lp64_address.sh` compiles `src/str.c` with the game's definitions (`build_str`, `-w`) and links it into the driver, so the test exercises the game's `strtol`; the 32-bit pass shows it, since the C library's would return `LONG_MAX` there for the first case. With `str.c` and `gu.h` at 27ef8ef the harness printed `PASS (32-bit)`, then at 64 bits `FAIL: strtol reports a number past 32 bits as -1`, `FAIL: strtol("-5") is -5` and `FAIL: FTOFIX32 past 32768.0 does not wrap` and exited 1, in the x86_64 and the aarch64 container; with the fix it prints `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` (x86_64) and `PASS (64-bit)` (aarch64), and the probe prints `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` and `ABI probe OK (32-bit)`. *Every `long` read* (a search of `src/` and `include/PR/` for the type outside comments and strings, `long long` aside; line numbers are those at 27ef8ef; "compiled" means compiled by the PC build, from the 64-bit trees' `compile_commands.json`):

| Where | What | Compiled on PC | Kind | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `include/PR/gbi.h` `Hilite` | `long int force_structure_alignment[4]` | yes (every game file, and the renderer) | layout (renderer format) | fixed: `gbi_long` |
| `gbi.h` `Gsetcolor` | `unsigned long color` | yes | layout (command) | fixed: `gbi_ulong` |

| `include/PR/gu.h:38` | `FTOFIX32`'s `(long)` cast | yes (`mtxutil.c`) | arithmetic | result changed past 32768.0; fixed |
| `gbi.h` `G_DEPTOZSrg` | uses `FTOFIX32` | macro with no user | arithmetic | follows `FTOFIX32` |
| `src/str.c:94` | `ULONG_MAX`, `(unsigned long)(~0L)` | yes | arithmetic | overflow bound changed; fixed |
| `src/str.c:95`, `str.h:12`, `memp.c:42`, `frametiming.c:145` | `strtol`'s `long` return | yes | arithmetic | negative results changed; fixed in the `return`, prototypes unchanged |

*LP64-003 task 11, the strict batch, part A (2026-11-16), on the branch `lp64/addr-strict`. Task 11 part A built: commit "Keep the game's Vertex at 16 bytes on 64-bit builds".* The game's `Vertex` (`src/bondtypes.h`) is shaped like the renderer's 16-byte `Vtx`, but the union at +8 held `struct Vertex *LinkedTo` and `void *CollisionRelatedNode`, so at 64 bits it was 24 bytes and every `Vertex` array, file or run time, had the wrong stride (the plan's decision 3; `test_wardrobe.sh`'s 64-bit half failed on it, `ASSERTION FAULT - paNativeFit(...)` at `test_wardrobe.c` line 246). (1) At 64 bits the union holds `u32 LinkOffset` in place of the two pointers: an offset from the model file's base, 0 for none; at 32 bits the struct is unchanged. A new macro beside it, `VERTEX_COLLISION_NODE(base, vertex)`, is the model node a collision vertex links to: at 32 bits `((vertex).CollisionRelatedNode)`, at 64 bits `base + LinkOffset`, or `NULL` for 0, with `base` the collision record's `BaseAddr` (where `modelPromoteNodeOffsetsToPointers` sets the file's base). Its two readers use it: `chrCreateBloodStain` (`src/game/chr.c`, the read and the `!= NULL` test of `CollisionVertices[bestindex]`) and the `GE_COLAUDIT` audit in strict `src/game/model.c` (`portModelCollisionAudit`). The third site of the brief, the DLCOLLISION case of `modelPromoteNodeOffsetsToPointers`, writes the slot rather than reading it: its loop unswaps the generator's half-swapped link word and its `CollisionRelatedIndex`, then `PROMOTE`s the link to a pointer. At 64 bits there is no pointer to make, so that loop is compiled only at 32 bits (unchanged there), with a comment that LP64-004's model converter writes the offset and the models guard stops a 64-bit load until then; what the slot holds after conversion is LP64-004's, as the plan says. No converter changed (`romfile_model.c` swaps the +8 word as two `s16`, which the unchanged `s`/`t` member still overlays). (2) `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts `sizeof(Vertex) == 16` at both widths, written first: at 64 bits it failed (`static assertion failed: "Game vertex stride"`) before the change and passes after; at 32 bits it passed before and after. The `POINTER_SIZED(Vertex, LinkedTo)` assertion is 32-bit only, and at 64 bits the probe asserts `LinkOffset` is 4 bytes at offset 8. (3) `scripts/port/harness_widths.sh`: `HARNESS_PENDING` is empty; `test_wardrobe.sh` passes at 64 bits (`test_wardrobe: PASS (64-bit)` in the aarch64 container, and both halves in the i686 container), so the list has no entry left. *Windows comparison:* `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (HEAD bc80f12) exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`: no 32-bit function changed, so no gallery image can change from this commit. *Task check:* step 1 in the x86_64 and the aarch64 containers (`build/lp64/gate`, `gate-video`, wiped between them): `330 files compiled, 0 failed` and `361 files compiled, 0 failed`, exit 0 in both; step 2 in the i686 container, the Debug headless build exit 0 and the 20-mission smoke 20 of 20 `PASS`; step 3 as above; step 4 in both containers, exit 0, `OK: 51 narrowings in 6 files, all allowed` and `OK: 21 unprototyped calls in 9 files, all allowed` (unchanged; `lp64_casts.py check` unchanged at 27); step 5 in the aarch64 container, `OK: stopped at "animation tables"` for `build/lp64/boot/IronSights` and `build/lp64/boot-san/IronSights`, exit 0. The 43 harness lines of the CI tests step ran in the i686 container: 42 exited 0 (`test_buffers.sh` without `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1`), among them `test_wardrobe.sh` and `test_ads.sh` at 32 and 64 bits and `test_abi_probe.sh`; `hand_gallery.py verify --allow-pending` exited 1, `Gallery is stale for strict rendering inputs; regenerate references`, which is expected on this branch until the owner's laptop regenerates the gallery. *Not run:* the x86_64 boot check, the sanitizer variant of `test_buffers.sh`, the browser build, the video executable at run time, any 64-bit stage load, anything in CI, the gallery.

*LP64-003 task 11 part A, second commit: "Size Model storage by its type and test model words at full width".* (1) *`Model` storage.* `model.c` hands out an entry of `g_ModelSlots` or `g_AnimModelSlots` as a `Model`; at 32 bits the slot's `unk02`, `unk08` and `unk10` are the `Model`'s `rwdatalen`, `obj` (0 while the slot is free) and `datas`. At 64 bits a `Model` is 264 bytes against a 192-byte animated slot and a 32-byte plain one, and `obj` and `datas` move to 0x10 and 0x20. `src/game/objecthandler.h`: at 64 bits each slot is a union of `unk00`/`unk02` (still `rwdatalen` at 2) with a whole `Model model`; at 32 bits both structs are unchanged. New accessors `MODEL_SLOT_OBJ(slot)` and `MODEL_SLOT_RWDATA(slot)` are `((slot).unk08)` and `((slot).unk10)` at 32 bits and the `Model`'s `obj` and `datas` (as the `void *` that `unk10` is) at 64 bits; `modelmgrInstantiateModel`, `modelmgrInstantiateModelWithAnim` (`model.c`) and `modelmgrAllocateModelSlots`, `modelmgrAllocateAnimModelSlots` (`src/game/initunk_005520.c`) use them. Allocations come from types: `model.c`'s `0x20` is `sizeof(struct ModelSlot)` and its `0xc0` is `4 + sizeof(struct AnimModelSlot)` (the same expression `initunk_005520.c` sizes the slot array with), 0x20 and 0xc0 at 32 bits; the read-write data, indexed through `union ModelRwData **` (`modelGetNodeRwData` returns `&data[index]`), is `numRecords * sizeof(*model->datas)` in both functions (the brief named the first; the animated one had the same `* 4`) and the spare slots' `* sizeof(u32)` is `* sizeof(union ModelRwData *)`, 4 bytes an element at 32 bits and 8 at 64. (Correction from the final review: this held only for those four sites. `modelCalculateRwDataIndexes` still counted `sizeof(record) / 4` units, and five more stores gave 4 bytes a slot; the "LP64-003 final review fix wave" note below has them and their fix.) `src/game/bondview.h`: in `struct hand` the run `field_B68`..`field_B84`, which `gunfire.c` views as the gun's `Model`, and the run `modeldatas`..`field_C04`, which it passes as that model's read-write data (32 records at most), are each a union at 64 bits with a `Model field_B68_model` and with `union ModelRwData *modeldatas_slots[32]`; in `struct player` the run from `something_with_watch_object_instance` to `field_2E8` (the pause watch's `Model`) and the run `field_2EC`..`field_3B0` (its read-write data, 50 slots) likewise with `Model watch_model` and `watch_rwdata_slots[50]`. The existing fields come first in each union, so the positional initializers of `struct hand` (`unk_092E50.c`, `initBondDATA.c`) still fill them in order; both compile at 64 bits with no warning. `bondview2.c`'s `sub_GAME_7F07E7CC` used the raw offsets `0x230` (three times), `0x2ec` and `0x220` from `g_CurrentPlayer`; at 64 bits it uses `&g_CurrentPlayer->watch_model`, `watch_rwdata_slots` and `step_in_view_watch_animation`, and at 32 bits the four lines are as they were. The layout probe asserts, at 32 bits, `sizeof(Model) == 0xbc`, `Model`'s `rwdatalen`, `obj` and `datas` at 2, 8 and 0x10, both slot sizes (0x20, 0xbc) and their field offsets, `struct hand` (0x3a8) with `field_B68`, `mtxlist`, `modeldatas`, `field_C04` and `volley` at 0x2f8, 0x304, 0x318, 0x394 and 0x398, and `struct player` (0x2a80) with the offsets 0x220, 0x230, 0x2ec, 0x3b0, 0x3b4 and the three aliases below; these were written first and passed before and after the change. At 64 bits it asserts that each slot holds a `Model` at offset 0 with `unk02` on `rwdatalen`, and that each of the four runs holds a `Model` or its 32 or 50 slots; these failed before the change (`static assertion failed: "model slots hold a Model"`, and no `model`, `field_B68_model`, `modeldatas_slots`, `watch_model` or `watch_rwdata_slots` member) and pass after. The probe's printed report of the two sizes is gone, now that they are asserted. Inside the player's watch run three named fields are `Model` members at 32 bits only (`field_23C` is `render_pos`, `watch_scale_destination` is `scale`, `pause_watch_related_adjust` is `animframe1`), read by name in eleven places; this commit left them, and the third commit below reads them through the `Model` at 64 bits. In `gunfire.c` (part B), `flashvisptr = ((s32 *) (&hand->modeldatas)) + RwDataIndex` steps 4-byte words where `modelGetNodeRwData` steps pointer-sized ones, which differs at 64 bits. (2) *Sentinels.* `PROMOTE` (`model.c`, the PC form) tests `PORT_WORD_HAS_SEGMENT(var, 0x05)` (`port/include/port_hostptr.h`, now included by `model.c`): at 32 bits `((uintptr_t)(var) & 0xFF000000) == (0x05 << 24)`, the old test; at 64 bits the whole word is compared, so a host pointer whose bits 24 to 31 are 0x05 is not rebased. `loadAnimationFrame`'s `anim->address & 0x80000000` was measured first: a scratch export of HEAD (bc80f12) under `build/lp64/`, with a temporary `fprintf` trace on each branch (printing the first three hits and every power of two), was built as the i686 headless reference and ran the 20-mission smoke (20 of 20 `PASS`). The RAM branch never ran; the copy branch ran in every mission (at least 1,024 times in each, 4,096 or more in Cradle and Egypt), with every address between 0x08e96260 and 0x08fffe30, the compiled-in animation data in the Linux executable's image. The scratch copy was deleted. At 64 bits the test is `!PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(anim->address) && (anim->address & 0x80000000)`: a host address always takes the copy branch, as every measured one does at 32 bits, and only a 32-bit word with bit 31 set is taken for RDRAM; the reason is in a comment there. The 32-bit expression is unchanged. The Windows build was not measured; its image is at 0x10000000 and its arenas at 0x20000000, below bit 31. (3) *Prototypes:* `model.c` declares `romCopy` through `<ramrom.h>`, `printf` through `<stdio.h>` (in its PC-only include block; a block-scope declaration made the file's later `printf` calls conflict) and `portPtrLooksBad` in `portModelCollisionAudit`, as the file already declares `portModelAuditWalk`; `bondview2.c` includes `ob.h` (`get_pc_buffer_remaining_value`), and `chrpropDeregisterRoom` (`chrai.h`), `sub_GAME_7F059334` (`matrixmath.h`), `currentPlayerSetMatrix10C4`, `currentPlayerSetMatrix10C8`, `currentPlayerSetViewToWorldMtxf` and `bondviewSetCurrentPlayerPosition` (`bondview.h`) are declared beside their neighbours. `texSelect` is left out: declaring it (through `othermodemicrocode.h`) changed the 32-bit code of `dogfnegx`, which draws the muzzle flash and inlines `sub_GAME_7F073038`'s call (`movups %xmm1,%xmm0; addss %xmm3,%xmm0; subss %xmm1,%xmm3` became `movups %xmm3,%xmm0; subss %xmm1,%xmm3; addss %xmm1,%xmm0`, the same sum with its operands swapped), which is not one of the accepted kinds for a function on the weapon path; its call passes pointers and 32-bit integers only, so the unprototyped call is right at 64 bits as well. `lp64_unprototyped_allowed.txt`: `src/game/bondview2.c` 7 deleted, `src/game/model.c` 4 to 1 with that reason; `unprototyped --check` 21 calls in 9 files before, `OK: 11 unprototyped calls in 8 files, all allowed` after. (4) *`long`:* `model.c:1504` `bitoffset += (unsigned long) width` and `bondview2.c`'s `static long killat` (now line 9670) are arithmetic, as Task 10's table says: the sum goes back to the `u32` `bitoffset`, and `killat` holds `atol`'s value of `GE_KILLBOND`, compared as `(u32) killat`; the same at both widths, so neither is edited. *Windows comparison:* `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (HEAD b6b4c04) exited 1, `.text: bytes differ (3365376 vs 3365376 bytes, 12 bytes differ, first at offset 0x127ae)`. Two functions differ, read from both disassemblies (`i686-w64-mingw32-objdump -d`); neither draws, and `loadAnimationFrame` is on the animation path that poses drawn animated models, the pause watch among them: **`loadAnimationFrame`** (`model.c`), where `romCopy`'s prototype reorders the two stores of its first two arguments to the outgoing stack slots (`mov %edi,(%esp)` and `mov %eax,0x4(%esp)`) around the `and $0xfffffff0,%ebx` that rounds the size, two stores to distinct non-volatile objects with no read of either and no call between them; and **`solo_char_load`** (`bondview2.c`), where `chrpropDeregisterRoom`'s prototype makes the inlined `bondviewDeregisterPlayerRoom` load its two arguments (`movswl 0x2a04(%esi)`, `mov 0xa8(%esi)`) through `%edx` instead of `%eax`, a register choice (both are caller-saved and `%eax` is reloaded after the call). Every other function, `dogfnegx` included once `texSelect` was left out, is identical. These two functions must be named in the laptop hand-off. Both differences change no behaviour (in `loadAnimationFrame`, two argument stores reordered before the `romCopy` call), so no image is expected to change from them. *Task check:* step 1 in the x86_64 and the aarch64 containers (trees wiped between them): `330 files compiled, 0 failed` and `361 files compiled, 0 failed`, exit 0 in both; step 2 in the i686 container, the Debug headless build exit 0 and the 20-mission smoke 20 of 20 `PASS`; step 3 as above; step 4 in both containers, exit 0, `OK: 51 narrowings in 6 files, all allowed` (unchanged) and `OK: 11 unprototyped calls in 8 files, all allowed`; `lp64_casts.py check` `OK: 27 truncating casts in 12 files, all allowed` (unchanged); step 5 in the aarch64 container, `OK: stopped at "animation tables"` for `build/lp64/boot/IronSights` and `build/lp64/boot-san/IronSights`, exit 0. *LP64-003 task 11 part A, third commit, after review: "Read the watch model's fields through its Model at 64 bits and correct the collision vertex record".* (1) `src/game/bondview.h` gains four member names, written after `->`: `WATCH_MODEL_RENDER_POS`, `WATCH_MODEL_SCALE` and `WATCH_MODEL_ANIMFRAME1` are `field_23C`, `watch_scale_destination` and `pause_watch_related_adjust` at 32 bits (so those sites' tokens are unchanged) and `watch_model.render_pos`, `.scale` and `.animframe1` at 64 bits; the eleven reads use them (`bondview2.c`, ten: the pause-tilt timing, the watch's pause-menu fade, its position and scale and `bondviewTransformManyPosToViewMatrix`'s matrices; `options.c`, one debug print). Nothing writes these fields by name. A bounded look at the rest of the two runs (every field from `something_with_watch_object_instance` to `field_2E8` and from `field_B68` to `field_B84`, searched for `->name` and `.name` in `src/` and `port/`) found one more: the hand's `mtxlist` is the gun `Model`'s `render_pos` at 32 bits, written by name at `gunfire.c:1131` (`hand->mtxlist = rwmtx`) and read through the `Model` at `gunfire.c:2333`. `GUN_MODEL_RENDER_POS` (`mtxlist` at 32 bits, `field_B68_model.render_pos` at 64) is defined for it; `gunfire.c` is part B's, so the site is not yet changed. The layout probe asserts at 32 bits, for each of the four, that its offset from the run's first field equals `offsetof(Model, member)` (written first; passing before and after). (2) The DLCOLLISION comment in `modelPromoteNodeOffsetsToPointers` now says what the 64-bit branch does not do: it neither unswaps nor promotes the +0x8 link and does not unswap the +0xc `CollisionRelatedIndex` of a generator-emitted record. The index unswap is not kept on its own, because the loop decides which records are raw from the link word, and LP64-004 converts both together. `raw` is declared only where it is read (`#if !defined(TARGET_N64) && !IS_64_BIT`; the 32-bit tokens are unchanged). *For LP64-004's model converter:* for each collision vertex of a generator-emitted record, in ROM-loaded and compiled-in models alike: unswap the two 16-bit halves of the +0x8 word; write `LinkOffset = word - 0x05000000`, relative to `BaseAddr` (= `fileramaddr`), matching `PROMOTE`'s rebase; unswap `CollisionRelatedIndex` at +0xc. Today `romfile_model.c` writes the slot only as two `s16`, and no code writes the slot at 64 bits. (3) The new prototypes' comments name the defining files (`bondview.c`, `chrprop.c`, `matrixmath.c`). (4) The probe runs `VERTEX_COLLISION_NODE`: no link is `NULL`, and at 64 bits a link of 0x40 is the base plus 0x40 (at 32 bits the stored pointer); against a deliberately wrong form that ignores 0 it printed `ABI probe FAIL: VERTEX_COLLISION_NODE (1 cases)`. *Windows comparison:* `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (HEAD ffa12c3) exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`. *Checks:* step 1 in the x86_64 and the aarch64 containers, `330 files compiled, 0 failed` and `361 files compiled, 0 failed`; step 4 in both, `OK: 51 narrowings in 6 files`, `OK: 11 unprototyped calls in 8 files`, `lp64_casts.py check` 27 in 12 files; step 5 in aarch64, `OK: stopped at "animation tables"` for both executables; step 2 in i686, build exit 0 and 20 of 20 `PASS`; `test_abi_probe.sh`, `test_lp64_address.sh`, `test_wardrobe.sh` and `test_ads.sh` pass at 32 and 64 bits in the x86_64 container and at 64 bits in aarch64. *Not run:* the other CI harness lines for this commit, the x86_64 boot check, the browser build, any 64-bit stage load, CI, the gallery.

*LP64-003 task 11 part B, first commit (2026-11-16), on the branch `lp64/addr-strict`. Task 11 part B built: commit "Carry texture and model addresses whole through the gun and arm code".* Type, accessor, cast and include changes only: no hand or arm vertex, UV, colour, material, triangle order, depth or render setup changed, and nothing new is computed per frame. (1) *Texture addresses in the arm code.* A `G_SETTIMG` word holds the texture's data address, at 64 bits a whole host address (`texLoad` stores whole pointers since Task 7), and the arm and grip code stored and compared it in `u32`: `armSkinImage`'s argument and its cache of the two skin textures, `portArmGripSkin`'s (`port_grip_mesh.c`), the closed cuff's and the boundary edges' `image` (`ArmCuffCap`, `ArmBoundaryEdge`), `armSurfaceOwners`' owner table and `armCopyPart`'s copy of it, the current image in `armFindCuff`, `armSurfaceOwners`, `armCopyPart` and `armWatchBackLayout`, the native skin triangles' `image` (`NativeSkinTriangle`, `port_native_arms.c`) and the image parameter of `PortArmSurface` and `PortArmKeepTriangle` (`port/include/port_arm_mesh.h`) with their four implementations (`paKeepHand`, `paNativeSurface`, `paGripKeep`, `paGripSurface`) and the test driver's `testSurface`. Each is `uintptr_t` now; at 32 bits `uintptr_t` has the size of `u32`, so no 32-bit size or offset changed (the structures above are file-local and change size only at 64 bits). On i686 and MinGW it is `unsigned int`, the type `u32` is, so the type did not change either. On wasm32 (the browser build) it is `unsigned long`: the same size, but a different type, and the `PortArmSurface` and `PortArmKeepTriangle` typedefs and their implementations changed type with it there. The browser build of this branch is checked by CI only; it was not built locally. The four truncating casts `(u32)(uintptr_t)texture->data` (`port_arm_mesh.c` 3, `port_grip_mesh.c` 1) are `(uintptr_t)texture->data`, so both lines leave `lp64_casts_allowed.txt` (`OK: 27 truncating casts in 12 files` before, `OK: 23 truncating casts in 10 files` after). (2) *Command words in the arm code.* A loop that reads a command's second word for several opcodes keeps it in a `uintptr_t` local (`GFX_W1_ADDR`), because for a `G_SETTIMG` the word is an address; its triangle indices and vertex offsets are taken with masks, which do not narrow. `paDecode` keeps the hand's `G_MTX` word, which `portWardrobeRenderNode` copies into the sleeve's own `G_MTX`, in a `uintptr_t` (its `matrix` argument too), so its segment-3 test `(w1 >> 24) != 3` reads the whole word and a host address whose bits 24 to 31 are 3 is refused; the `G_VTX` segment-5 tests of `paDecode` gain the same. `armTriangleIndices`, called only for `G_TRI1` and `G_TRI4`, reads its second word as data (`GFX_W1_DATA`). First words and opcodes are read through `GFX_W0` and `GFX_OP` (`port_arm_mesh.c`, `port_native_arms.c`, `port_grip_mesh.c`, `port_knife_ads.c`, each now including `port_gfxwords.h`). Where a declaration `u32 w0=...,w1=...,op=w0>>24;` became two types, the three declarators keep their order (`u32 w0; uintptr_t w1; u32 op`): the first try put `op` before `w1`, and that moved a store or a register in `paLayout`, `portArmSectionBounds` and `portWardrobeRenderNode` in the Windows build; in their original order the executable is identical. (3) *`gunfire.c`.* `gunUpdateAndFire` writes the gun `Model`'s `render_pos` as `hand->GUN_MODEL_RENDER_POS` (`bondview.h`; `mtxlist` at 32 bits, `field_B68_model.render_pos` at 64), which `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` reads through the `Model`: at 64 bits it assigns `(RenderPosView *) rwmtx` (a `RenderPosView` is a union whose first member is the `Mtxf`, as `front.c` already casts), and at 32 bits the statement expands to the old `hand->mtxlist = rwmtx`. The muzzle flash's visibility word `flashvisptr` is `(s32 *) (hand->modeldatas_slots + RwDataIndex)` at 64 bits, the slot `modelGetNodeRwData` returns (pointer-sized slots, part A), where `((s32 *) (&hand->modeldatas)) + RwDataIndex` stepped 4-byte words; the 32-bit line is unchanged under `#else`. The three ammo-icon places pass `(u32) imageoffset` to `portAmmoIconPtr(u32 icon)`: the `uintptr_t` local holds, at that point, the 32-bit `IconImage` read on the line before, an image-table number, not an address. (4) *Prototypes* (7 places): `gunfire.c` declares `sub_GAME_7F05E978` (`gun.c`) and `save_img_index_to_obj_ani_slot` (`propobj.c`) beside its existing forward declaration of `sub_GAME_7F05EA94`; `ads_hands.c`, `joy_port.c`, `port_graphics.c` and `port_knife_ads.c` include `<str.h>` for `strcmp` and `strncmp` (the repository's `include/string.h` declares neither); `port_native_arms.c` includes `<string.h>` for its two `memcpy` calls. No callee was left out: none of these prototypes changed a 32-bit function. `lp64_unprototyped_allowed.txt` loses the five lines (`OK: 11 unprototyped calls in 8 files` before, `OK: 4 unprototyped calls in 3 files` after: `glad.c` 2 for the second commit, and the blocked `port_build_time.c` and `model.c` lines). (5) *The five strict `words.w0` writers*, reviewed: `model.c:5295` (`_SHIFTL(G_TRI4, 24, 8) | _SHIFTL(2, 0, 4)`), `gunfire.c`'s beam-flash matrix in `sub_GAME_7F061E18` (`_SHIFTL(G_MTX, 24, 8) | ...`, now file line 2069) and the gallery clear in `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` (`(u32)0x4f<<24`, line 2149), `bondview2.c:12886` (`PORT_FILLRECT_Q`, `((u32) G_FILLRECT << 24) | ...`) and `port_native_arms.c`'s `paStockHandList` (`words.w0 &= ~(15u << (j*4))`). `_SHIFTL` (`include/PR/mbi.h`) and the three explicit forms are `unsigned int` expressions, which convert to the 8-byte word by zero extension, and the fifth is an AND, which can only clear bits; none can set the upper half, so none is changed. (6) *Tests, written first:* `scripts/port/test_wardrobe_lp64.c` (new, included by `test_wardrobe.c`; at 32 bits its functions are empty, since a word is the whole address there) checks at 64 bits that a word equal to a skin texture's address only in its low 32 bits is not skin to `armSkinImage` or `portArmGripSkin`, that `paDecode` keeps a segment-3 matrix word and refuses one with bit 32 set, that `paNativeSurface` does not sample a skin triangle whose image matches only in its low word, and that `armFindCuff`'s cap keeps a whole image. Before the change each failed in the aarch64 container, run one at a time with the earlier ones skipped: `ASSERTION FAULT - armSkin && !armAliased`, `aliased == -1`, `cap.count == 6 && cap.image == 1050 + LP64_HIGH_WORD`, `!memcmp(&saved, &mapped, sizeof(mapped))`, and, with only `port_grip_mesh.c` reverted, `gripSkin && !gripAliased`; after it `test_wardrobe: PASS (64-bit)`. *Narrowing table* (35 of the plan's 51 places; the other 16 are `gfx_pc.cpp`'s, in the second commit; lines are the file's before this commit):

| Place | What the value holds | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `port_arm_mesh.c:78` `armSkinImage(w1)` | a `G_SETTIMG` texture address | parameter `uintptr_t`, argument `GFX_W1_ADDR` |
| `port_arm_mesh.c:207` `armListLength` op | opcode | `GFX_OP` |
| `port_arm_mesh.c:269` (2) `portArmSectionBounds` w0, w1 | command word; a second word of any opcode | `GFX_W0`; `uintptr_t` `GFX_W1_ADDR` |

*LP64-003 task 11 part B, second commit (2026-11-16), on the branch `lp64/addr-strict`. Task 11 part B built: commit "Read display-list words at pointer width in the renderer".* (1) *`gfx_pc.cpp`'s 16 narrowing places.* `C0` and `C1` read their fields from `GFX_W0(cmd)` and `GFX_W1_DATA(cmd)`: every `C1` use extracts a masked field of a data word, never an address. `gfx_run_dl` takes its opcode with `GFX_OP(cmd)`. The data-word commands read `GFX_W1_DATA(cmd)`. `gfx_sp_moveword`'s light count is `(uint8_t) ((data - 0x80000000U) / 32)`: the lines above stop the game unless the quotient is between 1 and `MAX_LIGHTS + 1`, so the value cast is a small count, not an address (a 64-bit host address in `data` would fail that range test first). Lines are the file's before this commit:

| Place | What the value holds | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `gfx_pc.cpp:147` `C0` | a field of the command word | `GFX_W0(cmd)` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:148` `C1` | a field of a data word | `GFX_W1_DATA(cmd)` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:6063` `gfx_sp_moveword` `G_MW_NUMLIGHT` | the light count, range-checked just above | `(uint8_t)` on the quotient |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8297` `gfx_run_dl` opcode | opcode | `GFX_OP(cmd)` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8520` `portHudTextOffsetDecode` | a tagged HUD text offset | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8650`, `:8653` `G_SETGEOMETRYMODE`, `G_CLEARGEOMETRYMODE` | geometry mode bits | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8682` `G_SETTIMG_FB_EXT` | a framebuffer index | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8715` `G_SETFILLCOLOR` | a fill colour | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8819` `G_SETFB_EXT` | a framebuffer index | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8830` `G_RDPSETOTHERMODE` | the low other-mode word | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8845` `G_RDPHALF_2` / `G_RDPHALF_CONT` | half of a CPU-built RDP triangle command | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8858` `G_DXLU_GROUP_EXT` | a group number | `GFX_W1_DATA` |
| `gfx_pc.cpp:8869`, `:8887` `G_HITMARKER_EXT`, `G_HUD_VECTOR_EXT` | an RGBA colour | `GFX_W1_DATA` |

(2) *`seg_addr`* returns a host pointer before either segment test at 64 bits (`#if IS_64_BIT`, `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(w1)`: its upper half is non-zero), so an odd host address can no longer be taken for PD's tagged segment form by its `w1 & 1` test. *LP64-003 task 11 part B, review fix (2026-11-16), on the branch `lp64/addr-strict`: commit "Compile the display-list word check only when asked for, and correct the narrowing rule's text".* (1) *The command-word check is opt-in.* `gfx_run_dl`'s test is compiled only under `#if IS_64_BIT && defined(GE_LP64_DL_CHECK)`. Neither `NDEBUG` nor the build type controls it any more. `CMakeLists.txt` defines `GE_LP64_DL_CHECK` inside its `GE_SANITIZE` branch, and nowhere else; there is no new CMake option. A developer can add it by hand with `-DGE_LP64_DL_CHECK` in `CMAKE_C_FLAGS` / `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`. The `GE_SANITIZE` branch also applies to 32-bit sanitizer builds. There the macro changes their compile commands but not their code, because `IS_64_BIT` is 0. The default configurations, 32-bit and 64-bit, never enter that branch, so their compile commands do not change. *Which builds compile the test now:* only `gfx_pc.cpp` holds it, and only `GE_VIDEO` trees compile that file. The headless trees, among them the gate tree and the `boot` and `boot-san` executables of the task check, use `headless_stubs.c`. Measured in aarch64: `nm` finds no `gfx_run_dl` in either boot executable, and both link lines name `headless_stubs`. So after this commit the test is compiled only into a 64-bit `GE_VIDEO=ON` + `GE_SANITIZE=ON` build, or a 64-bit video build given the macro by hand. No 64-bit build can run a stage yet, so the test has not executed anywhere. The default 64-bit video tree (`gate-video`, the configuration a player build would use) lacks it. With that tree's recorded flags, in both containers, the preprocessed `gfx_pc.cpp` contains the message 0 times and the object does not contain it. Adding `-DGE_LP64_DL_CHECK` (x86_64) gives 1 and the object contains it. A 64-bit `GE_VIDEO=ON GE_SANITIZE=ON` configure in aarch64 (`build/lp64/san-video`) records `-DGE_LP64_DL_CHECK` for `gfx_pc.cpp`, and that command compiles the file with the message in the object. The `#if` line replaced the old one in place, so no later line moved. `scripts/port/test_pointer_bits.sh` gains check 2e, written first. It asserts that the default 64-bit video tree's `gfx_pc.cpp` command lacks `-DGE_LP64_DL_CHECK` and that a 64-bit `GE_SANITIZE=ON` video configure has it. Before the CMake change it failed in i686 with `FAIL: 64-bit sanitizer video build lacks GE_LP64_DL_CHECK`; after it, `Pointer-bits configure checks passed`. (2) *Trace:* the `GE_TRACE_DL` dump in `gfx_run_dl` prints `"dl %p: %02x %08" PRIxPTR " %08" PRIxPTR` with `(uintptr_t)` casts, instead of `%08x` with `(unsigned)` ones. At 32 bits the format literal has the same bytes. (3) `AGENTS.md`'s sentence on the two static checks no longer names the deleted `lp64_narrowing_allowed.txt` as the current allowlist. It now says that a missing file allows none, that no narrowing place is allowed, so that file exists only for a deliberately allowed place with its reason, and that the rule lives in `scripts/port/lp64_static_checks.py`. (4) `test_check_against_a_missing_allowlist_fails_naming_each_place` also asserts that the place line (`  a.c:1:`) is printed. (5) Item 1 of the first part B commit and items 3 and 4 of the second commit above were corrected to match. *Windows comparison:* `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (HEAD 31716c2) exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`. *Task check:* step 1, fresh trees in x86_64 and then aarch64: `gate: 330 files compiled, 0 failed`, `gate-video: 361 files compiled, 0 failed`. Step 4 in both containers: `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files, all allowed` (no allowlist file), `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files, all allowed`, and casts `OK: 23 truncating casts in 10 files, all allowed`. Step 5 in aarch64: both boots `OK: stopped at "animation tables"`. In i686: `test_pointer_bits.sh` passes, and so do the 24 tests of `test_lp64_static_checks.py`. *Not run:* step 2 (the 32-bit executable is identical), the CI harness lines, a full sanitizer video link, the browser build, CI itself, gallery regeneration and any 64-bit stage load.

*LP64-003 final review fix wave (2026-11-16), on the branch `lp64/addr-strict`.* A review of the whole milestone (e873bfe..a7f4ca9) found no Critical issue and nine findings, F1 to F9; this wave fixes them in one pass, because after the branch lands a fix to a strict-tier file needs another trip to the owner's laptop. Every code fix in a strict-tier file is 64-bit only or a macro whose 32-bit expansion is the site's old expression, token for token; two non-strict files changed tokens at both widths to a form of the same value (`port_weapon_export.c`: `numRecords * 4` became `MODEL_RWDATA_BYTES(numRecords)`, `<< 2` at 32 bits; `glass2.c`: the literal 12 became typed indexing, as the F4 paragraph says); each commit's `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` exited 0. *First commit: "Count model read-write data in pointer-sized slots and set the gun's render data by member at 64 bits" (F1 to F3, with four more places of the same kinds found while reading).* The reviewer's numbers were measured again first, with a scratch program compiled with the probe's flags at both widths in the x86_64 container (deleted afterwards): `ModelRwData_HeaderRecord` 96 bytes at both widths; `HeadPlaceholderRecord` and `DisplayList_CollisionRecord` 8 at 32 bits and 16 at 64; the other seven records 4; `ModelRenderData` 64 bytes at 32 bits and 80 at 64 (`zbufferenabled` at 8, `flags` at 12, `cullmode` at 72); `struct hand` 0x3a8 and 0x528; the player's `hands[0].throw_item_pos_related` at 0xad8 and 0xcb4, its `m[3]` at 0xb08 and 0xce4, `throw_item_pos_related_prev.m[3]` at 0xb48 and 0xd24; `field_654` to `field_6CC` 124 bytes at both widths; `Model` 0xbc and 0x108; `struct sImageTableEntry` 12 and 16. All as the reviewer measured. (1) New `port/include/port_model_words.h` (included by `src/game/model.h`): `MODEL_RWDATA_UNITS(record)` is `sizeof(record) / 4` at 32 bits and the record's size in `union ModelRwData *` slots, rounded up, at 64 (24, 2, 2 and 1 units at 32 bits; 12, 2, 2 and 1 at 64, never more than at 32, so the hand's 32 slots and the watch's 50 are right as built); `MODEL_RWDATA_BYTES(count)` is `((count) << 2)` and `count * (s32) sizeof(union ModelRwData *)`; `MODEL_NODE_SLOT_BYTES(n)` is `((n) << 2)` and `n * (s32) sizeof(ModelNode *)`; `MODEL_STORAGE_PAD` is `0xfb` and `(s32) sizeof(Model) + 0x3f`; and, at 64 bits only, `portRenderDataFromWords(rd, words)`, which sets a `ModelRenderData` by member from words 1 to 15 of a 32-bit render template. (2) *F1.* `modelCalculateRwDataIndexes` (`model.c`, nine lines) counts `MODEL_RWDATA_UNITS(struct ModelRwData_...)`. The five stores: the watch-menu weapon's `spb8` (`gunfire.c`, `set_enviro_fog_for_items_in_solo_watch_menu`) is `union ModelRwData *spb8[0x80 / 4]` at 64 bits (32 slots, as 0x80 bytes are at 32); `watchRenderController`'s `rwdata` is `union ModelRwData *rwdata[26]` at 64 bits; `bondview2.c`'s single-player weapon buffer steps `MODEL_RWDATA_BYTES(nrec)` past the gun model's read-write data where it stepped `nrec << 2`; the player's gait run `field_654`..`field_6CC` (`src/game/bondview.h`, given by `initBondDATAdefaults.c` to `animInit`; it complains from 31 records) is a union at 64 bits with `union ModelRwData *gait_rwdata_slots[31]`, like the hand's and the watch's runs; `port_weapon_export.c`'s tank allocates `MODEL_RWDATA_BYTES(header->numRecords) + 16`. Found beside the weapon buffer's store: the `Model` placed in the same buffer was given `ALIGN64_V3(cursor + 0xfb)`, `sizeof(Model) + 0x3f` at 32 bits, so at 64 bits the 264-byte `Model` overlapped the read-write data placed 192 bytes after it; it steps `MODEL_STORAGE_PAD`. Both `bondview2.c` edits replace their line in place, as does `bondviewSelectCuff`'s below, so no `assert` line number in that file moves. (3) *F2.* The 16 template words map to the 32-bit members one to one: word 0 `basemtx`, 1 `zbufferenabled`, 2 `flags`, 3 `gdl`, 4 `mtxlist`, 5 to 11 `unk14` to `unk2c`, 12 `PropType`, 13 `envcolour`, 14 `fogcolour`, 15 `cullmode` (the probe asserts the 32-bit size and these offsets). At 64 bits the first-person gun (`D_80035CC4`, after `D_80035CC0`) and the watch-menu weapon (`D_80035D04`, after `D_80035D00`) call `portRenderDataFromWords` in place of the word loop, which gives `basemtx` `NULL`, `zbufferenabled` 1, `flags` 3 and the rest zero, as the 32-bit loop does; the pointer words are 0 in every template and a 32-bit word cannot be a host address at 64 bits, so the helper sets the three pointer members to `NULL`. `watchRenderController`'s copy from `(u8 *) D_80035D04 + 0x3c` reads, at 32 bits, `D_80035D04`'s last word (0x80035D40 on the N64) and then the first 15 words of `watchControllerButtonBases`, which follows it at 0x80035D44; at 64 bits it calls the helper on `watchControllerButtonBases`, the same member values (`NULL`, 1, 3, then zeros). Found the same way: the ejected casing's `render_data` (`sub_GAME_7F068EC4`) was a struct copy from the 16-word `g_DefaultCasingModelRenderData`, which at 64 bits read past the array and set `basemtx` to `0x100000000` and `flags` to 0; at 64 bits it is built by the helper from `&g_DefaultCasingModelRenderData[1]` before the function's own member writes. None of the four functions can be reached without a ROM, so the probe's run-time check of the helper (each of 15 distinct words lands in its member, pointer members `NULL`) and the 32-bit offsets carry the test. (4) *F3.* At 64 bits `THROWMTX`, `THROWPOS(k)` and `THROWPREV(k)` (`gunfire.c`, the casing code) are `&g_CurrentPlayer->hands[handnum].throw_item_pos_related`, its `.m[3][k]` and `throw_item_pos_related_prev.m[3][k]`; the probe asserts at 32 bits that 0xad8, 0xb08 and 0xb48 are exactly those members' offsets in the player, so the raw offsets name them. The extra search: `gunfire.c`, `gun.c`, `bondview2.c` and `model.c` for a cast of `g_CurrentPlayer`, a hand or another struct pointer to a byte pointer with a number or a variable byte offset added, `g_CurrentPlayer + 0x...` and `#define ..._OFFSET 0x...`. Found: `bondview2.c`'s four watch offsets (already behind `IS_64_BIT` since Task 11), the casing render data's source above (not an offset), and two byte-offset walks of a model file header's `Switches` array (4-byte entries at 32 bits, 8 at 64): the watch-menu weapon's loop over entries 18 to 27 (`((u8 *) bodymodel->Switches) + j + 0x48` and `+ 0x5c`), now `bodymodel->Switches[(0x48 + j) / 4]` and `[(0x5c + j) / 4]` at 64 bits, and `bondviewSelectCuff`'s `offset = switchindex << 2` (the cuff on the arm), now `MODEL_NODE_SLOT_BYTES(switchindex)`. The rest of what the search printed are steps through arrays by their element size (`sizeof(Mtxf)` and `0x40` over `Mtxf`), the ALIGN64 cursor arithmetic in the weapon buffer, and image pointers passed to the HUD. (5) *Tests, written first:* `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts each record's slot count at both widths (24 and 12 for the header record, 2 for the head placeholder and the collision record, 1 for the rest), that `MODEL_RWDATA_BYTES(1)` and `MODEL_NODE_SLOT_BYTES(1)` are a pointer, that `MODEL_STORAGE_PAD` is `sizeof(Model) + 0x3f`, that the gait run holds 31 slots (and at 64 bits that `gait_rwdata_slots` starts at `field_654`), the 32-bit `ModelRenderData` layout and the three throw offsets, and runs `portRenderDataFromWords` at 64 bits. Before the change the 64-bit probe stopped on `static assertion failed: "the player's gait read-write run holds 31 slots"`; after it, `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` and `ABI probe OK (32-bit)` (x86_64 container). Against deliberately wrong forms, restored after each: with `MODEL_RWDATA_UNITS` as `sizeof(record) / 4` at 64 bits the probe failed on the header, head-placeholder and collision records; with the helper's `flags` taken from word 1 it printed `ABI probe FAIL: portRenderDataFromWords (1 cases)`; with the second throw offset as 0xb00 the 32-bit build failed on `struct player.hands[0].throw_item_pos_related.m[3] offset`. The hand and arm contracts are untouched: no vertex, UV, colour, material, triangle or depth setup changed, and at 32 bits every changed line is under `#else` or a macro with the old expansion. *Windows comparison:* `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (HEAD a7f4ca9) exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs` (`port_weapon_export.c` is in the Windows build). *Checks for this commit:* the 64-bit gate in the aarch64 container, `330 files compiled, 0 failed` and `361 files compiled, 0 failed`; `narrowing --check` `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files`, `unprototyped --check` `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files` (aarch64); `lp64_casts.py check` `OK: 23 truncating casts in 10 files`; `test_abi_probe.sh` as above. The full task check runs on the wave's final tree (below). *Second commit: "Step the bullet spark's image table by its element and read its colour by name" (F4).* `bullet_spark_render` (`src/game/glass2.c`, not strict tier) found its frame's image as `(struct sImageTableEntry *) (((u8 *) thing->unk0C) + (frame * 12))` in five places (two `width`, two `height`, the `texSelect` argument); the entry is 16 bytes at 64 bits, so every frame past 0 would have read and loaded a misaligned entry of `explosion_smokeimages`, `scattered_explosions` or `flareimage2`. Each is now `&((struct sImageTableEntry *) thing->unk0C)[frame]`. The vertex colour read `((u8 *) thing)[0x28]` to `[0x2b]`, the four `u8` fields after the `f32`s, which follow the `void *unk0C` and so move by four bytes at 64 bits; they are now `thing->unk28`, `unk29`, `unk2A` and `unk2B`. Both forms are the same accesses at 32 bits: `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`. The probe asserts the entry's size, 12 at 32 bits and 16 at 64 (none did before), and at 32 bits `unk28` at 0x28 and `unk2B` at 0x2b; these pass before and after the change (they pin the layout the old literals named, and a static assertion cannot see `glass2.c`'s arithmetic). The plan's "Hand-off items checked" row for the `sImageTableEntry` stride, which said "indexed in C: consistent, owner none", now notes this file. `test_abi_probe.sh` printed `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` and `ABI probe OK (32-bit)` (x86_64 container). *Third commit: "Take the renderer's opcode from the whole command word at 64 bits" (F5).* Since Task 11 part B, `gfx_run_dl` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) read its opcode as `GFX_OP(cmd)`, which casts the first word to 32 bits, so at 64 bits a command word with a non-zero upper half (a writer that sign-extended, the one thing the plan's "readers do not mask" rule exists to expose) decoded as a valid opcode, and the opt-in `GE_LP64_DL_CHECK` fault was the only thing left that could see it. At 64 bits the walker now reads `uint32_t opcode = (uint32_t) (cmd->words.w0 >> 24);`: the shift is of the whole word and the conversion explicit (the narrowing check stays at 0), so such a word gives an opcode above 0xFF. Two per-opcode tables are indexed by it before the `switch`, `roc_dbg_ops[256]` (a command count per opcode) and `ge_hot_op[256]` (whether an opcode leaves renderer state alone); at 64 bits both are indexed by `(uint8_t) opcode`, so such an opcode cannot index past them on its way to the `switch`. No case matches an opcode above 0xFF, so it reaches the walker's `default`, which today prints `gfx: runaway context:` with the menu and display-list pointers and the last 24 display-list jumps to stderr, then calls `sysFatalError("Unknown GBI opcode 0x%02x at %p.\nw0 %08" PRIxPTR "\nw1 %08" PRIxPTR, ...)`, which stops the game with the whole opcode and both whole words in the message: that is how such a word shows itself at 64 bits. The 32-bit lines are unchanged under `#else`; no `assert` or `__LINE__` follows these lines in `gfx_pc.cpp` (the file's last `assert` use is `SUPPORT_CHECK`'s definition at line 66 and its uses before line 8200), so the added lines move no compiled line number, and `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`. Nothing new is computed at 32 bits; at 64 bits the shift replaces the cast and the two table indexes take a byte. `port/include/port_gfxwords.h`'s comment now says what holds: writers must keep the upper half zero (from "a value whose upper half is zero", as two writers are signed but never negative, in place of "from an unsigned 32-bit value"); `GFX_W0` and `GFX_OP` give the N64's 32-bit command word and discard the upper half; the renderer's walker does not use them for the opcode at 64 bits; and `GFX_W1_DATA` also reads `G_VTX`'s segment-relative word in `port_baked_light.c`, of which only the low 24 bits are used. The game-side readers that shift `words.w0` themselves (`image.c`, `port_arm_mesh.c`, `port_knife_ads.c`) are unchanged. No ROM-free test reaches `gfx_run_dl`; the 64-bit gate compiled the file (aarch64, `361 files compiled, 0 failed` for the video tree) and the narrowing check stayed at 0. *Fourth commit: "Fail on a failing -dumpmachine, assert the pending list is empty, and correct two comments" (F7 to F9).* (1) *F7.* `scripts/port/harness_widths.sh` ran `machine=$("$cc" -dumpmachine 2>/dev/null || true)`, which hid a failing compiler; it now fails with `harness_widths: CC -dumpmachine failed:` and the compiler's output, as the `-dM` probe does. A machine that is simply not x86 behaves as before (no 32, no failure). `scripts/port/test_harness_widths.sh` gains two cases: the stand-in compiler's new `FAKE_DUMPMACHINE_FAIL=1` must fail and show its message, and the shipped `HARNESS_PENDING` (read after sourcing the helper, before the test's own list overrides it) must be empty, as the plan's Review Focus 6 expects at the close. Before the fix, and with `HARNESS_PENDING=("test_wardrobe 64")` in a scratch edit of the helper (restored), the test printed `FAIL: a failing -dumpmachine fails and shows the compiler's message: expected a failure mentioning [fake: no machine], got [status=0 ]` and `FAIL: the shipped HARNESS_PENDING is empty: expected [], got [test_wardrobe 64]`; after it, `test_harness_widths: PASS` in the aarch64 and x86_64 containers. (2) *F8.* `port/include/port_hostptr.h` says that `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR`'s argument must be pointer-sized or unsigned, since at 64 bits a signed 32-bit value with bit 31 set sign-extends and reads as a host pointer. Its three callers: `loadAnimationFrame` (`model.c`) passes `ModelAnimation.address`, declared `intptr_t` (pointer-sized, signed); `seg_addr` (`gfx_pc.cpp`) a `uintptr_t`; `port/web/runtime.c` a `const u8 *` (browser build, 32-bit only). None passes a signed 32-bit value, so nothing changed. `address` being signed matters only for how it is filled: a 32-bit file word with bit 31 set must be zero-extended into it, which is the animation converter's (LP64-004; in the hand-over below). (3) *F9.* `lp64_diagnostics.py` keeps `NARROWING_ALLOWLIST`, since `narrowing --check` reads that path and a missing file allows none; its comment now says the file is normally absent. `test_lp64_diagnostics.py` (39 tests) and `test_lp64_static_checks.py` (24) pass. *Windows comparison:* exit 0, `identical in loaded code and data` (the header change is a comment). *Fifth commit: "Assemble LP64-003's hand-over lists and record the final review fix wave" (F6; records only).* The two lists below gather the hand-over items from the task notes, each checked against the code at the wave's last code commit (81c99cd); the plan's status row points at them and leaves Task 12. *Full checks on the final tree* (code as at 81c99cd; this commit changes only `FORK_CHANGES.md` and `native_64bit_plan.md`): `compare_win32.py commits a7f4ca9 HEAD` (HEAD 81c99cd) exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`, so the wave changed no 32-bit function. Step 5 in the aarch64 container and in the x86_64 container (trees `build/lp64/x86-boot` and `x86-boot-san`): `OK: stopped at "animation tables"` for the plain and the sanitizer executable, exit 0 in both. The CI tests step's harness lines in the i686 container (42 lines; the configure, build, gate and static-check lines are the task check's): 41 exited 0, `test_buffers.sh` without `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1` (it hangs under i686 emulation), `test_wardrobe.sh`, `test_ads.sh`, `test_abi_probe.sh`, `test_lp64_address.sh`, `test_harness_widths.sh` and `test_pointer_bits.sh` among them, the harnesses at 32 and 64 bits; `test_lp64_diagnostics.py` ran there separately (39 tests, OK); `hand_gallery.py verify --allow-pending` exited 1, `Gallery is stale for strict rendering inputs; regenerate references`, the expected result on this branch. **LP64-003 hand-over to LP64-004** (assembled in the final review fix wave from the task notes above and checked against the code on `lp64/addr-strict` at the wave's last commit; line numbers are that commit's):

- *The ten guards.* `portLp64RequireConverter(class)` (`port/include/port_lp64.h`) logs `ge: lp64: stopping: asset class "NAME" has no 64-bit converter yet (LP64-004)` and exits with status 5 at 64 bits; at 32 bits it is `((void) 0)`. Class, guarded function and place: text banks, `romdataTextPreprocess` (`port/src/romdata.c:900`); fonts, `portFontBuildSegments` (`port/src/segments.c:348`, before the ROM or compiled-in choice); textures, `texLoad` (`src/game/image.c:2543`, covering every caller); animation tables, `portAnimDataInit` (`port/src/animdata.c:248`, before the ROM or compiled-in choice; the boot stops here today); models, `romfileModelConvert` (`port/src/romfile_model.c:412`) and the compiled-in branch of `load_object_fill_header` (`src/game/objecthandler_2.c:372`); collision tiles, `romfileStanConvert` (`port/src/romfile_stan.c:65`) and `portStanPack` (`src/game/stan.c:605`); setup files, `romfileSetupConvert` (`port/src/romfile_setup.c:502`) and `proplvreset2`'s compiled-in walk (`src/game/prop.c:1980`); backgrounds, `romfileBgConvert` (`port/src/romfile_bg.c:68`) and `load_bg_file`'s compiled-in branch (`src/game/bg.c:1103`); audio banks, `alBnkfNew` (`port/src/audio_stubs.c:238`); music sequences, `musicSeqPlayerInit` (`src/music.c:798`). A class is marked converted in `port/src/port_lp64.c`'s `s_AssetConverted` table (all ten entries 0), in the commit that lands its converter; `python3 scripts/port/lp64_boot.py --rom ROM --expect-stop NAME [--stage NAME] EXECUTABLE...` then checks that the boot stops at the next class.
- *Boot order of the in-place conversions*, measured in Task 4 by marking classes converted in scratch builds: the animation segments' byte-order pass (`portAnimDataInit`, before the game's boot), the text banks, the animation table's relocation (`boss.c:282`), then fonts somewhere after it (not between the text banks and the relocation, as the plan inferred by reading), then the audio banks and the music table, then the title's stage load.
- *File layouts this milestone found*, all read in place and left for the converters: the Op11 record (`ModelRoData_Op11Record`, `src/bondtypes.h`; fields move from 0x40 to 0x80); `ModelFileTextures` (12 bytes in the file, 16 in C; `romfile_model.c` walks 12); `objecthandler_2.c:302,305` (`Switches` and `Textures` placed by `s32` strides over the file, and `RootNode` after `Textures` at the C stride); `bg.c:1124` (`((u32 *) gptr_stan)[1]`, a stan header word, in a trace); `prop.c:1523`'s intro walk (`SetupIntroCamera` is 14 words at 64 bits, the compiled-in intro has 10); the bg env slot (`bg_envdata_entry_local.data`, an `s32` tested `< PORTMAX` at `bg.c:1222`, cannot hold a host pointer); `Acmd` (nine `abi.h` macros truncate buffer addresses); the twelve file-record unions (the seven setup link records in `src/bondtypes.h`: `LinkRecord`, `LockDoorRecord`, `SafeObjectRecord`; `SetupIntroCamera`'s `lang1c` and `lang20`; `pname`; the firing animation tables' `anim` in `src/game/chr.h` and `initialanim` in `src/game/initactorpropstuff.c`); and Task 8's file-layout rows: `Switches[n]->Data` read as `f32 *` (`chraction.c`, two places; `propobj.c`, one), the setup prop walk by `sizepropdef` (`cleanup_objects.c`, `loadobjectmodel.c`), the setup records returned as `ObjectRecord *` (`loadobjectmodel.c`, two) and `expand_ani_table_entries`' in-place relocation of the compiled-in animation table (`initanitable.c`, two).
- *The 19 files this ROM lacks* (the 32-bit smoke's log): the bg files of `sho`, `eld`, `imp`, `ash`, `lue`, `rit`, `ear`, `lee`, `lip`, `wax` and `pam`, and the stans of `ear`, `eld`, `lee`, `lip`, `lue`, `pam`, `rit` and `wax`. At 64 bits their compiled-in copies are not linked; a stage that needs one stops at the bg guard in `load_bg_file`, which runs before its stan is loaded.
- *The pools and what each does when full* (Task 3's table has the detail): the memory banks fall back to `permanent` and then stop the game with `Memory bank exhausted (bank N "name", request N bytes)`; the high arena and its dedicated mappings stop it at 64 bits with `ge: NAME: could not map N bytes above 4 GB` (or `a request of N bytes is too large to round up`); these two are the only ones that name themselves and stop. Frame data stops with `Frame data buffer exhausted` (named, fatal). The graphics buffer is not checked (writers run past its end; only `GE_ROOM_AUDIT` notices). Room blocks from `mema` fail by returning `NULL` and the room is not drawn (a message only with `GE_ROOM_AUDIT`). Model slots return `NULL` to the caller with no message. A texture pool short of space points the texture at the pool's start, which draws as garbage, and prints `ge: TEXOOM` for the first 12. The music heap's `alHeapAlloc` returns `NULL` with no message and `musicSeqPlayerInit` copies into it unchecked.
- *Collision vertices.* For each collision vertex of a generator-emitted DLCOLLISION record, in ROM-loaded and compiled-in models alike, the model converter must unswap the two 16-bit halves of the +0x8 word, write `LinkOffset = word - 0x05000000` (relative to the record's `BaseAddr`, which is `fileramaddr`, matching `PROMOTE`'s rebase), and unswap `CollisionRelatedIndex` at +0xc. Today `romfile_model.c` writes the slot only as two `s16`, and no code writes it at 64 bits (the loop in `modelPromoteNodeOffsetsToPointers` is 32-bit only). `VERTEX_COLLISION_NODE` (`src/bondtypes.h`) treats `LinkOffset` 0 as no link, so a link to a node at file offset 0 cannot be expressed: the converter must bias the encoding or show that no such link exists.
- *Unprototyped allowlist:* `texSelect` stays undeclared in `src/game/model.c` (its prototype changed the 32-bit register use of `dogfnegx`, which draws the muzzle flash; the call passes only pointers and 32-bit integers, so it is right at 64 bits), and `strcmp` stays undeclared in `port/src/port_build_time.c` (`<str.h>` includes `<ultra64.h>`, which breaks `test_build_time.sh`'s `-Werror` build with only `port/include`); `lp64_unprototyped_allowed.txt` carries both, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files`.
- *What no tool sees.* 64-bit C builds pass `-Wno-incompatible-pointer-types` (`CMakeLists.txt`), so a wrong-typed pointer argument, for example a pointer to a 4-byte field passed to `texLoad(uintptr_t *)`, compiles silently. A struct viewed through a cast or a raw offset has no check either: the plan counted 155 such casts in `src/` and `port/src/`, and the final review's F1 to F4 (read-write slots, render templates, throw offsets, image stride) were found by reading, as were this wave's extra four (the casing's render template, two `Switches` byte walks and the weapon buffer's `Model` step).
- *Unexecuted checks.* The display-list word check (`GE_LP64_DL_CHECK`, defined only by `GE_SANITIZE`) has never executed, since no 64-bit build has walked a display list; `seg_addr`'s 64-bit host-pointer test, which runs first for every address word, is unmeasured for cost. Suggested for LP64-005: measure both, and consider enabling the check by default at 64 bits. Since the fix wave the walker itself rejects a command word with a non-zero upper half (`Unknown GBI opcode`), with or without the check.
- *Untested until a guard lifts:* `portTexReplaceRom` (behind the textures guard, reached from `texLoad`); the crouch branch of the stan locus callback at 64 bits (Task 8's ROM-free test covers the ladder and the clear); the alias cases of the arm mesh's owner table (Task 11 part B's tests cover the skin image, matrix word, surface and cuff). The fix wave's render templates, throw matrices, `Switches` walks and read-write stores are in functions no ROM-free test reaches; the probe pins their layouts and runs `portRenderDataFromWords`.
- *`ModelAnimation.address`* is `intptr_t`, pointer-sized and signed, and `loadAnimationFrame` passes it to `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR`: the animation converter must zero-extend a 32-bit file word into it, or a word with bit 31 set reads as a host pointer.
- *`FTOFIX32`* in `guMtxF2L` converts to a 32-bit integer at every width since Task 10; for a value of 32768.0 or more in magnitude the conversion is out of range, which gives `INT_MIN` on x86 and saturates (`INT_MAX` for a positive value) on ARM.
- *`gunfire.c`'s `watchRenderController`* copies its render template from `(u8 *) D_80035D04 + 0x3c` at 32 bits, which reads the last word of `D_80035D04` and 60 bytes of the next global, `watchControllerButtonBases` (inherited, unchanged); at 64 bits it builds the same values by member.
- *For the macOS project:* `port/src/port_lp64.c` stops a 64-bit build that is not Linux with an `#error` (the executable-image range comes from `dl_iterate_phdr`; another platform must supply it); in `portAllocHighRaw` (`port/src/pcsched.c`) the `_WIN32` branch precedes the `IS_64_BIT` one, so a 64-bit Windows build would take the hinted `VirtualAlloc` path.
- *The one deliberate change of 32-bit behaviour in the milestone:* the two `atof` reads, `viSetupCurrentPlayerView` (`src/fr.c`, `GE_GLFARX`) and `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` (`src/game/bgfog.c`, `GE_FARX`), now read `atof`'s `double` result; they run only when those variables are set.
- No longer true, so not listed: a pending harness half (`HARNESS_PENDING` is empty and `test_harness_widths.sh` asserts it); a narrowing allowlist (none is needed).

under qemu-i386). No source, build file or tool changed for it; the scratch copies

afterwards. *Where `main` stood then:* the 64-bit headless executable logs
`ge: lp64: address space OK` and exits with status 5 at `animation tables`;
the ten guards are at the lines the hand-over list gives. *Boot order of the
ten classes*, measured by treating each class as converted in turn in a
scratch copy (a bit mask read by `portLp64AssetConverted`, a stand-in for the

(`musicSeqPlayerInit`), textures (the title's `lvlStageLoad`: `texReset`,
`texLoadFromDisplayList`, `image_bank.c:240`), fonts (the same stage load:
`load_font_tables`, `lv.c:802`), models (the legal screen:
