(`load_bg_file` at `bg.c:1100` and `:1111`, `proplvreset2` at `prop.c:1950`),
by reading `lv.c:835-931`: that part was not run. `GE_STAGE` does not skip
the title, so the model class is needed before any mission. This corrects the
hand-over list, which had fonts before the audio banks. *The stand-ins and
what each showed:* (1) animation headers are 0x14 bytes at
`data + PTR_ANIM_x`, an address 83 sites in six files form from a constant;
the 173 headers are at least 0x30 apart, the last at 0xE7C0 of 0xE7E0, and 102
sit at 4 mod 8. A `ModelAnimation` declared packed and 4-byte aligned at 64

let the boot pass with no change to `model.c`; unpacked, the sanitizer build
stops at a misaligned member access. (2) Text banks: the table kept as native
4-byte offsets and `langGet` adding the bank's address (its N64 branch); the
three relabelled strings fit in the bytes of the strings they replace.
(3) Audio banks: new records for the five kinds that hold pointers, 448
records and 16,448 bytes for the effects bank and 312 and 11,216 for the
instruments, the other five kinds left in the file image. (4) Music: 63
entries widened from 8 to 16 bytes (508 to 1,016). (5) Textures: treated as
converted with no change, `texReset` ran clean, also under the sanitizers.
(6) Fonts: `struct font` built at 3,688 bytes (2,932 at 32 bits) and the font
list widened from 0xC0 to 0x180. With all six, the plain and the sanitizer

treated as converted and no converter, the boot dies in

*LP64-004 task 1, the converter interface, the oracle build and the boot check's run mode (2026-11-16). Task 1 built: commits "Add the converter interface, the oracle build and the boot check's run mode" "Keep the demo header at the cart's size and describe it as it is" and "Make the reservation and frame-count checks able to fail, and reuse the offset map's storage".* No game behaviour changes and no class is converted: the 64-bit executable still stops at `animation tables`. (1) The shared helpers. `port/include/port_romconv.h` declares what every converter uses, and later tasks add their prototypes to it: `portConvBe16` and `portConvBe32` (ROM byte order); `portConvScratch(bytes)`, a grow-only buffer whose bytes are valid until the next call (it stops the game, named, if `malloc` fails, and at 64 bits passes the block to `portLp64CheckRegion`), and `portConvScratchReserve(bytes)`, which `romdataInit` calls once with 262,144 at the ROM load, inside `#if IS_64_BIT || defined(GE_LP64_ORACLE)`, so that no model (largest stock file 43,120 bytes) or setup (103,424) load allocates during play; `struct PortConvMap` with `portConvMapInit`, `portConvMapPut`, `portConvMapGet` and `portConvMapFree`, one slot for each 4 bytes of a file, where an offset never put, at or past the file's end or not a multiple of 4 (an odd one, or 0x0A, included) is a miss and a Put to one writes nothing. Every map uses one grow-only store: the reserve sizes it as well (262,144 bytes of file, 65,536 slots), Init clears only the slots the file needs, and Free gives the store back rather than freeing it, so after the reserve a map for a file of up to that size allocates nothing. Converters run one file at a time, so one map may be live: a second Init while one is returns 0 and logs `ge: lp64: converter map: a second map while one is in use`. At 32 bits Init returns 0 for a file of 0xFFFFFFFD bytes or more, whose slot array's byte size would wrap (the check is compiled only where `SIZE_MAX` is that small). The map is 4-byte grained by design: a converter whose references can point at any byte (strings, byte code) must remap them as an owning block's new offset plus the distance into it, or change the map's grain in that task with its tests. And `portConvRefuse(asset, file, why, ...)`, which logs `ge: lp64: cannot convert CLASS "FILE": WHY`. `port/src/romconv_common.c` (209 lines) implements them. `port/include/port_romlayout.h` starts the file layouts, structs named `Rom...` with `u8`, `u16`, `u32` and `s16` fields and a `_Static_assert` on each size: `RomDemoHeader` (0xE8 bytes, the cart's demo header: the fields of `ramromfilestructure` and its four trailing padding bytes), `RomBriefObjective` (4) and `RomBrief` (48). (2) The CMake rules. `port/src/romconv_*.c` leave the port source list unless `GE_POINTER_BITS` is 64 or `GE_LP64_ORACLE` is on, and get `-Werror=incompatible-pointer-types` (the 64-bit build otherwise passes `-Wno-incompatible-pointer-types`). The new `option(GE_LP64_ORACLE ...)` is a configure error at 64 bits (`GE_LP64_ORACLE=ON is a 32-bit build (GE_POINTER_BITS=32)`) and outside a headless build (`GE_LP64_ORACLE=ON needs a headless build (GE_HEADLESS=ON)`), and defines `GE_LP64_ORACLE`. That build also compiles `port/src/port_lp64_oracle.c` (only it does) and `port/src/port_lp64.c`, whose class names (`portLp64AssetName`) are now compiled at 64 bits or with `GE_LP64_ORACLE`; the rest of that file is 64-bit only, as before. GCC's `-w` silences a `-Werror=` as well (checked: `gcc -w -Werror=incompatible-pointer-types` accepts a mismatched pointer), so the oracle build drops the 32-bit `-w` from the directory's options and gives it as a source option to every source of the executable except the converters. That block is the last in `CMakeLists.txt`, so it also reaches the sources added after `add_executable`: `scripts/port/sentry.cmake` adds the crash adapter `port/crash/reporting_linux.c` there. (The first commit set it before that include, which left the adapter without `-w`; the third moved it.) After the move, the default 32-bit build (plain and headless) and the 64-bit builds (headless and video), each configured in the x86_64 container, produced a `compile_commands.json` byte-identical, paths normalised, to one from a worktree of the second commit (329, 329, 331 and 331 entries). A configure of the default 32-bit build, plain and headless, in the x86_64 container produced a `compile_commands.json` identical to one from a worktree of 41543f9 (329 entries each, paths normalised); the worktree was removed. (3) The oracle. `port/include/port_lp64_oracle.h` declares `portLp64OracleBytes(asset, file, inplace, converted, size)`, which logs `ge: lp64: oracle: CLASS FILE identical (N bytes)` or `... DIFFERS at +0xOFF (in-place XX, converter YY)`, and `portLp64OracleResult(asset, file, identical, detail)` for a comparison that is not of bytes (`identical (DETAIL)` or `DIFFERS (DETAIL)`); both are `((void) 0)` without `GE_LP64_ORACLE`. `port/src/port_lp64_oracle.c` counts each class's files and differences and, through a constructor that registers an `atexit` handler (no hook in shared code), logs one line a class at exit, `ge: lp64: oracle: CLASS: N files, M differ`. It reads `GE_LP64_ORACLE_SWEEP`: set to 1 it asks for the sweeps that later tasks add (converting files no run loads); no class has one yet, so the exit report only says `GE_LP64_ORACLE_SWEEP=1: no class has a sweep yet`. `GE_ROMPROBE=1` is the game's own (`romdataFilesApply`, `port/src/romdata.c`): at boot it loads every served file except the bg files through the normal load path and its preprocessing (`ge: romdata: GE_ROMPROBE: 681 served files loaded and probed` in the run below). `scripts/port/lp64_oracle.py --rom ROM --classes "A,B" EXECUTABLE` boots once with both variables for 600 frames, then runs the 20 missions through `audit_buffers.py`'s own `mission_smoke` and `MISSIONS` (loaded by path, not copied) for 600 frames each, sums the exit lines of the 21 logs, and exits 0 only if every run passed and reported and each named class has N above zero and M zero; a run whose log is missing (a smoke that failed before writing it) is a failure naming it, `STAGE: no log at PATH`; logs go to `--logs` (default `oracle-logs` beside the executable). (4) The boot check. `scripts/port/lp64_boot.py --expect-run [--frames N]` (600 by default; exclusive with `--expect-stop`, and `--frames` is refused with `--expect-stop`) passes a run that exits with status 0, logs the address line, logs `pcsched.c`'s `ge: frame limit reached: frames=N` with N the expected count (a run that quits cleanly before its frames are up fails, `no "ge: frame limit reached: frames=600" line`, as does another count, `ran 120 frames, expected 600`), and logs no asset-class stop, no `ge: fatal signal`, no sanitizer line and no `ge: lp64: pool` or `ge: lp64: cannot convert` line, and prints `OK: ran N frames (EXECUTABLE)`; its timeout is 120 s for each 600 frames begun. `--expect-stop` now also fails on those last two lines and is otherwise unchanged. (5) The demo header. The brief had `ramromreplay.h` define `RAMROM_FILE_HEADER_SIZE 228` for the three `sizeof(struct ramromfilestructure)` in `ramromreplay.c` (`load_ramrom_from_devtool`, `test_if_recording_demos_this_stage_load`, `replay_recorded_ramrom_at_address`), on the plan's reading that the struct is 228 bytes at 32 bits and 232 at 64. The first commit did that, and the Windows comparison exited 1 (`.text`: 3 bytes, `movl $0xe8` became `$0xe4` twice and `addl $0xe8` became `$0xe4` once, in those three functions): MinGW aligns the struct's two `u64` fields to 8, so it is 232 bytes in the Windows build too. The cart's recordings reserve 0xE8 bytes for the header, and playback already steps past it by `RAMROM_HEADER_ROMSIZE` (0xE8, `ramromreplay.c`), not by `sizeof`. So 232 is the cart's size, the N64's, MinGW's and every 64-bit build's, and i686 Linux's 228 is the exception. By the coordinator's ruling the second commit restored `ramromreplay.h` and `.c` to their text at 41543f9 (the task changes neither) and made `RomDemoHeader` describe the cart's 0xE8 bytes. The layout probe asserts `sizeof(RomDemoHeader) == 0xE8`; `sizeof(struct ramromfilestructure)` is 0xE8 at 64 bits and 228 at 32 (the probe runs on Linux); and at both widths the game struct's `offsetof` of `randomizer`, `stagenum`, `savefile`, `savefile.times`, `totaltime_ms`, `mp_weapon_set`, `aim_option` and `mp_flags` equals the matching `RomDemoHeader` offset; and `sizeof(RomBrief) == 48`. Checked: with the 228-byte layout the 0xE8 assertion failed, and a deliberately wrong 64-bit `== 0xE4` failed in the x86_64 container, so the probe compiles that header at both widths. *For the hand-over:* the 32-bit Linux build's demo header struct is 4 bytes shorter than the cart's and the Windows build's; that matters only where its size is used, the three sites above (a copy length on playback and the Indy devtool load, and the recording path's step), and nothing reads those four bytes. (6) The pointer-free formats, confirmed by reading: briefings are 24 half-words (`front.c`'s `struct BriefingData`, `u16 brief[4]` and ten `{u16 textid; u16 enabled_difficulty}`), swapped in place by `romdataFilePreprocess`'s `case CLASS_BRIEF` (`port/src/romdata.c:994`); the fog tables are read by `portFogServeFromRom` (`src/game/bgfog.c:908`) record by record with `sizeof(EnvironmentRecord)` and `sizeof(EnvironmentFoglessRecord)`, structs of `u32`, `s32`, `f32`, `s16`, `u16` and `u8` fields only (`src/game/bgfog.h:144` and `:160`), so the same size at both widths; and none of the 253 struct bodies in `src/aicommands2.h` has a pointer member (their member types are `u8`, `s8`, `s16` and `s32`; the lists are found by ID through the setup class's table). (7) Tests. `scripts/port/test_romconv.sh` builds `scripts/port/test_romconv_common.c` with `romconv_common.c` and `port_lp64.c` at each width through `harness_widths.sh` (the 32-bit half with `-DGE_LP64_ORACLE`, as only the oracle build compiles converters at 32 bits), with `-Werror=incompatible-pointer-types`; every later converter test joins this script. Its thirteen cases: `portConvBe32` and `portConvBe16`, a 64-byte file's map returning what was put (a new offset of 0 included), missing an offset never put and an odd one, missing 0x40 and 0x44 in a 64-byte map with nothing written by putting them, missing 0x0A without touching 0x08, scratch writable at 100 then 200,000 bytes, after the reserve a request of 262,144 returning the block reserved with the 64 bytes written through it intact, maps of 64 and 0x40000 bytes after the reserve using the same storage, a second live map refused by name, a 0xFFFFFFFD-byte map refused at 32 bits, and the refusal line. (The reservation check first compared only addresses, and passed against a reserve stubbed out: both sizes are above glibc's mmap threshold, and the freed block's address came straight back. The bytes written through it tell the two apart.) `scripts/port/test_lp64_oracle.py` (13 tests): the summing on three sample logs (all identical, one file differs, a class with no file), counts added over runs, and the command line against stand-in executables (a clean class over the boot and the 20 missions gives `text banks: 47 files, 0 differ`; `--classes ""`; a difference; a named class never compared; an executable without the oracle; a failed boot; a failed mission; a mission log the smoke never wrote). `test_lp64_boot.py` gains 16 tests (33 in all): `--expect-run` passes a stand-in that logs the address line and the frame limit line and exits 0, and fails one that exits 0 without the frame limit line, one whose line has another count, one that stops at a class, logs a pool line, logs a refusal, exits 5, lacks the address line, logs a fatal signal or a sanitizer line; `--frames`; the two refused option combinations; and `--expect-stop` failing on a pool or refusal line. `test_pointer_bits.sh` gains checks 7 to 7e: the two configure errors; no `romconv_` source, no oracle and no `port_lp64.c` in the default 32-bit build; the converters and not the oracle at 64 bits; the converters, the oracle and `port_lp64.c` in the oracle build; `-Werror=incompatible-pointer-types` on `romconv_common.c` at 64 bits and in the oracle build, `-DGE_LP64_ORACLE` there, no `-w` on it, and `-w` on another source and on the crash adapter. Both new tests are in the CI tests step. *RED, before the code:* `test_romconv.sh` (x86_64) failed with `port_romconv.h: No such file or directory`; `test_pointer_bits.sh` failed at `oracle64: configure should have failed`; the ABI probe failed with `port_romlayout.h: No such file or directory`; `test_lp64_oracle.py` could not load `lp64_oracle.py`; `test_lp64_boot.py` had 10 errors (`--expect-run` unknown) and 2 failures (the `--expect-stop` refusals). *What ran (GREEN):* `test_romconv.sh` printed `test_romconv: PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` in the x86_64 container and `PASS (64-bit)` in the aarch64 one; `test_pointer_bits.sh` passed with checks 7 to 7e (x86_64); `test_abi_probe.sh` printed `ABI probe OK` at 64 and 32 bits (x86_64); `test_lp64_boot.py` (31 tests) and `test_lp64_oracle.py` (12) passed on the host. *LP64-004 task 2, pools that fail quietly say so at 64 bits (2026-11-17). Task 2 built: commits "Name the pools that fail quietly on a 64-bit build" and "Fail a smoke mission whose log names an exhausted pool or a refused conversion".* At 64 bits records and display-list commands grow, so some of the game's pools hold less than at 32 bits, and four of them failed without a word (the pools table of "LP64-003 task 3" above). Each now names itself in the log at 64 bits, two of them stop the game, and the graphics buffer, whose unit is the command, is doubled (the plan's decision 4). Nothing changes at 32 bits. (1) `port/include/port_lp64.h` and `port/src/port_lp64.c` (now 332 lines): `portLp64PoolExhausted(const char *pool, u32 request)` logs `ge: lp64: pool "POOL" exhausted (request N bytes)` and returns, at most eight lines a pool a stage (counted by the pool's name, compared as text; a ninth distinct name would be logged without a limit, and there are four); `portLp64PoolFatal(const char *pool, u32 request)` logs the same line, always, and exits with status 6 (statuses 4 and 5 are the low address and the unconverted class). A third function the brief does not name, `portLp64PoolStageBegin()`, starts the count again: "a pool a stage" needs a stage boundary, and `port_lp64.c` cannot read the game's stage number (the ROM-free tests and `test_buffers.sh`, `test_model_bounds` and `test_romconv.sh` link it without the game), so `portLateLoadStageBegin` (`port/src/port_late_loads.c`, which `boss.c` calls before every `lvlStageLoad`) calls it. The header now includes `<PR/ultratypes.h>` for `u32`, as `port_romconv.h` does. The name comparison is a local loop, not `strcmp`: the game's `include/string.h` does not declare `strcmp`, and the unprototyped check counted the first version's call (1 against an allowance of 0) until it was replaced. At 32 bits all three are macros that expand to `((void) 0)`, and `port_lp64.c` stays out of the 32-bit source list. (2) The five calls, in upstream-owned files, each a single call with no guard of its own (the macro is the 64-bit condition), except in `dyn.c`: the music heap, `alHeapDBAlloc` (`src/libultra/audio/heapalloc.c`, the one `CMakeLists.txt` compiles), in its failure branch, `portLp64PoolFatal("music heap", bytes)`, fatal because `musicSeqPlayerInit` copies into the result unchecked (the file gains `#include "port_lp64.h"`); room memory, `bgLoadRoomModelData` (`src/game/bg.c`), `portLp64PoolExhausted("room memory", allocsize)` where `memaAlloc` returns `NULL` (the one-line `if (data == NULL) goto end;` becomes a braced block with the call before the `goto`) and as the first statement after the PC-only `fail:` label, which every loader's -1 reaches (each -1 is a block too small for the room's data), so the request logged is the block that did not hold the room; the room is still not drawn, as at 32 bits; the texture pool, `texLoad` (`src/game/image.c`), beside `ge: TEXOOM`, `portLp64PoolExhausted("texture pool", iszlib ? 0xA28 : 0x10CC)`, the minimum free space the test wanted, and the texture still points at the pool's start; the graphics buffer, `portDynAuditFrameEnd` (`src/game/dyn.c`), before its `GE_ROOM_AUDIT` early return, inside `#if IS_64_BIT`: when the frame's end is past the active buffer's end (`(u8 *)gdlEnd > g_GfxBuffers[g_GfxActiveBufferIndex + 1]`), `portLp64PoolFatal("graphics buffer", ...)` with the frame's use in bytes, fatal because the commands past the end have overwritten the next allocation. `boss.c` calls `portDynAuditFrameEnd` every frame with the master list from `dynGetMasterDisplayList`, so the buffers are set. `dyn.c` gains `#include "port_lp64.h"` beside `port_dyn.h`. (3) Decision 4: at 64 bits `dynInitMemory` multiplies the stage's graphics buffer size by `(s32) (sizeof(Gfx) / 8)` (2) after the PC doubling, inside `#if IS_64_BIT` with the 32-bit tokens untouched, so it holds as many commands as at 32 bits (at most 520 KB more of a stage bank, the plan's figure). Room memory is not scaled (the decision). *Render performance:* the frame-end check runs every frame of a 64-bit build: one comparison of two pointers already in registers (corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H: it loads the next buffer's start through two globals, `g_GfxActiveBufferIndex` and `g_GfxBuffers`, and compares it with the frame's end, its argument), no driver call. *LP64-004 task 3, animation tables (2026-11-17). Task 3 built: commit "Convert the animation table's headers on a 64-bit build".* The first converter of the milestone, and the first class the 64-bit boot reaches. A file header in the `animation_data` segment is 0x14 bytes (three 4-byte offsets and four small fields) at the offset a `PTR_ANIM_*` constant names, and game code forms a header's address from that constant, so headers cannot move; at 64 bits the run-time `ModelAnimation`'s three address fields are 8 bytes. As the planning stand-in showed, the header is rewritten in place and declared packed. (1) `src/bondtypes.h`: at 64 bits `ModelAnimation` is declared `__attribute__((packed, aligned(4)))`, so `address` is at 0, `unk04` at 8, `bitDescriptors` at 12, `unk0C` at 20, `unk0E` at 22, `bitStream` at 24 and the unread tail from 32; the 32-bit declaration is unchanged (the attribute sits in an `#if IS_64_BIT` around the closing line). (2) `port/include/port_romlayout.h` gains `RomAnimHeader` (0x14 bytes: `entries_offset`, `frames`, `unk06`, `unk07`, `descriptors_offset`, `unk0c`, `frame_bits`, `stream_offset`); `portAnimDataInit`'s byte-order pass, unchanged, leaves it in native order at both widths. (3) `port/src/romconv_anim.c` (new, 306 lines): `portAnimHeadersConvert(table, tablesize, staged, stagedsize, entries, tables, ntables)` first checks every entry of the 0-terminated lists (1 is empty) and refuses, through `portConvRefuse` and with nothing written, an offset whose 0x20 bytes are not all inside the table (or whose file header is not inside the staged image) and two distinct headers less than 0x20 apart; the 0x20 rule holds at both widths, so the 32-bit oracle checks the 64-bit spacing. Then for each distinct header it reads the `RomAnimHeader` at `staged + offset` and writes the `ModelAnimation` members at `table + offset`: `address = entries + entries_offset`, `bitDescriptors = staged + descriptors_offset`, `bitStream = staged + stream_offset`, each offset zero-extended; a header listed twice is written once. Last, every entry becomes its header's address. At 64 bits a header takes 0x20 bytes and so overwrites the 0xC bytes after its file header in the permanent copy; its pointers lead into the static staging image, which keeps the file layout. The checks are a nested loop over the entries (186, so about 17,000 comparisons at boot), which needs no memory and so cannot clash with the scratch buffer. (4) `port/src/animdata.c`: `portAnimStagedData()` and `portAnimStagedEntries()` return the staging arrays through their real declarations (the game's `bondgame.h` externs declare one `u32 *`, which the sanitizer's object-size check trips on); they are compiled at 64 bits and in the oracle build only, so the shipped 32-bit program does not gain two functions. The guard `portLp64RequireConverter(PORT_LP64_ANIMATIONS)` stays as the class's, with its comment saying what now converts. (5) `src/game/initanitable.c` (`alloc_load_expand_ani_table`): at 64 bits the two `expand_ani_table_entries` calls are one `portAnimHeadersConvert` call over both tables (`animation_table_ptrs2`, declared as `struct ModelAnimation *[]`, is passed as `intptr_t *`), and a 0 result stops the game with `sysFatalError("Cannot convert the animation table's headers")`; at 32 bits the two calls are unchanged, followed in the oracle build only by `portAnimHeadersOracle`. The file includes `port_romconv.h` and declares `sysFatalError` inside `#if IS_64_BIT || defined(GE_LP64_ORACLE)`. (6) `port/src/port_lp64.c`: the `animation tables` entry is 1. (7) The oracle, `portAnimHeadersOracle` (`romconv_anim.c`, `GE_LP64_ORACLE` only): after the in-place relocation it copies the staging image, recovers the two tables' offsets from the relocated entries, runs the converter on the copy (the staging image as `staged`), and for each distinct header compares 0x14 bytes through `portLp64OracleBytes`, one file a header. The in-place relocation points `bitDescriptors` and `bitStream` into the permanent copy and the converter into the staging image, so both pointers are compared as offsets from their own image (the other fields, `address` included, byte for byte), and each table entry is compared as an offset from its table (a mismatch is logged as a differing file through `portLp64OracleResult`). *`loadAnimationFrame` (strict `model.c`, not edited):* LP64-003's 64-bit test is `!PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(anim->address) && (anim->address & 0x80000000)` for the RAM branch. The converter writes a host address (the staging entries array plus the zero-extended offset, at most 0xFFFAC), which the startup check places above 4 GB, so it takes the copy branch, whose `romCopy` is a `memcpy` from that address on PC, as every measured 32-bit address does. Writing the bare file offset instead would also take the copy branch (no upper bits, bit 31 clear) and copy from a low address, so the host address is the only value that works, and the reader needs no change. *Where the boot reaches the converter:* `boss.c` calls `langInit` (the text banks guard) before `alloc_load_expand_ani_table`, so the boot check's stop at `text banks` shows only that `portAnimDataInit`'s guard passes; the converter is not reached in a real run until text banks are converted (Task 4). To run it on the stock ROM now, a scratch copy under `build/lp64` (deleted afterwards, never committed) called `alloc_load_expand_ani_table` before `langInit`, with a trace: in the aarch64 container the plain and the sanitizer 64-bit executables converted all 173 distinct headers with no refusal, every entry lay in the permanent copy, every `address` in the entries array and every descriptor and stream pointer in the staging image (the second header, at 0x144, has `address` at +0x2B4C, `ANIM_ENTRY_fire_standing`'s offset), `loadAnimationFrame` of the first and the last frame of each of the 173 animations ran (resetting the frame buffer between calls) with no sanitizer report, and both runs then stopped at `text banks` with status 5. A first version of that trace, which called `loadAnimationFrame` 346 times without resetting the 0x2D0-byte frame buffer, overran it and corrupted the tables; that was the trace's fault, and the sanitizer did not see it because the buffer is an uninitialised common symbol under `-fcommon`, which ASan does not instrument; so are `_animation_entriesSegmentRomStart` and `_animation_dataSegmentRomStart` (`port/src/segments.c`), the staging image `bitDescriptors` and `bitStream` point into, so the sanitizer build does not bound reads of either image. The root-motion reads of `bitDescriptors` and `bitStream` in `model.c` (`modelAnimReadRootMotionValue` and its neighbours) were not exercised by any 64-bit run of this task, since the scratch run called `loadAnimationFrame` only; they are plain member reads through pointers into the staging image. *Tests, written first* (`scripts/port/test_romconv_anim.c`, new, run by `test_romconv.sh` at both widths, its 64-bit half with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`; the 32-bit half links `port_lp64_oracle.c`): on a 0x100-byte image built in the test with headers at 0x1C, 0x60 and 0xA4, two 6-byte descriptors at 0x30 and a stream at 0x40, and the list `{0x1C, 1, 0x60, 0xA4, 0x1C, 0}`: the header at 0x1C has `address == entries + 0x2B4C`, 77 frames, `unk0E == 0x260` and the other fields; its pointers lead to `staged + 0x30` and `staged + 0x40`; `bitDescriptors[1].bitCount == 7` read through the pointer; the entries are the headers' addresses, 1 and the end unchanged and the repeat equal to the first; no byte outside a header's 0x20 changes; the staging image is not written; and a header at 0xF0, and headers at 0x1C and 0x30, are refused with the table and the list unchanged and the line `ge: lp64: cannot convert animation tables "animation_data": ...`. *LP64-004 task 3, review follow-up (2026-11-17): commit "Refuse an animation header whose descriptor or stream lies outside the staged image".* The task review approved the converter and raised four minors; three are fixed here. (1) `portAnimHeadersConvert` (`port/src/romconv_anim.c`, now 329 lines) now bounds the references it builds. In the measuring pass, before anything is written, a header whose `descriptors_offset` or `stream_offset` is at or past `stagedsize` refuses the whole conversion, naming the header and both offsets. Before this, an out-of-range value would have produced a pointer outside the staging image, which `model.c` then reads through; it was safe only because `portAnimDataInit` validates the descriptor range first. `entries_offset` cannot be bounded, because the interface has no entries size; the brief's signature is kept, and the comment in `port/include/port_romconv.h` states the precondition: `entries + entries_offset`, and the frames read from it, lie in the entries image. No code checks this today: `portAnimDataInit` checks only that the `animation_entries` segment is its full 0x169EC0 bytes, and at 32 bits `expand_ani_table_entries` adds the offsets unchecked too. That size is known in `animdata.c` (`ANIM_ENTRIES_SEG_SIZE`) but not at the game's call in `initanitable.c`. (2) `scripts/port/test_romconv_anim.c` adds six cases: one field of each of the headers at 0x60 and 0xA4 is asserted; a two-table case with a header repeated across the tables (and a 1 in the second); a file header outside the staged image (staged size 0xB0, the header at 0xA4 with its own references inside); a descriptor offset at the staged image's end; a stream offset past it. The refusal cases also check that `table` and the list are unchanged. The "nothing written outside a header" case now uses the bytes the converter writes, `offsetof(ModelAnimation, unk14)` (0x20 at 64 bits, 0x14 at 32), so at 32 bits it also checks that bytes 0x14 to 0x1F after a header stay unchanged. Each of the other new assertions failed against a deliberately broken converter (x86_64, reverted after each): without the staged-header check, `a file header past the staged image's end is refused`; with a cursor that stops at the first table's end, the two-table case; with only the first header written, the every-header and two-table cases; with 0xC more bytes zeroed after each 32-bit header, the written-bytes case. *LP64-004 task 4, text banks (2026-11-17). Task 4 built: commit "Keep text bank slots as offsets on a 64-bit build".* The second converter. A text bank is a table of big-endian, bank-relative 4-byte offsets followed by the strings, and at 32 bits `romdataTextPreprocess` rewrites each slot in place as the string's address, which `langGet` returns; a 4-byte slot cannot hold a 64-bit address. (1) `port/src/romconv_text.c` (new, 251 lines): `portTextBankConvert(data, size, base, bank, patches, npatches)` measures the table as the in-place code does (its size is the smallest non-zero offset, which must be a multiple of 4 and at most the bank's size) and returns the slot count, 0 for an empty bank (every byte zero, the cut stages' 32-byte banks) or -1 after `portConvRefuse` with nothing written. Before writing, it checks every relabel that names the bank and a slot of its table, and refuses the bank, naming the slot, when the slot names no string, the string has no terminator inside the bank, the relabel is longer than the string, or the string shares a byte (terminator included) with another slot's string, a suffix as well as an identical offset. These checks apply at both widths, as Task 3's spacing rule does, so that the 32-bit oracle checks the stock relabels against the 64-bit rule; at 32 bits a relabel that broke them would show as a differing bank, and none does. It then reads the table from a copy in `portConvScratch` and writes each slot: 0 stays 0, an offset at or past the bank's size becomes 0 with today's line (`ge: romdata: text BANK: slot N offset 0xX beyond the N-byte bank - zeroed`), and otherwise the slot becomes the offset in native byte order at 64 bits, or `(u32) (base + offset)` at 32, where a relabelled slot then takes the patch's address as today (of two patches of one slot the last wins). At 64 bits each relabel is then copied, with its terminator, over its slot's string. (2) `port/include/port_romconv.h`: `struct PortTextPatch` and the converter's declaration. `port/src/romdata.c` now includes that header at every width, for the type, which `sTextPatches` uses instead of its anonymous struct (same layout). (3) `port/src/romdata.c`: at 64 bits `romdataTextPreprocess` keeps the guard and the compressed-bank line, calls the converter with `base = (uintptr_t) data`, keeps the empty-bank and `text BANK N slots from the ROM (port relabels applied)` lines, and zeroes a bank the converter refused, so that every slot reads as not loaded rather than as a big-endian offset (the refusal line fails `lp64_boot.py` and the smoke). The effects (`sfxctl`) and instruments (`instrumentsctl`) bank files are SGI revision B1 banks, big-endian, whose records hold 4-byte file offsets where libaudio's structs hold pointers; at 32 bits `alBnkfNew` (`port/src/audio_stubs.c`) rewrites each offset in place as an address, which an 8-byte pointer cannot fit. (1) `port/include/port_romlayout.h`: `RomBankFile` (4 bytes), `RomBank` (12), `RomInstrument` (16), `RomSound` (16) and `RomWaveTable` (20), each with a size assertion, and the byte counts of the five kinds that stay in the file (envelope 14, key map 6, book header 8, ADPCM loop 44, raw loop 12). (2) `port/src/romconv_bank.c` (353 lines since the review fixes below; their record checks are in `port/src/romconv_bank_records.c`, 243 lines, sharing `port/src/romconv_bank_walk.h`): `portBankConvertedSize(file, size, tablesize, name)` walks the graph from the header without writing and returns the bytes of new records, one `ALBankFile` and one record per distinct bank, instrument, sound and wave table, each rounded up to 8 (at 64 bits an `ALBankFile` is 8 + 8 per bank, an `ALBank` 16 + 8 per instrument, an `ALInstrument` 16 + 8 per sound, an `ALSound` 32 and an `ALWaveTable` 32 bytes); `portBankConvert(file, size, table, tablesize, out, outsize, name)` measures again, refuses an `outsize` below that or an `out` not 8-byte aligned, clears exactly the measured bytes and writes each record once (true for every accepted file since the review fixes: no two records may share a byte), its `flags` byte 1, its pointers into `out`. Envelopes, key maps, ADPCM books and loops stay in the file image and are turned to native byte order there, once each, as `alBnkfNew` does; a wave's base is `table` plus its offset, and a 16-bit raw wave's samples are swapped in the table once per base. An instrument or bank offset of 0 gives a pointer to the file itself and is not followed, as in `alBnkfNew`. Each record's new offset and kind are kept in the shared offset map (`PortConvMap`, kind in the low three bits). Refusals, through `portConvRefuse` naming the bank (`sfxctl`, `instrumentsctl`) with nothing written: a revision other than `0x4231`, a negative count, a record or array past the file's end, an offset not a multiple of 4, an ADPCM book of negative order or predictor count, one offset reached as two kinds of record, and, since the review fixes, two records that share a byte and an ADPCM or raw wave whose samples pass the wave table. The file's `flags` bytes are not read. (3) `port/src/romconv_bank_oracle.c` (new, 290 lines, all under `GE_LP64_ORACLE`): `portBankGraphsEqual` walks two graphs from the header and compares every scalar field; a pointer to a built record is equal when both lead to records that compare equal or both to their file's start, and B's record must not lie in its file; a pointer to an in-file record is equal when both are at one file offset with the same bytes; a wave's base when both are at one table offset. `portBankOracle` converts a pristine copy of the file and table into new memory, compares the graphs, then the two tables byte for byte. The comparison sits in its own file because `romconv_bank.c` reached the 500-line limit with it. (4) `port/include/port_romconv.h`: the declarations, with `PR/libaudio.h` included. Both converter functions take the wave table's size and the bank's name since the review fixes, unlike the plan's signatures (see that note). (6) `src/music.c`: the two `alBnkfNew` calls are each `#if IS_64_BIT` `portBnkfConvert` / `#elif defined(GE_LP64_ORACLE)` `portBnkfOracle` / `#else` the unchanged call. (8) `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts that offset and that `ALBankAlt_s.instArray` is at `ALBank.instArray`. (9) `port/src/port_lp64.c`: the `audio banks` entry is 1. Only `alBnkfNew`, now 32-bit only, reads the `flags` bytes. `audio_pc.c` reads only the command list. *Tests, written first* (`scripts/port/test_romconv_bank.c`, new, 498 lines then and 295 since its later split, a count corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H, run by `test_romconv.sh` at both widths, its 64-bit half under the address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers): a 0x144-byte bank built in the test (one bank of two instruments, three sounds, two envelopes, two key maps, an ADPCM wave with its book and loop, a raw wave with its loop) and a 0x100-byte table: the measured size counts each distinct record once (264 bytes at 64 bits, 176 at 32); the bytes written are exactly the bytes measured and nothing past them changes; the brief's graph assertions; the bank's, instruments' and sounds' fields; a shared envelope native once; the ADPCM wave with its book and loop native in the file; the raw wave with its loop and both samples swapped, and two raw waves of one base swapped once; the percussion instrument written once; an instrument offset of 0 as the file's start; a buffer one record short and one not 8-byte aligned each refused with nothing written; and eight refusals, each with its reason. *LP64-004 task 5, review fixes (2026-11-17): commit "Refuse audio banks whose records overlap or whose waves pass the table".* The review of c4d4cd6 found two defects in the converter, both fixed in the measuring pass. (1) The write pass turns envelopes, books and loops to native order in the file as it first reaches them, and later reads built records from the same file bytes; the map refused only one offset reached as two kinds, not two records whose bytes overlap. An envelope inside an instrument not yet reached changed that instrument's sound count before the write pass measured it again, so the walk outgrew the measured buffer: the reviewer's file (sound A's envelope at instrument B + 4, B's bend range 0x0200 and sound count 1, which the swap turns into 2) gave `heap-buffer-overflow ... WRITE of size 8 ... in bankWriteSound ... 8 bytes after 160-byte region` under the address sanitizer, and other such files refused only after writing. Now every reached record claims the 4-byte slots of its file bytes, an instrument's and a bank's offset arrays and the header's bank list included (`portBankClaim`, `port/src/romconv_bank_records.c`), and a record whose bytes another record already holds is refused, naming both (`the instrument at 0x30 overlaps the envelope at 0x34`); the same record reached again at one offset as one kind is accepted, as before (shared envelopes, wave tables, key maps, the percussion instrument). As a backstop, `bankReach` refuses in the write pass a record that would take OUT past the measured bytes. (2) A raw wave's samples were swapped at `table + base` for `len >> 1` samples with no bound. Both functions now take the wave table's size and the bank's name: `portBankConvertedSize(file, size, tablesize, name)` and `portBankConvert(file, size, table, tablesize, out, outsize, name)`. These signatures differ from the plan's (and the brief's), because its own constraints, that no input makes a converter write outside its buffers and that a refusal names the file, cannot be met without the table's size and the name (controller's ruling). An ADPCM or raw wave whose base + len (summed in 64 bits) passes the table is refused when measuring; every refusal names the bank instead of "ctl image". `portBnkfConvert` takes the table's segment name and looks its size up with `romdataSeg`, as the oracle already did, and stops the game if the table it was given is not that segment; `music.c` passes `"sfxtbl"` and `"instrumentstbl"`. (3) The raw-base rule, each base swapped once as in `alBnkfNew`, no longer scans the offset map's slots (which also read the map's fields directly): one bit per byte of the table marks a base reached by a raw wave, in the converters' scratch buffer with the owner slots (`portBankChecksInit`); for the effects bank (a 23,488-byte file, a 797,360-byte table) that is 5,873 slots of 5 bytes and 99,671 bytes of bits, 129,036 bytes, under the 262,144 that `romdataInit` reserves, so it does not allocate. (4) Files: `romconv_bank.c` keeps the walk and the public functions (353 lines); the record checks and the in-file byte order are in `port/src/romconv_bank_records.c` (new, 243 lines) through the internal header `port/src/romconv_bank_walk.h` (new, 95 lines). The tests' fixture is `scripts/port/test_romconv_bank_fixture.c` and `.h` (new, 188 and 81 lines), shared by `test_romconv_bank.c` (295 lines) and the new `scripts/port/test_romconv_bank_checks.c` (145 lines), both run by `test_romconv.sh` at both widths, under the sanitizers at 64 bits. *New tests:* the reviewer's overlap file is refused when measuring, with nothing written; records shared by offset are accepted; a raw wave running past the table, a raw wave whose base + len wraps 32 bits and an ADPCM wave past the table are refused, each naming its wave table and the table's size; a raw wave ending exactly at the table's end is converted. RED, against c4d4cd6's converter through a scratch adapter of the new signatures (x86_64 container, deleted): at 64 bits the overlap case gave the reviewer's report exactly (`heap-buffer-overflow`, `WRITE of size 8`, `bankWriteSound`, `8 bytes after 160-byte region`), and at 32 bits glibc aborted (`malloc(): corrupted top size`); with the overlap case left out, the three table cases failed at 32 bits, and at 64 bits the first failed and the wrapping one stopped with an address-sanitizer SEGV in `bankWriteWave`. A scratch mutant whose raw-base bit is never set fails "two raw waves of one base swap it once". GREEN: `test_romconv: PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` (x86_64), `PASS (64-bit)` (aarch64), `ABI probe OK` at both widths. *Stock ROM:* no stock record overlaps another and every stock wave lies in its table: the oracle (i686, `--classes "animation tables,text banks,audio banks"`) exit 0, `animation tables: 3633 files, 0 differ`, `text banks: 255 files, 0 differ`, `audio banks: 42 files, 0 differ`, with no `cannot convert` line in any log; the 64-bit boot (aarch64, plain and sanitized) `OK: stopped at "music sequences"` for both, still logging `sfxctl: 16448` and `instrumentsctl: 10520` bytes of records. *Checks:* task check step 1 in the aarch64 and the x86_64 containers, exit 0 in both, `336 files compiled, 0 failed` and `367 files compiled, 0 failed` (one more file each), `OK: 0 narrowings`, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls`; `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (HEAD c4d4cd6) exit 0, `identical in loaded code and data`; `lp64_casts.py check` `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`; `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts all` `SUMMARY all findings=0`. *Not run in this round:* the i686 20-mission smoke (the 32-bit game does not compile these files), the x86_64 boot check, the other CI harness lines, and the browser build. *Left to the final review:* the oracle comparing which records are shared as well as their values, and fixture cases for a shared book and loop, a bank-list offset of 0 and more than one bank.

*LP64-004 task 6, music sequences (2026-11-17). Task 6 built: commit "Build the music sequence table at its run-time size on a 64-bit build".* The fourth converter. The sequence bank (the `musicsampletbl` segment, `music.sbk`, 126,667 bytes in the stock ROM) starts with a big-endian header of a 16-bit count and a 16-bit word nothing reads, then one 8-byte entry a sequence: a 4-byte offset from the file's start and two 16-bit lengths. At 32 bits `musicSeqPlayerInit` copies the header and entries into the music heap, swaps them in place, and `musicSeqFileNew` adds the segment's address to each offset in `RareALSeqData.address`; at 64 bits that pointer slot makes an entry 16 bytes and the header 8, so the in-place copy cannot hold it. (1) `port/include/port_romlayout.h`: `RomSeqTable` (4 bytes: `count`, `unk`) and `RomSeqEntry` (8 bytes: `offset`, `uncompressed_len`, `len`), each with a size assertion. (2) `port/src/romconv_seq.c` (new, 119 lines): `portSeqTableSize(file)` is `offsetof(RareALSeqBankFile, seqArray) + count * sizeof(RareALSeqData)`, read from the count alone; the count is 16-bit, so the size is at most 1,048,568 bytes at 64 bits and never wraps. `portSeqTableConvert(file, filesize, out, outsize)` first refuses, through `portConvRefuse` naming `musicsampletbl` and writing nothing, a file shorter than its header, a file shorter than the header and its `count` entries (computed in 32 bits from the 16-bit count, at most 524,284, so no count wraps), and an `outsize` below `portSeqTableSize`; then it clears the table's bytes and writes `seqCount`, `unk` as the file stores it (as the 32-bit copy leaves it; nothing reads it), and for each entry the offset zero-extended into `address` and the two lengths in native order. `musicSeqFileNew` then rebases the table unchanged. Neither function bounds an entry's offset or lengths: the brief's own test converts an offset of 0x80000010 from a 28-byte file. *LP64-004 task 8, textures and the display-list expander (2026-11-17). Task 8 built: commit "Expand ROM display lists to host commands and count them by size".* The fifth class marked converted: the 64-bit boot now passes the title's texture loads and stops at `fonts`. The textures class needed no file converter (a texture's pool record is built field by field from the inflater, by its C type) but two places that move display lists by the 8-byte ROM stride, and the expander that Tasks 9 to 15 will call. (1) `port/src/romconv_gfx.c` (new, 158 lines) with its section in `port/include/port_romconv.h` (which now includes `<PR/gbi.h>` for `Gfx`): `portGfxFromRom(dst, src, commands)` turns each 8-byte big-endian command into one `Gfx`, both words read into `u32` locals and stored zero-extended, first command to last; `portGfxFromRomBackward` does the same last to first; `portGfxFromWords(dst, words, commands)` does it for commands already in native 4-byte words. Each reads exactly 8 bytes a command and writes exactly `commands * sizeof(Gfx)` bytes at `dst`; `commands` 0 reads and writes nothing (either pointer may be `NULL`). They take no size for `dst`: the header says the caller guarantees `commands * sizeof(Gfx)` bytes there, twice the source at 64 bits. The header states the overlaps each accepts, with G = `sizeof(Gfx) - 8` (0 at 32 bits, 8 at 64): the forward two take `dst` at or before `src - G * (commands - 1)` (at 32 bits `dst == src`, in place), the backward one `dst` at or after `src - G` (so `dst == src`, or `dst` later in the same buffer). *Departure:* the brief's interface text had the backward function serve a destination "starting at or before" the source and its test run it on "a buffer holding 3 commands at its end and room for 3 `Gfx` from its start"; at 64 bits that layout is the forward function's (written last to first, command 2 lands on command 1 before it is read), so the fixture runs that layout through `portGfxFromRom`, and the backward function gets the layout `texCopyGdls` has. (2) `src/game/tex.c`: `texLoadFromGdl` counts `srcsize / (s32) sizeof(Gfx)` commands at 64 bits, inside `#if IS_64_BIT`, with `count = srcsize >> 3;` kept at 32 bits. *Departure:* the brief's `srcsize / sizeof(Gfx)` is not the same 32-bit instruction: `srcsize` is `s32`, so dividing by a `size_t` divides unsigned, and `i686-w64-mingw32-gcc -O2` emits `shrl $3` for it where `>> 3` is `sarl $3` (and `/ (s32) 8` is `sarl` after a rounding `cmovns`), checked on a three-line file in the x86_64 container. `texCopyGdls(arg0, arg1, bytes)` copies `arg0` to `arg1` (its N64 body writes `arg1`), last command first because the room loaders put `arg1` later in the same block; at 64 bits it is `portGfxFromRomBackward(arg1, arg0, bytes >> 3)`, its 32-bit body kept. *Departure:* the brief named the forward function, which corrupts that overlap. The function's comment gains its callers: the two room loaders, and `sub_GAME_7F0762E0` (`objecthandler_2.c:162`), whose PC branch returns before that call. `tex.c` includes `port_romconv.h` under `#if IS_64_BIT || defined(GE_LP64_ORACLE)`. (3) `port/src/port_lp64.c`: `textures` is 1. *Where each destination's room comes from, at 64 bits:* `portConvertModelGdl` (`objecthandler_2.c`, the PC model path, reached from Task 11) gives `texLoadFromGdl` `n * sizeof(Gfx)` bytes of host commands and a destination of `(n * 4 + 96) * sizeof(Gfx)` from `portAllocHigh`, in `Gfx`, so it scales; the N64 model path (`objecthandler_2.c:162`, `:185`) is dead on PC. The two room loaders (`bgLoadRoomPrimaryGdl`, `bgLoadRoomSecondaryGdl`, `bg.c`) are not ready for 64 bits and are not changed here: their block is one `memaAlloc` ("room memory", not scaled, the plan's decision 4) of the room's cached size, or the longest free block on a first load; after `bgDecompress` writes E bytes of commands at the block's start, `scratch = dst + (allocsize - E)` places `texCopyGdls`'s destination E bytes from the block's end, where 2E bytes are written at 64 bits, E past the end, and `texLoadFromGdl` is then given E as the size, half the commands. Task 12's interface already owns those lines (`portGfxFromRomBackward` where `texCopyGdls` is called, 2E bytes of the block, `room memory` reported when they are not there, host bytes to `texLoadFromGdl`), and no 64-bit run reaches them before `backgrounds` is converted (`load_bg_file` stops first). The largest stage's lists total 114,992 bytes at 32 bits (Silo, the planning scan), so as much again at 64. *Step 3, `texLoad` read at 64 bits* (`image.c` `texLoad`, `texInflateZlib`, `texInflateNonZlib`, `texInitPool`, `texFindInPool`, `texFreeBytesInBuffer`): `struct tex` is 16 bytes, 4-aligned, at 32 bits and 24 bytes, 8-aligned, at 64 (`data` moves from 4 to 8; measured with a copy of the declaration, gcc in the x86_64 container); every reader names its fields, and `sub_GAME_7F0CCB38`'s raw word read is behind LP64-003's `IS_64_BIT` branch. The pool steps by the type: `rightpos--`, `cur++` in `texFindInPool`, `end = (struct tex *) (start + len)`, `texFreeBytesInBuffer` a difference of two addresses (no address held in 32 bits; the result is a size). `leftpos` advances by 8 for the texture number and by `bytesout`, which both inflaters round to 8. The slot is `uintptr_t *` (LP64-003), the number is `*updateword & 0xffff`, the ROM offsets are 24-bit fields, `romCopy`'s source is `(uintptr_t) &_imagesSegmentRomStart` plus the offset masked with an unsigned constant, `tex->data = pool->leftpos` and `*updateword = osVirtualToPhysical(tex->data)` are pointer-sized. The inflaters write the record's fields by name and the pixels through `u8 *`; their bit reader holds `u8 *`; `decompressdata`'s Huffman tables are a static `struct huft` array on PC (`decompress.c`), so they scale with the 16-byte `struct huft`. No literal record size. The two thresholds (`0x10CC` non-zlib, `0xA28` zlib) are a free-space test made before the 8-byte number and the record are taken. A texture that fills TMEM leaves 8 bytes less at 64 bits: a 2,048-byte CI8 image and its 512-byte palette need 2,584 of 2,600 bytes at 32 bits and 2,592 at 64; a 4,096-byte image needs 4,120 of 4,300 and 4,128. Neither threshold bounds the inflaters at either width (they accept 4,096 texels an image for zlib and 8,192 for non-zlib, more than one level, and never test the right side), so the margin is the same heuristic, 8 bytes narrower; not changed. Pool lengths are multiples of 8 (`0x12C00`, `0x19000`, `0x400000`, the stage pool's KB count times 2,048); the title's stage pool records are 8-aligned (the sanitizer boot through those loads reports no misaligned access); the weapon pools (`gun.c`, Task 11; `bondview2.c`, strict tier) are not reached before `models`. *Other readers of `struct tex`, the pool or a texture's list* (`src/game/`, `port/src/`): `tex.c`'s list builders read fields by name and write `tex->data` through `gDPSetTextureImage` (pointer-sized at 64 bits since LP64-003); `texLoadFromGdl` reads opcodes as `(u8) (w0 >> 24)` and numbers by mask; `texWriteTextureCmd` copies `w1` whole; `texSelect` (`othermodemicrocode.c`) reads the number 8 bytes before `PHYS_TO_K0(tconfig->index)` (`uintptr_t`); `texLoadFromDisplayList` walks the compiled-in lists (host `Gfx` at either width; `globalbank_rdram_offset` is 0 on PC); `port_textures.c` (`portTexReplaceRom`, `portTexContextSet`, the crosshair) and the strict-tier `port_arm_mesh.c` and `port_grip_mesh.c` hold `tex->data` as `u8 *` or `uintptr_t`. One reader is wrong at 64 bits and is left: the `GE_DUMP_BOND` traces in `sky.c` (`waterrec`) and `model.c` (strict tier, `shadowrec-*`) dump a record as two `Gfx`, 32 bytes of a 24-byte record, so for the pool's last record 8 bytes past its end; both run only with that variable set. *Tests:* `scripts/port/test_romconv_gfx.c` (new, run by `test_romconv.sh` at both widths, sanitized at 64): the plan's two commands (opcode and `w0`; `w1` and the second `w0`), pointer-sized words, `0xFFFFFFFF` zero-extended in `w0` and in `w1`, nothing written past the commands, `commands` 0 with a `NULL` source, the backward call on separate buffers equal to the forward one and writing nothing after, forward at its tightest overlap (`dst` G * 2 bytes before the source) and with the source at the end of room for three `Gfx`, backward at its tightest (`dst` G bytes before), in place and into a buffer's end (`dst` 8 bytes after the source), each against the forward call on separate buffers with a `Gfx` of fill before and after; native words; and at 32 bits the oracle on an overlapping copy, identical and with one word changed. `scripts/port/test_lp64_textures.c` (via `test_lp64_address.sh`, both widths): with a `t00042.bmp` in the test's root, `portTexReplaceRom` rewrites the bytes its 4x4 RGBA16 record addresses and the record keeps the whole address of those bytes (a static pool, above 4 GB at 64 bits); a texture without a file returns 0 with its record and bytes unchanged. *Departure:* the brief says the function "stores the replacement's whole address in the `struct tex`"; it writes the replacement into the pool bytes and never writes the record, so the test asserts that. RED (aarch64), with the header's prototypes and an empty `romconv_gfx.c`: `test_romconv.sh` failed, `undefined reference to 'portGfxFromRom'` (and `portGfxFromRomBackward`). Each new case was then seen failing against a broken copy: words stored through `(s32)` (four cases), the backward function walking first to last (three overlap cases), the forward one walking last to first (both forward overlap cases), the forward loop one command long (AddressSanitizer, `global-buffer-overflow` in `portConvBe32`); `portTexReplaceRom` without its final copy, with `tex->data` written back cut to 32 bits, and changing `width` before its miss test (each case failing its assertion). GREEN: `PASS (64-bit)` (aarch64) and `PASS (32-bit)`, `PASS (64-bit)` (x86_64) for both harnesses. *Oracle:* `textures` is checked, on the expander only: in the oracle build `texCopyGdls` calls `portGfxCopyOracleBefore` (which converts a copy with `portGfxFromRomBackward`: the span both buffers cover at the same offsets when they overlap, else the source alone) and `portGfxCopyOracleAfter` (which compares the 32-bit copy's bytes, as file `room list N`) around its unchanged body, so every room list a run loads compares the converter with the shipped copy on ROM data. Task check step 5 (i686), with `textures` added to `--classes`, exit 0: `textures: 2509 files, 0 differ` (the 20 missions' room lists, the largest 4,896 bytes; the boot run loads none; an earlier run of the same check, before a cast-only edit to the oracle's pointer comparisons, counted 2,506, the missions' room loads varying from run to run), with `animation tables: 3633 files, 0 differ`, `text banks: 255 files, 0 differ`, `audio banks: 42 files, 0 differ` and `music sequences: 21 files, 0 differ`. That is the 32-bit result only: at 32 bits a `Gfx` is 8 bytes, so the oracle cannot see the 64-bit stride or overlap, which the fixtures cover. The texture pool records have no converter to compare. *Windows comparison and performance:* `compare_win32.py commits 521ec80 WORKTREE` exited 0, `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`; `texLoad`'s per-texture path is not changed, and no shipped build's code changed, so no benchmark is owed. *Load before play:* each conversion runs where the 32-bit one runs: `texCopyGdls`'s expansion at the room's load, `texLoadFromGdl` at the room's or the model's load; nothing moves to first use. *Task check:* step 1 in the aarch64 and the x86_64 container, exit 0: `338 files compiled, 0 failed`, `369 files compiled, 0 failed`, `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files, all allowed`, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files, all allowed`; step 2 in the i686 container, the Debug headless build exit 0 and the 20-mission smoke exit 0 with 20 of 20 `PASS`; step 3 as above; step 4, `OK: stopped at "fonts"` for the plain and the sanitizer executable (aarch64) and for the plain one (x86_64); step 5 as above. The CI tests step's 46 harness lines (all but its gate configure, build and static-check lines, which step 1 ran) in the x86_64 container, `test_buffers.sh` there without `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE`: 46 of 46 exit 0, `lp64_casts.py check` `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed` (unchanged), `hand_gallery.py verify --allow-pending` pending (deferred inputs); in the aarch64 container `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 test_buffers.sh` exit 0. `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts all`: `SUMMARY all findings=0`. *Not run:* steps 6 and 7 (from Tasks 11 and 16); the late-load audit (no 64-bit build can run it yet); the browser build (CI after the push); any 64-bit run of `texCopyGdls` or `texLoadFromGdl` on game data (the boot reaches neither before `fonts`).

*LP64-004, record pools sized by their records (2026-11-17): commit "Size record pools by their records on a 64-bit build".* A fix the plan lists no task for: it is not an asset class, marks nothing converted and leaves the 64-bit boot's stop where it was. (1) The fault. `src/game/objecthandler.c` gave the PC build's `ModelHitEntry` pool a real array, `char g_ModelHitEntries[600 * 0x14]`, the record size written as the 32-bit literal. `ModelHitEntry` (`src/bondtypes.h`: model, root node, sort value, next, prev) is 0x14 bytes at 32 bits and 40 at 64, and `initModelHitEntryFreeList` (`src/game/initunk_005450.c`) threads all 600 records, so at 64 bits it wrote 24,000 bytes into a 12,000-byte array and overwrote whatever the linker placed after it. AddressSanitizer did not see it because the build's uninitialised globals are `-fcommon` common symbols, which ASan gives no redzones. The x86_64 sanitizer boot with the Task 9 font converter in the working tree showed it: the overrun landed on `player_num`, and the first `lvlTick` stopped with UBSan's `joy.c:643: shift exponent 56 is too large for 32-bit type 'int'` in `cheatButtonSampleInput` via `joyGetButtons`; the aarch64 sanitizer boot passed with the overrun in place. The array is now `char g_ModelHitEntries[600 * sizeof(ModelHitEntry)]`: the same 12,000 bytes at 32 bits (the Windows program is identical in loaded code and data to ae0393d), 24,000 at 64. With the array that large the init is right at 64 bits: entry 599's `prev` is `&entries[598]` (the PC branch already replaced the N64 `g_ModelHitEntriesPenultimate` label, which exists only in the `TARGET_N64` stand-ins, as nothing on PC reads through it), and entry 0's `prev` and entry 599's `next` stay NULL from bss. `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` pins the record at 0x14 bytes at 32 bits and 40 at 64; the array's size is the count times that `sizeof` by its definition, and its definition is the only place the size appears (users see `extern char g_ModelHitEntries[]`). (2) The sweep. `src/` and `port/src/` were searched for byte or word arrays that stand in for bss labels or pools and are used as records. No other plain instance: the objecthandler N64 stand-ins (`g_ModelHitEntriesPenultimate`, `dword_CODE_bss_80076AE0`) are `TARGET_N64` only; `g_DefaultCasingModelRenderData` (`gun.c`), `D_80035CC4` and `D_80035D04` already go through `portRenderDataFromWords` at 64 bits (LP64-003); `ramrom_data_target[0x380]` (`lv.c`, a `ramromfilestructure` with no pointer), `watchControllerButtonBases`, `D_80034CA4` and `D_80034E0C` (no pointer), `g_gfxDramStack` and `g_gfxYieldBuf` (u64) do not grow; `animations_frame_buffer[0x2D0]` holds animation frame bytes copied from ROM; `dword_CODE_bss_80069458[0xC0]` is passed to `initAnimationsBuffer` as its unused argument and never read; the stacks, decompression and image scratch buffers hold bytes; and the `segments.c` ROM staging arrays belong to their asset classes' converters in the plan. No candidate is left open.

*LP64-004 task 9, fonts (2026-11-17). Task 9 built: commit "Build the font tables at their run-time layout on a 64-bit build".* The sixth class marked converted: the 64-bit boot now builds the title's font tables and stops at `models`, at the legal screen's model load, as far as the planning stand-ins went. A Latin font segment (`fontbankgothic`, 0x24B0 bytes; `fontzurichbold`, 0x3540) is the 13 x 13 kerning table, 94 character records of six big-endian words, then the glyph bytes; a record's last word is its glyph's offset from the segment's start, which `struct fontchar` keeps in its pointer slot `pixeldata`. At 64 bits that slot is 8 bytes and 8-aligned, so a record is 32 bytes and `struct font` is 0xE68 bytes, 0x2F4 more than the file's 0xB74-byte table; the font list (`fontdl`, 24 commands, 0xC0 bytes) is 0x180 bytes of host `Gfx`. (1) `port/include/port_romlayout.h`: `RomFontChar` (six `u32`: `index`, `baseline`, `height`, `width`, `kerningindex`, `pixel_offset`; 24 bytes) and `RomFont` (`u32 kerning[169]; RomFontChar chars[94];`, 0xB74 bytes), each with a size assertion. (2) `port/src/romconv_font.c` (new, 177 lines) with its section in `port/include/port_romconv.h`: `portFontConvertedSize(romsize)` is `romsize - sizeof(RomFont) + sizeof(struct font)`, and 0 when `romsize` is below the table or the sum would pass 0xFFFFFFFF (possible only at 64 bits). `portFontConvert(rom, romsize, out, outsize)` refuses through `portConvRefuse` (class `fonts`, file "font"), writing nothing, a file shorter than the table, a size that would wrap, an `outsize` below the converted size, and a non-zero `pixel_offset` below `sizeof(RomFont)` or at or past `romsize`, naming the glyph; then it writes the table field by field through locals and `memcpy` (so `out` may have any alignment), the padding zero, each `pixeldata` `pixel_offset + 0x2F4` zero-extended (0 stays `NULL`), then the glyph bytes as they are. Nothing past the converted size is written; `load_font_tables`'s own fix-up then adds the copy's address, unchanged. `PORT_FONTDL_COMMANDS` (24) and `PORT_FONT_STAGED_SIZE(converted)` (rounded up to 16) are beside them. (3) `port/src/segments.c`, every change behind `IS_64_BIT` (or `GE_LP64_ORACLE` for the oracle) with the 32-bit tokens unedited in the other branch: the two fonts' `Start`/`End` spans and staging arrays are `0x24B0 + 0x300` and `0x3540 + 0x300` bytes and the font list's span `0x180`; `portFontBuildSegments` calls a new `portFontConvertSegments`, which checks that each span and staging array is what the converter's image needs (`PORT_FONT_STAGED_SIZE(portFontConvertedSize(size))`, and 24 `Gfx` for the list), converts both fonts into their staging arrays with the array's size as the room, expands the list with `portGfxFromRom(_fontdlSegmentRomStart, d, 24)` (the source is the ROM image, the destination a 16-aligned `.bss` span of exactly 0x180 bytes, so they do not overlap), and stops the game through `sysFatalError`, naming the segment, on a refusal or a wrong span. *Departure:* the brief gives the spans as `0x24B0 + 0x2F4` and `0x3540 + 0x2F4`. Built that way, the sanitizer boot reported `textrelated.c:172: member access within misaligned address ... for type 'struct font'`: `load_font_tables` allocates each span from the stage bank (MEMPOOL_STAGE), `portMempAllocate` (`port/src/port_memp.c`) hands out the next bytes without rounding, so every allocation's alignment is the sum of the sizes before it, and 0x27A4 is 4 mod 8, so Zurich Bold and every later stage allocation would sit 4 bytes off 8-byte alignment. The spans are therefore the converted size rounded up to 16 (0x2F4 to 0x300), which keeps the bank as aligned as at 32 bits, where both stock sizes are multiples of 16; the converter writes the converted size, +0x2F4 on the file, and the 12 bytes after it in each staging array are padding that stays zero (the fixture checks that nothing past the converted size is written). The requirement is the 8-byte alignment of `struct font` and `struct fontchar` at 64 bits, which the pointer slot `pixeldata` gives them. `load_font_tables` and `lvInit` are not edited: they size by the labels. (4) `port/src/port_lp64.c`: `fonts` is 1. (5) `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c`: `sizeof(RomFont) == 0xB74`, `sizeof(struct font) - sizeof(RomFont)` is 0x2F4 at 64 bits and 0 at 32, `struct fontchar` 32 and 24 bytes. *The staging sizes are checked three ways*, since ASan does not check `-fcommon` globals such as these arrays, and each check sees something different (reworded in the LP64-004 fix wave, which added the second): (a) the ROM-free fixture sees the converter, never the arrays: it asserts that `portFontConvertedSize` gives 0x24B0 + 0x2F4 and 0x3540 + 0x2F4 at 64 bits (the sizes themselves at 32), that `PORT_FONT_STAGED_SIZE` of those is 0x24B0 + 0x300 and 0x3540 + 0x300, the numbers `segments.c` is written with, that 24 `Gfx` are 0x180 bytes (0xC0 at 32), and that a stock-sized font converts into exactly its converted size and is refused one byte short; (b) `segments.c` sees its own arrays at compile time, in every 64-bit build, ROM or not: it asserts that 24 `Gfx` are 0x180 bytes and that each staging array's `sizeof` is `PORT_FONT_STAGED_SIZE(ROMSIZE - sizeof(RomFont) + sizeof(struct font))`, `portFontConvertedSize`'s formula, for the stock segment's ROMSIZE (an array of 0x24B0 + 0x2F4 fails the build: `static assertion failed: "Bank Gothic's staging array holds its converted table and glyphs"`); (c) the boot sees the ROM it runs with: at every 64-bit boot `portFontConvertSegments` compares each label span and staging array with the size the converter needs for that ROM's segment before converting, passing the array's own size as the room, so a span or array one byte off stops the boot by name.

*What bounds a glyph's reads:* only where a glyph starts is checked, as the brief asks. The text renderer (`textRenderGlyph`, `textRenderGlyphOutlined`, `textrelated.c`) loads `((width + 7) & ~7) * height` bytes from `pixeldata`, `portFontClearPadding` writes inside that rectangle, and the open and Enhanced font code reads the same rectangle; nothing compares it with the font's allocation, at 32 bits or at 64. At 64 bits every glyph moves by the same 0x2F4 as the allocation grows, so each glyph's distance from the allocation's end is unchanged: a glyph inside the allocation at 32 bits is inside it at 64. In the stock ROM the furthest glyph read ends 8 bytes before the end of each font's glyph bytes (measured, below). No check was added.

*Readers, at 64 bits with the converted layout:* `load_font_tables` (`textrelated.c`) copies the span, indexes `chars[i]` by its type and rebases `pixeldata` in `uintptr_t`; `portFontClearPadding`, `textRender`, `textRenderOutlined`, `textRenderGlyph`, `textRenderGlyphOutlined`, `textDrawGlyphQuad`, `textMeasure`, `textWrap` and the Japanese path read fields by name through `struct fontchar *`/`struct font *` and index `chars[c - 0x21]` and `kerning[a * 13 + b]` by type; `gDPLoadTextureBlock` puts `pixeldata` whole into a pointer-sized `Gfx` word. `bondview.c` and `bondview2.c` (strict tier, read only) keep the tables in `struct font *`/`struct fontchar *` (`copy_1stfonttable`, `setFontTables`); `front.c`, `mpmenu.c`, `options.c`, `gunfire.c` (strict, read only), and the port's HUD, console, menu, clock, hit-map and startup code (`port_hud.c`, `port_console.c`, `port_headshots_menu.c`, `port_reinforcements_menu.c`, `port_mission_clock.c`, `port_mission_times.c`, `port_hitmap_draw.c`, `port_startup.c`) pass the two pointers to those functions or read a character's fields by name. The text styles: `portOpenFontsGlyph` (`port/fast3d/open_fonts.cpp`, Iron Sights) and `portEnhancedFontsGlyph` (`port/fast3d/enhanced_fonts.cpp`, Enhanced) receive `pixeldata` as `const unsigned char *` and key their registries by that pointer (`std::unordered_map<const uint8_t *, ...>`); the renderer (`gfx_pc.cpp`) looks a glyph up by the texture's `const uint8_t *` address; `enhanced_font_masks.cpp` reads `kerning` by index through `int32_t *`; `port_enhanced_fonts.c` holds only the style setting; `libultra_shim.c` has weak no-op stand-ins. No reader walks a font by the file's 24-byte record, and none keeps a glyph's or font's address in a 32-bit integer, so nothing in the strict tier needs a change. `ptr_font_DL` (`lv.c`): `lvInit` copies the list's span (now 0x180 bytes) at boot, before the first stage load builds it, so the copy is zeros at both widths, as the plan's hand-over check found; the segment it is bound to is never called through, and the three lists are called by symbol.

*Tests:* in four new files, following the audio banks' pattern so that none passes 500 lines: `scripts/port/test_romconv_font_fixture.c` and `.h` (124 and 58 lines: the test font, the output room, the log capture and the shared checks), `test_romconv_font.c` (249 lines: the sizes and the conversion) and `test_romconv_font_checks.c` (220 lines: the refusals and the oracle), one assertion a field, a size and a refusal, every refusal checked to leave `out` untouched; `test_romconv.sh` builds and runs both programs at both widths, the 64-bit half under the address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers: the brief's font (glyph 0 width 5, height 7, kerning index 3, at 0xB80 with eight bytes from 0xA1; glyph 93 at 0) measures `sizeof(rom) - 0xB74 + sizeof(struct font)`, converts, and gives kerning[168] 0x55, the metrics, `pixeldata` 0xB80 - 0xB74 + `sizeof(struct font)` with 0xA1 there, and glyph 93 `NULL`; also kerning[0] -2, the padding zero, nothing written past the image, the stock and staged sizes above, offsets at 0xB74 and at the last byte accepted, and refusals for a file of 0xB73 bytes, a room one byte short, a size that would wrap (64 bits), and pixel offsets 0xFFFFFF, 0xB88 (the file's end), 0xB73 and glyph 93's 4. In the 32-bit (oracle) half the oracle finds a staged font and font list identical and finds one changed byte. After the split, each of 23 deliberately broken copies of the converter made one of the two programs fail at one width at least (the seven that pass at the other width change nothing there: the growth and the wrap at 32 bits, the oracles at 64), against the same copies as before the split ( growth not applied, 0 not kept, kerning unswapped, a field from its neighbour, no glyph copy, no padding clear, a byte too many, the measure off, each check removed or off by one, a write before the checks, the two oracles short; and `PORT_FONT_STAGED_SIZE` unrounded); the RED run of the brief's step 1 failed with `undefined reference to 'portFontConvert'`. *Measured on the stock ROM* with a temporary dump in `load_font_tables` (not committed): for both fonts, the kerning table's hash and, for every glyph, its five fields, its offset from the end of `struct font` and a hash of the `((width + 7) & ~7) * height` bytes read from `pixeldata`, after the fix-up, are identical between the 32-bit (i686) and the 64-bit (aarch64) build, 190 lines each.

*LP64-004 task 10, the model file converter (2026-11-17). Task 10 built: commit "Add the model file converter".* The converter and its tests only: nothing calls it yet, `models` stays 0 in `port/src/port_lp64.c`'s table, and the 64-bit boot still stops at `models` (Task 11 wires it into the loader and marks the class). A model file is the switch slots (4 bytes each), the texture entries (12), the root node, then nodes (24 bytes), records, vertex, collision-vertex, point-usage and inline-texel blocks and display lists, all naming one another by segment-5 offsets; at 64 bits slots, entries, nodes, records with references and every list command grow, so the file cannot be converted in place. (1) `port/include/port_romlayout.h`: `RomModelNode`, `RomModelTexture`, `RomModelVertex` and one struct for each record kind with `romfile_model.c`'s sizes (Header 16, Group 28, DL 20, DLCollision 32, DLPrimary 16, LOD 16, BSP 36, BBox 28, Gunfire 40, Shadow 32, Switch 8, Op06 24, GroupSimple 20, Head 4, Interlink 28, Op11 76, Op05 424, Op07 432), each with a size assertion. (2) `port/include/port_romconv.h`: `portModelConvertedSize(file, size, numSwitches, numtextures, name)` returns the converted size (a multiple of 8) or 0 after `portConvRefuse`, and `portModelConvert(file, size, out, outsize, ...)` returns 1, or 0 after `portConvRefuse` with nothing written. (3) Four sources under 500 lines each, compiled only at 64 bits and in the oracle build: `port/src/romconv_model.c` (242 lines: the layout, the two passes, the output checks), `romconv_model_walk.c` (402: the walk and the ownership of each 4 bytes), `romconv_model_refs.c` (230: the one reference lookup, the list words, the promotion check) and `romconv_model_records.c` (424: one field map a record kind and the block writers), with the shared declarations in `romconv_model_walk.h` (138). Both functions run the same plan: the walk claims every item reachable as `romfile_model.c`'s `walk` reaches it (`Next`, `Child`, a LOD's `Affects`, a switch's `Controls`, a BSP's two children, each record's lists and blocks, the list calls, the switch slots and inline texels), marking which item owns each 4 bytes of the file; the layout places each item at its run-time size in a private grow-only store (not `portConvScratch`, which Task 11's loader uses for the file copy) and the shared offset map; then a checking pass runs the writers with no output, resolving every reference through the map. `portModelConvert` checks the room, alignment and overlap, clears exactly the measured bytes and runs the same writers again, so the writing pass finds nothing new to refuse. Every offset, count and extent is bounded against the file in 64-bit arithmetic. What it writes follows the brief: references `0x05000000 | new offset` zero-extended into the field, 0 kept; scalars swapped by `romfile_model.c`'s field maps; vertices 16 bytes with six half-words swapped and a collision vertex's link at 64 bits written as `LinkOffset` (the target node's new offset) and `CollisionRelatedIndex`; lists through `portGfxFromRom`, then segment-5 `G_VTX`, `G_SETTIMG` and list-call words moved, segment 3 and 4 words and `G_SETTEX` copied; `Gunfire.Image` and `Shadow.image` the texture entry's new offset. *Departures, each because the code at 32 bits is the reference:* the output keeps the file's order instead of grouping items by kind, each item aligned to a pointer (8 at 64 bits, 4 at 32) and bytes no item owns copied where they lie, so that at 32 bits the image is the in-place one byte for byte (Task 11's oracle compares whole images); the total is rounded up to 8. Opcodes 3 and 17 are swapped with the group map and 20 with the header map, as `walk` does (opcode 17's own map in `romfile_model.c` is unused); Op11's two half-words at 0x44 are swapped as one word, Op05's and Op07's data as words, and a Head record is 4 bytes in the file and in the output. A G_VTX may load from inside a vertex block (the brief's fixture does), and a block of no elements is not owned by anything: `PexplosionbitZ`'s DL record has `numVertices` 0 but its list loads 16 vertices from 0x98, which the in-place path leaves unswapped, and the converter copies those raw bytes where they lie too. `probe.c` asserts that Group, GroupSimple and Interlink keep their first float at 0 at both widths; a BBox keeps its model number at 0, so the assertion is that its floats start at 4. (The three first-float assertions were removed by LP64-005 task 3's review batch 2, 2026-11-18: they held for any layout, and batch 1's `POSITION_FIRST` assertions in `probe_overlays.h` pin those records' positions.)

*Refusals.* Everything `romfile_model.c`'s `walk` and `romfileModelConvert` count as bad: counts that leave no room for the root, an inline texture deeper than 3 or with texels outside the file, a node below the root or past the file, a record past the file, a DLPRIMARY with more than 0x2000 quads, a vertex or point-usage block past the file, a list with no end command before the file's end or in 0x8000 commands, and a file with no vertices and no display lists. Beyond those, each because the conversion or the game's later walk would otherwise go wrong (no stock file trips one): more than 4096 pending nodes or 32 nested list calls, a vertex, collision-vertex or point-usage block counted above 0x8000 (an extra refusal, not parity: `romfile_model.c`'s `swapVertices` and `swapPointUsage` skip such a block silently and leave it unswapped; a count with no block is ignored, as there), an item at an offset not a multiple of 4, two items sharing a byte or one offset reached as two kinds, a list calling itself or two calling each other, a reference that is neither 0 nor segment 5 or names something other than its kind or nothing at all (the gap bytes), a G_VTX loading past its vertex block, an opcode without a record that names one or one with a record that names none (`modelPromoteNodeOffsetsToPointers` would read through `NULL`), node links that make the game's promotion walk (`Child`, a LOD's `Affects`, `Next`, `Parent`) loop, an Op05 or Op07 record with children or non-zero references (nothing converts what they name), an inline texture with no texels, a collision link to a non-node or to the node at new offset 0, a segment-5 word in a list command whose word is an address the converter does not move, an item that would end past 16 MB in the converted file, and an output buffer too small, `NULL`, not 8-aligned or overlapping the file. Malformed graphs end: a node or list reached twice is claimed once, so a `Next` or `Child` cycle ends the walk and the promotion check refuses it; a record reached as a node and overlapping blocks are refused when claimed; list call cycles are refused by the path of calls being walked.

A random file is almost always refused at its first node, so the random half exercises the header and first-node checks only; the mutated files, and the argument that every write is placed by the layout and checked against the measured total, carry the in-bounds property for deep files. `test_romconv.sh` builds both at both widths, the 64-bit half under the address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers, the 32-bit half with `romfile_model.c` (with `-Wno-unused-const-variable` for its unused opcode 17 map). 2992 of the 10,000 mutated files are accepted at 64 bits.
