*Task 10 review fixes (2026-11-17): commit "Refuse model references past 16 MB and other list addresses".* The task review found two defects in "Add the model file converter", fixed on top of it. (1) References past 16 MB. The game rebases a reference as `value - 0x05000000 + addr` (`model.c`) and the renderer takes a segment word's low 24 bits, so a new offset at or past 0x01000000 would run into the segment byte (`0x05000000 | 0x01000010` is `0x05000010`, offset 0x10) and name the wrong bytes; an accepted file of about 9 MB (a long `Next` chain, many list commands or a raw tail) could lay items there, and the converter wrote them in bounds but wrong. The layout now refuses, in the measuring pass, any item or run of raw bytes whose converted bytes would end past 0x01000000, naming the file, the item's kind and its file offset; this replaces the 4 GB check, which it subsumes. The bound is on every byte placed, so every offset a reference can name is below 16 MB: a reference names an item's start, a place inside a vertex, point-usage, texel or raw block (`G_VTX` into a block, a texture's inline texels) or the collision link's node, and each of those offsets is the map entry of a byte the layout placed; an item that ends exactly at 0x01000000 is accepted, because no reference names an item's end. (2) Segment-5 words in other list commands. Counted over the 512 stock model files with a scratch counter (not committed, deleted): 47 commands other than `G_VTX`, `G_SETTIMG` and the two calls have 0x05 in `w1`'s top byte, 45 `G_TRI4` (0xB1; first in `CbaronsamediZ`), one `G_SETTILESIZE` (0xF2) and one `G_SETTILE` (0xF5) (both in `PgoldeneyelogoZ`). In GE's F3D none of those `w1` is an address: `G_TRI4` holds vertex indices and the two tile commands tile settings, and both the renderer and the in-place path treat them as data. The opcodes whose `w1` is an address (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp` resolves it through `seg_addr`) and that the converter does not remap, `G_MTX` (0x01), `G_MOVEMEM` (0x03), `G_SPRITE2D_BASE` (0x09), `G_INVALTEXCACHE_EXT` (0x34), `G_SETZIMG` (0xFE) and `G_SETCIMG` (0xFF), never occur with segment 5 in the stock ROM, so a segment-5 word in one now refuses the file, naming the list, the command and its offset; every other command is copied, and `port_romconv.h` lists which opcodes carry an address. (3) Also: `claimBlock` ignores a count above 0x8000 when its block's reference is 0 (as the in-place path does) and still refuses one that names a block, worded above as an extra refusal; `itemAt` computes a block's end in 64 bits, as `end * 4` wrapped for a file above 0xFFFFFFFC bytes. *Tests:* `scripts/port/test_romconv_model_checks.c` gains a file whose raw tail ends exactly at 16 MB (accepted, measured 0x01000000) and one 4 bytes longer (refused, the line naming "the raw bytes at" and "past the 16 MB"), built from a small file and a zeroed 16 MB buffer; a segment-5 word in each of the six address commands (refused); a count of 0x9000 with a block (refused) and without one (converts, equal to the in-place result at 32 bits). The three refusal cases failed against "Add the model file converter" first, at 64 bits (aarch64) and 32 (x86_64): 8 failures, six "a segment-5 address in another command", "a count above 0x8000 with no block converts", "a file whose last item ends past 16 MB is refused". A new `scripts/port/test_romconv_model_shapes.c`, run by `test_romconv.sh` at both widths, covers two shapes the stock ROM has and the fixture lacked: an odd point-usage count (three half-words) mid-file with its padding half-word kept and at the file's end in a slot cut short, and a DL record counting no vertices whose list loads two from its `Vertices` (`PexplosionbitZ`'s shape), each with a 64-bit value check and the 32-bit image equal to the in-place one; and a `G_TRI4` whose indices start with 0x05, copied. `sameAsInPlace` moved into the fixture builder for it. *Checks:* `test_romconv.sh` passes at 32 and 64 bits in x86_64 and at 64 (sanitizers) in aarch64; step 1 in x86_64 and aarch64: 343 and 374 files compiled, 0 failed, `OK: 0 narrowings`, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls`; `test_abi_probe.sh` OK at both widths; the scratch stock sweep rerun gives the same totals as before (512 convert at 64 bits, 3,289,344 bytes in, 4,015,208 out, each writing exactly its measure; at 32 bits all 512 identical to the in-place result); `compare_win32.py commits ec70039 WORKTREE` on this change exits 0, identical in loaded code and data. Not rerun: steps 2, 4 and 5 (nothing the boot, the 32-bit game or the oracle runs changed: the converter is not called and the oracle does not compare models yet) and the CI lines.

*LP64-004 task 11, models wired into the loader (2026-11-17). Task 11 built: commit "Convert model files at load on a 64-bit build".* The seventh class marked converted, and the first time a 64-bit game runs frames: the 64-bit headless executable now loads and converts the legal screen's and the Nintendo logo's models and runs 600 frames of the title, plain and under the sanitizers on aarch64 and x86_64, and a mission (Dam) stops at `backgrounds`. (1) `src/game/objecthandler_2.c` (`load_object_fill_header`), every change inside `#if IS_64_BIT` with the 32-bit tokens unedited in the `#else`: `Textures` follows the switch slots by pointer stride, `(struct ModelFileTextures *) ((struct ModelNode **) filedata + numSwitches)` (the same address as the `s32` stride at 32 bits; `RootNode = &Textures[numtextures]` was already typed); a served file goes to `romfileModelConvertWide` instead of `romfileModelConvert`, with the room the caller's `size` for a load to an address and `fileGetCapacity` for a bank load; `fileSetSize` commits the converted image's size rounded up to 16. `portConvertModelGdl` needed no change: it already counts and allocates in `Gfx` (Task 8). (2) `src/game/ob.c`/`ob.h`: `u32 fileGetCapacity(s32 index)`, inside `#if IS_64_BIT`, returns `rom_remaining`, where `fileIndexLoadToBank` records the block it allocated (all the stage memory left for a first load, the last committed size plus the compressed copy for a reload) and which only `fileSetSize` changes. (3) `port/src/romfile_model.c`, at 64 bits only: `romfileModelConvertWide(data, filesize, room, numSwitches, numtextures, name, &commit)` measures with `portModelConvertedSize`, refuses by name an image larger than the room (`ge: lp64: cannot convert models "NAME": its N-byte image does not fit the R-byte room`), copies the file to `portConvScratch(filesize)` (reserved at boot to 262,144 bytes, so no stock model allocates during play; a request it cannot grow to stops the game, `ge: lp64: converter scratch: cannot allocate`), converts it back into the block with `portModelConvert` and returns 1 with the image's size. On any refusal (the converter's, the room's, or a write the converter declines) nothing was written; it then zeroes the bytes the 64-bit switch slots and texture entries take at the block's start, so the header's `Switches` and `Textures` read as empty (null switches, texture number 0) rather than as the unconverted big-endian file, commits the larger of the file and those bytes, and returns 0; the existing branch then points `RootNode` at its empty node and logs `... could not be converted - rendering nothing`. If even those bytes do not fit the room, it stops the game through `sysFatalError`, naming the model. With `GE_MODELTIME=1` it logs `ge: modeltime: NAME image N bytes of a R-byte room (file F)`. The conversion runs where `romfileModelConvert` runs (the model's load, including during play, as at 32 bits); nothing moves to first use. (4) `src/game/gun.c`, inside `#if IS_64_BIT`: the per-hand weapon buffer `size_item_buffer` is 0x21540 (0x14820 times 13/8, rounded up to 16), the weapon room `D_80032464` 0xBE70 (from 0x7530), the trigger and watch laser room 0x11DC0 (from 0xAFD0) and the left hand's room 0x133E0 (from 0xBD70), each texture pool starting after its room as before. (5) `port/src/port_lp64.c`: `models` is 1, so the boot passes the legal screen. The compiled-in branch's guard in `load_object_fill_header` passes too from now on; a 64-bit build links no compiled-in model (`GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK=OFF`), and every model file is served from a stock ROM. (6) The oracle. `port/src/romconv_model_oracle.c` (new, 144 lines, compiled with the other `romconv_` sources and empty outside the oracle build): `portModelOracle` converts a file by both paths, `romfileModelConvert` in a copy and `portModelConvert` into new memory, and compares the whole images, both before the promotion, as `models NAME`; a refusal by either path or an image of another size counts as a difference. `portModelOracleSweep` reads the game's three compiled header tables (`assets/obseg/{gun,chr,prop}/*ModelFileHeaders.inc.c`) through its own `MODELFILEHEADER`, which keeps each name and its two counts (a header NAME is the file G, C or P NAME Z), loads each file through `fileIndexLoadToAddr` into a 256 KB buffer with its lookup entry put back, as `GE_ROMPROBE` does, and runs the comparison. `romdataFilesApply` runs it when `GE_LP64_ORACLE_SWEEP` is set, through `portLp64OracleSweepRequested` (new in `port_lp64_oracle.c`/`.h`, which no longer logs "no class has a sweep yet"). *Departure:* the brief puts the sweep in `port_lp64_oracle.c` and the oracle call in `romfile_model.c`; `port_lp64_oracle.c` is linked into the ROM-free converter tests, which have no file loader, so the sweep and the comparison live in their own file, as the audio bank oracle does (`romconv_model_oracle.c`), and only the boot's sweep compares models: the real loads of a run are the same files, so counting them again would not add a file. (7) `scripts/port/lp64_boot.py`: `--stage` also sets `GE_STAGE_AFTER=1`, as the mission smoke does; alone, `GE_STAGE` waits 120 ticks, the whole of an `--expect-stop` run, so `--stage dam` never reached the mission (it ran its 120 frames at the title and failed "no asset-class stop"). New test `test_stage_option_launches_the_mission_at_once` (`test_lp64_boot.py`), RED before the change (exit status 3 from the stand-in), GREEN after.

No stock model passes its 64-bit room. The `bondview2.c` row bounds the record words (`MODEL_RWDATA_BYTES`) by one record per 8 bytes of the 32-bit files, as the header tables carry no record counts; the real figure is smaller. Unscaled at 64 bits `gun.c`'s three rooms would leave 3,160, 2,328 and 2,392 bytes, the planning scan's "about 5 percent". *The wallet Bond's room is not scaled* (the review's ruling: scale it to 0x10400 only if the room stays inside its allocation and nothing placed after the model is squeezed or overlapped). The first holds: `ptr_logo_and_walletbond_DL` is 0x78000 bytes from `MEMPOOL_STAGE` (`initmenus.c:34`). The second does not: `init_menu05_fileselect` (`front.c:2598`; 2599 before the LP64-004 fix wave H's correction) expands the file-select background, just before `load_walletbond`, at `buf + 0xA000` (`sub_GAME_7F008DE4`, `title.c:500`: 0x40400 bytes of image to `buf + 0x4A400`, its compressed source after that, in the 0x6E000 bytes left), and the briefing (`front.c:17312`; 17308 before the LP64-004 fix wave H's correction) puts its file at `buf + 0xA000` and its language bank from `buf + 0xA200` to `buf + 0x78000`, the allocation's end. A room of 0x10400 would let a model write 25,600 bytes into the image; no free space follows the model. So the 2,592-byte margin (6.3 percent of the room) is accepted: the wallet Bond is one fixed stock file, its 64-bit image measured at 38,368 bytes, and an image past 40,960 would be refused by name (`ge: lp64: cannot convert models "PwalletbondZ" ...`) and render nothing, never overwrite the background. In the 64-bit runs the legal page's image was 9,832 bytes and the Nintendo logo's 39,968, each in a 245,760-byte room. No `ge: lp64: pool` line appeared in any run.

*A refusal, tried.* A scratch build (aarch64, sanitizers; the change was reverted) that set every room from an environment variable: with 9,000 bytes both menu models were refused (`ge: lp64: cannot convert models "PlegalpageZ": its 9832-byte image does not fit the 9000-byte room`), took the "rendering nothing" branch with their tables zeroed, and the run finished its 600 frames with exit status 0 and no sanitizer report; with 16 bytes the game stopped, `ge: FATAL: The model PlegalpageZ was refused and its 80 bytes of tables do not fit its 16-byte room`.

*What the task's runs executed, and what no real run has executed yet.* The 600-frame run loads only two models by the address path, `PlegalpageZ` and `PnintendologoZ`, and reaches no menu; the Dam run stops at `backgrounds` and executes none of this task's code. No real run has yet executed: a bank load through `fileGetCapacity`; the refusal path outside the scratch build above; any of `gun.c`'s rooms; `bondview2.c`'s models; `title.c`'s gun barrel Bond; the GoldenEye logo; the wallet Bond; the attract cast; and the chr and prop loads of a mission. *Stage pool, unmeasured:* the two weapon buffers (`initBondDATA.c:241` and `245` allocate `size_item_buffer[]` from `MEMPOOL_STAGE`) now take 2 x 52,512 more bytes of the stage pool at 64 bits; whether the pool absorbs them is unmeasured until a mission runs, so the next task looks for a `ge: lp64: pool` line in its mission runs.

*LP64-004 task 12, backgrounds (2026-11-17). Task 12 built: commit "Build the background's room and portal tables and expand room lists on a 64-bit build".* The eighth class marked converted: a 64-bit mission (Dam) now passes `backgrounds` and stops at `collision tiles`, plain and under the sanitizers on aarch64 and x86_64. A bg file's front matter is still turned to native byte order in place by `romfileBgConvert`, once per file. At 32 bits the game then reads the room table (24-byte `bg_room_data`, three offsets and a position) and the portal table (8-byte `bg_portal_data_entry`) in the file; at 64 bits those records are 40 and 16 bytes, so they are built in new memory. The offsets stay segment 0x0F words, zero-extended into their pointer-sized fields, so `BG_SEG_TO_PTR`, the file-position arithmetic, the csize differences and the portal promotion in `load_bg_file` run unchanged. The visibility commands and the portal points stay in the file (no pointer in either). (1) `port/src/romconv_bg.c` (new, 327 lines then and 339 now, a count corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H): `portBgTablesSize` measures the two tables from the header (the room table ends at its closing record, the first record after index 0 whose primary offset is 0, which is the test `load_bg_file`'s room count makes, reading no other field of that record; the portal table ends at its first entry whose offset is 0, the test the game's portal walks make) and returns 40R + 16P rounded up to 8, or refuses by name: a header offset that is not a 0x0F word or lies outside the file, a room table with no record whose primary offset is 0 before the smallest of the vis and portal offsets above it, a room offset (the closing record's included) that is not a 0x0F word, an end marker with a zero offset, a portal table with no entry whose offset is 0 before the file's end, a portal offset that is not a 0x0F word, and points that run past the file. Of these the game itself tests none: the bound by the vis and portal offsets is the span `romfileBgConvert` turns to native order, and the others are extra refusals that every stock file passes (the oracle's sweep converts all 25 without a refusal). The closing record's point and secondary words are copied, not checked (corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H: they are checked, as every room record's three offset words are, to be 0 or a segment 0x0F word, then copied); the sweep found all 25 stock closing records all zeros. `portBgTablesConvert` writes rooms then portals into a room of at least that size, 8-byte aligned, and refuses (as "bg file") a smaller or misaligned room, writing nothing. `portBgRoomListExpand` places a room's display list (below). (2) `port/src/romfile_bg.c`, at 64 bits only: `portBgTablesLoad` stops the game by name (`sysFatalError`) for a bg that is not served from the ROM (a 64-bit build links no compiled-in copy that a converter could read), for a file the converter refuses, and for a write it refuses; otherwise it takes 8 bytes more than the size from `MEMPOOL_STAGE` (the pool does not round) so the tables start 8-byte aligned, converts, and logs `ge: lp64: bg tables NAME: R room records, P portal entries, N bytes of the stage pool`. `load_bg_file` calls it right after `romfileBgConvert`, where the 32-bit game takes the room table's address, before stan, the room count, the env walk and the portal passes; the two later assignments of the room list and of `g_BgPortals` are skipped at 64 bits. Because the stage pool is reset for each stage, the tables are built fresh at every load (the plan's decision 6). A stage pool that cannot give the bytes stops the game inside `portMempAllocate` ("Memory bank exhausted", naming the bank and the request). Measured from the oracle's detail lines (R and P as the 32-bit tables hold them), the stage pool cost per mission at 64 bits is: Dam 8,688 bytes (139 room records, 195 portal entries), Control 6,040, Depot 5,592, Aztec 5,344, Silo 5,088, Facility 4,968, Archives 4,392, Bunker 2 4,064, Frigate 3,968, Caverns 3,880, Train 3,448, Surface and Surface 2 3,320 each, Streets 3,320, Jungle 2,848, Egypt 2,720, Statue 1,912, Bunker 1 1,824, Cradle 1,584 (one portal entry), Runway 1,256. No run logged a `ge: lp64: pool` line. (3) Room lists. `bgDecompress` leaves a room's E bytes of 8-byte N64 commands at the block's start; the 32-bit loaders copy them to the block's end with `texCopyGdls` and let `texLoadFromGdl` write the processed list back from the start. At 64 bits both loaders (`bgLoadRoomPrimaryGdl`, `bgLoadRoomSecondaryGdl`) call `portBgRoomListExpand`, which expands the E bytes into 2E bytes of 16-byte `Gfx` ending at the block's end through `portGfxFromRomBackward`; with `allocsize >= 2E` the destination starts at or after the source, as that function needs. When the block is smaller it writes nothing and returns -1, and the caller's existing fail path logs its `room memory` line; an E of 0 is an empty list (the list pointer at the block's end, 0 returned, nothing written), as at 32 bits, where `texCopyGdls` copies nothing and both loaders' caller, `bgLoadRoomModelData`, adds 0 to `used` (the primary branch takes any result of 0 or more; the secondary tests `result > 0` and fails only below 0); an E that is negative or not a multiple of 8 is refused by name. No stock room has a 0-byte list among the 2,508 room lists the 32-bit oracle's 20 missions loaded in their 600 frames (`textures room list N`; the smallest is 32 bytes); the rooms the smoke does not load were not measured. Sizes after it are host bytes. `texCopyGdls` keeps its 64-bit branch, which now has no caller that runs (its comment in `src/game/tex.c` says so, with the same line count). (4) Unnamed strides in `src/game/bg.c`. The two ray-test sites in `bgTestRayIntersectionInRoom` (`roomnum * 24 ... + 12`) and the two at the room-table reads near the end of the file now use `sizeof(bg_room_data)` and `offsetof(bg_room_data, pos)`; the Windows program stayed identical. Two sites changed the 32-bit code when typed (GCC allocated registers differently), so their old tokens stay under `#if !IS_64_BIT`: `sub_GAME_7F0B37EC`'s `((u8 *)g_BgPortals)[(portal << 3) + 6] |= 2` (typed `controlbytes1 |= 2` at 64 bits; the first comparison found the function 16 bytes longer) and `sub_GAME_7F0B8DF4`'s `offset += 8` (`sizeof(bg_portal_data_entry)` at 64 bits; the second comparison found 83 bytes of different registers). Every other reader of the two tables is typed: in `bg.c` the load, the csize and file-position arithmetic, the room centres and bounding boxes, the env walk and the portal functions; `bgroomtrans.c`; `port_baked_light.c`; `chrprop.c`'s two portal reads. `port/fast3d` has none. Pointer differences between a table entry and the file occur only in N64 branches. (5) `port/src/port_lp64.c`: `backgrounds` is 1. (6) The oracle. `port/src/romconv_bg_oracle.c` (new, 348 lines then and 398 now, a count corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H; empty outside the oracle build): at the end of a first `romfileBgConvert`, before any of `load_bg_file`'s passes, `portBgTablesOracle` compares the in-place 24- and 8-byte records with the converter's output field by field, as `backgrounds NAME`, with the detail `R room records and P portal entries, A and B bytes at 64 bits`; `portBgOracleSweep` converts a copy of every bg file `levelinfotable` names that the ROM's directory holds with data (34 names, 9 not in the ROM or empty, 25 swept); a file the directory holds with bytes that the game does not serve, and a file past the sweep's 64-file list, count as differences rather than as skips. The success line also says what each file's closing room record holds (`closing record all zeros (point 0x0, secondary 0x0)` for all 25). `romdataFilesApply` runs the sweep after the model sweep. (7) Tests: `scripts/port/test_romconv_bg.c` (20 field tests: sizes, placement, every room and portal field, the zero records, the file left unwritten) and `test_romconv_bg_checks.c` (12 refusals, each with nothing written, and 8 tests of the list expander), on a front matter built in `test_romconv_bg_fixture.c`; `test_romconv.sh` builds both at each width, with the sanitizers at 64 bits. RED on aarch64 (64-bit only): the link failed, `undefined reference to 'portBgTablesSize'`. GREEN: `test_romconv: PASS (64-bit)` on aarch64; `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` in the i686 container. A scratch mutation pass (39 mutations of `romconv_bg.c`, aarch64, 64 bits) was killed by the tests every time. *Departures:* the brief's fixture header (vis 0x7C, portals 0x8C, first points 0xA4) leaves 0x68 bytes for the room table, not a whole number of 24-byte records, so the fixture moves the vis commands, the portals and the points 0x10 later and asserts the first portal's offset as `0x0F0000B4`; the list expander is a port helper rather than code in `bg.c`; the converter refuses more than the brief names (segment words, the end marker, portal points, alignment, the header); `portBgTablesConvert` names its refusals "bg file" because its signature takes no name; the tables carry 8 bytes of alignment padding; the two strides above keep their 32-bit tokens; the oracle and the test fixture are files of their own. *Reloads (step 3, a measurement only, nothing changed because of it).* An oracle soak that loaded Dam twice compared the 32-bit tables at the second load, before its passes, with a fresh conversion: 334 fields differ, all in the portal table: 61 portals have `connectedRoom1` and `connectedRoom2` exchanged (the first load's `bgOrderPortal`, through `bgSwapConnectedRooms`), 18 have a different `controlbytes1`, all in bit 0: 14 have it set in the file and clear in place (the first load's pass `controlbytes1 &= 0xfe`), 4 clear in the file and set in place (a door opened during play, `bg.c` near line 6931); and 194 portal offsets hold the first load's promoted addresses. No room field differs. The 32-bit game runs its passes again over that state, a 64-bit game over fresh tables, and the passes give both the same result: bit 0 is cleared either way, the promotion repeats, the value 2 (bit 1) is set from the compiled `specialportalarray`, and `bgOrderPortal` is decided by the portal's points (`sub_GAME_7F0B96CC` reads only those) and the two room centres, so its first result is one a second pass leaves alone (it exchanges the rooms only when the first room's centre lies beyond the plane and the second's does not). That is reasoning from the code; the state after the second load's passes was not compared.

*LP64-004, the special-portal walk's end (2026-11-17). Commit "End the special-portal walk at its own array on a 64-bit build".* Found by Task 13, whose collision converter lets a 64-bit mission start get past the stan load for the first time: `sub_GAME_7F0B37EC` (`src/game/bg.c`, called at the end of `load_bg_file`'s room set-up) walks `specialportalarray` as bytes until its pointer reaches `&g_BgCurrentRoom`, the N64 address of the next variable. The walk is right only where the linker puts `g_BgCurrentRoom` straight after the 20-byte array. In the 64-bit sanitizer build of Dam it read past the array (`bg.c:382:33: runtime error: load of address ... with insufficient space for an object of type 'u8'`, the bytes shown being the array's last four, `11 00 3a ff`, then zeros), and the plain aarch64 executable timed out after 120 s at the same place: with the fix and nothing else changed, both reach the next stop. At 64 bits the end is now the array's own end, `specialportalarray + sizeof(specialportalarray)`; the 32-bit line keeps its tokens under `#else`, so the shipped program is unchanged (`compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`, exit 0; `lp64_casts.py check`: `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`). The 32-bit builds still depend on that layout. On its own this commit changes nothing a run reaches: a 64-bit mission still stops at `collision tiles` before the walk; Task 13's commit makes the walk run and records the boot checks.

*LP64-004 task 13, collision tiles (2026-11-17). Task 13 built: commit "Keep the collision file's header record outside the file on a 64-bit build".* The ninth class marked converted: a 64-bit mission now passes `collision tiles` and stops at `setup files`, plain and under the sanitizers on aarch64 and x86_64, both for Dam (5 room slots) and for Caverns (none). A stan file is a two-word header (`unk`, `first_tile`), one 4-byte slot a room and a zero slot, then the tiles to a zero word. The tiles hold no address (a point's link is a `u16` offset in 8-byte units from `standTileStart`, `ptr_firstroom - 0x80`), so they are converted in place at both widths exactly as `romfileStanConvert` always has (word 0 rotated right by 8, the mid and tail nibbles reversed, the point halfwords swapped). Only the header depends on the pointer width: the game reads it as `struct StanPrefixRecord`, two pointers, and of those reads only `ptr_firstroom` (`stanLoadFile`'s write of `prefix->stanfile` goes through `&stan_prefix`, the global itself, not into the file). **The plan's design** was to write the 16-byte record over the file's first 16 bytes at 64 bits, covering the two header words and the first two room slots, and to refuse a file with no room slot. The oracle showed that 18 of the 27 stock stans have no room slot, their first tile at 0x0C right after a 12-byte header: ame, arch, arec, ark, ash, cat, cave, cryp, depo, dish, imp, jun, len, oat, ref, sev, sevb and sevx; the 9 with rooms are azt (30), crad (7), dam (5), dest (2), pete (1), run (11), silo (8), stat (1) and tra (2). A 16-byte record over a 0-room file would overwrite its first tile, so the task stopped and the coordinator ruled (2026-11-17): **the record lives outside the file at 64 bits**. (1) `port/src/romconv_stan.c` (new, 261 lines), declared in `port/include/port_romconv_stage.h` (new; `port_romconv.h` is at its length limit) with the file layout in `port/include/port_romlayout_stage.h` (new). `portStanConvert(data, size, base, name)` checks everything before it writes: the header against its room table (`first_tile == 8 + (rooms + 1) * 4`, any number of rooms from 0), the first tile inside the file, every room offset inside the tiles (corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H: in `[first_tile, size)`), and the whole tile walk to its zero word, each tile's header and points inside the file and its point count at most 10. It refuses by name otherwise, writing nothing. It then converts the tiles; at 32 bits it also rebases the room slots and writes the record over the two header words, last, so its result equals the in-place pass byte for byte, 0-room files included; at 64 bits it leaves the header words and room slots as the file has them. `portStanRecordFill(data, size, base, record, name)` applies the same header rule and bounds, sharing the converter's code, and fills `{NULL, base + first_tile}`; on a refusal it returns 0 after `portConvRefuse` and leaves `*record` untouched. Because it reads only the header, which the 64-bit conversion does not touch, it gives the same record before and after conversion. A tile's size is computed (`8 + 8 * max(count, 3)`, `list_of_tilesizes`' values) rather than read from `stan.c`'s table, which romconv sources do not link; the oracle compares with the in-place pass, which uses the table. (2) `port/src/romfile_stan.c`: at 64 bits `romfileStanConvert` calls the converter and stops the game by name on a refusal (`Cannot convert the collision file NAME`); the file owns one static `struct StanPrefixRecord` and `romfileStanRecord(data, size, name)` fills it, stopping the game by name on a refused header. The 32-bit body is unchanged under `#else`, beside the oracle's `romfileStanOracle` (`#ifdef GE_LP64_ORACLE`), which converts a copy with `portStanConvert` at the file's own address and compares the whole file; `romdata.c`'s stan case calls it in the oracle build. (3) `src/game/bg.c`, `load_bg_file`'s 64-bit branch: a stan that did not load from the ROM is refused by name (no compiled-in stan is linked at 64 bits), then `gptr_stan` is pointed at `romfileStanRecord(file, the bank size the file loaded into, name)` and the trace prints the file, the record and the first tile; the 32-bit branch keeps its tokens. (4) `port_lp64.c` marks `collision tiles` converted. **One record at a time.** A static record is enough because only one stan is live at once: `load_bg_file` is the only caller of `stanDetermineEOF` and `stanLoadFile` and the only user of `gptr_stan`; both set the global `stan_prefix` to the record they are given, and every read of `ptr_firstroom` in `stan.c` (`stanDetermineEOF`, `stanLoadFile`, `stanBuildRoomData`, `stanMatchTileName`, `stanFindFloorTileBelowY`, `sub_GAME_7F0AFB78`) goes through `stan_prefix` or that argument. The boot's probe (`GE_ROMPROBE`) converts every served stan but builds no record. `portStanPack` and `portStanPackForProbe` run only on compiled-in stans, never at 64 bits. Multiplayer and cutscene stages load through the same `load_bg_file`, and each stage load refills the record before `stanDetermineEOF` reads it; nothing keeps a record or `ptr_firstroom` across a stage load (corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H: the record and `ptr_firstroom` stay as they are between stage loads, as stale as at 32 bits, and each load refills them before they are read). The room slots are read only by `DEBUG`-only `sub_GAME_7F0AF630` (no build defines `DEBUG`), by `portStanPack`, and by 32-bit paths. Tiles are found from the walk and `firststaninroom`, never from the slots; pads resolve a tile by name through `stanMatchTileName`, and chrs, props, the player and waypoints hold full pointers. (5) Tests: `scripts/port/test_romconv_stan.c` (new, 497 lines, both widths in `test_romconv.sh`, which links `romfile_stan.c` at 32 bits for the comparison) covers the stock-shaped file, the tile headers and points, the room slots (rebased at 32 bits, unchanged at 64), the record from `portStanRecordFill` before and after conversion, a 1-room file (first tile at 0x10) and a 0-room file (first tile at 0x0C: at 64 bits the record points at `data + 0x0C`, the 12 header bytes are unchanged and the first tile's words are the converted tile), each equal to the in-place pass at 32 bits, and each refusal, every one leaving all bytes as they were. The 11-point refusal uses a file in which the 11-point tile fits and is followed by its zero word, so with the count check removed the converter returns 1 and the test fails by its own assertion. Mutants run on aarch64 and i686: the count check removed, the 64-bit header write forced, `portStanRecordFill` not checking, the first-tile bound removed and the 32-bit record not written each fail at least one assertion (no crash) at the width where they change the code. `scripts/port/test_stan_callbacks.c` adds the crouch branch the plan left untested: a crouch link sets the record's flag and `stanGetLocusField0` returns non-zero. **Dam's rooms.** With this commit Dam's 64-bit load runs `bgRoomCalcBB` for each of its rooms (1 to 138), which loads a room's lists through Task 12's expansion and deletes them again, one room at a time, with no `room memory` line. Many rooms loaded at once during play is still unmeasured (Task 16's smoke). **An inherited 32-bit hazard.** The special-portal walk's 32-bit line still ends at `&g_BgCurrentRoom` (the "special-portal walk's end" note above), so the 32-bit builds depend on the linker placing that variable straight after `specialportalarray`.

Task 14 built: commit "Add the setup file converter for the tables and the intro".* The converter for the setup files' tables, lists, names, AI code, intro and credits table; the prop records go through stubs that Task 15 replaces. It is not wired into the loader: `setup files` stays unconverted in `port/src/port_lp64.c`, and a 64-bit mission still stops there. At 32 bits a setup file is swapped in place by `romfile_setup.c` and the game reads its records in the file; at 64 bits the header (`struct stagesetup`, 80 bytes), pads (56), bound pads (80), waypoints (24), waygroups (24), paths (16), AI lists (16), name tables (8 a slot), the intro camera (56) and the credits record (16) all grow, so they are built in new memory. (1) `port/src/romconv_setup_walk.c` (342 lines) and `romconv_setup_walk.h` (157): one enumeration drives both the measure and the write. It records, for each 4-byte slot of the file, which item owns it, claiming the header, then the tables in the file's reading order (pads, bound pads, waypoints, waygroups, paths, AI lists, pad names, bound pad names) and each record's s32 lists; every walk is bounded by the file and refused by name when it finds no terminator. Lists may share words (one list starting inside another); a list running into any other item, overlapping items, unaligned items and items outside the file are refused. Of these the game tests none. A zero or unaligned offset in the header's first eight fields is refused (the two name tables may be absent). (2) `port/src/romconv_setup_intro.c` (342): the intro walk by `kSetupIntroKinds` (`port/generated/setup_kinds.h`), the credits table to its `{0, 0}` text IDs, and the prop list to `PROPDEF_END` by `kSetupPropdefKinds`; an unknown intro or prop type is refused. The camera is written at its C size with its two text IDs in the low words of their unions and `prev` zero-extended. At 64 bits the credits record's table field holds the table's offset in the output, which `bondview_r.c` adds `g_ptrStageSetupFile` to; at 32 bits it holds the table's address, as the in-place pass writes. The game walks the intro by `sizeof` with no alignment, so at 64 bits a camera or credits record that would start at 4 mod 8 is preceded by one word `INTROTYPE_MAX << 24`, which all three intro walkers (`bondview_r.c`, `prop.c`'s `portMeasureIntro`, and `bondview2.c`, read not edited) step over by design: each has a default arm that steps 4 bytes, and the pad word reads as type 10. The credits record is stepped over in `bondview2.c` by coincidence: its default arm steps 4 bytes into the record and reads the zero padding (bytes 4 to 7 at 64 bits) as a SPAWN, landing on the next record, which holds only while that padding is zero. The same default arm also covers WATCH, and there the walk mis-steps. The cause is the PC arm of `INTRO_TYPE` (`src/game/bondview.h:2574`), which takes a type word's top byte: after the 4-byte step into a WATCH record the walk reads the `hours` word as a type by its top byte, so a small value reads as type 0, a 12-byte SPAWN. On the N64 (`bondview.h:2572`) the type is the whole word, so `hours` and `minutes` are unknown types that step 4 bytes each and the walk stays in step. This walk is `mp_respawn_handler`'s (`bondview2.c`), run when a multiplayer player respawns after dying; it acts only on ITEM and AMMO records (the start weapons and ammunition, given again) and steps over the rest. Worked example, the 32-bit walk over stock Dam (`assets/obseg/setup/UsetupdamZ.c`, words counted from the intro's start): six cameras, then the WATCH at word 60 (hours 11, minutes 30); the walk reads 11 at word 61 as a SPAWN and steps to word 64 (the spawn's index 33, again a SPAWN), then 67 (the first swirl's 2, a SPAWN), then 70 (0x14300000, type 20, a 4-byte step), then 71 (0x8000, a SPAWN), and is back in step at word 74, the second swirl. It skips the SPAWN at word 63 and the swirl at word 66, which this walk ignores, so on Dam it loses nothing it acts on. The tree has a source for each of the 34 stock setup files: `scripts/filelist.u.csv` lists 34 setup `.bin` files, 26 under `assets/obseg/setup` and 8 under `assets/obseg/setup/u`, and each has its `.c` beside it. 13 are multiplayer setups (`Ump_`), and none of them has a WATCH record (no `_mkshort(0, 7))` in any of the 13). The walk's only caller is `mp_respawn_handler`, reached only on a multiplayer respawn, and with two or more players `prop.c` loads the `Ump_` file; so the mis-step does not run in the shipped 32-bit game's multiplayer respawn path. Of the 21 solo setups, 20 have a WATCH record (all but Len). A scratch simulation of the walk's rule over all 34 sources (deleted afterwards) shows what it would do over those 20 if it ever ran there: in 18 the walk skips the first ITEM after the WATCH, a start weapon (17 where a SPAWN follows the WATCH, and Crad, where the ITEM follows it directly); over Dam it skips only a SPAWN and a swirl; over Depot it reads a word with top byte 9 as the end and stops early, skipping only swirl records. It misreads no other word as an ITEM or AMMO record, though any `hours` or `minutes` value whose top byte is 1 or 2 would be. What remains unverified is that the sources in the tree match the ROM's files, which this record takes as given (`port/generated/setup_kinds.h` was generated by comparing the two). **At 64 bits** the converter writes a pad word only before a CAMERA or CREDITS record that would start at 4 mod 8 (`romconv_setup_intro.c`'s `introWalk`), so: a WATCH followed by a record that needs no pad overshoots exactly as at 32 bits (a test pins this with Dam's order, WATCH, SPAWN, ITEM: at both widths the walk skips the SPAWN and the ITEM and lands on the end); a WATCH followed by a CREDITS record ends correctly with or without a pad, because the overshoot lands on the credits record's zero padding word, read as a SPAWN; a WATCH followed by a CAMERA with a pad lands on the camera's start where at 32 bits it lands 4 bytes into the camera, so the path differs between widths. The every-kind fixture's `bondview2.c` walk reaches the end at 64 bits because a CREDITS record follows its WATCH there, and at 32 bits stops at the credits table word, whose top byte decides the rest. The fix is explicit WATCH and CREDITS arms in `src/game/bondview2.c`, a strict-tier file this task does not edit; it would change the 32-bit game's behaviour wherever the walk mis-steps today, so it is a decision for the owner, not a 64-bit-only repair. (3) `port/src/romconv_setup_records.c` (318): the header (ten offsets from the output's start, zero-extended; `SETUP_PROMOTE` is unchanged) and the record writers. Every reference (`plink`, the waypoint and waygroup lists, a path's list, an AI list's code, a name) goes through `portConvMapGet`, and a miss refuses the file. The map is 4-byte grained, so names and AI code, which may start at any byte, are resolved inside the runs of slots no item owns: those runs are copied whole and every slot mapped, a reference resolves to `map(value & ~3) + (value & 3)`, and it is valid only in such a run, with its NUL (a name) or an `AI_EndList` byte (AI code) before the run ends. The AI check is a necessary condition only; the converter does not parse AI commands, whose sizes are game code (`chraiitemsize`). Bytes nobody names are copied unchanged. (4) `port/src/romconv_setup.c` (226): items laid out in the file's order, each at its output alignment (8 for records holding pointers), `portSetupConvertedSize` (rounded up to 8) and `portSetupConvert` (refuses a NULL, misaligned, short or overlapping output, writing nothing; clears the output, writes each item with a backstop against the measured footprint; frees the map on every path). (5) `port/src/romconv_setup_props.c` (44): `portSetupPropsSize` and `portSetupPropsConvert`, stubs that accept only a prop list that is the end record alone and refuse anything else ("holds records the prop converter does not convert"). The declarations are in `port/include/port_romconv_stage.h` and the file layouts (`RomSetupHeader`, `RomPad`, `RomBoundPad`, `RomWaypoint`, `RomWaygroup`, `RomPath`, `RomAiList`, `RomCreditsEntry` and the intro records) in `port/include/port_romlayout_stage.h`, since `port_romconv.h` is at its length limit. (6) Shared code: `src/bondtypes.h`'s `SetupIntroCredits.unk04` is `uintptr_t` under `IS_64_BIT`, and `src/game/bondview_r.c` adds the setup file's base to it under `IS_64_BIT`, the 32-bit line unchanged under `#else`. (7) `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts the setup records' sizes at both widths and the camera's field offsets. (8) Tests, every byte invented: `scripts/port/test_romconv_setup_build.h` (274, the fixture builder), `test_romconv_setup.c` (the brief's assertions, every table, list, name, the intro walked by `sizeof`, the camera and credits, `bondview2.c`'s walk over the credits record, and at 32 bits equality with `romfile_setup.c`'s in-place result) and `test_romconv_setup_checks.c` (297; every walk bounded, wrong kinds, overlaps, buffers, 10000 random and 10000 mutated files each converted in exactly the bytes measured or refused with nothing written), run by `test_romconv.sh` at both widths, the 64-bit half under the sanitizers. **Departures from the plan:** the output keeps the file's order; the converter is split over five files to stay under 500 lines; the intro pad word; the extra refusals above. **Finding:** where one s32 list starts inside another, `romfile_setup.c` swaps the shared words twice, leaving them big-endian; the converter swaps each once. No stock list shares words, so the stock ROM is unaffected, and the 32-bit equality test uses a fixture without nested lists. Once the oracle compares setup files (Task 15), a file where two lists share words will show a difference there, because the converter swaps those words once and the in-place pass twice: the oracle will be correctly flagging the in-place defect, and the stock ROM has no such file. **Stock sweep** (a scratch harness, deleted afterwards with the setup files it extracted; nothing ROM-derived is committed): the 34 setup files, with a scratch prop double that copied prop records by their kinds. At 32 bits 0 refused and 0 differ from the in-place pass (the credits word compared relative to each buffer), 1,600,720 bytes. At 64 bits 0 refused, 1,600,720 bytes to 1,760,968 (props at their file size), smallest Ump_setupoatZ 6560 to 7104, largest UsetupdamZ 81808 to 90688, sanitizer clean. Counted: 7019 pads, 2828 bound pads, 2902 waypoints, 341 waygroups, 92 paths, 661 AI lists (none at an odd offset), 851 pad names and 98 bound pad names, 63 cameras, one credits record with 271 entries, and one intro pad word at 64 bits (UsetuplenZ, before its credits record).

*Checks:* the oracle (task check step 5, i686, `--classes "animation tables,text banks,audio banks,music sequences,textures,fonts,models,backgrounds,collision tiles"`, setup files not yet among them): every class 0 differ (`collision tiles: 47 files`, `backgrounds: 45`, `models: 512`, `textures: 2506`, Task 13 counted 2508), boot and 20 missions ran, exit 0. Boot checks on aarch64, plain and sanitizer (`build/lp64/boot`, `boot-san`): `lp64_boot.py --stage dam --expect-stop "setup files"` and `--stage caverns --expect-stop "setup files"` print `OK: stopped at "setup files"`, and `--expect-run --frames 600` prints `OK: ran 600 frames`; the stop does not move, so the x86_64 boot was not run. `test_romconv.sh`: `PASS (64-bit)` on aarch64, `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` in i686. `test_abi_probe.sh`: OK at 64 bits on aarch64, at 32 and 64 bits in x86_64. Step 1 in the aarch64 container and, as CI lines, in the x86_64 container: `gate: 352 files compiled, 0 failed`, `gate-video: 383 files compiled, 0 failed`, `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files, all allowed`, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files, all allowed`. Step 2: the i686 build and its 20-mission smoke, 20 of 20 passed, exit 0. Step 3: `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` (HEAD f6e2e6d) with this change: `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`, exit 0. The 54 command lines of the CI tests step in the x86_64 container (`test_buffers.sh` without `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE`, whose sanitized 32-bit half hangs under qemu-i386): `harness lines: 54, failures: 0`, among them `lp64_casts.py check`: `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`. *LP64-004 task 14, review fixes (2026-11-17).* A commit after "Add the setup file converter for the tables and the intro". (1) A second intro fixture, `scripts/port/test_romconv_setup_intro.c` (new, 404 lines, run by `test_romconv.sh` at both widths, the 64-bit half under the sanitizers): the main fixture with its intro replaced by one record of every kind the kinds table has (SPAWN, ITEM, AMMO, SWIRL, ANIM, CUFF, CAMERA, WATCH, CREDITS, END), every word an invented value that differs from its neighbours and changes under a byte swap, the type words a u16, a byte and the type. It reproduces the three intro walks the game has by their stepping rules: `bondview_r.c`'s and `prop.c`'s visit every record and pad word and reach the end at both widths. `bondview2.c`'s, whose default arm steps 4 bytes over WATCH, CREDITS and any other type, misreads the WATCH at both widths (it reads `hours`, 11, as type 0 and steps 12 more, 4 bytes past the WATCH's end): at 64 bits that lands on the credits record, past the pad word, and the credits record's zero padding then reads as a SPAWN, so the walk reaches the end; at 32 bits it lands on the credits record's table word, an address, whose top byte decides the rest, so the test follows the walk only that far. *LP64-004, the player's gait model storage (2026-11-17). Commit "Give the player's gait model room for a 64-bit Model".* Found by Task 15, whose setup converter lets a 64-bit Dam start get past the setup load for the first time. `initBondDATAdefaults.c` and `bondhead.c` use `&g_CurrentPlayer->model` as the gait model itself, held in the player's words from `model` to `field_650` (0xBC bytes, the 32-bit `Model`), with its read-write data from `field_654`. LP64-003 gave the watch and hand models a `Model` union at 64 bits but not this one: the 64-bit `Model` is 264 bytes, so it ran 72 bytes into `gait_rwdata_slots` (model at 1792, read-write data at 1984). `modelInitRwData` then wrote a float over `unka0`, the model's callback, and `sub_GAME_7F06D490` (`model.c:1105`, reached from `initBondDATAdefaults.c:175`, `lv.c:957`) called it: the aarch64 executables stopped at `pc 0x42d8999b` (a SIGBUS, with ASan `BUS on unknown address`) right after `ge: mp spawn p0`. At 64 bits `src/game/bondview.h` now holds the run from `model` to `field_650` in a union with `Model gait_model_storage`, as the watch model's run does, so the read-write data starts at 2056; the 32-bit layout is untouched. This commit left two readers wrong at 64 bits: `animFlipFlag` and `field_5C0` are the model's `gunhand` and `animframe1` only in the 32-bit run, and at 64 bits they land on a byte of `scale` and on padding; the note "the gait run's named fields" below fixes them. `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts at 64 bits that the run holds a `Model`; without the header change that assertion fails (`the player's gait model run holds a Model`). *Checks:* `test_abi_probe.sh`: OK at 64 bits on aarch64, at 32 and 64 bits in x86_64. With Task 15's working tree, the plain aarch64 Dam run that faulted reaches `ge: frame limit reached: frames=600`, exit 0. `lp64_casts.py check`: `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`. The Windows comparison of this commit is recorded in the Task 15 note. On its own this commit changes nothing a run reaches: a 64-bit mission still stops at `setup files`.

*LP64-004 task 15, setup files: the prop records and the wiring (2026-11-17). Task 15 built: commit "Convert setup files at load on a 64-bit build".* The tenth class marked converted: a 64-bit Dam start now loads its setup file and runs 600 frames, plain and under the sanitizers, on aarch64 and on x86_64. (1) `port/src/romconv_setup_props.c` (196 lines) replaces Task 14's stubs. `struct PortSetupWide {filewords, widewords, npointers, pointerword[16]}` and `portSetupWide(type)` (declared in `port/include/port_romconv_stage.h`; NULL past type 48) give each prop record type its file size, its run-time size and the file words that hold a pointer. The rule: each file word is swapped by its kind (`port/generated/setup_kinds.h`; `portSetupKindWord`, now exported from `romconv_setup_intro.c`), a pointer word goes to the next 8-aligned offset and is written as 8 bytes, zero-extended, and the record is padded to `widewords`. At 32 bits `widewords` equals `filewords` and nothing moves, so the output equals the in-place image byte for byte. `portSetupPropsSize` and `portSetupPropsConvert` share one measuring walk (known type, record inside the list, the rule's bytes within `widewords`, the list ending exactly at `PROPDEF_END`) and refuse by name otherwise, writing nothing. **The table was derived from the code that reads each record, not from the brief**, which had none: the `ObjectRecord` types have pointers at words 4, 5, 26 and 27 (prop, model, the collision block and projectile; 144 bytes at 64 bits) plus their own (door 50, 51, 61, 62; collectable 33; monitor 32, 34; multi-monitor 32, 34, 61, 63, 90, 92, 119, 121; autogun 49 to 51; vehicle 32, 41, 43; aircraft 32, 43, 44); guard 6; link 1, 2; switch and lock door 1 to 3; tag 2, 3; photograph, enter room and watch-menu text 3; deposit in room 4; rename 8, 9 (read as `textoverride`); safe item 1 to 4. Glass, safe and gas-releasing records are read as `ObjectRecord`; objective start (`objective_entry`), camera position and guard attribute hold no pointer. CCTV's C record is 63 words against the file's 59, a link's is read only through `Index1`/`Index2`, copy-item is one file word against an 8-byte record and type 41 is one file word read as `ObjectRecord`: for these four the fixture checks the rule, not `sizeof`. The brief's claim that tinted glass differs from its record is wrong: its record matches the file. (2) `src/game/loadobjectmodel.c`: at 64 bits `sizepropdef` returns `widewords` (one pointer's words for an unknown type). (3) `src/game/prop.c`: at 64 bits a setup that did not load from the ROM stops the game by name (no compiled-in setup is linked at 64 bits), and the fix-up loop after the load works by member (`GuardRecord.Preset` and an object's `damage` rotated by 16, `objective_entry`'s `unkC` byte-reversed and `reserved` rotated, the watch-menu text's `reserved` rotated, the guard attribute's `unk8` byte-reversed); the 32-bit word-indexed switch is under `#else`. (4) `src/game/initobjects.c`: `initSetLevelLoadPropSafeItem` writes the safe record's `next` through `struct SafeObjectRecord` at 64 bits. (5) `port/src/romdata.c`: at 64 bits `romdataFilePreprocess`'s setup case measures the image, refuses it by name when it passes the block (`portConvRefuse`, then a fatal error), copies the file to the converter scratch and writes the image into the same block, so `g_ptrStageSetupFile` points at the converted image, and stores the image's size in the entry's `poolRemaining`, which `fileIndexLoadToBank` commits after the call; the capacity is the entry's `rom_remaining`, which the load functions record before loading (`fileGetCapacity`, Task 11). It logs `ge: romdata: setup NAME converted: N bytes from the file's M, in a C-byte block`. In the oracle build the case calls `romfileSetupOracle` (new `port/src/romconv_setup_oracle.c`, 154 lines: the in-place pass, the converter into new memory, the credits table word compared as an offset, then a byte comparison), and `portSetupOracleSweep` counts as differing any setup the ROM holds that is not served. (6) `port_lp64.c` marks `setup files` converted; `GE_LP64_TEST_UNCONVERTED` (never defined by CMake) lets `test_lp64_address.sh` build a driver whose setup class is still unconverted, so the status-5 stop and `lp64_boot.py --expect-stop` stay tested. **Departures:** `src/game/ob.c` is unchanged: the brief had ob.c call `romdataFileConvert(index, data, size, capacity)`, but ob.c is at the 628-line limit of the standards check and three wrapped call sites took it to 641, so the conversion sits in `romdataFilePreprocess` and reads the capacity ob.c already records (a load to an address through its second branch does not record it; no setup loads that way). The oracle lives in its own file, not `romfile_setup.c`. `port_romconv.h` and `lp64_oracle.py` are unchanged. **Prop-list walkers:** all step in 4-byte units by `sizepropdef`, so all follow `widewords` at 64 bits: `prop.c` `load_proptype` (77), `portMeasurePropDefs` (1498, compiled-in setups only, never at 64 bits), `portLintSetup` (1723), `portPropDump` (1886), the fix-up loop (2128, 32-bit; the 64-bit one walks the same way), 2719 and 2894; `cleanup_objects.c:83` (`u32 *`); `loadobjectmodel.c` 286, 315, 343 and 599; `objective_status.c:205`. Records are then read through their C types, which the table matches; `setupGetCommandIndexByProp` (`loadobjectmodel.c`) reads `->prop` of every record, also of records with no such field, an inherited over-read that this task leaves as it is. **Sizes** (64-bit probe, `GE_ROMPROBE=1`, aarch64): the 34 setups grow from 1,600,720 to 1,874,552 bytes, 12.3% (UsetuplenZ, 9328 to 10480) to 20.3% (Ump_setupstatueZ, 17616 to 21200); the largest is UsetupjunZ, 103424 to 120552; every image is 8-aligned. *LP64-004 task 15, the setup oracle's cast check (2026-11-17). Commit "Rebase the setup oracle's credits word at full width".* `python3 scripts/port/lp64_casts.py check` failed on a9b5f36 with `port/src/romconv_setup_oracle.c: 1 truncating casts, allowed 0` (line 71, `(u32) (uintptr_t) image`): Task 15 ran the check before the new file was added to Git, so its report's `OK` did not cover it, and CI's tests step would have failed. The declaration is fixed, not the allowlist: the credits word is read into a `uintptr_t` and rebased there, and written back whole; the file is compiled only in the 32-bit oracle build, which a `_Static_assert` on `sizeof(uintptr_t) == 4` now states.
