*LP64-004, the gait run's named fields (2026-11-17). Commit "Read the gait model's flip and frame through its Model on a 64-bit build".* Found by the review of Task 15. The player's words from `model` to `field_650` (`src/game/bondview.h`) are the gait `Model` at 32 bits, and two of their names are read as model fields: `bheadFlipAnimation` (`src/game/bondhead.c`), the gait model's flip callback in every mission (`initBondDATAdefaults.c` installs it, `model.c` calls it each time the gait animation loops), toggles `animFlipFlag`, which at 32 bits is `Model.gunhand` (run offset 36), the flip the model applies; and the gait switch (`bheadAdjustAnimation`) takes its start frame from `field_5C0`, `Model.animframe1` (run offset 40), and passes `animFlipFlag` to `modelSetAnimation` as the flip. At 64 bits `gunhand` is at 72 and `animframe1` at 76, while `animFlipFlag` stays at 40 (the low byte of the 64-bit `Model.scale`) and `field_5C0` at 44 (padding after `scale`). So since 9f37737 a 64-bit run flipped the low byte of the gait model's scale on every gait loop (0.1f is 0x3DCCCCCD; the byte went 0xCD to 0, then 1 and 0, a change of at most 205 units in the last place, about 1.5e-6 in a scale of 0.1), never alternated the gait's mirror, and started each gait change from the padding word, which nothing writes, instead of the current frame. The gait model drives only the first-person head bob (`bondheadmatrices`); nothing indexes memory by these values, so the Dam runs of Task 15 had a slightly different head bob, no memory fault. At 64 bits the three sites now use `gait_model_storage.gunhand` and `.animframe1`; the 32-bit lines are unchanged under `#else`. **Every name in the run** was checked against every reader and writer in `src/` and `port/src/` (by member name and by raw player offsets; strict-tier files read only): only those two names are used, both in `bondhead.c`, which is not strict-tier, and the player's `model` member itself is used only as `&g_CurrentPlayer->model`, the run's address. At 64 bits `model` (unk00) and `field_59C` (chr) still meet their fields; every other name is displaced (for instance `field_5C4`, 32-bit `unk2c`, lands on `attachedto`; `field_5D4`, `endframe`, on `anim`). `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` pins the aliasing: `GAIT_RUN(name, field, how)` asserts at 32 bits that each of the 50 names is at its `Model` field's offset, and at 64 bits that every name marked `GAIT_SAME` still is; `GAIT_BRANCHED` marks the two names whose readers take the 64-bit field, and `GAIT_UNREAD` the 46 no code reads, which `scripts/port/test_abi_probe.sh` checks by searching `src/` and `port/src/` for a member access to any of them. Marking `animFlipFlag` `GAIT_SAME` fails the 64-bit probe (`gait run animFlipFlag is Model.gunhand`), and marking it `GAIT_UNREAD` fails the search, naming the `bondhead.c` lines. **Tightened in the second review (2026-11-17, commit "Check every gait run name the probe declares"):** the probe declares its line count (`GAIT_RUN_NAMES 50`) and the test fails unless it parses exactly that many `GAIT_RUN` lines across the three kinds, so a differently formatted line no longer drops out; the search allows spaces after `->` or `.`; and each `GAIT_BRANCHED` name must have a reader. The test's comment says what it still does not catch: an access split across lines, a name built by token pasting or reached by raw offset, and whether every reader of a BRANCHED name takes the 64-bit field. Each new failure was seen with a scratch edit (a line with a space after the parenthesis, `field_5A0` marked BRANCHED, a `p-> field_5A4` read), restored afterwards. *Checks:* `test_abi_probe.sh` OK at 64 bits on aarch64 and at 32 and 64 bits in x86_64; `lp64_casts.py check` OK; `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` against a9b5f36, recorded in the Task 15 fix report; the boot runs after all of this round's fixes are in the note "task 15, review fixes" below.

*LP64-004, stage-bank records sized by literals (2026-11-17). Commit "Size the player, the inventory and the anim model slots by their records on a 64-bit build".* The third defect of the family after `g_ModelHitEntries` (69759f6) and the gait model's room (9f37737); the earlier sweep looked at global arrays, not at stage-bank allocations. **What overran:** `alloc_additional_item_slots` (`src/game/inititemslots.c`) allocated `equipmaxitems * 0x14` bytes, the 32-bit `struct InvItem`, and `bondinvReinitInv` (`bondinv.c`) then wrote `.type` of each of the `equipmaxitems` items (30 plus the stage's extra slots) at the 64-bit stride of 32 bytes, so every 64-bit mission wrote up to 12 bytes an item past its block, Dam included, into whatever the stage bank allocated next. And `initBONDdataforPlayer` (`src/game/player.c`), found by this sweep, allocated every player as 0x2A80 bytes (US/JP; 0x2A70 for EU), the 32-bit `struct player`, which is 0x30A0 bytes at 64 bits, so every 64-bit mission's player ran 1568 bytes past its block from the moment it was written. The Task 15 Dam runs, sanitizer included, ran with both overruns: the stage bank is one allocation, so AddressSanitizer saw every write as in bounds. Now `inititemslots.c` sizes the inventory by `sizeof(struct InvItem)` at both widths (0x14 at 32 bits, so the 32-bit program is unchanged), and at 64 bits `player.c` allocates `sizeof(struct player)` (the 32-bit literals stay under `#elif`). **The anim model slots** (`modelmgrAllocateAnimModelSlots`, `src/game/initunk_005520.c`) are allocated as `count * (4 + sizeof(struct AnimModelSlot))` and indexed at `sizeof(struct AnimModelSlot)`: the slot is a `Model` (0xBC bytes at 32 bits, 264 at 64), and the 4 is the N64's spare word a slot (the original allocated `count * 0xC0`). At 32 bits 0xC0 keeps the bank 16-aligned; at 64 bits 268 a slot left the bank cursor at 4 mod 8 after an odd count, and the next stage records that hold pointers, which need 8-byte alignment (the model converter refuses an output that is not, and UBSan reports a misaligned `struct InvItem`), started misaligned: Caverns and Facility stopped there. At 64 bits the same bytes are rounded up to 16, as the 32-bit stride keeps the bank. `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` pins `sizeof(struct InvItem)` (0x14 / 32), the 64-bit player outgrowing the literal, and the slot record (0xBC at 32 bits, a multiple of 8 at 64). **The sweep** of the stage-start allocations in `src/game/init*.c` sized by a literal or a count times a literal: `inititemslots.c:19` (InvItem, 20 / 32 bytes; fixed); `initunk_005520.c:77` (AnimModelSlot, 188 / 264, plus 4; fixed as above); `initintromatrices.c:9-15` (0x80 and 0x40 bytes of `Mtx`, 64 bytes at both widths; correct); `initmenus.c:34` (0x78000 bytes, a byte arena that the legal screen, logos and gun barrel load models and display lists into, each load bounded by a byte count, and models converted by Task 11 refuse an output that does not fit; correct as an arena) (superseded by fix waves A and B: not correct for everything placed in it, since at 64 bits the gun barrel's display list was skipped as 32 commands of 8 bytes in `title.c` and the briefing's language bank was stepped as `argg / 8` commands in `front.c`, neither bounded by its byte count; see those notes); `initmenus.c:37,39` (video buffers in pixels; correct); `initobjects.c:72` (`g_MaxNumRooms * 4` bytes of `s16`, 2 bytes at both widths; correct); `initBondDATA.c:241,245` (the hand weapon buffers, byte arenas sized by `gun.c`'s table; correct as arenas). Outside `init*.c`, beside the player: `prop.c`'s 0x30-byte autogun beam (`struct beam`, 44 bytes at both widths) and `propobj.c`'s two 0x50-byte collision blocks (`collision_data`, 76 at both) fit; `vtxstore.c`'s `* 0x10` arrays hold `Vertex`, 16 bytes at both widths. **Correction (second review, 2026-11-17):** the sweep missed `src/game/model.c:158`, the reset-time anim model slot (`modelmgrInstantiateModel` while `g_ModelIsLvResetting`, when no slot among the first `g_MaxAnimModelSlots - ANIM_MODEL_RESET_SPARE` is free), allocated as `4 + sizeof(struct AnimModelSlot)` bytes: 0xC0 at 32 bits, 268 at 64, which leaves the cursor at 4 mod 8. Its record fits; the defect is the alignment of the next block. So not every allocation the sweep listed as fitting is harmless at 64 bits: "correct" above means the record fits its block, and the font tables and that slot fit but misaligned what followed (corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H: that slot did; the font tables are 0x27B0 and 0x3840 bytes at 64 bits and misalign nothing). `model.c` is strict-tier and unedited; the allocator note below makes all three harmless. *Checks:* in the note "task 15, review fixes" below.

*LP64-004 task 15, review fixes (2026-11-17).* Commit "Consume the setup block's capacity and record what the 64-bit runs cover", after the three commits above. (1) **The wiring stands as built** (the coordinator's ruling: `src/game/ob.c` is at the repository's 628-line limit and cannot take the brief's call sites). Its one hole: `fileIndexLoadToAddr`'s second branch never sets `rom_remaining`, so the capacity `romdataFilePreprocess` read there would have been an earlier load's. The setup case now consumes the capacity: it reads the entry's `rom_remaining`, sets it to 0, and `romdataSetupConvert` refuses by name a capacity below the file's size (`The setup file NAME loaded into a block of N bytes, below its M`), so a path that records none reads 0 and stops instead of using a stale block. Nothing else reads a setup entry's `rom_remaining` after its load: the readers are `get_rom_remaining_buffer_for_index` and `fileGetCapacity`, called only from `objecthandler_2.c` for model files, `fileSetSize`, which writes it, and the boot probe, which saves and restores the whole entry around each load; every load function writes it again before its next load. (2) Comments made true: `romdataSetupConvert`'s comment says the copy and the offset map use the scratch reserved at boot and that the checking pass mallocs and frees a buffer for the prop list's output on every load (its earlier "no stock setup allocates" was wrong), and `port/include/romdata.h` says that at 64 bits `romdataFilePreprocess` reads and clears a setup's `rom_remaining` and writes its converted size to `poolRemaining`. (3) **What has run at 64 bits**, on this commit: Dam, Caverns and Facility each run 600 frames, plain and under the sanitizers, on aarch64 and on x86_64 (`lp64_boot.py --stage NAME --expect-run --frames 600`: `OK: ran 600 frames` for all twelve runs). Each run's `ge: lp64:` lines are the address line, `audio bank sfxctl: 16448 bytes of run-time records`, `audio bank instrumentsctl: 10520 bytes`, `music sequence table musicsampletbl: 63 sequences, 1016 bytes` and the stage's `bg tables` line (Dam 139 rooms, 195 portal entries, 8688 bytes; Caverns 66, 77, 3880; Facility 80, 110, 4968); no pool, refusal or stop line. The other 17 missions have not been run at 64 bits; that is the next task's smoke. The other 31 setups were converted at 64 bits only by the boot probe (`GE_ROMPROBE=1`), never walked by the game. Which object records the three missions load at 64 bits (`GE_PROPDUMP=1`, which lists the object-shaped records by type): Dam doors, props, keys, alarms, collectables, monitors, 4 multi-monitors, hats, ammo, glass and tinted glass; Caverns the same kinds with 10 multi-monitors and 3 autoguns; Facility also 19 gas-releasing records. None of them loads a CCTV, vehicle, aircraft, safe or tank record; the dump does not list the other kinds (links, tags, safe items, lock doors, renames, objective records), which were not counted. The record types not loaded here are covered only by the table tests (`test_romconv_setup_props.c`) and by reading the code, until the 20-mission run. *Checks:* on this commit's tree: `test_abi_probe.sh` OK at 64 bits on aarch64 and at 32 and 64 bits in x86_64; `test_romconv.sh` `PASS (64-bit)` on aarch64, `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` in i686; the oracle with the ten classes, `setup files: 54 files, 0 differ` and every other class 0 differ (`textures: 2510 files`), `the ROM holds 34 setup files`, boot and 20 missions ran, exit 0; the twelve boot runs above; step 1 in the aarch64 container (`gate-a64`, `gate-video-a64`) and in the x86_64 container: `353 files compiled, 0 failed`, `384 files compiled, 0 failed`, `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files, all allowed`, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files, all allowed`; step 2, the i686 build and its 20-mission smoke, 20 of 20 PASS, exit 0; the 45 CI harness lines besides the configure, build and gate lines (x86_64 container, `test_buffers.sh` without `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE`): `harness lines: 45, failures: 0`, among them `lp64_casts.py check`, `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`. `compare_win32.py commits` for each commit of this round against the one before it (a9b5f36 to the oracle commit, to the gait commit, to the sizing commit, to this commit's tree): `identical in loaded code and data`, exit 0 each.

*LP64-004 task 15, an 8-aligned bank cursor at 64 bits (2026-11-17). Commit "Keep every bank block 8-aligned on a 64-bit build".* The N64 and 32-bit allocators round nothing: each caller rounds its own request (most with ALIGN16), and a block starts wherever the last one ended. At 64 bits a block holding pointers needs 8-byte alignment, and three stage-bank callers ask for sizes that are not multiples of 8: the font tables (`textrelated.c:153,171`, each its ROM length) (corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H: not the font tables, which at 64 bits ask for their label spans, 0x27B0 and 0x3840 bytes, Task 9 having padded them to 16), the anim model slots (`initunk_005520.c:77-83`, rounded to 16 at 64 bits by the sizing commit above) and the reset-time slot at `model.c:158` (268 bytes; strict-tier). Now `portMempAllocate` and `portMempResize` (`port/src/port_memp.c`), at 64 bits only, move the cursor past a block's end to the next multiple of 8 from the bank's start, never past the bank's end; banks start 16-aligned (`mempSetBankStarts`), so every block starts 8-aligned. The 32-bit lines are unchanged under `#else`. Why it is safe, from every reader of the cursor: a block still starts exactly at the cursor, so `mempGetBankSizeLeft`'s bytes still fit exactly (ob.c's whole-remainder load at `ob.c:315-330` and its trim through `mempAddEntryOfSizeToBank`, and `fileSetSize`, `ob.c:479`, which resize the last block in place and keep its start); `mempResetBank` sets the cursor to the bank's start and `mempNullNextEntryInBank` to 0, as before; nothing outside `src/memp.c` and `port_memp.c` reads `g_mempPools`; and no caller treats two blocks as one (`dyn.c`'s second and third buffers are offsets inside one block, every other paired allocation, the intro matrices, the hand weapon buffers, `vtxstore.c`'s arrays and the explosion buffers, keeps its own pointer). The caller-side paddings (the anim slots' round to 16) are now redundant at 64 bits but kept. Whether a stock run reaches `model.c:158`: counted with a temporary log line in a scratch build (removed afterwards; `model.c` is unedited), 0 times in the title, Dam, Caverns and Facility, 600 frames each on aarch64. The stage bank's use at the end of each level reset, measured the same way with the allocator change and without it, is identical (title 3,624,336 bytes, Dam 4,098,008, Caverns 4,132,064, Facility 4,002,704, of 66,805,760; the cursor 8-aligned at both ends of each reset), so on those runs the change inserts no byte. `scripts/port/test_memory_banks.c` (run by `test_buffers.sh` at both widths) allocates 13 bytes and checks where the next block starts (16 bytes on at 64 bits, 13 at 32), trims a block to 3 bytes, and checks that a request for `mempGetBankSizeLeft`'s bytes gets them all, in the stage bank, with no fallback; without the allocator change it fails at 64 bits at the first check. *Checks:* in the Task 15 report's "Fix round 2".

*LP64-004 task 16, the 20 missions at 64 bits and the load census (2026-11-17). Task 16 built: commit "Run the 20 missions on a 64-bit build and compare what they load"; its review's fixes: commit "Make the census smoke's fixed tick an option and record what the runs cover".* **The 20 missions:** the plain 64-bit executable runs all 20 on aarch64 and on x86_64, and the sanitizer executable on aarch64, 20 of 20 `PASS` each: for 600 frames on the game clock at the base commit (2da378d), and for 1800 frames at one field a frame with the change (below). No run stopped, so no defect was found or fixed. No log has a pool, refusal, converter or stop line or a sanitizer report. **How owner decision 3's "with no `ge: lp64:` line" is read** (the controller's reading when this note was written; the owner accepted that reading on 2026-11-17 ("Accept the reading", in the session that closed LP64-004, as that session relayed it)): no pool, refusal, converter or stop line; the informational lines every 64-bit run prints are allowed. The informational kinds, each printed once a run or once a file: `address space OK` (`port/src/port_lp64.c`, the boot's address check), `audio bank NAME: N bytes of run-time records` (`port/src/audio_stubs.c`, the sfxctl and instrumentsctl banks), `music sequence table NAME: ...` (`audio_stubs.c`), `bg tables NAME: ...` (`port/src/romfile_bg.c`, each stage's background), and in the oracle build only the `oracle:` lines (`port/src/port_lp64_oracle.c`, `romconv_*_oracle.c`); a `DIFFERS` line among them passes a smoke mission and fails `lp64_oracle.py`, which judges each class by its `N files, M differ` total (added in the LP64-004 fix wave H; fix wave G pins it in a test). The kinds that fail a mission, each with what catches it: `pool "NAME" exhausted` and `cannot convert CLASS "FILE": ...` by the smoke's markers (`REFUSAL_MARKERS` in `scripts/port/lp64_boot.py`, shared by `audit_buffers.py`), whatever the exit status; `stopping: asset class ...` by its exit status 5; the address check's failures (`... is below 4 GB`, `the executable image has no loaded segments`, `malloc block ... could not be allocated`) by exit status 4; `converter scratch: cannot allocate` and `converter map: cannot reserve` by `EXIT_FAILURE`; `converter map: a second map while one is in use` by the `cannot convert` line its caller prints next. `scripts/port/test_audit_buffers.py` holds the reading: a log with each informational kind passes, a log with each marker line fails, and a run that stops with status 5 fails. This task adds no kind to the `ge: lp64:` namespace: the setup image's byte line is `ge: romconv: setup NAME image: ...` (nothing parses it; the census leaves it out). **The census:** `scripts/port/lp64_census.py` `compare DIR32 DIR64` takes, for each mission log of two smoke folders, the multiset of `ge: romdata:` lines naming a model, a setup, a stan, a bg file or a text bank, with their counts (runs of spaces made one, order ignored), and exits 0 only if every mission's two multisets are equal and the 32-bit one has at least one line of each of the five kinds; otherwise it prints each failing mission's first line found at one width only. It leaves out every other line, among them the `ge: lp64:` lines, the `ge: romconv:` setup image line, and the `seg`, `brief` and `texture table` lines; its help says so and names `--fixed-tick`. `types DIR` sums the `ge: census:` lines below; an opcode beyond the name table is listed as unknown. `scripts/port/test_lp64_census.py` (9 tests, sample logs written in the test: equal sets in another order with other padding pass; a missing model fails and is named; a count that differs fails; a model loaded twice at one width fails; a mission with no model line fails though both sides are equal; a missing log fails; `types` lists loaded and unloaded kinds; an opcode above 24 is listed as unknown; no census line fails) is in the CI tests step. **What the converters print:** before this change the 64-bit logs had no model line (the in-place model pass that prints it does not run at 64 bits), a stan line with only the byte count and a setup line in another form, so `compare` failed every mission. At 64 bits, after a successful write, `romconv_model.c` prints `model NAME converted (N nodes, V verts, D DLs)` from the converter's own walk (`romconv_model_walk.c` counts the nodes, render and collision vertices and lists it claims, a called list once), `romconv_setup.c` prints `setup NAME converted (P propdef words, I intro words, N pads)` from the prop list, intro and pad table it claimed, and `romconv_stan.c` prints `stan NAME converted (T tiles, R rooms, B bytes)`, B the tiles' end; `romfile_stan.c`'s byte-count line is removed and `romdata.c`'s setup byte line becomes `ge: romconv: setup NAME image: N bytes from the file's M, in a C-byte block`. With `GE_LP64_CENSUS=1` the model and setup converters also print `ge: census: model NAME opcodes OP=N ...` and `ge: census: setup NAME props TYPE=N ...` (new `port/src/romconv_census.c` and `.h`, `portSetupPropsCount` in `romconv_setup_props.c`). In the oracle build (32 bits) none of these lines is printed, so its logs keep the in-place lines only. ROM-free tests: new `scripts/port/test_romconv_census.c` (the model converter's line equals `romfile_model.c`'s own for a file whose primary list calls its secondary, then the opcode line; the stan line's counts; the census line; at 32 bits nothing), `test_romconv_setup.c` (the setup converter's line equals `romfile_setup.c`'s, now linked at both widths), `test_romconv_setup_props.c` (the type counts), `test_romconv_stan.c` (its "nothing is logged" now allows the `ge: romdata: stan` line at 64 bits); a broken count (lists, pads or tiles) was checked to fail them. **The fixed tick, an option of the smoke:** on the game clock the census differed in 11 missions, all by the first-person weapon and left hand (`GwppksilZ`, `GwppkZ`, `Gmp5ksilZ`, `GfistZ`, `GuziZ`, `Csuit_lf_handZ`), loaded at 32 bits only: they load when the intro's Bond swirl ends, and the emulated 32-bit run, being slower, passed more game fields a frame and ended the swirl inside 600 frames (Frigate: frame ~410 at 32 bits, ~590 at 64). `audit_buffers.py --mission-smoke --fixed-tick` sets `GE_FIXEDTICK=1` (one game field a rendered frame, no clock wait: `src/game/frametiming.c`) and `GE_LP64_CENSUS=1`; without the flag the smoke is as before this task, so the ASan and LSan smokes of `scripts/port/buffer_audit.md` (which documents the flag) keep the game clock, where a slow or long frame advances several fields. `lp64_oracle.py` gains `--fixed-tick` and `--frames N` for its missions (default 600, no flag). `test_audit_buffers.py` checks both forms of the smoke's environment and `test_lp64_oracle.py` that the two options reach the smoke. The task's first commit had made the fixed tick the smoke's default at 600 frames, which covered less: about 10 s of game time a mission, the oracle's missions loading 2473 textures where Tasks 13 to 15 had 2506 to 2510, and no weapon load in Dam, Frigate or Caverns. *The frame count, 1800, measured:* a 64-bit flagged smoke of 3000 frames (aarch64) shows, from the `ge: frame N` markers every 60 frames, the frame window in which each mission first loads its first-person weapon: Egypt (480, 540]; Aztec, Bunker 1 and 2, Control, Facility, Streets and Train (540, 600]; Archives, Frigate and Jungle (600, 660]; Caverns, Cradle, Runway and Severnaya surface 2 (660, 720]; Depot and Statue (720, 780]; Severnaya surface 1 (780, 840]; Silo (900, 960]; Dam (1140, 1200]. The left hand `Csuit_lf_handZ` loads with the weapon in 18 missions; Frigate (`Gmp5ksilZ`) and Caverns (`GuziZ`) load no hand model by frame 3000. So every load is in by frame 1200, and 1800 adds half again as margin; at 1800 the oracle's missions load 2521 textures, more than the 2506 to 2510 of the game-clock runs. *The task check's flagged steps (dated note in `scripts/port/native_64bit_lp64_004.md`, "Task check"):* steps 2, 5, 6 and 7 are run as

    python3 scripts/port/lp64_env.py run --arch i686 -- python3 scripts/port/audit_buffers.py --mission-smoke build/lp64/ref-i686/IronSights --rom /rom/baserom.u.z64 --frames 1800 --fixed-tick --jobs 2 --output build/lp64/ref-i686/smoke.json
    python3 scripts/port/lp64_env.py run --arch i686 -- python3 scripts/port/lp64_oracle.py --rom /rom/baserom.u.z64 --classes "animation tables,text banks,audio banks,music sequences,textures,fonts,models,backgrounds,collision tiles,setup files" --frames 1800 --fixed-tick build/lp64/oracle/IronSights
    python3 scripts/port/lp64_env.py run --arch aarch64 -- python3 scripts/port/audit_buffers.py --mission-smoke build/lp64/boot/IronSights --rom /rom/baserom.u.z64 --frames 1800 --fixed-tick --jobs 4 --output build/lp64/boot/smoke.json
    python3 scripts/port/lp64_census.py compare build/lp64/ref-i686 build/lp64/boot

(the configure and build lines as the plan has them; step 6 also with `build/lp64/boot-san/IronSights` and, in the x86_64 container, a plain tree `build/lp64/boot-x64`). *Census (task check step 7, 1800 frames, flagged):* `compare build/lp64/ref-i686 build/lp64/boot` exits 0, `census: 20 of 20 missions load the same at both widths`, 1031 lines compared (811 model lines, 20 each of setup, stan and bg, 160 text): Dam 55, Facility 60, Runway 44, Severnaya surface 1 59, Bunker 1 65, Silo 51, Frigate 57, Severnaya surface 2 51, Bunker 2 66, Statue 33, Archives 57, Streets 45, Depot 52, Train 50, Jungle 50, Control 48, Caverns 54, Cradle 36, Aztec 56, Egypt 42; also 20 of 20 against the x86_64 and the sanitizer smokes. (At 600 frames before the review: 1008 lines.) *Types* (`types build/lp64/boot`): the setup converter converted every prop record type but 0 NOTHING, 15 DEBRIS, 16 UNK16, 31 OBJECTIVE_NULL and 41 UNK41, among them CCTV (15 records in 4 setups), switches (10 in 3), vehicles (9 in 2), aircraft (6 in 5), tanks (2 in 2), safes (5 in 5), safe items (6 in 4) and lock doors (27 in 4); the game instantiated them at each stage load, but whether each type's own code ran is not established. The model converter loaded node opcodes 1 HEADER, 2 GROUP, 4 DL, 8 LOD, 9 BSP, 10 BBOX, 12 GUNFIRE, 13 SHADOW, 18 SWITCH, 21 GROUPSIMPLE, 22 DLPRIMARY, 23 HEAD and 24 DLCOLLISION. **Verified by fixtures only:** prop record types 0 NOTHING, 15 DEBRIS, 16 UNK16, 31 OBJECTIVE_NULL and 41 UNK41, and model opcodes 0 NULL, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 14, 15 INTERLINK (which no stock model reached here), 16, 17, 19 and 20 (unnamed in `bondconstants.h`). **What the runs exercised:** bank loads of models through `fileGetCapacity` (811 model loads over the 20 missions), character and prop models, the setups of the 17 missions not run before (each converted at its stage load with the in-place pass's counts), the stage load of each mission's rooms, and the first-person weapon's rooms in all 20 missions, with the left hand's in 18 (not Frigate or Caverns). **Not exercised by any run of this milestone:** everything that needs input or more play time than the flagged runs' 1800 fields (about 30 s of game time, no input, the player standing at the start): room streaming as the player moves, many rooms loaded at once, the peak of room memory (the mema heap) and of the stage bank (the figures below are snapshots at a frame limit, not peaks), weapon switches and pickups, combat and deaths, objectives completed, mission ends and the next stage's load; the attract cast (no attract demo runs); sound (a headless build stubs the audio pump, so nothing is synthesized or mixed); the multiplayer path (no multiplayer run); and the model opcodes and prop types above. **Memory, measured with a scratch build (deleted) at the frame limit of 600 frames, one field a frame:** the stage bank (66,805,760 bytes) holds 3,292,688 to 3,816,128 bytes at 32 bits and 3,899,752 to 4,399,552 at 64 (bunker2, 6.6%), 12.4% to 20.0% more; the graphics buffer's doubling (+262,144), the weapon buffers (+105,024), the setup image (Dam +14,624), the bg tables (1,256 to 8,688), the player record (+1,568) and the model images (`GE_MODELTIME=1`: Dam +50,440, Caverns +51,760, Statue +31,040) account for all but about 40 KB (Statue) to 285 KB (Caverns), which the run-time records allocated by `sizeof` take and which was not decomposed further. These are not peaks, and 8 missions had loaded the weapon by then. The 64-bit allocator's 8-byte rounding (a7970b8) inserted no byte in any measured run (corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H from "real": the 1800-frame runs were not instrumented) (207 to 888 stage-bank blocks a run, none padded), so the rounding itself is covered only by `scripts/port/test_memory_banks.c`. The permanent bank holds 113,824 bytes at 32 bits and 114,016 at 64; no allocation spilled into it. Room memory (the mema heap, which the plan left unscaled) has 1,960 to 41,520 bytes less free at 64 bits at that frame limit, its longest free block at least 148,800 bytes (Silo); no room-memory line in any run, but with no movement its peak was not reached. *Checks:* step 1 in the x86_64 and the aarch64 container: `354 files compiled, 0 failed`, `385 files compiled, 0 failed`, `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files, all allowed`, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files, all allowed`. Step 6 (flagged, 1800 frames): plain and sanitizer on aarch64 and plain on x86_64, 20 of 20 PASS each, exit 0, no sanitizer report; the only `ge: lp64:` kinds in their logs are `address space OK`, `audio bank` (two a run), `music sequence table` and `bg tables`, 20 runs each. Step 7: above. `test_romconv.sh`: `PASS (64-bit)` on aarch64, `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` on x86_64. `test_audit_buffers.py` (12 tests), `test_lp64_census.py` (9) and `test_lp64_oracle.py` (14) pass. CI's tests step, all 55 command lines run one by one in the x86_64 container: 54 pass; `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 bash scripts/port/test_buffers.sh` did not finish here, its sanitized 32-bit `test_model_bounds` spinning under `qemu-i386` for over 30 minutes (and, in the i686 container, for 12 minutes; corrected in the LP64-004 fix wave H) and stopped, so it is not established on this Mac; the line's halves run apart pass (`MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64` sanitized, `PASS (64-bit)`; `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=32` unsanitized, `PASS (32-bit)`, and its `test_audit_buffers.py` run). *LP64-004 fix wave A, display-list rooms sized for 8-byte commands (2026-11-17). Commit "Give the pause, watch and gun barrel display lists room for 16-byte commands".* What was wrong: three display lists built by hand in storage sized in bytes for 8-byte N64 commands, which at 64 bits (a `Gfx` is 16 bytes) overran it. Found by the final whole-milestone review, by reading (one confirmed by a compiled layout probe); no run reached any of them, since no 64-bit run has pressed a button or walked a display list. (1) The watch static (`src/game/bondview.h`, written by `bondview2.c` on every pause): the writer emits exactly three commands, `sub_GAME_7F0A3B40`'s vertex load and modify-vertex and the end, with no loop; the room, `buffer_for_watch_static_DL[1]` and the six `s32` fillers after it, is 32 bytes (4 commands) at 32 bits and 40 bytes (2.5 commands) at 64, so the end command's address word overwrote `healthdamagetype` and `eyeheight`. At 64 bits the run is now a union with `Gfx watch_static_dl_storage[3]` (48 bytes, exactly the three commands, no slack), as `gait_model_storage` was done; the 32-bit member list is unchanged and `bondview2.c` (strict tier) is not edited. (2) The pause watch background (`src/game/options.c`, `draw_background_health_and_armor`): `dynAllocate(0xF8)` twice, which `portDynAllocate` rounds to 256 bytes, 16 commands at 64 bits; `draw_watch_background` (`glass2.c`) writes 17 commands without the fan (8 vertex loads, 8 triangle pairs, the end) and 29 with it (2 vertex loads and a triangle pair, then 3 commands for each of 8 steps, a closing triangle pair and the end). `sp3C` always takes the 17 and `sp40` either. Both allocations are now `31 * sizeof(Gfx)`, 0xF8 at 32 bits and 496 bytes at 64: 31 commands of room for at most 29, so there is no 30th, 31st or 32nd command. (3) The gun barrel list (`src/game/title.c`, `initializeGunBarrelIntro`): 0x100 bytes carved for `sub_GAME_7F01BFF8` (`title3.c`), which for 0x1E vertices writes 31 commands (two passes of a 16-vertex load and 14 triangles, then the end), 496 bytes at 64 bits, so commands 16 to 30 lay in the barrel image that `sub_GAME_7F008DE4` expands next. The carving is now `32 * sizeof(Gfx)`, 0x100 at 32 bits and 0x200 at 64. *The menu buffer after the change* (0x78000 bytes, `initmenus.c`): the barrel vertices take 0x200 (30 `Vtx`, 480 bytes, at both widths), the list 0x100 / 0x200, the expanded image 0x40400, with the 0x1A580-byte compressed image copied after it to be read while the expansion writes below it (no overlap: at 64 bits the image is written to [+0x400, +0x40800) and read from [+0x40800, +0x5AD80)), then the texture pool 0x12C00 from the same place; the models get the rest, 150,784 bytes at 32 bits (Task 11's figure) and 150,528 at 64, which the loads bound by that size. The largest stock load there, 48,976 bytes at 64 bits, leaves 101,552 (Task 11's row said 101,808 at 64; corrected in its table). Nothing is placed after the models in this sequence, so nothing is pushed past the buffer's end. *Pinned:* `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts each of the four pause list rooms in the player, from its first member to the next named one, against the commands its writer emits, at both widths: the watch static (3 commands; room 4 at 32 bits, 3 at 64), the screen select backdrop (`2 * WATCH_NUMBER_SCREENS + 1` = 11; room 40 / 22), and each watch bar (built by `buildGaugeBarDL` with 0x2E vertices; the probe counts its loop at run time: 37 commands; room 230 / 115), and that each room is `Gfx`-aligned. A writer that emits more fails the probe only where its count follows a header constant (the backdrop) or once its count here is raised; the other counts are from reading `bondview2.c`, which the probe cannot see. With the `bondview.h` change taken out, the 64-bit probe fails to compile: `static assertion failed: "the watch static list's room"` (aarch64). The options and title counts are constants of the code, not of a header, so no `_Static_assert` can see them; they rest on the reading above. *The storage search* (this commit, repeating the review's and adding two it did not finish): fixed `Gfx` arrays, `(Gfx *)` casts (76 in `src` and `port/src`), lists ended outside the master list, every `dynAllocate` and literal-sized `mempAllocBytesInBank` call, stack and static arrays of literal size cast to a record pointer, and record casts or arguments taking a filler member's address, over `src/` and `port/src/` with the strict tier read. Real: the three above and the briefing's span (the next commit); everything else fits or holds no pointer (the fix-wave report lists each candidate with its verdict). One near miss: `image.c`'s and `bg.c`'s 0x2100-byte stack buffers, handed to the inflater as `struct huft` tables (8 bytes at 32 bits, 16 at 64), are not used on PC: `decompressdata` (`src/game/decompress.c`) routes every caller to its typed 2048-entry workspace. Verification: `test_abi_probe.sh` passes at both widths (x86_64 container: `ABI probe OK (64-bit)`, `ABI probe OK (32-bit)`; aarch64: 64-bit); the Windows comparison of this commit against its parent is identical (fix-wave report).

*LP64-004 fix wave B, the briefing's language bank (2026-11-17). Commit "Place the briefing's language bank after the briefing on a 64-bit build".* What was wrong: `front.c`'s briefing setup puts the briefing file at the menu buffer's +0xA000 with a 0x200-byte limit (`argg`), steps past it with `temp_s0 += argg / 8` on a `Gfx *`, and gives the stage's language bank the rest, `argg * 879` = 450,048 (0x6DE00) bytes. With 8-byte commands the step is 0x200 and the bank's span is [+0xA200, +0x78000), ending exactly at the end of the 0x78000-byte buffer (`initmenus.c`); with 16-byte commands it is 0x400 and the span ends at +0x78200. `load_resource` (`ob.c`) places a compressed file at the end of the span it is given and expands it downwards, so every briefing at 64 bits wrote 0x200 bytes past the block (into `ptr_menu_videobuffer`, which nothing reads on PC, so no effect was seen). Found by the final whole-milestone review, by reading; Tasks 4 and 11 had noted the +0xA400 placement but judged it unreachable because banks are a few KB, which missed the load's placement at the span's end. No run reached it (no 64-bit run opens a briefing). What was done: at 64 bits the step is `temp_s0 = (Gfx *) ((u8 *) temp_s0 + argg);`, a byte step, so the bank's span is [+0xA200, +0x78000) at both widths, ending at the block's end; the 32-bit tokens are unchanged. The briefing record itself (`struct BriefingData`, 16-bit text IDs) holds no pointer and fits its 0x200 bytes at both widths. *The neighbouring carvings of the same buffer,* checked for the same `Gfx *` step: the file-select background (`init_menu05_fileselect`) takes `buf + 0xA000` by `intptr_t` arithmetic and `sub_GAME_7F008DE4` advances it as a `u8 **`, in bytes (0x40400 of image, then the 0x1A580-byte compressed copy, inside the 0x6E000 bytes it is given); the wallet Bond (`load_walletbond`) loads into the buffer's first 0xA000 bytes by a byte count; the legal, Nintendo and GoldenEye logos and `GE_LOGOMODEL` use `u8 *` offsets (0x19000, 0x3C000); the attract cast steps a `u8 *bufferPtr`; the Rareware logo copies its ROM segment by its byte length; the gun barrel intro steps a `u8 *gfxBuffer` (its list's carving, fixed in fix wave A, was a byte count, not a `Gfx *` step). None steps a typed pointer by a byte count, so the briefing was the only instance. Verification: by reading and the arithmetic above (no ROM-free test can drive the briefing setup); the Windows comparison of this commit against its parent is identical (fix-wave report).

*LP64-004 fix wave C, nothing falls back to compiled-in data at 64 bits (2026-11-17). Commit "Stop a 64-bit build by name on a file the ROM does not serve".* What was wrong: a 64-bit build links no compiled-in file of a served class (CMake refuses `GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK` at `GE_POINTER_BITS=64`, so their weak symbols are NULL), but three paths still behaved as if it did. A file of a served class that the ROM's directory lacks (romdata.c logged "keeping the compiled-in copy") went through `ob.c`'s NULL-address path, `resource_load_from_indy`, which on PC loads nothing and may inflate whatever the bank last held; the model loader's compiled-in branch (`objecthandler_2.c`) then promoted that as a model graph, now that the models class is converted and its guard no longer stops. The `GE_ROMTEXT`/`GE_ROMBRIEF`/`GE_ROMSETUP`/`GE_ROMSTAN`/`GE_ROMMODEL`/`GE_ROMBG=0` knobs (`romdataClassEnabled`) took a class off the ROM onto that same nothing: before this change a 64-bit Dam run with `GE_ROMTEXT=0` printed `ge: fileIndexLoadToBank: NO LINKED DATA for file index 670` and died with a segmentation fault (status 139, aarch64). And a text bank that arrived still 1172-compressed was left as it was at 64 bits, where `langGet` would add its compressed words to the bank's address as offsets. Found by the final whole-milestone review (I1 and its fix-now item 5), by reading. What was done, 64-bit only: (1) `romdataRequireServed` (`port/src/romdata.c`, declared in `port/include/romdata.h`), called at the start of `ob.c`'s `fileIndexLoadToBank` and `fileIndexLoadToAddr` (at 32 bits it is a macro that expands to nothing; one fork comment beside it is rewrapped so that `ob.c` stays within the repository's 628-line limit), stops the game before the load with `The CLASS file NAME is not served from the ROM; a 64-bit build has no compiled-in copy to read` for a file of a served class (text, brief, setup, stan, model, bg) that the ROM does not serve; romdata.c's boot line for such a file now says `a load of it stops a 64-bit build`. (2) The model loader's compiled-in branch stops by name too (`The model NAME is not served from the ROM; a 64-bit build cannot read its compiled-in copy`), after the class guard, for any path that reaches it. (3) `romdataClassEnabled` ignores the knobs at 64 bits and says so once per class (`ge: romdata: GE_ROMTEXT=0 ignored: a 64-bit build has no compiled-in text files`). (4) A text bank that arrives compressed is zeroed, as a refused bank is, so every slot reads as not loaded. (5) `portRomdataSegsApply` (`port/src/segments.c`) stops by name when the textures' bank (`images`), an audio bank's control or wave table, the music samples or the gun barrel image is missing from the ROM (`The ROM segment NAME is missing; a 64-bit build has no compiled-in copy to read`); before, it logged `NONE IN THIS BUILD - will crash` and went on. *What a 64-bit build does for a file or segment the ROM does not serve, class by class, after this change:* text banks: stops by name at the load (before: the indy path, an unloaded or stale bank); fonts: exits with status 3 and `no font segments in the ROM and no compiled-in copies` when a font segment is missing or not its stock size (unchanged; a converter refusal stops naming the segment); textures: stops by name at boot when the `images` bank is missing (before: a crash at the first texture); animation tables: exits with status 3 and `no animation segments in the ROM and no compiled-in copies` (unchanged); models: stops by name at the load, and in the loader's compiled-in branch (before: garbage promoted); collision tiles: stops by name at the load (before: by name after it, `bg.c`, still in place); setup files: stops by name at the load (before: by name after it, `prop.c`, still in place); backgrounds: stops by name (`romfile_bg.c`, unchanged: bg files are used in place, not loaded through `ob.c`); audio banks: stops by name at boot when `sfxctl`, `sfxtbl`, `instrumentsctl` or `instrumentstbl` is missing (before: `portBnkfConvert`'s segment check passed a NULL table equal to a NULL segment, and the bank was read from NULL); music sequences: stops by name (`audio_stubs.c`: a sequence bank that is not its ROM segment or is shorter than its header; unchanged), and at boot now when `musicsampletbl` is missing. Briefings, a served class outside the ten, stop by name at the load like text banks. On the stock ROM nineteen directory entries are missing, the background and collision files of the eleven cut stages (eleven bg, eight stan), which no mission loads. Verification (aarch64, plain 64-bit executable): Dam for 300 frames with `GE_ROMTEXT=0`, and with `GE_ROMMODEL=0 GE_ROMSETUP=0`, now runs to its frame limit, status 0, with the `ignored` lines; a scratch build (reverted) that withheld `LdamE` from serving stopped Dam with status 1 and `ge: FATAL: The text file LdamE is not served from the ROM; a 64-bit build has no compiled-in copy to read`; the cut stage Eldorado (`GE_STAGE=44`) stops, as before, with `The bg file bg/bg_eld_all_p.seg is not served from the ROM` (its bg is read before any load through `ob.c`). The model loader's stop, the compressed-bank zeroing and the missing-segment stops are reached by no run (the stock ROM serves every model and segment and its banks arrive inflated); they rest on reading. The 32-bit code is unchanged (every edit is under `IS_64_BIT` or the 32-bit macro above); the Windows comparison of this commit against its parent is identical (fix-wave report).

*LP64-004 fix wave D, the narrowing check sees `Aword` (2026-11-17). Commit "Count audio command words as pointer-sized in the narrowing check".* What was wrong: `PR/abi.h`'s `Aword`, the type of an audio command's two words, is `uintptr_t` at 64 bits (Task 7), but GCC names the typedef, not `uintptr_t`, when it narrows one, so `lp64_static_checks.py`'s narrowing check did not list `u32 x = cmd.words.w1;`, which CI would have passed while the mixer has never run at 64 bits. Found by Task 7's review and the final whole-milestone review, by reading. What was done: `Aword` joins `uintptr_t`, `intptr_t` and `romptr_t` as a pointer-sized source type (`POINTER_SIZED` and the module's help), and the two opcode-word reads in `port/src/audio_pc.c` (the run and the browser's count, `u32 w0 = list[c].words.w0;`) take an explicit `(u32)`: only their 32-bit data is used, and at 32 bits `Aword` is `unsigned int`, so the cast is the same code. `scripts/port/test_lp64_static_checks.py` gains `test_an_aword_source_is_listed_too` (a compiler line naming `'Aword' {aka 'long unsigned int'}` is listed), which failed before the type was added (`'' != 'a.c:5:7: Aword -> u32 | ...'`) and passes after (25 tests). With a scratch line `u32 x = list[c].words.w1;` in `audio_pc.c` (reverted), `narrowing --check` on the aarch64 gate trees exited 1 naming `port/src/audio_pc.c:422:17: Aword -> u32`; without it, it prints `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files, all allowed` (aarch64 here; both containers at the wave's end, fix-wave report). `lp64_casts.py check` still prints `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`: it does not count the two casts, which are not pointer round trips. The narrowing allowlist stays absent (none allowed).

*LP64-004 fix wave E, the converter headers split (2026-11-17). Commit "Split the audio and background converter declarations into their own headers".* What was wrong: the milestone holds its new files under 500 lines, but `port/include/port_romconv.h` had reached 628, the repository's hard limit, and `port/include/port_romlayout.h` 521. Found by the final whole-milestone review (I4). What was done, with no declaration changed: the audio bank and music sequence sections of `port_romconv.h` (with the `PR/libaudio.h` and `music.h` includes only they needed) moved to a new `port/include/port_romconv_audio.h` (159 lines), its backgrounds section to the end of `port/include/port_romconv_stage.h` (now 299), and the audio bank and music sequence layouts of `port_romlayout.h` to a new `port/include/port_romlayout_audio.h` (123); `port_romconv.h` is now 397 lines and `port_romlayout.h` 414 (figures corrected at the close, from `wc -l`; this note first gave 395, 300 and 413). Each includer takes the header that declares what it uses: `audio_stubs.c`, `src/music.c`, `romconv_bank.c`, `romconv_bank_records.c`, `romconv_bank_oracle.c`, `romconv_bank_walk.h`, `romconv_seq.c` and the bank and sequence tests the audio headers; `romconv_bg.c`, `romconv_bg_oracle.c`, `romfile_bg.c`, `src/game/bg.c` and the three background tests the stage header. The oracle comment's 126-character line in `port_romconv.h` (Task 8's) is wrapped, and the headers' opening comments say where each class now is (the stage layout header no longer says `port_romlayout.h` has no room). Verification: the 64-bit gate compiles every C and C++ file of both aarch64 trees (`354 files compiled, 0 failed`, `385 files compiled, 0 failed`); `test_romconv.sh` passes at 64 bits (aarch64) and at 32 and 64 bits (i686 container); the i686 oracle build (`-DGE_LP64_ORACLE=ON`) builds; `romdata.c`, which includes `port_romconv.h` at every width, is in the shipped 32-bit build, and the Windows comparison of this commit against its parent is identical (fix-wave report).

*LP64-004 fix wave F, four small corrections (2026-11-17). Commit "Note the relabel rule, drop UNK41 from the fix-up, sweep unserved stans and pin the font arrays".* Each found by the final whole-milestone review (its minor items and the deferred list), by reading; no run reached any of them. (1) What was wrong: the relabel table `sTextPatches` (`port/src/romdata.c`) said nothing of Task 4's 64-bit rule, though a relabel that breaks it works at 32 bits and refuses the whole bank at 64. What was done: a comment at the table says that at 64 bits a relabel is copied over the ROM string it replaces, so it must fit that string and share no byte with another slot's string, or the whole bank is refused at 64 bits while the 32-bit build still works; only the oracle build or a 64-bit boot with the ROM catches it, and CI has no ROM. (2) What was wrong: the 64-bit fix-up loop in `proplvreset2` (`src/game/prop.c`) listed `PROPDEF_UNK41` with the object records whose `ObjectRecord.damage` word it rotates, but a type-41 record is one word in the file and 8 bytes at 64 bits (`romconv_setup_props.c`'s `WIDE(1, 2, 0, 0)`), so the rotation would land well past the record, in whatever follows it (no stock setup has one). What was done: the case is dropped from the 64-bit switch, with a comment; the 32-bit branch, which rotates `pd[29]` for type 41 as upstream does, is unchanged. (3) What was wrong: the collision-file oracle compared only the stans a run loads, so a stan the ROM holds but the game does not serve was never compared, and the 47 identical files were the only evidence that all were served. What was done: in the oracle build `romdataStanOracleSweep` (`port/src/romdata.c`, run with the other sweeps under `GE_LP64_ORACLE_SWEEP`) counts each stan in the ROM's directory that is not served as a difference (`collision tiles NAME DIFFERS (the ROM holds it, but it is not served)`), as the background and setup sweeps do, and logs `ge: lp64: oracle: stan sweep: the ROM holds N stan files`. It lives in `romdata.c`, not `romfile_stan.c`, because `test_romconv.sh` links `romfile_stan.c` with `GE_LP64_ORACLE` into a ROM-free test that has no file table. On the stock ROM (i686 oracle build): `the ROM holds 27 stan files` and no difference; with `GE_ROMSTAN=0` (which a 32-bit build still honours) all 27 are listed as differing. (4) What was wrong: the two font staging arrays in `port/src/segments.c` were checked against the converter only at a 64-bit boot with the ROM and, by number, in the ROM-free fixture, which never sees the arrays. What was done: two `_Static_assert`s at 64 bits that each array's `sizeof` is `PORT_FONT_STAGED_SIZE(ROMSIZE - sizeof(RomFont) + sizeof(struct font))` for its stock segment (`segments.c` now includes `bondtypes.h` and `port_romlayout.h` at 64 bits); built with Bank Gothic's array at 0x24B0 + 0x2F4 the aarch64 build failed with `static assertion failed: "Bank Gothic's staging array holds its converted table and glyphs"`, and with 0x300 it builds. The fixture's comments (`scripts/port/test_romconv_font.c`) and Task 9's note above ("checked three ways") now say what each check sees. The Windows comparison of this commit against its parent is identical: every change is under `IS_64_BIT` or `GE_LP64_ORACLE`, or a comment.

*LP64-004 fix wave G, a new kind of `ge: lp64:` line fails by default (2026-11-17). Commit "Fail a 64-bit run on any lp64 line outside the informational list".* What was wrong: the 20-mission smoke (`scripts/port/audit_buffers.py`) and the boot check (`scripts/port/lp64_boot.py`) failed a run only on the two markers `ge: lp64: pool` and `ge: lp64: cannot convert`, so any other kind of `ge: lp64:` line, such as `converter map: a second map while one is in use` in a run that exits 0, or a kind added later, passed; and no test pinned that an oracle line passes a mission. Found by the final whole-milestone review (minor) and Task 2's and Task 16's reviews, by reading. **LP64-004 hand-over to LP64-005** (assembled at the close from the final review's hand-over list, the controller's ledger of the milestone's reviews and the task notes above, and checked against the code on `main` at bbcac00):

- *Three decisions waited for the owner at the close; all three are answered.* The second and third the owner settled on 2026-11-17 by accepting the LP64-005 plan's recommendations (the intro walk is left as inherited; the wallet's room is scaled by 13/8 at 64 bits by moving the file-select background's start). The first is settled too: the owner accepted that reading on 2026-11-17 ("Accept the reading", in the session that closed LP64-004, as that session relayed it). (1) The reading of decision 3's "with no `ge: lp64:` line": the runs allow the informational kinds in `INFORMATIONAL_PREFIXES` (`scripts/port/lp64_boot.py`), because LP64-003's startup check prints `ge: lp64: address space OK` on every 64-bit run; if the literal reading was meant, those lines need another prefix (a mechanical rename). (2) `src/game/bondview2.c`'s intro walk in `mp_respawn_handler` (strict tier) has no WATCH or CREDITS arm, and PC `INTRO_TYPE` (`bondview.h`) reads a WATCH record's hours as a SPAWN, so the walk goes out of step after a WATCH at both widths; it runs only on a multiplayer respawn, none of the 13 `Ump_` setup sources in the tree has a WATCH, and the fix (explicit arms) is an edit to a strict-tier file that changes 32-bit behaviour. (3) The wallet Bond's room (`load_walletbond`, `src/game/front.c`) stays 0xA000 bytes at 64 bits, where `PwalletbondZ`'s image leaves 2,592 bytes (6.3 percent); it cannot grow, because the file-select background is expanded at +0xA000 in the same buffer, and an image that does not fit is refused by name and the menu shows no wallet model.
- *No 64-bit run has pressed a button or walked a display list.* The runs are the title for 600 frames and each solo mission's start for 1800 frames, headless, with no input. Never executed at 64 bits: pause, the watch pages, file select, the briefing, the gun barrel list, multiplayer, the attract cast and the attract demos, cheats, stage transitions, the cut stages, play beyond 1800 frames (room streaming, peak room memory) and the renderer's walk of any list, so `GE_LP64_DL_CHECK` and `seg_addr`'s 64-bit host-pointer test (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) have never run either, nor the arm mesh's alias cases (`port/src/port_arm_mesh.c`). The first run with input and a renderer should be a sanitizer build with the renderer (`GE_SANITIZE=ON`, `GE_VIDEO=ON`), which compiles in `GE_LP64_DL_CHECK`.
- *Sound synthesis and mixing have never run at 64 bits.* Headless builds compile `port/src/headless_stubs.c`'s empty `portAudioPump` instead of `port/src/audio_pc.c`, so no 64-bit run has made an audio command. `Acmd` (`include/PR/abi.h`) is exercised only by the interpreter's ROM-free test (`scripts/port/test_audio_buffers.c`), `aPan` not at all (`A_PAN` is defined nowhere), and the converted bank graph's views (`ALBankAlt_s`, `ALInstrumentAlt_s` in `src/snd.h`) by the layout probe and a scratch read that played nothing. `GE_AUDIO_CAPTURE` needs a 64-bit build with audio.
- *The final fix wave's four overruns* (the pause list `buffer_for_watch_static_DL` in `src/game/bondview.h`, the watch background lists in `src/game/options.c`, the gun barrel list in `src/game/title.c`, the briefing's language bank span in `src/game/front.c`) are on paths no run reaches. The three display-list fixes (73308dd) are pinned by the layout probe's room assertions (`scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c`) and by reading; the briefing span fix (a657b4b, `front.c` only) has no probe assertion and rests on reading only. So are fix wave C's stops and its compressed-bank zeroing, and the removal of `PROPDEF_UNK41` from the 64-bit prop fix-up (since LP64-007 Task 7 a ROM-free fixture holds the missing-segment stop and the zeroing; no run reaches them still).
- *The storage family is not exhausted.* Ten 64-bit defects outside the converters were storage for a record or a display list sized by a literal or by filler members, or a member read by position over another record: the model hit pool `g_ModelHitEntries` (`objecthandler.c`, 600 times 0x14 bytes for a 40-byte record; 69759f6); the player's gait model storage (`bondview.h`, too small for a 64-bit `Model`; 9f37737); the gait run's flip and frame names (`bondhead.c`, which landed on `Model.scale` and padding; 46ba04d); the player record (`player.c`, 0x2A80 bytes for 0x30A0), the inventory (`inititemslots.c`, 0x14 bytes an item for 32) and the anim model slots' 268-byte stride (`initunk_005520.c`, leaving the stage bank at 4 mod 8) (all three a27e1bd, with the 8-aligned bank cursor a7970b8 after it); the pause list (`bondview.h`, one `Gfx` and six `s32` for three commands), the watch background lists (`options.c`, `dynAllocate(0xF8)` for 17 or 29 commands) and the gun barrel list (`title.c`, 0x100 bytes for 31 commands) (all three 73308dd); and the briefing's bank span (`front.c`, stepped as `Gfx`, 0x200 bytes past its block; a657b4b). The sanitizers reported none of them as an overrun, since each lay inside one allocation or a common symbol (the model hit pool was found through a UBSan shift report on the `player_num` it corrupted, and the gait model storage as a crash). Two sweeps were made and each missed one found later: the first (69759f6) read global byte arrays only, so the inventory's stage-bank allocation was found by Task 15's review; the second (a27e1bd) read the stage-bank allocations, found the player's, and missed `model.c:158`'s 268-byte request (strict tier; harmless since a7970b8), found by its re-review. The final review then found the four display-list and briefing overruns by reading; it did not search stack byte arrays cast to records outside the model code, or `s32` filler runs overlaid by records other than `Model` and `Gfx`. `AGENTS.md` now carries a rule for the family.
- *Covered by fixtures only:* model node opcodes 0, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19 and 20 and setup prop record types 0, 15, 16, 31 and 41, which no mission of the smoke loaded (`lp64_census.py types` at the close), and the model converter's refusals of inputs the stock ROM does not have.
- *Pool and heap figures are snapshots* at the frame limit of the run each note names, not peaks. The measured figures: the music heap, 281,584 of 753,664 bytes at 64 bits after the music table (Task 6 note) and 329,584 after the two audio command lists doubled (Task 7 note), against 219,120 at 32 bits; the background tables' stage-pool cost per mission, Dam's 8,688 bytes the largest of the 20 and Runway's 1,256 the least (Task 12 note); and the stage bank at the 600-frame limit, 3,292,688 to 3,816,128 bytes at 32 bits and 3,899,752 to 4,399,552 at 64 of 66,805,760 (Task 16 note, "Memory"). Room memory is not scaled at 64 bits (decision 4 scaled only the graphics buffer): the mema heap that room blocks come from is `-ma` times 1024 bytes, doubled on PC and taken from the stage bank (`src/boss.c`, the stage reset), with no 64-bit factor; the pool line's `(request N bytes)` is the block tried or the free space wanted, not the size a fix needs (`portLp64PoolExhausted`, `port/src/port_lp64.c`); and the graphics buffer's per-frame end check (`src/game/dyn.c`) still owes its benchmark.
- *Inherited unbounded reads at both widths*, not introduced here: an animation's stream length and entries offset (`portAnimDataInit`, `port/src/animdata.c`, bounds only the descriptor range); a sequence's address, `len` and `uncompressed_len`, and the init loop's 63 entries whatever the count (`src/music.c`); the end of an AI list (`romconv_setup_records.c` only confirms an `AI_EndList` byte before the unowned run ends); a glyph's extent (`width * height`, fonts); and a wave of a type other than ADPCM or raw 16-bit, which gets `table + base` unchecked (`romconv_bank.c`, as `alBnkfNew`). LP64-007 Task 7 bounded them in the 64-bit converters, all but one part of a sequence's lengths: whether its inflated stream fits the track buffer it is played into, which the converter cannot know. Its note names that part and the other reads left in shared code.
- *The 32-bit special-portal walk* (`sub_GAME_7F0B37EC`, `src/game/bg.c`) still ends where the linker places `g_BgCurrentRoom` after `specialportalarray`; the 64-bit walk is bounded by the array (428d224).
- *Stale background pointers:* on a stage that does not call `load_bg_file`, `g_BgPortals` and `ptr_bgdata_room_fileposition_list` point at reset stage-pool memory at 64 bits (at the ROM image at 32); no reader was found, by a search that was not exhaustive.
- *Two `GE_DUMP_BOND` diagnostics* read a texture record as two `Gfx`, 8 bytes past it at 64 bits: the shadow record's in `src/game/model.c` (strict tier) and the water's in `src/game/sky.c`; they run only with that variable set.
- *Display-list words the model converter copies:* `port/include/port_romconv.h`'s opcode rule does not name `G_MOVEWORD` (copied, which is right for `G_MW_SEGMENT`), and a crafted `G_TEXRECT` tail whose next word has opcode 0x04, 0xFD or 0x06 would be read as an address, as the in-place walk reads it; well-formed lists cannot reach it. Since LP64-007 Task 7 the model converter refuses a `G_TEXRECT` not followed by `G_RDPHALF_2` and `G_RDPHALF_CONT`.
- *For macOS:* `scripts/port/test_audio_buffers.c` maps its buffers with Linux `mmap` flags (`MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE`), and the 64-bit bank cursor (`cursorAfter`, `port/src/port_memp.c`) is absolutely 8-aligned only because the arena is page-aligned (`mmap`).
- *From the plan:* the late-load audit of a 64-bit build is owed (the converters run where the in-place passes run, but models and rooms do more work during play); the eleven cut stages still stop by name (decision 7); decision 6's measurement (a Dam reload found 334 portal fields left by the first load, none in the rooms) is a 32-bit question for LP64-006.
- *Stale wording in the guard, for a code change:* the stop message of `portLp64RequireConverter` still says "has no 64-bit converter yet (LP64-004)", and the comment above the table in `port/src/port_lp64.c` tells its history ("All zero in LP64-003; LP64-004 set each class's entry ...") rather than that every entry is now 1; the stop now fires only through `GE_LP64_TEST_UNCONVERTED` or an entry set back to 0.
- *One CI line cannot run on the Mac:* `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 bash scripts/port/test_buffers.sh` spins under qemu-i386 in its sanitized 32-bit half (`test_model_bounds`); its two halves run apart there (the 64-bit half sanitized, the 32-bit half not), and CI, which runs it natively, is its evidence.

**Milestone LP64-005 (first playable), planned and accepted on 2026-11-17, done on 2026-11-20; every task is on `main` (the task notes after this paragraph were written as each commit was made; the close and the hand-over to LP64-006 are its last note and the two lists after it):**
[the milestone's plan](scripts/port/native_64bit_lp64_005.md) lists fifteen tasks and fourteen decisions for the owner, each with a recommendation; the first, the reading of "no `ge: lp64:` line", is settled (the owner accepted that reading on 2026-11-17 ("Accept the reading", in the session that closed LP64-004, as that session relayed it), recorded by the commit "Record the owner's acceptance of the reading of no ge: lp64: line"), and the owner accepted the other thirteen together afterwards (below). The planning commit adds the plan, this paragraph, the status table's LP64-005 row and the hazard inventory's list "Found while planning LP64-005" (documentation only: no source, build file or test changed, so no game rebuild, render regeneration or benchmark applies). **Measured for the plan** (Mac containers, GCC 13.3; aarch64 native, x86_64 translated by Rosetta 2, i686 under qemu-i386; scratch builds and one scratch copy of the tree under `build/lp64`, deleted afterwards; no log, trace, recording or picture is kept in Git). *Headless, 64 bits.* Each of the 14 attract demos (`GE_DEMO`, 3,000 frames) plays to its end on the plain and on the sanitizer executable with exit status 0 and no sanitizer report, ending with `totaltime end (timer/limit)` at the tick the i686 build ends it (dam1 438, dam2 445, facility1 410, facility2 538, facility3 380, runway1 388, runway2 388, bunker1 482, bunker2 771, silo1 501, silo2 503, frigate1 328, frigate2 384, train 464). The per-tick traces (`GE_DEMODIAG`) differ: the i686 build stays exact with the N64's recorded random seed through all of seven demos (facility1 to 3, runway2, bunker1, silo2, train) and parts from it at tick 217, 44, 301, 332, 280, 116 and 64 in the others, while the 64-bit build parts from it at tick 2 in all fourteen, having made more random draws in the first tick of play (111 against 76 in Dam, 196 against 146 in Facility, 33 against 23 in Runway, 75 against 54 in Bunker, 245 against 179 in Silo, 156 against 117 in Frigate, 144 against 110 in Train). The cause, found with `GE_RNGTRACE` and a layout probe compiled at both widths: `weaponIsOneHanded` (`src/game/chraction.c:343`) reads a weapon's record through a `ChrRecord` cast as `act_bytes.padding[84]`, byte 128 at 32 bits (`WeaponObjRecord.weaponnum`) and byte 140 at 64 bits, where `weaponnum` is at 144, so every armed guard takes the unarmed idle branch. Three more reads by position were found by reading and confirmed by the probe: `chraction.c:2240`, `:2258` and `:2306` (`((u16 *) header)[2]` for an animation's frame count, half of a pointer at 64 bits), `src/game/unk_092E50.c:271` and `:277` (`((u32 *) list)[8]`, the third command at 64 bits where the fifth is meant) and `src/game/options.c:564` (a debug cursor); `src/sched.c:334` has a fourth that is dead on PC. With stand-ins for the first three in a scratch copy, dam1, runway1 and runway2 trace identically to the i686 build for every tick, and the other eleven first differ at tick 227 (dam2), 406 (facility1), 35 (facility2), 114 (facility3), 113 (bunker1), 325 (bunker2), 186 (silo1), 54 (silo2), 125 (frigate1), 158 (frigate2) and 70 (train); the aarch64 and the x86_64 (Rosetta 2) 64-bit traces are identical to each other for all fourteen; in facility2 at tick 34 the i686 build makes one draw at `gunfire.c:4419` that the 64-bit build does not, undiagnosed. With `GE_FIXEDTICK=1` a demo is not the demo (dam1 ends by its terminator at tick 455 after 454 vsyncs), and with `GE_NOSLEEP=1` the frame limit passes before the game has run, so the plan's runs use neither. All 13 multiplayer arenas with 2 and with 4 players, Temple with 4 players in scenarios 1 to 7 and Cuba run 1,800 frames, plain and under the sanitizers (34 runs, exit 0, no report). Twelve stage numbers stop by name with status 1: a solo load of Citadel, Complex or Temple (`The setup file UsetupcatZ`, `UsetuprefZ`, `UsetupdishZ` `is not served from the ROM`) and level ids 42, 44, 47, 49, 51, 52, 53, 55 and 56 (`The bg file bg/bg_sho_all_p.seg is not served from the ROM` and eight siblings), so "the eleven cut stages" are eleven background files the ROM does not serve, nine of which `bg.c`'s level table names (these nine level ids; `bg_imp` and `bg_ash` have no level id, measured in the fix wave below); on those twelve the i686 build runs Temple solo, ends in a segmentation fault on Complex and the nine ids, and hangs on Citadel. Under the sanitizers the three setup stops are preceded by a stack-buffer-overflow in `strncpy` from `indyrescmdCheckFileExists` (`src/game/indy_commands.c:203`), inherited at both widths. `GE_LOADTOUR=24` on the 20 missions and six arenas exits 0 everywhere with no `ge: lp64: pool` line: 848 room visits, 11 tours complete and 15 ending early with `(the mission ended there)`. A headless build cannot press a button: `osContGetReadData` (`port/src/libultra_shim.c`) zeroes the pads and the `GE_INPUTPLAY` hook is inside `#ifdef GE_VIDEO`. *With video, 64 bits.* A `GE_VIDEO=ON` tree configures, compiles and links at 64 bits (17 s in the aarch64 container, 53 s in the x86_64 one), and with `GE_SANITIZE=ON` in aarch64. With `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen` it runs in the images as they are, on Mesa 25.2.8's llvmpipe (GL 4.5 compatibility); `dummy` cannot make a GL context. Every run that makes sound fails: Dam with signal 11 in `alEnvmixerPull` (`src/libultrare/audio/env.c:94`), the runway1 demo in `__allocParam` (`src/libultra/audio/synthesizer.c:247`), four-player Temple with `ASSERTION FAULT - samples >= 0 - env.c, line 104`, and under the sanitizers `env.c:94:20: runtime error: member access within misaligned address ... for type 'struct ALParam'`. The cause: the synthesizer's parameter pool holds records of `sizeof(ALParam)`, 32 bytes at 64 bits (`synthesizer.c:127`), and `alSynStartVoiceParams` writes an `ALStartParamAlt`, 40 bytes there, whose `wave` pointer lands on the next record's `next` link (both are 28 bytes at 32 bits); the pool lies inside the static music heap. With one pointer of room added in a scratch copy, the sanitizer video executable ran the title, Dam, Facility, the runway1 demo, four-player Temple and `GE_MENU=select` and `options` for 900 frames each with no report (8 to 71 pictures each: under the sanitizers, four at a time, less than one picture a second; the plain executable drew 256 in 1,500 frames). In the renderer, `roc_part_key` (`port/fast3d/gfx_roomcache.inl:155`) drops a list address's upper bits at 64 bits (used only with `room_cache=2`), and `phVector` (`port/src/port_hud.c:349`) leaves the upper halves of three commands' words unwritten. *macOS.* On the Mac itself with clang, 10 of the 33 `scripts/port/test_*.sh` harnesses pass at 64 bits; thirteen stop at `include/PR/os.h:1033:13: error: expected parameter declarator`. **Planned shape:** one tool (`scripts/port/lp64_play.py`) that runs sets of cases and judges each by what its log shows; sanitizer builds that poison the game's arenas and drop common symbols, proven on the defects already fixed; a reviewed list of every record read through another type, checked in CI; the measured defects fixed with a check that failed first; recorded pads replayed in a headless build for the paths that need a button; video offscreen in the containers, with a 32-bit video reference; sound sized, made audible and recorded; pool peaks printed; the late-load audit at both widths; strict-tier work on `lp64/play-strict` through one laptop trip. **Not measured:** any path that needs a button; sound that is not silence at 64 bits; more than a few dozen pictures a run under the sanitizers; any pool's peak; real x86 hardware and a GPU. **Accepted by the owner on 2026-11-17** (commit "Record the owner's acceptance of the LP64-005 plan"): all fourteen recommendations of the plan's "Decisions for the owner", the first in the session that closed LP64-004 and the other thirteen together ("Accept all 13") in the session that wrote the plan. *LP64-005 task 1, the play check (2026-11-17). Commit "Add the play check: sets of 64-bit runs judged by what they did" (Python tools, tests and documents only; no compiled file changed).* **What it is.** `scripts/port/lp64_play.py run --rom ROM --set NAME[,NAME...] [--jobs N] [--only CASE[,CASE...]] [--env NAME=VALUE]... --output DIR EXECUTABLE` runs each case of the named sets on a copy of the executable in a fresh temporary folder (every `GE_` variable of the caller dropped; `GE_ROM`, `GE_FRAMES`, `GE_SEED=1`, `GE_NOINISAVE=1`, `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0` and the case's variables set), seven at a time by default, writes `DIR/CASE.log` and `DIR/play.json`, prints `CASE: PASS` or `CASE: FAIL (first failing or missing line)` and ends with `OK: N of N cases` (exit 0) or `FAIL: M of N cases` (exit 1). A case fails on a status other than its own (0; 1 for a stop), a timeout (5 times its paced length plus 120 s, with the log's last line), a sanitizer marker, `ge: fatal signal`, `ASSERTION FAULT`, a failing `ge: lp64:` line (`failing_lp64_lines`, `SANITIZER_MARKERS` and `FATAL_SIGNAL` are imported from `lp64_boot.py`) and a missing required line. It never sets `GE_FIXEDTICK` or `GE_NOSLEEP` and refuses either from `--env` (exit 2). `traces --expect FILE DIR_REF DIR_NEW` compares each demo's `ge: demo tick` lines (the first playback of each log) and checks them against `scripts/port/lp64_demo_traces.txt` (a demo recorded as differing that now matches fails too); `traces --reference-check DIR_A DIR_B` prints `unstable` for a demo whose two runs differ; a log with no tick lines fails either, and so does one whose playback did not reach its end by the `demos` case's rule (fix round 1). `callers --tick T LOG EXECUTABLE` gives each `ge: rng draw` line of ticks T-1 and T as `tick function file:line` through `addr2line`, subtracting the `executable image` of the `ge: lp64: address space OK` line for a position-independent executable (read from its ELF header) and one byte, so that the call's own line is named. **Layout.** Later tasks add sets, options and subcommands, so the tool is six files, each under 500 lines: `lp64_play.py` (the command line), `lp64_play_cases.py` (the sets, the measured constants and each required line's pattern, quoted with the source that prints it), `lp64_play_judge.py`, `lp64_play_run.py`, `lp64_play_traces.py` and `lp64_play_callers.py`; *LP64-005 task 2, an inherited overrun the poisoned graphics pool found (2026-11-18). Commit "Stop writing a fifth explosion vertex into room for four".* With Task 2's poisoning of the graphics pool in the working tree, the first sanitizer pass of every set (aarch64, `build/lp64/boot-san`) failed 20 of 117 cases: the three planned setup stops and 17 cases (all 14 demos, `stage-jungle`, `tour-jungle`, `attract`, `soak`) with `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison ... WRITE of size 16` in `explosionRenderPart` (`src/game/explosion.c:1075`). The function allocates four vertices (`dynAllocateVertices(4)`) and stores the default vertex into `vertices[0]` to `vertices[4]`; its four display-list loads (`gSPVertex(..., 4, 0)`) read four, and nothing reads the fifth. `Vtx` is 16 bytes at both widths, so the 32-bit game has the same stray store: inherited from the N64 code, not a member of the storage family. Where it lands (`src/game/dyn.c`, `src/game/explosion.c`): `dynAllocateVertices(4)` advances `g_GfxMemPos` by exactly 64 bytes (alignment 1), so the fifth vertex is the 16 bytes at the new `g_GfxMemPos`, which at the time of the store no block owns; normally that is free pool space, which a later block's owner then overwrites, and nothing reads the stray vertex at either width (both `gSPVertex` loads of the function name 4). It corrupted live data only when the four-vertex block ended exactly at its half's end: at the end of half 0 the store hit the first vertex of half 1 (`g_VtxBuffers[1]`), the half the renderer may still be drawing; at the end of half 1 (`g_VtxBuffers[2]`) it hit the first bytes after the vertex buffers in the stage bank, the next stage-bank allocation. So removing it changes no picture or state of the 32-bit game except by removing that corruption. **Fix** (owner decision 13: an inherited defect with a few-line fix is fixed and named): the fifth store stays only in the N64 build (`#ifdef TARGET_N64`), where the decompiled code must keep matching; the four vertices drawn are unchanged. **This changes the 32-bit program:** the one changed function is `explosionRenderPart`, which loses one 16-byte store. `compare_win32.py commits 4ce5bea` against this commit's tree exited 1 (`.text` 16 bytes shorter, every later address shifted, so `.text`, `.rdata`'s jump tables, `.data`, `.reloc` and `.CRT` differ by position); of the 360 object files of the two Windows builds only `explosion.c.obj` differs, and `i686-w64-mingw32-objdump -d` of the two shows one change of code, in `_explosionRenderPart`: the `movups %xmm2,0x40(%eax)` that stored `vertices[4]` is gone (with one load moved by the scheduler and the function's branch targets 4 to 16 bytes earlier); every other function of the file disassembles the same. **Seen failing first:** the 17 cases above, on the sanitizer executable built from the working tree before this edit; after it (Task 2's note below) the full sanitizer pass reports no `explosionRenderPart` line. No ROM-free test: the function needs a stage's player, matrices and explosion state, and the poisoned play cases are its check.
*LP64-005 task 2, the arenas poisoned and common symbols dropped in sanitizer builds (2026-11-18). Commit "Poison the game's arenas and drop common symbols in sanitizer builds".* **Why.** AddressSanitizer saw neither a block of the stage bank, the room heap, the graphics pool or the music heap running into the next (each arena is one allocation the game carves up) nor an overrun of a global array without an initializer (`-fcommon` makes it a common symbol, which gets no red zone); LP64-004 found members of the storage family only by their wreckage. **What.** New `port/include/port_poison.h`: `PORT_POISON(address, bytes)` and `PORT_UNPOISON(address, bytes)` call `__asan_poison_memory_region` and `__asan_unpoison_memory_region` when the compiler defines `__SANITIZE_ADDRESS__` and are `((void) 0)` otherwise; `PORT_POISON_GAP` is 32 with the sanitizer and 0 without. Bank: `mempResetBank` (`src/memp.c`) poisons the whole bank; `portMempAllocate` (`port/src/port_memp.c`) unpoisons exactly the bytes asked for and, in a sanitizer build only, moves the cursor on past a 32-byte poisoned gap (`gapAfter`, after LP64-004's 8-byte rounding), dropped at the bank's end as the rounding is, so a request `mempGetBankSizeLeft` promised still fits and a sanitizer build runs out of no bank a plain build fits in; `portMempResize` poisons from the block to the old cursor and unpoisons the new size, so a shrink gives back poisoned bytes and a growth takes unpoisoned ones; both still find the bank's last block by `allocation == pool->prevpos` before touching anything, and the fall-back to the permanent bank and the exhaustion fatal come before any poisoning. Room heap (`src/mema.c`): `memaReset` poisons the heap (the free list lives in `g_MemoryAllocations`, never in freed blocks, so mema reads no poisoned byte itself), `memaAlloc` unpoisons the block, `_memaFree` poisons it, and `memaGrow` unpoisons what `memaRealloc`'s growth takes. Music heap: `alHeapInit` (`src/libultra/audio/heapinit.c`) poisons the caller's region and `alHeapDBAlloc` (`heapalloc.c`) unpoisons each block whole, its request rounded up to the 16-byte cache line: callers DMA whole lines into a block (`music.c` copies `ALIGN16_a` of the sequence table's request), which is code that is right; a first version unpoisoned only `num * size`, and a 32-bit sanitizer run of Dam died at boot with `use-after-poison ... WRITE of size 512 ... osPiStartDma ... romCopy ... musicSeqPlayerInit src/music.c:834` (the 64-bit build loads that table through its converter and never did this). Graphics pool: `dynGetMasterDisplayList` (`src/game/dyn.c`, the frame's first call, after `boss.c` admits the frame at `pendingGfx < 2`) poisons the half the frame writes from `g_GfxMemPos` to its end, and `portDynAllocate` (`port/src/port_dyn.c`) unpoisons each block's exact bytes. CMake: with `GE_SANITIZE` the C flags carry `-fno-common` instead of `-fcommon` (`CMakeLists.txt`, the one generator expression that gave `-fcommon`); shipped builds keep `-fcommon`.
