*LP64-005 task 2, review fixes (2026-11-18). Commit "Give every poisoning probe a deadline and find the emulated hang" (a test, a CMake comment and documents; no compiled game file changed).* **The hang.** Instrumented in a scratch copy under qemu-i386 (the i686 container), the parent forked, read and reaped all 17 children and printed the 17th probe's line, then spun at 98% CPU as the only process left: the hang was in the test's own exit. LeakSanitizer's check at exit hangs under qemu-i386 even in `int main(void) { return 0; }` built `-m32 -fsanitize=address` (killed by `timeout 30`, exit 124), with `ASAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0` too (no report is printed, so symbolizing and the pipe play no part), and exits 0 at once with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0`; a forking variant behaves the same. The 17th probe line was missing only because stdout was a buffered pipe lost when the process was killed. So the cause is emulation of the sanitizer runtime, not the test's pipe or fork; at 64 bits neither form hung: the b840ef2 test and this one each passed 30 of 30 runs in the aarch64 container (native) and 30 of 30 in the x86_64 container. **The fix, in `scripts/port/test_lp64_poison.c`.** Every probe has a deadline of 10 s: the child arms `alarm` (with the default action), and the parent polls the pipe without blocking, reaps the child with `WNOHANG`, stops reading as soon as the child has exited (it drains what is buffered and never waits for an end of file, so a process the child leaves holding the pipe cannot block it), and kills a child still running at the deadline; a probe that runs out of time fails as `FAIL: <probe>: timed out`. The whole run is bounded at 120 s by an alarm in the parent, which also covers the sanitizer's checks at exit: `FAIL: test_lp64_poison: timed out after 120 s (the probes, or the sanitizer's checks at exit)`. Standard output is line-buffered, and the test ends with one line per width naming its count, `test_lp64_poison: PASS (64-bit, 17 probes)`, so a skipped half cannot look like a pass. Shown in a scratch build (aarch64): a probe that loops forever ended in 10 s with `FAIL: scratch: a child that never exits: timed out` (as an expected death and as an expected life); a child that exits 0 leaving a grandchild asleep for 60 s holding the pipe was judged in 21 ms, and a dying one in 31 ms. **Runs.** `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64 bash scripts/port/test_buffers.sh`: aarch64 exit 0 and x86_64 exit 0, each with `test_lp64_poison: PASS (64-bit, 17 probes)`. `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=32` unsanitized (i686): exit 0 (the test is not built there). The sanitized 32-bit half (i686, emulated): with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0`, exit 0 with `test_lp64_poison: PASS (32-bit, 17 probes)` and `test_buffers: PASS (32-bit)`; the test alone with default options printed its 17 probe lines and `test_lp64_poison: PASS (32-bit, 17 probes)`, then failed by name at its 120 s bound in the exit's leak check, exit 1; the whole half with default options was killed by its 300 s bound (exit 124) with no line printed; its first program, `test_model_bounds` (not touched here), writes its one line into a buffered pipe, so where it stopped is not established beyond that, which fits every sanitized program meeting the same exit check under qemu but was not instrumented. The sanitized 32-bit half with leak detection on has passed nowhere seen; CI's native run is its evidence, and its log must show the 32-bit count line. **The record.** The explosion note above now says where the stray store landed (free pool space, live data only at a half's end). The plan's status row says which defect each mechanism reported. `buffer_audit.md` says "every instrumented global", adds two blind spots (up to 15 bytes past a music-heap request; the tail of the previous block's 8-byte shadow unit when a room-heap or pool block starts off an 8-byte boundary) and two readers a later task must handle in the hooks (`portStateFrame`'s whole-region copies, 32-bit only; a renderer reading a graphics-pool block rounded to 16). `CMakeLists.txt` explains why `GE_SANITIZE` is read before its `option()` line. `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` on b840ef2 before committing: `identical in loaded code and data`, exit 0 (the plain build's flags are unchanged).
*LP64-005 task 3, first part: the overlay lister (2026-11-18). Commit "Add the overlay lister: every record read through another type" (Python tools, their test, the reviewed list's header, one CI line and documents; no compiled file changed).* (The review fixes in the next note widen `offset`, `index` and `run`, add `--locals`, and replace this note's blind-spot list and counts; where they differ, the next note is current.) **Not yet reviewed.** This part builds the tool and lists the tree; `scripts/port/lp64_overlays_reviewed.txt` holds only its header (the line format and the four verdicts with what each requires) and no site line, so `lp64_overlays.py check` fails today and is not in CI. The review batches of Task 3 add the verdicts; the last of them adds `check` to the CI tests step and the `AGENTS.md` paragraph. **What it is.** `scripts/port/lp64_overlays.py list [PATH...] [--lines]` prints one site a line, `file:function:kind:text` (`--lines` adds the line after a tab, for review only); `check` requires each site to have exactly one line `file:function:kind:text<TAB>VERDICT<TAB>reason` in the reviewed list and each line to match a site, printing `OK: N sites, all reviewed` or every `unreviewed:` site and `stale:` line (exit 1); a malformed line, an unknown verdict, an empty reason or a repeated key is refused (exit 2). Verdicts: `typed`, `same` (names the probe assertion), `overlay-64` (behind `IS_64_BIT`, names the assertion), `dead` (says why); `fixed` is not one. Split by responsibility, each file under 300 lines: `lp64_overlays_source.py` (comments and literals blanked, preprocessor regions, the owner of each offset, normalization), `lp64_overlays_kinds.py` (`index`, `offset`, `opaque`, `record`), `lp64_overlays_types.py` (the record types, `run`). `scripts/port/test_lp64_overlays.py` (51 ROM-free tests) runs in the CI tests step. **The kinds, as built** (patterns on C text after the regions are applied, not a C parser): `index`, `(` cast to a pointer to a scalar type, or to a pointer to a pointer (`void **`), expression `)` `[` any index `]`; `offset`, a unary `*` on a cast of a parenthesised sum or difference, `*(T *) ((u8 *) x + K)`, or on a parenthesised sum whose left operand starts with a cast, `*((s32 *) x + 2)`, with K any operand; `opaque`, a member named `pad`, `pad_...`, `padN...`, `padding...` or `unk...` (not `pads`) reached by `.` or `->` with an integer-literal index, the text including the postfix chain before it; `record`, a cast to a pointer or pointer to pointer to a struct or union typedef or tag declared in `src/bondtypes.h`, `src/game/*.h` or `include/PR/libaudio.h`, with its operand (a cast of `NULL` or `0` is not listed); `run`, in the headers listed and `libaudio.h`, a non-pointer member of type `Gfx`, `Model` or a record followed directly by members named `field_...`, `pad...` or `unk...` that are not themselves of such a type, its text the declaration and the number of fillers. A parenthesised type is a cast only when an operand follows it and no identifier (other than `return` or `case`), `)` or `]` precedes it, so prototypes, declarators and `sizeof (T *)` are not sites (23 record-type parentheses in the tree are such). **Departures from the brief, each tested:** the brief's `offset` form does not match `src/sched.c`'s `*((s32*)client + 2)`, one of the five measured reads, so `offset` also takes a dereferenced sum whose left operand is a cast; `index` takes pointer-to-pointer casts (`((void **) gptr_stan)[1]` reads a pointer by position); a `run` filler that is itself a record ends the run and starts its own (otherwise each `coord3d unkNN` in a row of them was a run over the next). **Files.** Tracked `.c` and `.h` files under `src/`, `port/src/` and `port/include/` (the headers `src/` and `port/src/` compile, so their macros and inline functions are read), except the `romconv_`, `romfile_` and `romdata` loaders. Left out by default, each named in the help text: `port/fast3d` (the C++ renderer, strict-tier; `list port/fast3d` reads it as C and gives 5 sites, three `index` and two `offset` reads of texture data in `gfx_pc.cpp`; `roc_part_key`'s address key in `gfx_roomcache.inl` is another pattern, which no kind matches, and stays with Task 11's reading), `port/web` (the browser build, 32-bit wasm only), `port/crash`, `port/win` and `include/` (the SDK headers). **Regions.** A condition is evaluated with three values: `TARGET_N64`, `!IS_64_BIT`, `0`, the symbols no PC build defines (`TARGET_N64`, `VERSION_EU`, `VERSION_JP`, `DEBUG`, `BUGFIX_R1`, `REFRESH_PAL`, `AUD_PROFILE`, `ENABLE_USB`, `AIPARSE`, `XBLADEBUG`, `LIBDRAGON`: none is in `CMakeLists.txt` or `cmake/`, which the test checks) and those no 64-bit build defines (`_WIN32`, `__EMSCRIPTEN__`, `GE_WEB`: `CMakeLists.txt` refuses 64 bits on Windows and with Emscripten, which the test checks) are false; `IS_64_BIT`, `1`, `__SIZEOF_POINTER__ == 8` and the symbols `add_compile_definitions` gives every PC build (`VERSION_US` and the rest, checked against `CMakeLists.txt`) are true; any other symbol (`GE_VIDEO`, `__APPLE__`, `GE_LP64_ORACLE`) is unknown and its branch is kept with its `#else`. `&&`, `||`, `!` and parentheses combine them; `#else` and `#elif` follow a branch surely taken as false, and a true `#elif` after an unknown branch is kept and closes the `#else`; a region nested in one left out is left out. Measured on the tree: treating the never-defined symbols as unknown would add 14 `record` sites outside `src/game/propobj.c` and make that file's braces unbalance (a `#if !defined(BUGFIX_R1)` closes one), and treating `_WIN32` and the rest as unknown would add 5 `offset` sites (`portModuleFor`'s Windows image parsing, `port/src/main.c`). A file whose kept code leaves braces unbalanced is refused (exit 2) rather than misread. **Site identity.** The function is found from the braces: the identifier before the last top-level parenthesis of the text since the previous top-level `}` (so a definition over several lines, a K&R definition and a macro-qualified one are named by their function); a site in a file-scope initializer or declaration is owned by the object it defines; a cast in a `#define` body (continuation lines joined, before comments are removed, as C does) is owned by `#define NAME`. The text is normalized: whitespace removed except one space between two identifier characters, so moving or reformatting code changes no key; any other change to the text is a new site and its old line stale. The Nth occurrence of one key in a file has ` #N` appended, so a second copy added later is a new, unreviewed site. **What it cannot see, and what covers it:** a cast written through a typedef'd pointer type (pointer typedefs are not collected; nothing else covers it); a `void *` assigned to a record pointer without a cast, which C allows (nothing static; the demo traces and, for an overrun, the sanitizer runs with Task 2's poisoning, on the paths that run); an offset added to a pointer variable in an earlier statement, `p += 4; *(u16 *) p` or `p[4]` on a `u8 *` (the same runs only); `memcpy` between records of different types (the sanitizers only when it overruns; nothing for a copy of the right size and the wrong layout); a union read through another member, except a literal index into a member named as filler (the layout probe for the overlays it pins; the traces); a cast to a type outside the three header sets, `Gfx` and the port's own structs (the video runs see display lists that are drawn); a macro defined in a file outside the scope, and each expansion of a scoped macro (its definition is one site); a `//` comment that ends in a backslash, which C continues onto the next line. The compile gate sees none of these: they are valid C at both widths. **The tree** (`list`, `main` at 1b6a55a plus this change): 1,219 sites in 73 files, 113 `index`, 30 `offset`, 56 `opaque`, 995 `record`, 25 `run`; by folder, `src/game` 1,057 (100, 28, 56, 862, 11), `src` outside `game` and `libultra*` 59 (0, 1, 0, 44, 14: the 14 runs are in `bondtypes.h`), `src/libultra*` 93 (9, 1, 0, 83, 0), `port/src` 10 (4, 0, 0, 6, 0), `port/include` 0. The planning counts were 95, 6, 50, 380 and 7: the `record` figure here counts every cast whose target is declared in the three header sets, `struct` tags and math records (`coord3d`, `Mtxf`) included, each occurrence once; 20 sites are in files no PC build compiles (`bnkf.c`, `contpfs.c`, `conteepread.c`, `leointerrupt.c`, `xprintf.c`). Every one of the measured positional reads is listed: `src/game/chraction.c:weaponIsOneHanded:opaque:v->act_bytes.padding[84]` (and its `record` cast `(ChrRecord*)arg0->voidp`), `triggered_on_shot_hit:index:((u16*)sp80)[2]`, `... #2`, `((u16*)struck_ani->struck_anim)[2]`, `src/game/unk_092E50.c:sub_GAME_7F092E50:index:((u32*)MipMap2C_Something_Setup)[8]` with ` #2` and ` #3` and `((u32*)MipMap2C_Something2_Setup)[8]`, `src/game/options.c:sub_GAME_7F0A4B40:index:((s32*)pFontChars)[0x224]` and `src/sched.c:__scHandleRetrace:offset:*((s32*)client+2)`. **Found on a first reading of the list, by reading, not yet confirmed by the probe or fixed** (the review batches and Task 4 decide): four more reads of an animation header's frame count by position, `chrlvTickStand`'s two `((u16*)ANIM_FROM_TABLE(...))[2]` and `chrlvTickDie`'s two (`ModelAnimation` begins with an `intptr_t`, so at 64 bits halfword 2 is half of `address`, not `unk04` at 8: the same defect as the three Task 4 names); `set_actor_on_path`'s `self->act_init.padding[0x13] = -1`, which writes `act_patrol.lastvisible60` (byte 76) at 32 bits and `act_patrol.waydata.segdisttotal` at 64 bits, where the `path` pointer moves the rest by 4; and `play_hit_soundeffect_and_proper_volume`'s `self->act_ubytes.padding[45]`, `act_gopos.unk59` at 32 bits and a byte of `waypoints[1]` at 64 bits. **Checks run:** the test, first failing with `No module named 'lp64_overlays'` and then each new case failing before its code (`_WIN32` region, run ending, `pads`, `#elif` after an unknown branch, which found a defect in the first version); five deliberate breakages in a scratch copy (TARGET_N64 unknown, occurrences unnumbered, whitespace only collapsed, stale lines ignored, an unbalanced end accepted) each failed tests; `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: `identical in loaded code and data`, exit 0; the CI tests step's lines in the x86_64 container: all 59 lines exit 0 (`Ran 51 tests ... OK` for the new one; `lp64_diagnostics.py gate`: 354 and 385 files compiled, 0 failed; narrowing 0, unprototyped 2; `hand_gallery.py verify --allow-pending`: pending, the workflow file being a deferred input), the sanitized buffer line run as its 64-bit half there; after `git add`, `lp64_casts.py check`: `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`. *LP64-005 task 3, review fixes to the overlay lister (2026-11-18). Commit "List the offset reads the lister missed, and the stored casts" (Python tools, their test, the reviewed list's header and documents; no compiled file changed).* The task review found real sites the first version did not list, which is the detector's failure mode. **Fixed.** `offset` now judges the dereferenced expression after unwrapping redundant parentheses and chains of pointer and integer casts: a pointer cast of a sum or difference whose offset is constant or computed (`*((s32 *) ((u8 *) x + 8))`, `*((u16 *) (uintptr_t) (timg - 8))`, `*((Word4 *) (((u8 *) p) + offset))`: a computed offset is a read by position too, so the brief's "with a constant" is widened), a sum whose left operand is a pointer cast (`*(((u16 *) h) + 2)`), and a pointer cast of an address, `*(T *) &x[K]` and `*(T *) &p->member` (kept in `offset` rather than a sixth kind: it is a read at a position chosen by the address). A `*` after `else`, `do` or the `)` of an `if`, `while`, `for` or `switch` condition is a dereference (it was taken for a multiplication). `index` climbs parentheses that only wrap the cast group (`(((u16 *) h))[2]`). `run` reads struct declarations in `.c` and `.inl` files too (it found `src/game/bg.c`'s `Unk80081600`, `bbox2d unk0` and two fillers), and `.inl` files under the scope's folders are read (`port/src/port_hud_audit.inl`, which `port_hud.c` includes; it holds no site). `check` refuses (exit 2) a listing that repeats a key and one with no site. `__cplusplus` is false (the files are C; an `extern "C" {` block left its functions nameless), and an `#if` condition with arithmetic, a comma or a macro call is unknown and kept, where `#if 0 + X` was judged false. **The stored-cast aid.** `lp64_overlays.py list --locals` prints every scalar-pointer cast stored in a local or a member (`u16 *p = (u16 *) anim;`), `file:function:lhs=cast operand` with its line: 279 in the scope, 244 to locals and 35 to members. *LP64-005 task 3, a cast before a dereference in the overlay lister (2026-11-18). Commit "See a dereference written right after a cast" (Python tools, their test and documents; no compiled file changed).* The re-review found one root cause still open: a `*` after a cast's `)` was taken for a multiplication, so `(T) *(U *) e` was never seen, and three compiled reads were unlisted. **Fixed.** A `*` after the `)` of a cast is a dereference: the group is a scalar type, a pointer type or a single name, and it is not after an identifier (`sizeof (u32) * n`, a call) or `]`, nor after `)` unless that group is a cast too (`(s32)(u32) *(u16 *) p`). A single name in parentheses, `(x)`, may be a typedef name or a parenthesised variable, and the text cannot tell them apart; the tool counts it as a cast, so a doubtful `(x) * (T *) p` is listed, because a false site costs one review and a missed read costs silence. Reached, once `g_PlayerTickCount` reaches 2, for a remote player of a multiplayer game that holds a weapon held as a gun or a prop in each hand (firing groups 0, 1 and 3, every entry naming a table), or one that is unarmed or holds a non-gun item, is not crouched and has a non-zero sideways speed, whether or not it also moves forward (crouch positions 1 and 0 take entry 5 first; `bondview2.c:14732-14745` then test only `speedsideways`, choosing group 2's entries 3 and 4, `bondview.c:529-530`; its other entries name no table). The value goes to `modelSetAnimation` as a `ModelAnimation *` (when the body has no `anim2`) and into `players_cur_animation`; `modelSetAnimFrame`'s port guard `portPtrLooksBad` refuses only values below 0x10000 or misaligned, so `modelConstrainOrWrapAnimFrame` reads `anim->unk04` through it: a fault on the first tick in which such a player is processed. Its match with `cur` also gates `chrlvUpdateAimendbackShoulders`. A player's start and respawn weapon comes from the setup's first `INTROTYPE_ITEM` intro record (`bondview_r.c:225-245`, else the fist; `mp_respawn_handler` re-adds the records' items, `bondview2.c:12560`), or from Spawn with Weapon (`[display] mp_spawn_weapon`, default 0, always 0 headless). A scratch reader of the US ROM's 13 multiplayer setups (not committed, deleted) found in each exactly one such record, right hand, not for demos, naming the fist (group 2). So the plan's no-input multiplayer runs (13 arenas, 2 and 4 players, 1,800 frames; the `stages` set's `mp-` cases), whose players hold the fist and have no sideways speed, did not fault and do not exercise this path; Task 8's START-only respawn cases would not reach it either. *LP64-005 task 3, review batch 5, second commit: types that exist only as pointers (2026-11-18). Commit "List the record types a 64-bit build reaches only through pointers" (a new script and its test, the layout probe and its new `probe_views.h`, `test_abi_probe.sh`, the CI tests step, this inventory and the 64-bit plan; no compiled game file changed).* R11 applied to the whole tree. **Tool:** `scripts/port/lp64_pointer_types.py scan BUILD_DIR...` (standard library; `--explain TYPE` prints every counted use of one type). It is a separate script, not a subcommand of the lister, because its question is about declarations, not reads: it runs each C and C++ entry of a 64-bit tree's `compile_commands.json` through its own compiler with `-E`, so it reads exactly what the 64-bit build compiles (headers only where included, every `#if` evaluated by the compiler), which the lister's text patterns cannot. The types are the structs and unions defined in the record headers and in the `.c` files of the lister's scope. One is printed when no compiled line declares an object of it (variable, member, by-value parameter or return, value cast, compound literal), embeds it or takes its `sizeof`; lines reported under a `#line` directive are mapped back to physical lines. It does not count `sizeof *p` or a pointer step as sizing, so a type allocated only that way is printed and judged by hand. `scripts/port/test_lp64_pointer_types.py` (9 tests, added to the CI tests step) was written after the script; each of four mutations of the script (sizeof read as a pointer use, embedded declarators ignored, aliases unresolved, `#line` ignored) failed its own test. **Output** on the aarch64 container's `gate` and `gate-video` trees (configured as CI configures them): 113 types (10,247 bytes), 81 used only through pointers and 32 that no compiled line names outside their definition. **The table** (type; where its pointers come from and which record it really is; the members used, with compiled offsets at 32 and 64 bits where the view is not the record itself; verdict):

Each was seen failing on drift in the aarch64 container and at i686 `-m32`, each with its own message (9 drifts: a member inserted before the pinned one, in a header or in an edited copy of the `.c` file named through the script's `ABI_PROBE_*_C` variables; for auditnode the inserted member is a pointer, since a 4-byte one before `data` at 64 bits fills the padding after `opcode` and moves nothing). **R11 for batches 1 and 2:** the record types cast at their `same` and `overlay-64` lines of the index, offset, opaque and run kinds are `Model` (a real Model at 64 bits in field_B68's union), `ModelNode` (the header's first member, RootNode), `Word4` (one Vertex, batch 2), `TintedGlassRecord` (the record itself), a `void **` over StanPrefixRecord's two pointers, and the act structs over `act_init.padding` and `TankRecord.rect` and the Gfx runs, whose members the batch 1 assertions name one by one; none is a view with members read elsewhere that its line does not cover.

*LP64-005 task 3 as built, summary (2026-11-18). Commit "Close the record of every record read through another type" (`lp64_overlays.py`'s `check` and its test, the model scanner and its test, the reviewed list, the CI tests step, `AGENTS.md`, this inventory and the 64-bit plan; no compiled game file changed).* **The tool:** `scripts/port/lp64_overlays.py list` finds six kinds of record read through another type in `src/`, `port/src/` and `port/include/` (`index`, `offset`, `opaque`, `record`, `run`, `stored`; `--help` says what each covers), keyed by file, function, kind and normalized text with a `#N` suffix for repeats; `check` requires one line in `lp64_overlays_reviewed.txt` per site, a verdict and a reason, then prints `N defect lines` and, since this commit, `N measured lines` (test first: `test_lp64_overlays_check.py`'s two new tests failed before the count was printed). `check` now runs in CI's tests step (without `--no-defects`, which the milestone's last task adds once Task 4 and the strict branch have taken the defect lines off). Beside it: the layout probe's `probe_overlays.h`, `probe_stored.h` and `probe_views.h`, named by message in each `same` and `overlay-64` line; the ROM scanners `lp64_model_scan.py` and `lp64_setup_scan.py`, named in each `measured:` line; and `lp64_pointer_types.py` for R11. **Counts** at this commit, 1,634 sites: by kind 113 `index`, 165 `offset`, 56 `opaque`, 995 `record`, 26 `run`, 279 `stored`; by verdict 935 `typed`, 492 `same`, 32 `overlay-64`, 133 `dead`, 42 `defect` (37 `Task 4:`, 5 `strict:`, none `undecided:`); 114 lines are `measured:`. The gunfire.c slot 1 read was already settled in batch 5's first commit: the joypad, the one gun model with a group node in slot 1, never reaches it (its weapon stats lack WEAPONSTATBITFLAG_SHOW_FIRST_PERSON, so the block at gunfire.c:1085 is skipped), and its `flashvisptr` line says so.

The same defect, recorded at fix round 3: `setupCommandGetObject` has no label for NOTHING (0), DEBRIS (15) or UNK16 (16) (the "not included" comment, loadobjectmodel.c:540-543), so they fall through to `return obj;` (546) and are handed to its callers as ObjectRecords; each is one word at 32 bits (`sizepropdef`'s default) and 8 bytes at 64 (`WIDE(1, 2, 0, 0)`, romconv_setup_props.c:49, 64-65), with no `prop` at 16. That `return obj;` converts a PropDefHeaderRecord * with no cast, so it is no lister site; the four lines here carry it. Wrong at both widths. Reach: no stock setup, measured: `GE_ROM=ROM python3 scripts/port/lp64_setup_scan.py types` over the 34 setups lists no NOTHING, DEBRIS, UNK16 or UNK41 command. Repair, 64-bit only, each place right for its own switch: at prop.c:2530, prop.c:2739 and cleanup_objects.c:46 the `case PROPDEF_UNK41:` label goes in the `#else` of an `#if IS_64_BIT` whose 64-bit branch has no label; those switches have no `default`, so at 64 bits an UNK41 record is skipped (no domakedefaultobj, no INSIDEANOTHEROBJ reparenting, no objFreePermanently) and the walk steps past it by `sizepropdef`. At loadobjectmodel.c:506 removing the label is not enough: `setupCommandGetObject` (478-547) has no `default` and ends `return obj;` (546), so the record would still be returned as an ObjectRecord. There the repair is two conditionals, both of whose 32-bit sides are today's tokens exactly: line 506's `case PROPDEF_UNK41:` goes in the `#else` of an `#if IS_64_BIT` with nothing in its 64-bit branch, and a `default: return NULL;` inside `#if IS_64_BIT` (no `#else`) closes the switch after the `return NULL;` group. At 64 bits the function then returns the record only for the 21 object types and NULL for every other command type, UNK41, NOTHING, DEBRIS and UNK16 included; a type added to the enum later gets NULL at 64 bits until it is labelled into the object group (at 32 bits it falls through to `return obj;` as today). The default form was chosen over adding NOTHING, DEBRIS, UNK16 and UNK41 labels to the `return NULL;` group because it also covers later types; both leave the 32-bit tokens unchanged. NOTHING, DEBRIS and UNK16 need nothing at the other three places: prop.c:2376's and prop.c:2729's switches have no label for them and no `default`, and cleanup_objects.c lists DEBRIS and UNK16 in its non-object group (56-57) and has no label for NOTHING and no `default`; the other walks that read commands as objects are `setupGetCommandIndexByProp` (entry 10, whose type test excludes them), `setupFindObjForReuse` (loadobjectmodel.c:548, which reads only the type its callers ask for, COLLECTABLE or HAT, propobj.c:12241 and 12349) and the debug listing at prop.c:1851 (object labels only, no `default`); the swaps (prop.c:2018, 2073) and the counter `load_proptype` read no member. Every caller tests the result for NULL before using it: TAG prop.c:2663-2666, RENAME prop.c:2681-2684, prop.c:2749-2751, SWITCH prop.c:2807-2810, SAFE_ITEM prop.c:2841-2845, LOCK_DOOR prop.c:2875-2878 and chrprop.c:1945-1947. prop.c:2100 is already in the 32-bit-only swap. The 32-bit side is left as inherited.

**Inherited at 32 bits, for the owner.** Five defects are wrong at both widths; at fix round 1 the coordinator ruled their repairs 64-bit only, so the 32-bit program keeps them. For each, what the 32-bit program does today, its reach, and the one-line fix at both widths that would remove the `#if`:

- *Entry 10, setupGetCommandIndexByProp.* Today at 32 bits: the walk compares bytes 16 to 19 of every setup command with the prop; for a command shorter than 20 bytes (a 16-byte LinkRecord) that is the next command's header word, never a prop, so no stock walk stops early. Reach: none, by reading the one caller (chrprop.c:1943; no scanner command, the reach is a code path, not a ROM fact). Fix at both widths: the type test of the 64-bit form in place of line 338, admitting exactly the 21 types DOOR, PROP, KEY, ALARM, CCTV, MAGAZINE, COLLECTABLE, MONITOR, MULTI_MONITOR, RACK, AUTOGUN, HAT, AMMO, ARMOUR, GAS_RELEASING, VEHICHLE, AIRCRAFT, GLASS, SAFE, TANK and TINTED_GLASS (setupCommandGetObject's object group without UNK41; not NOTHING, DEBRIS or UNK16, which it lets fall through).
- *Entry 11, the texture number read 8 bytes before the texels.* Today at 32 bits: for a model with an inline texture entry the read is 2 bytes at 0x05xxxxxx - 8, an address the game does not own (a compiled-in 32-bit model may hold the texels' address instead, whose 8 bytes before are not a number either). Reach: no stock load, measured: `GE_ROM=ROM python3 scripts/port/lp64_model_scan.py textures` finds inline entries only in PgoldeneyelogoZ, PlegalpageZ and PnintendologoZ, loaded without a texture pool; reached by the GE_GUN_AUDIT diagnostic and a replaced or added model with an inline entry. Fix at both widths: `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST(id) &&` in the guard at gun.c:1051 and objecthandler_2.c:444.
- *Entry 12, UNK41, NOTHING, DEBRIS and UNK16 taken as objects.* Today at 32 bits: an UNK41 record's flags, flags2, prop and model are read from the next command (next+4, +8, +12, +16), and it can be passed to domakedefaultobj and objFreePermanently; `setupCommandGetObject` returns an UNK41, NOTHING, DEBRIS or UNK16 record as an ObjectRecord, whose callers then read `prop` (and write `runtime_bitflags` or `flags2`) on the next command's bytes. Reach: no stock setup, measured: `GE_ROM=ROM python3 scripts/port/lp64_setup_scan.py types` over the 34 setups lists no NOTHING, DEBRIS, UNK16 or UNK41 command. Fix at both widths: remove the `case PROPDEF_UNK41:` labels at prop.c:2530 and 2739, cleanup_objects.c:46 and loadobjectmodel.c:506 (the first three switches have no `default`, so the record is skipped), and add `default: return NULL;` to `setupCommandGetObject`'s switch (it has no `default` and ends `return obj;`, so removing the label alone would still return UNK41, and NOTHING, DEBRIS and UNK16, which have no label, are returned today); every caller tests for NULL.
- *Entry 16, mp_respawn_handler's intro step.* Today at 32 bits: a WATCH record is stepped by 4 bytes and its hours and minutes words are parsed as intro types; a CREDITS record by 4 and its table offset parsed as a type. Reach: no stock multiplayer setup, measured: `python3 scripts/port/lp64_model_scan.py intros` counts 88 SPAWN, 13 ITEM and 13 CUFF records in the 13 multiplayer setups and no WATCH or CREDITS. Fix at both widths: step each by its own size, as bondviewLoadSetupIntroSection does (strict tier, for the strict branch). On the branch `lp64/play-strict`, strict batch 1 made the 64-bit side so (WATCH and CREDITS cases inside `#if IS_64_BIT`); the 32-bit default is the `#else` of that conditional (bondview2.c:12601-12603 on the branch, 12587-12589 on `main`), and the fix at both widths would replace the conditional with its 64-bit side.
- *Entry 13, bgTestBulletHitBackground's opcode bytes* (last: no visible effect). Today at 32 bits: the back-scan compares w0's low byte with G_SETTILE and so stops at the wrong command or the list's start, and writes wrong `tileformat` and `tilesize`. Reach: every bullet that hits a room's background (chrprop.c:703, port_bullet_rooms.c:79, port_projectile_arc_world.c:150). This disagrees with the dispatch, which said no stock run reaches any of the five: this one is reached in every stage, but the two members it writes are read nowhere, so nothing changes on screen or in play at either width. Fix at both widths: the `w0 >> 24` and `(w0 >> 21) & 7` forms at bg.c:4979, 4984 and 4998.

*LP64-005 task 3, batch 5 review fix 1, first commit: stored forms and the measured rule (2026-11-18). Defect counts are unchanged: 41 lines as 16 defects (36 `Task 4:` lines as 13, 5 `strict:` as 3), each named once. **Also:** an `AGENTS.md` sentence was rewrapped, and a hand-over note on unk_092E50.c:277 was added after the gap list. **Counts:** 1,641 sites; 938 `typed`, 493 `same`, 32 `overlay-64`, 137 `dead`, 41 `defect`; 114 `measured:` lines.

The overlay lister's blind spots, consolidated: what the overlay lister cannot see, one form a line, with what covers it (the compile gate sees none of them; they are valid C at both widths):

- *A new or changed use of a stored pointer* (`p[3]` added after the `stored` site `p=(u16*)anim`): the store is the site and its uses are not, so the change makes no new site; the reviewed reason names the uses that were read, and the demo traces cover the paths they run.
- *A scalar-pointer cast passed as an argument and indexed in the callee* (`f((u16 *) anim)`): not a site; the demo traces only.
- *A view's member read away from the cast to it*: a type reached only through pointers is judged over every member read through it (R11). A new pointer-only type is covered: `lp64_pointer_types.py check` compares a scan of the CI gate trees with `lp64_pointer_types.txt` in the tests step and fails until the type has a row. A new member read through a type already listed (the `child->unk18` shape) is not covered: its row and probe assertion are updated by hand.
- *A `sizeof *p` or pointer-step allocation*: `lp64_pointer_types.py` does not count it as sizing, so such a type is listed and judged by hand (three are, in batch 5's table).
- *A cast through a typedef'd pointer type*: not covered.
- *A stored cast inside a compound literal* (`p = (T){ (u8 *) x }`), *or reached through an operator other than grouping, a conditional arm, a comma, a binary `+` or an initializer list* (`p = n - (u8 *) x`): not a `stored` site (the tool's help names both); a scalar-pointer cast there is seen only when it is indexed or dereferenced on the spot. A returned cast (`return (u8 *) x;`) is outside the kind, which is stores: the caller's use of the value is what reads it, and the demo traces cover those paths.
- *A declaration that disagrees with its definition in another file*: no compiler sees both, and the lister reads casts, not declarations. One is known: port/src/animdata.c:66 declares `animation_table_ptrs2` `extern intptr_t[]` while initanitable.c:220 defines it `struct ModelAnimation *[]` (and animdata.c:295 stores it in an `intptr_t *` with no cast); it is benign while the slots are pointer-sized, which probe_stored.h "an animation table slot is a pointer of intptr_t's size and alignment" pins (fix round 2).

Hand-over note (fix round 3, not a defect line): unk_092E50.c:277, in `sub_GAME_7F092E50`, sets `((u32 *) MipMap2C_Something2_Setup)[8]` from `((u32 *) MipMap2C_Something_Setup)[8]`, the other list's word, with its low byte replaced by the animated LOD fraction, where the four lines before it each read the list they write. Inherited. Today it has no effect at either width, because both lists' words at that place are equal before the low byte: at 32 bits each is the `gsDPSetPrimColor(0, 15, ...)` command's w0 (unk_092E50.c:22 and 39); at 64 bits each is the low half of `[2].words.w0`, the `gsDPSetTileSize(0, 2, 2, 0, 0)` the lines just above set with the same values. They would differ only if the two lists' commands diverged. Whether reading the first list was intended is unknown. Its two index sites are entry 5's, whose repair, writing `[4].words.w0` by name, is where to decide it.
- *A `void *` assigned to a record pointer without a cast*: the demo traces, and the sanitizer runs with Task 2's poisoning when the read overruns.
- *An offset added to a pointer variable in an earlier statement* (`p += 4; *(u16 *) p`): the same.
- *`memcpy` between records of different types*: the sanitizers when it overruns; nothing for a copy of the right size and the wrong layout.
- *A union read through another member*, except a literal index into a member named as filler: the layout probe for the overlays it pins, and the traces.
- *A `record` cast to a type outside the three header sets* (`Gfx`, the port's own structs): the video runs see display lists that are drawn. A scalar-pointer cast of any operand is seen only when it is indexed (`index`) or dereferenced (`offset`) on the spot.
- *Each expansion of a scoped macro* (the definition is one site), and macros defined outside the scope: not covered.
- *A `//` comment ending in a backslash*: not covered.
- *A node's `Data` read through a pointer already typed as the record, with no cast* (`position = objheader->Switches[i]->Data`): not covered by the lister; the ones found while reviewing, with what covers them: bondview2.c:10972 and front.c:2557 (fix round 1 of batch 3), chraction.c's `sub_GAME_7F02D630` slot 0 (an `f32 *` stored without a cast; batch 5), gunfire.c's slot 28 `hingedata` and slot 1 `Switch.RwDataIndex` reads (the same), and gunfire.c:2793 `watchRenderController`'s `objheader->Switches[i]->Data` for i = 1 to 12, passed as a position to `matrix_4x4_set_position` and `matrix_4x4_set_identity_and_position`: measured (`python3 scripts/port/lp64_model_scan.py slots --match '^joypad$' --slots 1-12`, batch 4), a group node in each slot of the joypad model, whose Origin floats are at 0, 4 and 8 at both widths (probe_overlays.h "ModelRoData_GroupRecord.Origin is the floats at 0, 4 and 8"); a replaced model with a record that holds pointers in one of those slots would be read as a different wrong position at each width. Also uncast and so not sites (batch 4): the autogun's slot 1 read in `objTick`, counted with its slots 2 to 6, and the monitor slot reads passed to `process_monitor_animation_microcode`. (Fix round 1 of batch 5 compared every earlier batch's gap notes with this list, the original "what it cannot see" and the notes of batches 3 and 4: these two were the only ones missing.)

*LP64-005 task 5, frigate2's first difference: a door's clearance test (2026-11-18). Commit "Read a guard's hidden flag through its ChrRecord when a door moves" (`src/game/propobj.c`, the new ROM-free test `scripts/port/test_lp64_typed_doorclear.c` in `test_lp64_typed_reads.sh`, `scripts/port/lp64_demo_traces.txt`, this inventory).* **How it was found.** frigate2 was the one demo still parting from the i686 trace, at tick 273 (Task 4). With `GE_RNGTRACE=273`, `lp64_play.py callers` named the same draws in both builds except one more in the 64-bit build, before tick 273's first `chrCheckTargetInSight`: `plot_course_for_actor` (chraction.c:3816), the 64-bit build making 23 draws to the i686 build's 22. Prints from a scratch copy of the tree under `build/lp64/` (never committed) named the rest. The call came from `chrlvTickGoPos`'s re-plot of a guard that has not moved for a while (chraction.c:9513), for guard 44, walking (ACT_GOPOS) toward a door. Its position was the same, bit for bit, in both builds through tick 261 and parted at 262: the i686 guard walked on, while the 64-bit guard stayed at the same x and z and re-plotted from tick 272 on. The guard's move test (`sub_GAME_7F01F614`, chr.c) first differed at tick 257, where `stanTestVolume` found door prop 84 in the guard's way in the 64-bit build only. The door's own state first differed at the same tick: up to 256 it opened identically, and at 257 the i686 door stopped with its speed set to 0 and its opening put back, while the 64-bit door kept opening into the guard. A door stops when `sub_GAME_7F0448A8` (propobj.c) finds a guard or player standing in its swing. **The defect.** For each guard or player prop, that test skipped one flagged hidden by reading `prop->obj` (an `ObjectRecord *` in PropRecord's union) and testing `(intptr_t) obj->model & 0x400`. The union holds a `ChrRecord *` for those props. `ObjectRecord.model` is at 0x14 at 32 bits, where `ChrRecord.chrflags` is, so the 32-bit build tests `chrflags & CHRFLAG_HIDDEN` (0x400). At 64 bits `model` is at 0x18 (it follows the 8-byte `prop`), where `ChrRecord.prop` is (`chrflags` stays at 0x14), so the test read bit 0x400 of the guard's prop pointer. Printed at ticks 255 to 258: for guard 44, the word read was 0x100008 (its chrflags) at 32 bits and 0xaaaac474b520 (its prop's address) at 64 bits, whose bit 0x400 is set. So the 64-bit door took the guard for hidden and ignored it. The read was by position through the wrong member of a union. `lp64_overlays.py` does not list union member reads (its `--help` says what it cannot see), so the reviewed list did not name the site. None of the five `strict:` defect lines was involved: the ammo icon width reads (gunfire.c) only place the HUD, and `playerTick`'s firing table read and `mp_respawn_handler`'s intro walk (bondview2.c) run only in multiplayer. **Repair, the same 32-bit code:** the local is a `ChrRecord *` read from `prop->chr`, and the test is `!(temp_v0_2->chrflags & CHRFLAG_HIDDEN)`. A player's viewer prop holds its body's `ChrRecord` or NULL there too (bondview2.c:626-627; bondview_r.c:700), so one read serves both prop types. No overlay remains, so the layout probe gets no new assertion. **Check, seen failing first:** `test_lp64_typed_doorclear.c` includes propobj.c and builds a door whose swing holds a guard. One case gives the guard chrflags without `CHRFLAG_HIDDEN` and an invented prop pointer with bit 0x400 set, and expects the door blocked (0). The other gives chrflags with the flag and a prop pointer without it, and expects the door clear (1). On the old code, at 64 bits (aarch64 container, `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64 bash scripts/port/test_lp64_typed_reads.sh`), both cases failed: `test_lp64_typed_doorclear: FAIL (64-bit): a guard without CHRFLAG_HIDDEN in the door's swing blocks it` and `... a guard with CHRFLAG_HIDDEN in the door's swing does not block it`. At 32 bits (i686 container) they passed. With the repair they pass at both widths. **Demos:** the i686 reference ran twice on this tree and agreed with itself: `OK: 14 demos agree with themselves`, frigate2 401 ticks in each. Against it, the plain and the sanitizer aarch64 runs both give `frigate2: identical (401 ticks)` and `OK: 14 demos, 14 identical, 0 differing as recorded`, so `lp64_demo_traces.txt` records frigate2 `identical`. **Checks**, after `git add`: `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: identical in loaded code and data, `.buildid` differs, exit 0. `lp64_casts.py check` 24 in 11 files. `lp64_overlays.py check` `OK: 1619 sites, all reviewed`, 5 defect lines, 108 measured lines (unchanged: neither the old nor the new read is a listed site). `test_lp64_overlays.py` passes (87 tests), with its pinned counts unchanged. *LP64-005 task 7, the inherited stack overrun (2026-11-18). Commit "Bound the file name that the host file check copies" (`src/game/indy_commands.c`, the new ROM-free `scripts/port/test_indy_file_name.c` in `scripts/port/test_buffers.sh`'s set, this inventory).* **The defect, at both widths and in the shipped 32-bit game:** `indyrescmdCheckFileExists` copied a file name into the 256-byte `strbuffer` of its `indy_resource_entry_type5` with `strncpy(cmd.strbuffer, name, sizeof(cmd.strbuffer))`. The game's own `strncpy` (`src/str.c`, linked into the Windows executable too: `ProjectMidas.map` places `strncpy` in `str.c.obj`) counts down only for the characters before the terminator, so for a name shorter than its count it writes the terminator and then count minus length zeros: one byte past the field. `fileGetIndex` reaches it for a file the ROM lacks, which is how the sanitizer `stops` cases `stop-citadel`, `stop-complex` and `stop-temple` died before their own stop line (sanitizer step 8 stood at 114 of 117). **The fix** asks `strncpy` for `sizeof(cmd.strbuffer) - 1`; the next line already terminates byte 255. For a name of 255 characters or fewer the field sent holds the name and then zeros, as before; for a longer one it holds the first 255 characters and a terminator, as before (the old copy wrote the 256th character and the next line overwrote it). Only the stray byte past the field is gone, so no caller sees a different command. The edit is on its own line, so no line number of the file moves. **The test:** `test_indy_file_name.c` includes `src/str.c` and `src/game/indy_commands.c`, captures what `osWriteHost` is given, and sends a 12-character name and a 299-character one, asserting the command's size (276 bytes), type and field. Against the old line its sanitized half died at both widths with `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow ... WRITE of size 1 ... in strncpy src/str.c:17`, `in indyrescmdCheckFileExists src/game/indy_commands.c:203`, `[32, 308) 'cmd' (line 196) <== Memory access at offset 308 overflows this variable` (64-bit half, `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64`, aarch64 container; 32-bit half, `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=32 ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0`, i686 container, emulated under qemu on this Mac). With the fix both halves print `test_buffers: PASS`, and the plain 32-bit half passes in the i686 container. The plain halves cannot see the overrun (it lands outside the field); they check the command. The sanitized line has not been seen passing as CI runs it (with leak detection, whose exit check hangs under qemu-i386). **The Windows comparison names this one function, as decision 13 allows:** `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` exits 1 with `.text: bytes differ (3365376 vs 3365376 bytes, 2 bytes differ, first at offset 0xa57c7)`. In the map that address, 0x100a67c7, lies in `indyrescmdCheckFileExists` (0x100a67a0 to 0x100a6820), and the disassembly of the two builds differs in one instruction, the count passed to `strncpy`: `movl $0x100, 0x8(%esp)` became `movl $0xff, 0x8(%esp)`. In the old 32-bit Windows function `cmd` is at -0x120(%ebp), its field ends at -0xc(%ebp), and the saved `%ebx` is at -0x4(%ebp): the stray zero landed in the frame's eight bytes of padding there, so the shipped game wrote it harmlessly; the new function writes nothing past `cmd`. **Checks**, after `git add`: `lp64_casts.py check` `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`; `lp64_overlays.py check` `OK: 1619 sites, all reviewed`, 5 defect lines; `test_lp64_overlays.py` 87 tests OK. The sanitizer `stops` set on the aarch64 executable built with the fix (`build/lp64/boot-san`): `OK: 12 of 12 cases`, and each of the three logs ends at its own `ge: FATAL: The setup file UsetupcatZ` (`UsetuprefZ`, `UsetupdishZ`) `is not served from the ROM` line, after `ge: fileGetIndex MISS`, with no sanitizer line. The task's other runs are in the next note.
*LP64-005 task 7, the absent host's unwritten answer (2026-11-18). Commit "Take no answer from the absent host as no file at 64 bits" (`src/game/indy_comms.c`, `scripts/port/test_indy_file_name.c`, the setup stops' lines in `scripts/port/lp64_play_cases.py` and `scripts/port/test_lp64_play.py`, this inventory).* **Found by** the first full sanitizer pass after the overrun fix: `stop-citadel` and `stop-temple` failed, each log ending at `ge: FATAL: The setup file UsetupcatZ` (`UsetupdishZ`) `did not load from the ROM; a 64-bit build cannot read it` instead of the expected `is not served from the ROM` line, though the `stops` set alone on the same executable had passed 12 of 12 minutes earlier, and `stop-complex` passed in the same run. **Cause, inherited at both widths:** `fileGetIndex` (`src/game/ob.c`) asks the Indy host about a name it does not hold through `indycommHostCheckFileExists`, which returns its local `response`. *LP64-005 task 10, the synthesizer's parameter pool (2026-11-19). Commit "Size the synthesizer's parameter pool by the largest update written into it" (`src/libultra/audio/synthInternals.h`, `src/libultra/audio/synthesizer.c`, the layout probe's overlay header, the new ROM-free `scripts/port/test_audio_synth.c` and `scripts/port/test_audio_synth.sh`, the CI tests step, this inventory).* **The defect, 64 bits only:** `alSynNew` built the parameter free list from `maxUpdates` records of `sizeof(ALParam)`, and each update taken from it is written through the view of its kind: `alSynStartVoiceParams` writes an `ALStartParamAlt`, `alSynStartVoice` an `ALStartParam`, `alSynFreeVoice` an `ALFreeParam`. Measured with a scratch program at both widths (GCC 13, x86_64 container): `ALParam` 28, `ALStartParam` 16, `ALStartParamAlt` 28, `ALFreeParam` 16 bytes at 32 bits, and 32, 24, 40 and 24 at 64, so at 64 bits a start's `wave` pointer (bytes 32 to 39) landed on the next record's `next` link, at every note: the planning runs' signal 11 in `alEnvmixerPull` and `__allocParam`. **The fix** declares `ALParamRoom`, the union of the four views (`synthInternals.h`), and `alSynNew` allocates and steps the pool by `sizeof(ALParamRoom)`, linking `&params[i].param`; `__allocParam` still returns `ALParam *`. At 32 bits the union is 28 bytes, so the program is the same (comparison below). **What it costs at 64 bits:** the pool grows from 256 records of 32 bytes to 256 of 40 at the default `GE_SNDSCALE` of 2 (`maxUpdates` 0x80 times 2), 2,048 bytes more of the music heap, which `GE_SNDDBG=1` reported as `ge: music heap 331632 of 753664 bytes used (GE_SNDSCALE=2)` on the fixed 64-bit video build (Dam, aarch64), so 329,584 before by the arithmetic (`alHeapDBAlloc` rounds each block to 16 bytes and both sizes are multiples of 16); the heap itself is not enlarged, and that run printed no `ge: lp64: pool` line. **Checks seen failing first.** The probe (`probe_overlays.h`) gains "a parameter pool record holds every update written into it" (`ALParamRoom` at least each of the four views, both widths), "a parameter pool record is 28 bytes at 32 bits", and "snd.c's ALSndpEvent fits an ALEvent with its state pointer where the message starts" (`sizeof(ALSndpEvent) <= sizeof(ALEvent)`, `common.state` at the offset of `msg` and of `msg.osc.vs`; the existing equal-size assertion stays). Before the fix the probe did not compile at 64 bits (`probe_overlays.h:351:23: error: 'ALParamRoom' undeclared here`); with it `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` (aarch64) and `ABI probe OK (64-bit)`, `ABI probe OK (32-bit)` (x86_64 container: the 64-bit half translated by Rosetta 2, the 32-bit half under qemu-i386). `test_audio_synth.c` builds, from invented numbers, one raw 16-bit wave of 2,000 samples of a square wave (level 12,000, half period 50), one sound and one instrument; starts a voice through `alSynAllocVoice`, `alSynStartVoiceParams` and `alSynSetVol` on a synthesizer made by `alInit` (64 updates, 4 voices, no effect); runs ten frames of 368 samples through `alAudioFrame` and the interpreter (`audio_pc.c` with `PORT_AUDIO_INTERPRETER_ONLY`); and asserts, each test in a child process so a stray write fails by name, that the interpreter skipped no frame, that the output has a non-zero sample, and that after 64 note starts and stops and 70 more frames (over a second, so every update posted outside a client callback has been applied) the free list holds its 64 records, each one of the pool's own. What the interpreter reads by address lives in one `mmap` block, since a 32-bit image under emulation sits below the 0x01000000 the validator takes for the lowest real address. Against the old pool: `test_audio_synth: noteStartsAndStopsGiveBackEveryParameter: killed by signal 11` at 64 bits (aarch64, and the 64-bit half in the x86_64 container) with `test_audio_synth: PASS (32-bit)`; a sanitized copy of the harness placed the write at `use-after-poison ... WRITE of size 8 ... in alSynStartVoiceParams src/libultra/audio/synstartvoiceparam.c:57`, the first record taken being the pool's last, whose `wave` lands past the pool in Task 2's poisoned music heap. With the fix: `test_audio_synth: PASS (64-bit)` (aarch64), `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` (x86_64 container). The test's other two assertions passed at 64 bits against the old pool too (one note in ten frames does not reach a reused record). `bash scripts/port/test_audio_synth.sh` joins the CI tests step. **Checks.** `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`, exit 0. *LP64-005 task 10, why every sample load was refused (2026-11-19). Commit "Read the reverb's delay taps as signed offsets at 64 bits" (`src/libultrare/audio/reverb.c`, `scripts/port/test_audio_synth.c`, this inventory).* **Found by** running Dam (`GE_STAGE=dam`, `GE_SKIPINTRO=1`, 300 frames) on a 64-bit video build with the parameter pool fixed, from a scratch copy of the tree (under `build/lp64/`, deleted) whose interpreter warning also printed the buffer state it refused and the eight commands before it. The planning run's one-time `ge: audio: WARNING - audio frame skipped (silent): command 15 op 0x04 ...` came with `in=320 out=0 count=13120`: command 14, `A_SETBUFF` with a count of 0x3340 bytes, and command 15, `A_LOADBUFF` at 0xAAACE85E94A0, while command 12, the load before it, read 0xAAAAE85E95E0: the address lay 0x1FFFFFEC0 bytes, 8 GB less 320, past the buffer it should read. Every frame of the mix was dropped (`327`, `556` and `552 frames skipped as invalid` in the log's 10-second health lines) and the recording was silence. **Cause, 64 bits only, not in the bank converter:** the planning run's guess at a wave table field was wrong; the loads are the reverb's (`AL_FX_CUSTOM`, `music.c`), not a voice's. `alFxPull` and `_loadOutputBuffer` (`reverb.c`) read the delay line at taps behind its write pointer, `&r->input[-d->input]`, `&r->input[-d->output]` and `&r->input[-(d->output - d->rsdelta)]`, where `ALDelay`'s `input` and `output` are `u32` sample counts (`synthInternals.h`). Negated as a `u32` the tap is 2^32 minus it; at 32 bits that index wraps the pointer back by the tap, at 64 bits it is a 33-bit byte offset added to the pointer, 8 GB minus twice the tap ahead. `_loadBuffer` then finds the pointer past the line's end and makes the count from the distance (13,120 bytes here), which no buffer of the mixer's 4 KB holds, and `portAudioCommandFits` refused the frame. **The fix** indexes by `-(s32)` of the tap at the three reads (four lines). At 32 bits a `u32` and an `s32` negation and the pointer arithmetic after it are the same instructions (comparison below), and at 64 bits the index is the tap's negative, which is what the 32-bit wrap meant. The declaration stays `u32`: an `s32` member would change the 32-bit program, which converts `output - input` from `u32` to `f32` for the chorus depth in `alFxNew` (`drvrNew.c`, live) and `alFxParamHdl` (dead on PC) through other instructions than an `s32`, and it would make the 64-bit build differ from the 32-bit one wherever a tap's arithmetic went negative. **Seen failing first:** `test_audio_synth.c` gains `noFrameIsSkippedWithTheRoomEffect` (`AL_FX_SMALLROOM`: `alFxPull`'s taps and `_loadOutputBuffer`'s plain read) and `noFrameIsSkippedWithTheChorusEffect` (`AL_FX_CHORUS`: the modulated read). Against the old `reverb.c`: `ge: audio: WARNING - audio frame skipped (silent): command 27 op 0x04 has address 0x10001B75ED0D0`, `test_audio_synth: with the small room effect the interpreter skipped 10 of 10 frames` (aarch64; in the x86_64 container's 64-bit half the address was 0x8001FF5650D0) and `PASS (32-bit)`; with only the chorus line reverted, `with the chorus effect the interpreter skipped 10 of 10 frames`. With the fix: `test_audio_synth: PASS (64-bit)` (aarch64), `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` (x86_64 container: the 64-bit half translated by Rosetta 2, the 32-bit half under qemu-i386). **On the game, 64-bit video build, aarch64, with both fixes:** the `sound` set's two cases (the next commit) pass with `0 frames skipped as invalid` in every health line and recordings of 37.95 s (Dam, peak 16,069) and 30.52 s (the title, peak 23,568); the figures recorded for the task are the next commit's. **Checks.** `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`, exit 0. After `git add`: `lp64_casts.py check` `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`; `lp64_overlays.py check` `OK: 1619 sites, all reviewed`, 5 defect lines (the one `reverb.c` line, `alFxParamHdl`'s `dead` verdict, cites no line of this file); `test_lp64_overlays.py` OK; `test_abi_probe.sh` `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` and `ABI probe OK (32-bit)` (x86_64 container). No record type changed.

*LP64-005 task 10, fix round 1: which translator each x86 container uses (2026-11-19). Commit "Say which translator each x86 container uses" (this inventory and the plan, text only; no figure changed, no game or tool file changed).* **What was found.** The x86_64 container is not emulated by qemu: Rosetta 2 translates its 64-bit processes. In `lp64_env.py run --arch x86_64 -- sh -c 'cat /proc/self/maps; readlink /proc/$$/exe'` the 64-bit `cat` maps `/run/rosetta/rosetta` (three segments from 0x800000000000) and the shell's `/proc/PID/exe` is `/run/rosetta/rosetta`; `/proc/cpuinfo` names `VirtualApple @ 2.50GHz`. Its 32-bit processes run under qemu: a 32-bit program built there with `gcc -m32` and left sleeping showed `/proc/PID/exe` `/usr/bin/qemu-i386` and the command line `/usr/bin/qemu-i386 build/lp64/emucheck/s32 ...`, and the same check in the i686 container gave the same (`/usr/bin/qemu-i386`), with its shell and Python under Rosetta 2 (Rosetta cannot run 32-bit x86). Docker Desktop's setting was read without changing anything: `docker info` names `Operating System: Docker Desktop`, `Architecture: aarch64`, kernel `7.0.14-linuxkit`, and does not show the Rosetta setting; `settings-store.json` holds no key naming Rosetta or the virtual machine, so the setting is at its default, and what the processes map is the evidence. So x86_64 builds and runs are translated at close to native speed, not real x86 hardware; i686 builds and runs (and every 32-bit `-m32` program in either container) are emulated by qemu-i386, which is what makes the 32-bit reference slow. **Corrected in place** (the controller's instruction to write "emulated under qemu" for x86_64 was the source; no implementer's measurement was wrong): LP64-001 task 4's re-recorded baseline ("16 emulated cores"); LP64-002 task 9's fourth commit ("linux/amd64 under emulation", now saying the translator was not recorded then); the LP64-003 milestone's measurement line; LP64-003 task 4 (the x86_64 boot executables); LP64-003 task 12 (what ran where); the LP64-004 milestone's measurement line; LP64-004 tasks 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 (the sanitized `test_buffers.sh` half hangs under qemu-i386, not "under emulation" of the container); FORK-089's validation paragraph (LP64-004 Task 5's Windows builds in the x86_64 container); the LP64-005 milestone's measurements for the plan; LP64-005 tasks 4, 6 (with its fix round's statement that the runs "were emulated", and the conclusion that its x86_64 timings "look like native ones" because runs are paced in real time: they are close to native because the translation is), 7, 8, 8's fix round 1, 9, and this task's three notes; and in `scripts/port/native_64bit_plan.md` the working fact "Linux x86_64 and i686 run under emulation", the LP64-001 row's Task 5 build times, and the LP64-005 row's x86_64 runs of Tasks 6, 7 and 8 and Task 9's i686 run (now "under qemu-i386"). Statements about qemu-i386 and the i686 container were left as they were. **Checked and left:** `AGENTS.md` names the emulated 32-bit reference and "an emulated container" as a slow host, both true of the i686 container; `lp64_play.py`'s help names "the emulated i686 container"; `lp64_env.py` names no translator. The milestone plans `native_64bit_lp64_003.md`, `_004.md` and `_005.md` say x86_64 "runs under emulation" in their working facts; they were not edited here (they are accepted plans, and the statement's rule, that nothing seen only there is a finding without real x86 hardware, still holds). **Checks.** `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: `identical in loaded code and data`, exit 0; after `git add`: `lp64_casts.py check`, `lp64_overlays.py check` and `test_lp64_overlays.py` as in the next note.
*LP64-005 task 10, fix round 1 (2026-11-19). Commit "Measure where 64-bit sound's frames come from and tighten the sound judge" (`scripts/port/abi_probe/probe_overlays.h`, `scripts/port/test_audio_synth.c`, `scripts/port/lp64_play.py`, `lp64_play_sound.py`, `test_lp64_play_sound.py`, `AGENTS.md`, the plan's LP64-005 row, this inventory). Tools, tests and documents only; no game file changed, so the headless play sets were not rerun.* **The probe (A1, A2).** The review was right that the pool assertion was never seen failing by its predicate: its only red was a missing type. It stays as the statement of the rule, with a comment saying what it can and cannot catch: a union is never smaller than a member, so it fails only if the largest view is dropped from `ALParamRoom` (at 64 bits; at 32 bits `ALParam` ties with it). Beside it, "a parameter pool record is the size of its largest update, ALStartParamAlt" (`sizeof(ALParamRoom) == sizeof(ALStartParamAlt)`, at both widths) and "a parameter pool record is 40 bytes at 64 bits" (with the 28-byte one at 32 bits). Seen failing on drifted copies (x86_64 container, 64-bit half): with `startAlt` taken out of the union all three failed; with a 48-byte member added to it the two new ones failed and the first did not. The `ALSndpEvent` assertion lost its `sizeof <=`, which the equal-size assertion above it already implies; its two `offsetof(..., common.state)` comparisons were seen failing on a copy of `snd.c` (through `ABI_PROBE_SND_C`) with an `s64` member before `common.state`: only "snd.c's ALSndpEvent fits an ALEvent with its state pointer where the message starts" failed. **What guards the pool.** The union's member list with these assertions catches the largest view dropped from it (at 64 bits) and a change of the largest view's size; dropping `start` or `free` changes nothing and fails nothing; `test_audio_synth.sh`'s `noteStartsAndStopsGiveBackEveryParameter` catches `alSynNew` sizing the records smaller than what is written into them (a start's write lands on the next record's link). A fifth record type written into the pool without joining the union is caught by neither: such a write would be at one of the ten `__allocParam()` calls in `src/libultra/audio/` (`synallocvoice.c` twice, `synfreevoice.c`, `synsetfxmix.c`, `synsetpan.c`, `synsetpitch.c`, `synsetvol.c`, `synstartvoice.c`, `synstartvoiceparam.c`, `synstopvoice.c`), of which `synstartvoice.c`, `synstartvoiceparam.c` and `synfreevoice.c` cast the record to another type today. **The synth test (S1, S2).** `noFrameIsSkipped` and `theOutputIsNotSilence` were seen failing under one-line mutations, each reverted (aarch64): with the voice's volume zeroed in `startNote`, only `theOutputIsNotSilence` failed (`10 frames of a square wave played as silence`); with `portAcmdValidate` made to refuse every frame (`if (1 || bad || ...)` in `port/src/audio_pc.c`), `noFrameIsSkipped` failed (`the interpreter skipped 10 of 10 frames`), as did the two effect tests. `fork` and `waitpid` are now checked without `assert`, so a build with `NDEBUG` still forks and waits. **Where the frames come from (B1).** The first note's cause, the floor top-ups, rested on a correlation. Measured in scratch copies under `build/lp64/` (deleted), with a counter per path in `portAudioPump` printed at exit, run through the `sound` set's own cases:

| Run | Pumps | Fields counted (per pump) | Per-field frames | Floor top-ups | Forced | Device clock | Recording |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64-bit sanitizer video, `capture-dam` (aarch64) | 1,801 | 7,500 (4.2) | 7,113 (99.5%) | 31 (0.4%) | 2 | 0 | 119.10 s |
| 64-bit plain video, `capture-dam` (aarch64) | 1,801 | 2,044 (1.1) | 1,987 (98.9%) | 21 (1.0%) | 2 | 0 | 33.50 s |
| 32-bit reference video, `capture-title` (i686, qemu-i386, alone) | 1,809 | 8,119 (4.5) | 8,051 (80.2%) | 1,975 (19.7%) | 10 | 0 | 167.27 s |

No field was dropped by the stall rule in any run; trimmed field frames were 387, 57 and 68, and frames recorded but over the queue's cap 528, 27 and 96. The three paths' samples add up to each recording's length exactly. **The cause, as measured:** `portAudioPump` runs once a frame of the game loop, about 1,800 times a case (1,801 and 1,809 counted), and makes one audio frame for each game field since the last pump; the field count follows elapsed time (`currentFrameCounter`, from `osGetCount`), so a run that takes longer gets more fields a pump and more frames. On the 64-bit builds nearly every frame is a per-field frame; the 32-bit reference under qemu-i386 has, besides 4.5 fields a pump, a fifth of its frames from the floor top-up, its device queue running low between slow pumps. The length recorded therefore follows the run's elapsed time: the sanitizer build's Dam recording was 239.97 s in the first round and 114.43 s this round; what else ran then was not recorded, and this round's ran alone. **A fair length comparison (B2)** needs both programs run at the same speed, which this Mac cannot give: a 64-bit host as slow as the 32-bit build under qemu-i386, or the 32-bit build on fast x86 hardware, would be one, or a capture whose frames follow game fields and not wall time. The `sound` set on the 64-bit plain video build in the x86_64 container (`build/lp64/strict-tree/video-x64`, `--timeout-scale 15`, alone on the machine) passed both cases in 81 s: `capture-title` 28.53 s, peak 22,207, non-zero 85.6%; `capture-dam` 41.85 s, peak 16,092, non-zero 94.3%; against the 32-bit reference its lengths are 0.15 and 0.15, its peaks 0.99 and 0.88, its shares 0.88 and 0.96. That container is translated by Rosetta 2 at close to native speed (the next note) while the reference runs under qemu-i386, so the two runs share neither a translator nor a speed: it is not a like-for-like comparison, and none was possible on this Mac. Step 4's length comparison stays recorded as not met across hosts of different speed, for the measured cause; it is handed to LP64-006, with its runs on real hardware and a capture that does not depend on wall time, which is also where whether the two programs make the same sound will be compared. **The judge (C1, S3, S4).** Each `sound` case also fails on any audio health line (`ge: audio: last N s: ... frames skipped as invalid`, `portAudioHealth`) whose count is not 0; this round also required at least one such line, which fix round 2 removed (below). That count is `s_StatSkipped`, which all three refusal sites increment: a refused frame (`portAcmdValidate`), a refused ADPCM block header and a refused resample span. The line is printed only for a window of 10 s or more with something to report (a dry queue, a frame over the cap or a refusal) and not for the last partial window, so a refusal in a run's last seconds is not seen; every recorded run here printed several. The length is now computed from the bytes read, not the header's frame count. `--env GE_AUDIO_CAPTURE` is refused on every set (`parallel cases would write one file`), and `AGENTS.md` says so. *LP64-005 task 11, the "Text file busy" race (2026-11-19). Commit "Start every play and smoke case from one executable copy made before the pool" (the new `scripts/port/run_copies.py` and `scripts/port/test_run_copies.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play_run.py`, `scripts/port/audit_buffers.py`, the CI tests step, this inventory).* **The race.** The play tool (`run_case` and the route builder's `recording_tick`) and the mission smoke (`audit_buffers.py`, `mission_smoke`) each copied the executable into the case's temporary folder with `shutil.copy2` and started the copy, from several threads at once. While one thread held its copy open for writing, another thread forked to start its own case; the forked child keeps a duplicate of every descriptor until its exec (close-on-exec closes it only then), so the first thread's exec of its finished copy failed with `OSError: [Errno 26] Text file busy`. It had been seen once in LP64-005 Task 10's step 8 and in CI's tests step on 4a9b541 (raised at `audit_buffers.py:120`, in `mission_smoke`'s thread pool, inside one of the ROM-free tool tests; which test was not traced here). **The fix.** `run_copies.SharedExecutable` copies the executable once, before the thread pool starts, into a private temporary folder, and `place(folder)` hard-links that closed copy into each case's folder under the executable's name; making a link opens no file for writing, so no fork can inherit a writer. A case's folder holds the same file under the same name as before (the game reads `midas.ini` from, and writes beside, its executable's folder), and a link that cannot be made (another file system) fails naming both paths rather than falling back to a racing copy; no retry loop. `audit_buffers.py` loads the helper by path, as it loads `lp64_boot.py`, since other tools load it by path. **The test.** `test_run_copies.py` runs two play cases and two smoke missions two at a time against a stand-in script, with the overlap made certain rather than waited for: the first child started through `subprocess.Popen` sleeps 1.5 s between fork and exec (a `preexec_fn`), and the first executable copy stays open for writing until a `Popen` has started, plus 0.3 s. Against the old code both tests failed with `OSError: [Errno 26] Text file busy: '/tmp/midas-buffer-.../IronSights'` and `'/tmp/midas-lp64-play-.../IronSights'` in five runs of five in the aarch64 container; with the fix they passed five of five (the one copy is made before any `Popen`, so the copy's wait times out after 2 s and no case can meet a writer, whatever the timing). On macOS an exec of a file open for writing succeeds, so there the test passes against either version; CI's Linux runner discriminates. It joins the CI tests step. **Checks.** The play, options, input, sound, traces and audit tests (136) pass; `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` identical in loaded code and data (tools only); `lp64_casts.py check` 24 in 11 files; `lp64_overlays.py check` 1,619 sites, 5 defect lines; `test_lp64_overlays.py` OK.

*LP64-005 task 11 fix round 1, a replayed demo's pad and the device assignment (2026-11-19). Commit "Keep a replayed demo's pad from starting a device assignment" (`src/game/options.c`, this inventory). Changes the 32-bit program, by the controller's ruling under decision 13 (an inherited defect, a few lines, the changed functions named); the owner reviews it at the laptop step.* **Cause.** In the `bunker2` attract demo the recorded pad opens the watch's Control tab and presses A on its first row, the device row (`PWROW_DEVICE`), which like the page and the assignment below is inherited from upstream (present at the repository's first commit, 718a122): `portWatchActivateRow` calls `portWatchAssignBegin`, which arms `input_pc.c`'s "press a button" assignment (`portInputAssignBegin`). That assignment owns the page until a device answers or its 10 s wall-clock timeout (`ASSIGN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `SDL_GetTicks`) runs out, and while it is armed the recorded START at tick 268 goes to `portWatchModalBack`, which cancels the assignment instead of closing the watch. On a host that reaches tick 268 within 10 s of the press the watch stays open and the replay diverges (it returns to the title at tick 710 with no exit line); on a slower one the timeout ends the assignment first and START closes the watch. So the shipped game's demo depended on the host's speed at both widths. Headless builds never diverged: `input_pc.c` is compiled only with video (`CMakeLists.txt`), and the weak `portInputAssignBegin` in `port/src/libultra_shim.c` arms nothing. Proof, from the Task 11 runs: a debug build with a 1 s timeout passed `bunker2`, and the emulated 32-bit video reference passed it because more than 10 s went by first. **Fix.** This fork's change to that inherited behaviour, in the upstream-owned `src/game/options.c`, which a later upstream merge must keep: `portWatchAssignBegin` arms the assignment only when `get_is_ramrom_flag()` is 0, so during demo playback the device row does what a headless build's does (the drop-down and key capture still close and the row's selection is reset, as before). The guard sits at the watch's one entry to the assignment, which every watch path calls (the A press through `portWatchActivateRow`, the mouse clicks on the device row, the raphnet page's input row and the harness's A); the folder (`src/game/front.c`) calls `portInputAssignBegin` itself but cannot receive replayed pads, since `is_ramrom_flag` is set when playback starts in the stage and cleared when it ends (`src/game/ramromreplay.c`). `GE_INPUTPLAY` replays (`port/src/inputrec.c`) are not ramrom playback and never set the flag, so they and a player's own presses arm the assignment as before. **Input idioms.** Keyboard, mouse, gamepad and touch start the assignment as before; only replayed demo input is excluded. No help text or menu path changes. **Check.** `options.c` cannot be compiled alone without stubbing most of the game, so the check is the run: `lp64_play.py run --set demos --only bunker2 --video --shots 120` on the plain aarch64 video build gave `bunker2: FAIL (missing line: ge: demo exit: totaltime end (timer/limit) at tick 771)` before and `bunker2: PASS (1601 pictures)` after. **Windows executable.** `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` exits 1 as the ruling expects; only `options.c`'s object changed (`.text` 0x60 bytes smaller, `.eh_frame` 8 bytes larger, the rest of the image moved with it). Three functions differ, and the owner reviews them at the laptop step: `portWatchAssignBegin` gains the call to `get_is_ramrom_flag` and its branch; `portWatchActivateRow` and `portWatchHarnessTick`, which GCC had inlined `portWatchAssignBegin` into, now call it (a call in the first, a tail call in the second) and lose their inlined copies, with nothing else changed.
*LP64-005 task 11 fix round 1, the hit marker's whole words (2026-11-19). Commit "Write the hit marker's floats as whole display-list words at 64 bits" (`port/src/port_hud.c`, `scripts/port/test_hud.c`, `scripts/port/test_hud_vector.inl`, this inventory).* The review found that the hit marker (`G_HITMARKER_EXT`, drawn on every hit while `hit_markers` is on, the default) wrote its x and y floats into its second command with `memcpy` of 4 bytes into each word, the pattern the HUD vector note above fixes, so at 64 bits each word's upper half kept what the buffer held. At 64 bits `portHudDraw` now calls `phHitMarker`, which writes both commands as whole words; the 32-bit build keeps the original lines in `portHudDraw` under `#else`, unchanged token for token. (Extracting one writer for both widths was tried first: GCC inlined it but scheduled `portHudDraw` differently, so the Windows executable differed, and it was dropped.) *LP64-005 task 12, a torn trace line (2026-11-19). Commit "Name a torn trace line instead of reading it as a difference" (`scripts/port/lp64_play_traces.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_play_traces.py`, this inventory; Python only, no compiled file changed).* **Why.** The demos' tick lines go to stdout and the game's other lines to stderr, both into one log, so a line of the other stream can cut a tick line in two. Strict batch 1 saw it once: in one i686 reference run a `ge: romdata: model GtriggerZ converted` line split facility1's tick-331 line, and `traces --reference-check` read it as `facility1: unstable (first differs at tick 331)`, although the remainder on the next line held the other runs' values. The old reader matched `ge: demo tick N` and compared whatever followed, so a tear read as a false difference and, where a difference at that tick was recorded, passed as "differing as recorded". **What changed.** `read_trace` accepts a tick line only when it is whole, field by field as `src/game/ramromreplay.c` prints it (`draws=`, `live=`, `rec=`, `p0=`, `p1=`, `b=`). A line that holds a part of one (`demo tick`, which a cut after it leaves in the first part, or ` p1=`, which a cut before it leaves in the second; no other line the game prints holds either, by a search of `src/` and `port/`) and is not whole is torn, wherever it falls before the first playback ends; that end is the first whole tick line whose number is not past the last one (the next playback's tick 1), so a tear after the exit line or in that tick-1 line itself is reported as a torn line of the first playback, at the tick after its last, which fails safe. Its tick is the number it holds when that is past the last whole tick, else the tick after it (a cut inside the number leaves a smaller one). The demo's comparison is then `NAME: torn line at tick T in LOG (another stream cut it)`, which is a problem, not a difference: the demo fails both `--expect` (whatever its line records) and `--reference-check`, so a torn line can neither pass as identical nor hide or stand for a recorded difference. A tear after the next playback's first whole tick line is outside the trace, as before. The logging is unchanged. **Tests (seen failing first).** Five new cases in `test_lp64_play_traces.py` build a log whose tick line is cut by a whole `ge: romdata` line: at character 40 with equal values (`torn line at tick 331`, status 1, no "first differs"), the same cut where a difference at 331 is recorded (status 1), a cut inside "demo tick" (character 9, `--reference-check`, torn at 331, not "unstable"), a cut inside the number (character 16, "tick 33", torn at 331), and a cut in a later playback (passes). Against the old reader four failed: the first printed `facility1: first differs at tick 331`, the second passed with status 0 (`OK: 14 demos, 13 identical, 1 differing as recorded`), the third printed `facility1: unstable (first differs at tick 331)` and the fourth `first differs at tick 331`; the later-playback case passed before and after. With the change `python3 -m unittest test_lp64_play_traces` ran 23 tests, OK; `test_lp64_play` and `test_lp64_play_options` OK. **Checks.** `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` on this change alone: `identical in loaded code and data`, exit 0. `lp64_casts.py check`: `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`. The narrowing and unprototyped checks and the game runs did not run for this commit (no C, C++ or build file changed); the task's runs at its end use the new reader.
