CI runs both halves.`; where the default build is not 64-bit it prints the same for the 64-bit half. The script still exits 0 on a skip (the other harnesses' rule, `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS`, is not applied here, so a 64-bit-only host can still run it), and a failing half still fails it: the first half's output is now captured to read its width, so `build_and_run` returns when the compiler fails instead of running a stale binary (a probe built from a scratch `gunfire.c` with `ModelHeader.Type` made `s32` printed the static-assertion error and exited 1). **CI runs both halves:** the tests job (`.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, `bash scripts/port/test_abi_probe.sh`) runs on `ubuntu-24.04` with `gcc-multilib` installed by `scripts/port/ci_dependencies.py`'s tests profile, so its gcc builds 64-bit by default and accepts `-m32`; CI is the evidence for the 32-bit half wherever a local host skips it. **Runs.** aarch64 container: `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` then the 32-bit skip line, exit 0 (before the change: the gcc error and `-m32 unavailable on this host, skipped`). i686 and x86_64 containers (the `goldeneye` image, gcc 64-bit by default with multilib): `ABI probe OK (64-bit)` and `ABI probe OK (32-bit)`, exit 0. *LP64-005 task 13, the pool peaks (2026-11-19). Commit "Report each pool's peak on a 64-bit build" (`port/include/port_lp64.h`, `port/src/port_lp64.c`, `port/src/port_memp.c`, `src/mema.c`, `src/game/dyn.c`, `src/libultra/audio/heapalloc.c`, `src/game/image.c`, `src/game/lv.c`, `scripts/port/lp64_boot.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_boot.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play.py`, the new `scripts/port/lp64_play_peaks.py` and `scripts/port/test_lp64_play_peaks.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.c` and `.sh`, the new `scripts/port/test_lp64_peaks.c`, `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, `AGENTS.md`, this inventory).* **What changed.** LP64-004 left the pool figures as snapshots at a run's frame limit; decision 10 of the LP64-005 plan (accepted) asks for each pool's peak before any pool is resized. At 64 bits each pool's allocator now reports its use through `portLp64PoolUse(const char *pool, u32 used, u32 size)` (`port_lp64.c`), which keeps the largest use of each pool since the last print (for a name that pools of several sizes share, `texture pool`, the use that was the largest share of its size), and `portLp64PoolPeaks` prints `ge: lp64: peak POOL USED of SIZE bytes` for each pool used since the last print, in the order of first use. It runs at each stage unload (`lvlUnloadStageTextData`, `src/game/lv.c`, after `cleanup_rooms` has given the rooms back) and at exit (`atexit`, registered by the first use), so a stop's FATAL line (`sysFatalError` calls `exit(1)`) and a pool's fatal line (`exit(6)`) are followed by the peaks; a run killed by a signal prints none. Never per frame. The pools and where they report: `stage bank` (`port_memp.c`, the stage bank's cursor after each block and each resize), `room memory` and `room memory largest request` (`mema.c`, the bytes allocated and not freed, and the largest block a request kept), `graphics buffer` and `vertex pool` (`dyn.c`, `portDynAuditFrameEnd`, each half's use at the end of each frame, beside LP64-004's overrun check), `music heap` (`heapalloc.c`, after each block) and `texture pool` (`image.c`, both ends' use after each texture is decoded into a pool). At 32 bits all of these are `((void) 0)` macros that do not evaluate their arguments, and their arguments are free of side effects; every call site is inside `#if IS_64_BIT` or `#ifndef TARGET_N64` except `heapalloc.c`'s, which, like that file's existing `portLp64PoolFatal` call, is unguarded and is the 32-bit macro at 32 bits. **Two uses that are given back at once.** A first run showed the stage bank at 100 percent in every stage: a file load (`fileIndexLoadToBank`, `src/game/ob.c`) takes all the bank has left (`mempGetBankSizeLeft`) and shrinks the block to the file once it is in. `port_memp.c` now reports such a block through `portLp64PoolHold`, which counts at the print only if no later use of the pool came first (the stage bank's use is its cursor, so the next use, normally the shrink, includes whatever was kept). Room memory has the same shape: a room's first load (`bgLoadRoomModelData`, `src/game/bg.c`) takes `memaGetLongestFree`'s answer and gives back the tail. `mema.c` tells `port_lp64.c` of each answer, allocation, growth and free (`portLp64RoomLongest`, `portLp64RoomTake`, `portLp64RoomGive`, `portLp64RoomReset`), and an allocation of exactly that answer counts as what it kept when its tail comes back, or whole at the next call or the print. The brief named only `portLp64PoolUse`; these five functions are this task's addition, because without them the stage bank and room memory would read near 100 percent in every run and decision 10 would raise both on a figure that is not demand. **Tools.** `ge: lp64: peak ` joins `INFORMATIONAL_PREFIXES` (`lp64_boot.py`), which the play tool and the mission smoke import, so a peak line fails no run; AGENTS.md names the line and the new command. `lp64_play.py peaks DIR...` (`lp64_play_peaks.py`) prints, for each pool, the peak that was the largest share of its size over every `DIR/*.log`, as `POOL: USED of SIZE bytes (SHARE%) in DIR/CASE`, marked ` ABOVE 80%` past decision 10's line and with `; N exhaustion lines` when the pool printed `ge: lp64: pool` lines; it exits 2 when no log holds a peak line. **Tests, each seen failing first.** `test_lp64_address.c`: three uses of 10, 30 and 20 of 100 print one line, `ge: lp64: peak test pool 30 of 100 bytes`, and a print with no use since the last prints nothing; at 32 bits nothing prints. `test_lp64_peaks.c` (new, built at both widths by `test_lp64_address.sh`): a held use followed by another use counts the later one, a held use nothing followed counts at the print, a room's first block counts as what it kept, and one held whole at the print counts whole. `test_lp64_boot.py`: a run with two peak lines passes (before the prefix was added it failed, `logged: ge: lp64: peak stage bank 2400000 of 3000000 bytes`). `test_lp64_play_peaks.py` (new, in CI's tests step): six cases. With the code weakened in a scratch edit each test failed: the last use kept instead of the largest, no grab handling, a held use never folded or never superseded, the room's grab not settled at the print, the tool's comparison by bytes instead of share and its line at 80 percent inclusive. Before the code, the C driver did not compile (`implicit declaration of function 'portLp64PoolPeaks'`). After: `test_lp64_address.sh` `PASS (64-bit)` in the aarch64 container and `PASS (32-bit)`, `PASS (64-bit)` in the i686 container, each with `test_lp64_peaks: PASS`; `test_lp64_boot.py` 37 tests OK; `test_lp64_play_peaks.py` 6 tests OK. **A first run before the commit,** on a 64-bit headless build of `main`'s tree with this change (`build/lp64/gate-a64`, aarch64, without the branch's strict fixes): `lp64_play.py run --set attract,stages` passed 58 of 58 cases with no `ge: lp64:` line but the informational kinds, and `peaks` read all seven pools; room memory peaked at 368,416 of 450,560 bytes (81.8 percent) in `mp-statue-4p`. The measurement over every set and what decision 10 makes of it are in the next note. **Checks.** Windows comparison (`compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`): `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`, exit 0. `lp64_casts.py check`: `OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`; `lp64_overlays.py check`: `OK: 1619 sites, all reviewed`. `port/src/port_lp64.c` is now 533 lines (an existing file; the repository's limit is 628).*

*LP64-005 strict batch, the room cache's part key (2026-11-19). On the branch `lp64/play-strict`, not on `main`; it lands through the laptop's regeneration in Task 15. Commit "Keep a part list's high address bits in the room cache key at 64 bits" (the new `port/fast3d/gfx_roomcache_key.h`, `port/fast3d/gfx_roomcache.inl`, the new ROM-free `scripts/port/test_roomcache_key.c` and `.sh`, this inventory).* **The defect (Task 11 Step 5).** `roc_part_key` is the whole identity of a model part in the room cache (`room_cache=2`; the default is 0): `roc_part_find` and `portPartCacheRegister` take the entry stored under the key without comparing its list or vertex base. It shifted the list's address left by 20 bits and XORed the vertex base; at 32 bits the shift keeps every address bit, at 64 bits it drops bits 44 and up, so two part lists 16 TiB apart with one vertex base got one key and the second would replay the first's captured geometry. Such addresses are in the user range of both containers (aarch64 maps at 0xaaaa... and 0xffff..., x86_64 at 0x55... and 0x7f...), so the key can collide at 64 bits; no run here was seen to collide: `lp64_play.py run --set stages --only dam --video --env GE_ROOMCACHE=2` on the aarch64 video build from before this commit passed (`stage-dam: PASS (1790 pictures)`, no `ge: FATAL` line) and logged 23 distinct parts whose lists lay at 0xffff7d200000 to 0xffff7d257f80, bit 47 set, so the old key was already dropping real address bits there; all 23 shared bits 44 and up, so no two of their keys were equal under the old key or the new one (checked from the log's `ge: roc: part` lines). A collision needs two part lists in different 16 TiB windows, as a heap list and an mmap'd one would be. **Fix.** The key moves to its own header so a test can include it; at 64 bits the list address is rotated left by 20 instead of shifted, which keeps every bit; the 32-bit side keeps today's expression in `#else`. The key stays a hash: as at 32 bits, the XOR with the vertex base can still map two distinct pairs to one key (inherited, both widths; not changed here). **Test, seen failing first.** `test_roomcache_key.sh` (harness widths) builds two list addresses that differ only in bit 44 with one vertex base: against today's key it failed at 64 bits in the x86_64 container (`test_roomcache_key: lists 0xa18e3f98 and 0x1000a18e3f98 share key 0xa18e34f830d20`, exit 134) and passed at 32; with the fix `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` in the x86_64 container and `PASS (64-bit)` in the aarch64 one. **Checks.** `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE` on the branch: `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs` (exit 0), so no shipped per-frame path changed and no benchmark is owed; the arm guide's contracts are untouched (no hand, arm or wardrobe file changed); `test_wardrobe.sh` and `test_ads.sh` PASS at 64 bits in the aarch64 and the x86_64 container on the branch; `lp64_casts.py check` 24 in 11 files; `lp64_overlays.py check` and `check --no-defects` pass on the branch. The hook on the branch prints that the gallery is stale and passes, as expected; the gallery was not regenerated.
*LP64-005 task 11 fix round 1, the room cache key test in CI (2026-11-19), on the branch `lp64/play-strict` only; it lands through the laptop's regeneration in Task 15. Commit "Run the room cache key test in CI and check bit 47" (`scripts/port/test_roomcache_key.c`, `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, this inventory). Test and CI only; nothing compiled changed.* The review found that nothing ran `test_roomcache_key.sh`, so the key's regression guard could never fail; the CI tests step now runs `bash scripts/port/test_roomcache_key.sh` after `test_hud.sh`. The test now checks two list pairs at 64 bits, one differing only in bit 44 (the lowest bit the old shift dropped) and one differing only in bit 47 (`0x7fff7d257f80` and `0xffff7d257f80`; bit 47 is set in every part list seen on aarch64), and pins each width's key for a fixed input to a literal: at 64 bits the rotated list (`0xffff7d257f80` with vertex base `0xffff6a1c0010` gives `0xfff72da8921c001f`), at 32 bits the shift by 20 (`0x0812f3a0` and `0x09a0c010` give `0x812f33a0c010`); the old 32-bit check compared the expression with a copy of itself. Seen failing, compiled against a scratch copy of the header with the widths' expressions swapped: at 64 bits the old shift fails both pairs (the bit 47 pair alone: `lists 0x7fff7d257f80 and 0xffff7d257f80 share key 0xfff7d2574e030d20`), and at 32 bits a changed expression fails the literal (`the 32-bit key is 0x812f33a0c011, expected 0x812f33a0c010`). At 32 bits a rotate and the shift give the same value, since nothing is above bit 31, so the literal guards the key's value and `compare_win32.py` remains the guard for its code. `test_roomcache_key.sh` passes at 32 and 64 bits in the i686 container and at 64 bits in aarch64. `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: `identical in loaded code and data`, exit 0. **Loop form, after landing (2026-11-20).** The landing on `main` (commit "Regenerate the review gallery for the strict-tier play fixes") failed the CI tests job in `test_harness_widths.sh`: `FAIL: no harness loops directly over $(harness_widths): expected [], got [scripts/port/test_roomcache_key.sh ]`. A loop over `$(harness_widths)` runs zero times when the helper fails, so the harness would pass having run nothing; the branch's Windows workflow had never run, since it runs on `main` only. Commit "Take the room cache key test's widths on their own line" makes the script take `widths=$(harness_widths)` on its own line, as the other harnesses do, so `set -e` stops it. In the laptop's goldeneye container (GCC 13.3, x86_64): `test_harness_widths: PASS`, `test_roomcache_key: PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)`.

*LP64-005 task 15 fix round 1, `weapons-dam` measured and what the close rests on (2026-11-20). Commit "Measure weapons-dam's miss and say what the close rests on" (this inventory and the plan's LP64-005 row; text only), after the task review found that the close called a failed done-condition case a run-to-run variation without the owner's acceptance and without saying the pass ran six cases at once.* **The runs.** The plain 64-bit headless executable (`build/lp64/boot`, the aarch64 container, native on the Mac), `lp64_play.py run --set input --only weapons-dam`, each run its own output folder, default timeout scale: ten runs one at a time, 10 of 10 `PASS`; twelve runs as two rounds of six simultaneous invocations, 11 of 12 `PASS`, the failure the full pass's: `out of order: ge: play: weapon 20 (change 30 of 30: right 20, left 0) only before ge: play: shots N (a shot with change 29 of 30)`. Counting the full pass (failed) and its three reruns (passed), the ten runs alone (all passed) and the twelve under load (eleven passed), 24 of 26 runs of `weapons-dam` on this executable passed. **What the failing run's log shows** (the `ge: play: tick N` line before each event gives the tick, the count of pad reads the route is built on): `weapon 4883` (both Spectres, change 29) at tick 4578 as in every run; no `shots` line while the trigger was held from tick 4620 for 30 ticks; then `weapon 20` (the M16) at tick 4698, 18 ticks after the next press at 4680. Every passing run but one logged `shots` at ticks 4620 and 4640 and then `weapon 19` at 4725 (the left Spectre put away) and `weapon 20` at 4728; the other passing run (the third alone) logged one shot at 4620, `weapon 4884` (M16 right, Spectre left) at 4698 and `weapon 20` at 4712, so it passed with a single shot. Change 29 came at tick 4578 in all 22 runs (and in the four runs compared change by change, alone1, alone3, load2-2 and the failing load2-3, every change from the first to the 29th came at the same tick); the failing run's next change came straight to the M16 at the press's usual 18-tick delay. So the change did happen and the press came on time; the dual Spectre fired nothing in a window where it fires twice in the other runs. The shot line did not land after the next weapon line, and game ticks did not fall behind the route's. **What varies.** The game clock advances by the retraces that passed since the last frame (`speedgraphframes`, `lvlTick` in `src/game/lv.c`), while the route counts pad reads, one a game frame; 8 to 12 of the 5,100 retraces went without a game frame in these runs (`frames=5100 gfxtasks=5088` to `5092`), and Bond first drew his gun at tick 1158 to 1161 and the game's state at a given route tick differs slightly from run to run: shots before change 29 ranged from 110 to 121, and single windows differ (change 13, `weapon 2827`, with 1 shot in some runs and 4 or 5 in others). Neither figure predicts the failure: the failing run missed 9 retraces and drew at tick 1159, as passing runs did. Under load the draw tick was later (1158 to 1161 against 1158 to 1160 alone), and the one failure in 22 came under load, which is not enough to tie it to load. Why the dual Spectre fired nothing in that one window was not found within the hour allowed; `GE_CHEATS=guns` gives infinite ammo, so it is not a gun run dry. Nothing in the case, the tool or the game was changed. Finding the cause would start with logging player 0's gun state at each change and each held trigger in the play log; a fix to the case or the game would need the input set rerun on the plain and sanitizer aarch64 and the plain x86_64 headless executables, and with video. The run folders were deleted after these figures were taken. **The record.** The plan's LP64-005 row: the lead sentence says the runs ran and passed except as noted, gives the render-thread pass as 27 of 108 short of ticks at their own frames with those 27 passing at eight times, says CI ran and the gallery was fresh on 925c38f and what changed after it, gives these counts, and says the owner is asked to accept the miss; the Windows comparison names 909e4a8 as text only over fbaecad, against which the branch's note records the comparison from bbcac00; the stall's reruns read three at the case's frames and one at eight times its frames, as in the hand-over. The close note above now says the headless passes ran six cases at once and gives these counts instead of "a run-to-run variation", names the parent for the Windows comparison, and names the render-thread cases that differ from the fix wave's. The hand-over says LP64-006 reruns Task 7's census on the landed code and gives these counts in its `weapons-dam` bullet; the owner's list asks for the miss to be accepted or investigated and says what clears the gallery.*

*LP64-006 task 1, why `weapons-dam` misses a shot (2026-11-21). Commit "Log player 0's gun state and name why weapons-dam misses a shot" (`port/src/port_playlog.c`, `port/include/port_playlog.h`, `scripts/port/test_playlog_gun.c` (new), `scripts/port/test_inputrec_headless.sh`, `scripts/port/lp64_play_route.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play_judge.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play_input.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_play_input.py`, this inventory, the plan's LP64-006 row). Harness builds only: `PORT_PLAY_HARNESS` is 0 in a 32-bit video build, and `compare_win32.py commits 625ebb1 WORKTREE` says `identical in loaded code and data`.* **The tools.** With `GE_PLAYLOG=2` the play log adds, for player 0, at each `weapon` line and on each pass while pad 0 holds `Z_TRIG`, `ge: play: gun tick=T clock=C global=G r=ITEM,STATE,ANIM,FIRING,HOLD,AMMO,NEXT l=...` (the input tick, `g_ClockTimer`, `g_GlobalTimer`, and each hand's `weaponnum`, `weapon_action_state`, `weapon_current_animation`, `weapon_firing_status`, `weapon_hold_time`, `weapon_ammo_in_magazine`, `weapon_next_weapon`); `GE_PLAYLOG=1` prints what it printed before. `GE_PLAYSTALL=T:MS` sleeps MS ms once at input tick T (through the weak `portPlaySleepMs`, which the test replaces), and `GE_PLAYHURT=T`, added because the gun state named another cause than the stall's, hits player 0 once at tick T through the game's own `record_damage_kills` (0.0625, the health a guard's hit took in the measured runs, with no attacker, as `propobj.c`'s hits are made). `lp64_play.py`'s judge reads a whole gun line as a play line (`PLAY_GUN`), not as a torn one. `scripts/port/test_playlog_gun.c` (linked with `port_playlog.c` at both widths by `test_inputrec_headless.sh`) checks the gun line's fields and order, that level 1 prints none, and that each of the stall and the hit happens once at its tick and not one tick either side; it failed first on `undefined reference to 'portPlayGunLine'`, then on the missing hit. `lp64_play_input.py` now names the items by `ITEM_IDS` (change 29 a pair of `ITEM_GOLDENGUN`, change 30 `ITEM_SILVERWPPK`), not "the dual Spectre" and "the M16". **The cause.** In solo play the game holds the trigger off while its damage display runs: `bondview2.c` sets `moveData.triggerOn = 0` while `damageshowtime >= 0` and one player plays (original behaviour), and the display lasts the frames `g_DamageTypes` (`bondview.c`) gives for Bond's health after the hit, 30 above five eighths and 35 to 60 below, so a hit on the tick before a window covers all 30 of its ticks. The case gives Bond every gun but no invincibility, so Dam's guards shoot him, and when a hit lands on the tick before a 30-tick trigger window (or earlier, at low health) the whole window passes with the trigger held on pad 0 and both hands idle with a loaded magazine and `weapon_hold_time` 0, and the case fails on that change. When the hits land depends on the guards' timing against the route's ticks, which varies from run to run on both widths because runs are paced by the host's clock; more machine load moves them more. The cause is the case's timing against original game behaviour, not a 64-bit defect, so nothing in the game changes here: the case moves to lockstep in Task 2 Step 5. **The failing windows** (gun lines with `GE_PLAYLOG=2`; a temporary local probe line, not committed, added `damageshowtime` and health for two of the batches). aarch64 (native, plain headless executable, six at once): 3 of 24 runs failed (change 25 once, change 29 twice); in each failing window both hands are state 0 (idle) with ammo in the magazine and hold time 0 on every tick of the held trigger, `clock=1` on each, where the passing runs' same window shows the left hand at state 2 (fire) with hold time 1 on the window's first tick (change 25: failing `l=17,0,0,0,0,8,17` from tick 4140 to 4169, passing `l=17,2,0,1,1,7,17` at 4140; change 29: failing `l=19,0,0,0,0,1,19` from 4620, passing `l=19,2,0,1,1,0,19` at 4620). With the probe, 3 of 12 failed, all at change 13: the probe shows a hit between ticks 2658 and 2700 (health 1.000 to 0.938) and `damageshowtime` 1 to 30 across the window 2700 to 2729, where the passing run's is -1. i686 (emulated, probe build, six at once): 1 of 6 failed, at change 29, with the same gun state, a hit about 7 ticks before the window (health 0.446 to 0.394) and `damageshowtime` 7 to 36 across it; the passing run's is -1. The same state on both widths. No gun line in any failing window had `clock` above 1. **Forced and prevented, ten runs each (six at once, then four), on each width.** The first hypothesis, a two-field frame: `GE_PLAYSTALL=2639:250` (the tick before change 13's press) moves `global` 7 fields ahead of the input tick on both widths, and change 13 fired in 10 of 10 runs on aarch64 and 10 of 10 on i686 (one aarch64 run failed instead at change 18, with the same gun state as the failing windows above: idle, a full magazine, hold time 0). Forced, a hit on the tick before change 13's window with the guards blind (`GE_CHEATS=guns,invis GE_PLAYHURT=2699`): 10 of 10 failed at change 13 on aarch64 and 10 of 10 on i686, change 13 the only window without a shot. Prevented: `GE_CHEATS=guns,invis` passed 10 of 10 on each width, and `GE_CHEATS=guns,invuln` 10 of 10 on each. With the default cheats and no `GE_CHEATS=guns,invis`, a forced hit at 2699 failed change 13 in 9 of 10 aarch64 runs; the tenth fired on the window's last tick (tick 2729); why was not examined (`record_damage_kills` ignores a hit while a display runs, so a guard's earlier hit would explain it, but no probe ran there). x86_64 was not used for these runs. **Task check** (steps 1 to 8 of the LP64-005 plan's, as its Task 15 ran them). Step 1, in the x86_64 and the aarch64 container (the aarch64 run in its own trees `build/lp64/gate-a64` and `gate-video-a64`): `355 files compiled, 0 failed` (headless) and `386 files compiled, 0 failed` (video), `OK: 0 narrowings in 0 files, all allowed`, `OK: 2 unprototyped calls in 2 files, all allowed`, `OK: 122 pointer-only types, as pinned in lp64_pointer_types.txt`. *LP64-006 task 2, lockstep (2026-11-21). Commit "Add lockstep: one retrace a game frame and a clock that counts them" (`port/src/port_lockstep.c` and `port/include/port_lockstep.h` (new), `port/src/pcsched.c`, `port/src/libultra_shim.c`, `src/game/frametiming.c`, `port/src/video.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `scripts/port/test_lockstep.c` and `scripts/port/test_lp64_compare.sh` (new), `scripts/port/lp64_play_cases.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play_run.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play_input.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_play.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_play_input.py`, `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, `AGENTS.md`, this inventory, the plan's LP64-006 row). Harness builds only: lockstep compiles where `PORT_PLAY_HARNESS` is 1, CMake leaves `port_lockstep.c` out of a 32-bit video build as it leaves `port_playlog.c`, and `compare_win32.py commits 1e547e4 WORKTREE` says `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`.* **What lockstep does.** With `GE_LOCKSTEP` set (read once; the log holds `ge: lockstep: on` once) the pump (`portPumpEvents`) never sleeps and sends the retrace message only to a scheduler client queue that does not already hold it, so each wait of boss.c's frame queue gets exactly one retrace however often a frame pumps; `portLockstepRetrace` counts the retraces delivered, and `osGetTime`/`osGetCount` answer `portLockstepMicroseconds()` (retraces times 1,000,000 / 60, whole numbers) scaled as before instead of the host's clock. `GE_FRAMES` and the once-a-second heartbeat count those retraces. A pump while every queue still holds its retrace (a wait inside a frame: the first build skipped these pumps entirely and joy.c's poll handshake then never completed, so the input tick stayed at 0) runs the pump's duties (pad poll, music fades, audio) but delivers, counts and moves nothing. `portFixedTick` is true in lockstep (a frame advances one field), `portTickHz` returns 60 (so `GE_TICKHZ` and midas.ini's `tickhz` are ignored), the pacing block is skipped (so `GE_NOSLEEP` has nothing to turn off), `portRenderThreadWanted` (`video.c`, a line beyond the brief's file list) returns 0, and a retrace delivered during a demo stops the run with `ge: FATAL: GE_LOCKSTEP cannot replay a demo` (exit 1). The audio client's queue, which nothing on PC reads, keeps its first retrace. With `GE_LOCKSTEP` unset every changed function takes its old path. `lp64_play.py`: `Case.lockstep` (default False) gives a case `GE_LOCKSTEP=1`; `--env GE_LOCKSTEP` is refused, as is the variable in a case's own environment, and a case of the `demos` or `attract` set marked lockstep is refused (`DEMO_SETS`). `inputrec.c`, listed in the brief, needed no change: a headless build's input tick is its pad reads, which lockstep makes depend on the game alone. **Tests.** `test_lockstep.c` (through the new `test_lp64_compare.sh`, at 32 and 64 bits in the x86_64 container, 64 on aarch64; it includes `libultra_shim.c` with its `clock_gettime` stubbed and `port_lockstep.c`, and links the real `pcsched.c`): `time_is_retraces_times_a_field` (16,666 us after one retrace, 1,000,000 after 60), `unset_reads_the_host_clock` (the stubbed 12.345678 s converted as before), `one_retrace_a_frame` (three pumps a frame, one retrace message a frame over 100 frames, `g_PortFramesPumped` 100, under a second of wall time). It failed first on `port_lockstep.h: No such file or directory`. `test_lp64_play.py` adds `lockstep_case_sets_the_variable`, `env_refuses_lockstep` and `demo_never_gets_lockstep`. `test_high_alloc.c` and `test_inputrec_headless.c`, which include `pcsched.c` and `libultra_shim.c`, still link without `port_lockstep.c` (`--gc-sections`). **Other readers of the host (Step 3).** Every `osGetTime` and `osGetCount` call reads the shim and so the lockstep clock: in `src/` boss.c (the boot seed `randomSetSeed(osGetCount())`, now 0 retraces, or `GE_SEED`; the admit gate; the stage-load hold), frametiming.c, audi.c, bondview2.c, chraction.c, lv.c, propobj.c, sched.c, speed_graph.c, usb.c and the libultra audio, io and os files; in `port/src/` joy_port.c's latch and wheel timers, pcsched.c's `portRetraceDutyDue`, port_console.c, port_state.c's toast and the projectile arc files. *LP64-006 task 3, the simulation trace (2026-11-21). Commit "Write one simulation line a tick to a trace file" (`port/src/port_simtrace.c` and `port/include/port_simtrace.h` (new), `src/game/lv.c` (its include and one call, last in `lvlTick`, under `#ifndef TARGET_N64`), `CMakeLists.txt`, `scripts/port/test_simtrace.c`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_streams.py` and `scripts/port/test_lp64_equiv_streams.py` (new), `scripts/port/test_lp64_compare.sh`, `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, this inventory, the plan's LP64-006 row). Harness builds only: `portSimTraceTick` expands to nothing where `PORT_PLAY_HARNESS` is 0, CMake leaves `port_simtrace.c` out of a 32-bit video build as it leaves `port_lockstep.c`, and `compare_win32.py commits 2951af5 WORKTREE` says `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`.* **What it writes.** With `GE_SIMTRACE=FILE` the game writes FILE afresh (opened once, mode `w`), one line a `lvlTick`, flushed after each tick, and nothing to the log: `T n=N timer=G seed=S16 draws=D players=P pI=X,Y,Z,FACING,HEALTH ... chrs=C:H8 props=R:H8 rooms=L:H8`. `pI` is the player in `g_playerPointers[I]` (its prop's position, `vv_theta`, `bondhealth`); each `count:hash` is a count and a 32-bit FNV-1a hash over the records' values, each value fed as four bytes lowest first, so the host's byte order cannot reach it. Guards: each slot of `g_ChrSlots` whose `model` is set, hashing slot, `actiontype`, `chrflags`, prop position bits and `damage` bits. Props: the active list from `g_ActivePropsHead`, hashing list index, type, flags and position bits. Rooms: each room from 1 whose `model_bin_loaded` is set, hashing the room number and that byte. Two refinements of the brief's wording, both stated in `port_simtrace.h`: a room hashes `model_bin_loaded`'s value rather than 0 or 1, because the same byte holds the room's unload age (`bgRoomsTickUnload`), game state a 0 or 1 would hide for up to four ticks; a guard's health is its `damage` field (the game keeps damage taken, not health left). The fixed parts (leading `T`, `key=value` fields separated by one space, floats as eight hex digits of their bits, `count:hash`) are as the plan gives them. `GE_SIMTRACE_DETAIL=A-B` adds after each T line of calls A to B (inclusive) one `G n=N slot= chrnum= action= flags= pos= damage=` line a guard and one `M n=N index= slot= type= flags= pos=` line a moving prop (one not on the active list at the previous call, or whose position bits changed; `slot` is its index in `g_Props`); prop positions are tracked every call, so call A compares with call A-1. A FILE that cannot be opened or written stops the run (`ge: FATAL: GE_SIMTRACE cannot open FILE: REASON`, or `cannot write`, exit 1); a malformed `GE_SIMTRACE_DETAIL` is reported on stderr and ignored. The trace only reads: it writes no game state, draws no random number and reorders nothing. `lp64_equiv_streams.py`: `first_difference('sim', a, b)` returns `None` or `Difference(index, field, a, b, line)` (index the tick `n`, field the key, with `G.` or `M.` before a detail line's key); a file with no line, a last line without a newline, a line that does not parse, T lines that do not count from 1, or a file that ends where the other goes on raises `Unreadable`; `python3 scripts/port/lp64_equiv_streams.py sim A B` prints `identical: N lines` or the first difference. **Tests.** `test_simtrace.c` (through `test_lp64_compare.sh`): `line_has_every_field_in_order` (a fabricated tick against a line whose hashes were computed apart from the C, in Python), `float_is_written_as_bits` (0.1f is `3dcccccd`), `one_bit_in_one_guard_changes_the_chr_hash`, `no_pointer_reaches_the_file` (the same state in fresh heap records and other `g_Props` slots gives the same line), `detail_range_is_inclusive` (2-3 of four calls) and `unopenable_file_stops_the_run`. `test_lp64_equiv_streams.py`: the four tests the brief names, plus `file_with_no_line_is_unreadable`, `line_that_does_not_parse_is_unreadable` and `detail_line_difference_names_its_record_field`. They failed first on `port_simtrace.h: No such file or directory` and `No module named 'lp64_equiv_streams'`. **No order follows an address (Step 3).** Guard slots: walked by index; `init_GUARDdata_with_set_values` (`src/game/chr.c`, its loop at line 1680) takes the first slot whose `model` is NULL, by index. Active props: walked by `next` from the head; only `src/game/chrprop.c` links that list, `chrpropActivate` (line 321) appending, `chrpropActivateThisFrame` (343) prepending and `chrpropDelist` (361) unlinking, with records from the free list that `init_load_objpos_table` (`src/game/initobjects.c`, lines 51 to 57) chains in index order and that `chrpropAllocate` and `chrpropFree` (`chrprop.c` 287 and 312) use last in, first out. Rooms: walked by index from 1 over `g_BgRoomInfo` (`src/game/bg.c` line 183), as `unload_rooms` walks them. Players: `g_playerPointers` by index (`src/game/player.h` line 76). None is ordered by a pointer comparison, so no list needed re-walking by index. **First traces (Step 4).** Dam (`GE_STAGE=dam`, no route, no cheats), `GE_LOCKSTEP=1`, `GE_FRAMES=1800`, `GE_SIMTRACE` set, twice on each of the plain aarch64 build (`build/lp64/boot`, native) and the i686 build (`build/lp64/ref-i686`, emulated under qemu): each file holds 1,797 `T` lines (the logs say `frames=1800 gfxtasks=1797`), the two files of each build are byte-identical, and the i686 and aarch64 files are byte-identical as well (one SHA-256 for all four), so this run gives Task 6 no first difference. The last line counts 36 guards, 194 active props and 6 loaded rooms; the props hash takes 1,673 distinct values over the run. A run with `GE_SIMTRACE_DETAIL=1000-1001` on aarch64 wrote 74 G and 8 M lines and the same T lines; the sanitizer build (`build/lp64/boot-san`) with details for every tick (68,759 lines) reported nothing and wrote the same T lines. **Task check (not a checkpoint).** Plain aarch64 play sets (`demos,stages,stops,menus,tours,attract,input`, `--jobs 6 --timeout-scale 2`): `OK: 146 of 146 cases`; the same on `boot-san`: `OK: 146 of 146 cases`. `compare_win32.py` as above. Every line of the CI tests step in the x86_64 container (translated by Rosetta), each under a 1,200 s deadline, the new `test_lp64_equiv_streams.py` line included: all passed (78 runs), among them `test_lp64_compare.sh` (`test_simtrace: PASS` at 32 and 64 bits), `lp64_casts.py check` (24 casts, all allowed), `lp64_overlays.py check --no-defects` (1620 sites, all reviewed, 0 defect lines), `lp64_diagnostics.py gate` (357 and 388 files compiled, 0 failed), `narrowing --check` 0, `unprototyped --check` 2 allowed and `lp64_pointer_types.py check` (122 types as pinned), with one exception to the step as written: its combined `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 bash scripts/port/test_buffers.sh` was not run here, because its sanitized 32-bit half spins under qemu on this machine, so it ran as its two halves, `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64 MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1` and `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=32` unsanitized, both passing; the combined line is CI's after the push. *LP64-006 task 4, the comparison build and its maths (2026-11-21). Commit "Add the comparison build with one tanf and atanf for every host" (`port/src/port_compare_math.c`, `scripts/port/test_compare_math.c` and `scripts/port/lp64_libm_sweep.c` (new), `CMakeLists.txt`, `port/include/port_playlog.h`, `port/src/main.c` (one `#ifdef GE_COMPARE` call after the boot line), `scripts/port/test_lp64_compare.sh`, `scripts/port/test_pointer_bits.sh`, `scripts/port/package_linux.py`, `scripts/port/package_windows.py`, `scripts/port/test_distribution.py`, `AGENTS.md`, this inventory, the plan's LP64-006 row). Never a shipped build: with the option off every build has the same sources, defines and link line as before, and `compare_win32.py commits f3d5e3c WORKTREE` says `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`.* **The option.** `-DGE_COMPARE=ON` defines `GE_COMPARE`, compiles and links `port/src/port_compare_math.c` (with `-ffp-contract=off` at either width) and logs `ge: compare: on` once, after the boot line (`main.c`); it works at either width, headless or with video. `PORT_PLAY_HARNESS` (`port_playlog.h`) gained `|| defined(GE_COMPARE)`, its other terms unchanged, and CMake keeps `port_playlog.c`, `port_lockstep.c` and `port_simtrace.c` in a 32-bit video build only when `GE_COMPARE` is on (all three: with the harness on, the play log's calls need `port_playlog.c` as well), so a 32-bit video comparison build has lockstep and the trace while the shipped 32-bit video build keeps PORT_PLAY_HARNESS 0. `-DGE_COMPARE_LIBM=ON` (refused without `GE_COMPARE`) is the twin with libm's functions: the file then holds only the log call, which says `ge: compare: on (libm)`. `package_linux.py` and `package_windows.py` refuse a tree whose `CMakeCache.txt` has `GE_COMPARE` on (`test_distribution.py`: `test_packagers_refuse_a_comparison_build`, `test_packagers_accept_a_tree_without_the_comparison_option`). **The maths.** `tanf`, `atanf` and `cosf` compute in double with only `+ - * /` and comparisons and round once to float: tan and cos from the nested Taylor series of sin and cos on [-pi/4, pi/4], atan from its series on |u| <= 7/16 after musl-style bands (atan(1/2), pi/4, atan(3/2), pi/2 - atan(1/a); constants rounded from exact integer arithmetic), and the reduction by pi/2 in integers (the float's 24-bit significand times 96 bits of 2/pi from a 256-bit table, modulo 4), so it is exact enough for any finite float. The file refuses to compile with x87 arithmetic on i686 (`__SSE2_MATH__` unset), with `__FLT_EVAL_METHOD__` other than 0 or with `-ffast-math`; `objdump` of the aarch64 object shows no fused multiply-add. `test_compare_math.c` (in `test_lp64_compare.sh`) checks each function within two ulp of the C library's double function over 100,000 inputs (any finite float, and [-16, 16)), `tanf(+-0)` is `+-0` and `atanf` odd, at 32 and 64 bits in the x86_64 container and at 64 in the aarch64 one. The same script builds and runs the sweep at each width and fails unless its in-tree hashes are `tanf e3ccc704`, `atanf f160154d` and `cosf 4c162bf1` (pinned in CI after the task's review: host-independent by design, unlike libm's `sinf`, `expf` and `powf`, which stay unasserted), so a change that brings back host dependence fails CI on the host it affects. **The sweep (Step 3).** `lp64_libm_sweep.c` prints an FNV-1a hash of 1,048,576 results of each of `sinf`, `cosf`, `tanf`, `atanf`, `expf` and `powf`; linked with each tree's own `port_compare_math.c.o` (`cmp-i686`, `cmp-i686-video`, `cmp-x64`, `cmp-a64`): `sinf cc151db4 cosf 4c162bf1 tanf e3ccc704 atanf f160154d expf 8be3a4cd powf 648805d1` on all three hosts. With libm alone: i686 `sinf cc151db4 cosf 665365c3 tanf 2903846d atanf f160154d expf 8be3a4cd powf 648805d1`, x86_64 `... cosf 7944cf67 tanf 87342b84 atanf 9969ac78 ...`, aarch64 `... cosf 7944cf67 tanf ba498e8d atanf c59a87a7 ...` (sinf, expf and powf equal everywhere). So `cosf` joined the file by the plan's rule: i686's glibc `cosf` is one ulp from the 64-bit hosts' at +-0x1.0e1c8p+6 (about 67.53), two of the sweep's inputs (`bc866cc3` against `bc866cc4`). `sinf`, `expf` and `powf` stay libm's (until MAC-001 Task 8, 2026-11-27: macOS's differ, so a comparison build now takes Arm's routines, whose sweep hashes are these hosts', and the harness pins all six; FORK-093). **The trees (Step 4).** Each configured as the existing tree of its kind plus `-DGE_COMPARE=ON`, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`, built and linked: `build/lp64/cmp-a64` (aarch64 container, `-DGE_HEADLESS=ON -DGE_POINTER_BITS=64`) and `cmp-a64-video` (`-DGE_VIDEO=ON -DGE_POINTER_BITS=64`); `cmp-x64` and `cmp-x64-video` likewise in the x86_64 container; `cmp-i686` (`--arch i686`, `-DGE_HEADLESS=ON`); `cmp-i686-video` (`--arch i686 --video`, image `midas-lp64-i686-video`, `-DGE_VIDEO=ON -DSDL2_LINUX_ROOT=/home/dev/sdl2-linux-i686 -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-D_scheduler_h_`). The libm twins are left to the tasks that use them. In `cmp-i686-video`, offscreen (`SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen`, `SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy`, `GE_NOINPUT=1`, `GE_TICKHZ=60`, a windowed `midas.ini`, `HOME` under `build/lp64`), a Dam run with `GE_LOCKSTEP=1 GE_FRAMES=600 GE_SIMTRACE` logged `ge: compare: on`, `ge: video: window + GL context up`, `ge: lockstep: on` and `frames=600 gfxtasks=597`, exited 0, and wrote 597 `T` lines. **Still the game (Step 5).** `lp64_play.py run --set demos` on the plain `ref-i686` (`OK: 14 of 14 cases`) and on `cmp-i686`, `cmp-x64` and `cmp-a64` (14 of 14 each), then `traces --expect scripts/port/lp64_demo_traces.txt build/lp64/play/ref DIR`: `OK: 14 demos, 14 identical, 0 differing as recorded` for each of the three, so the comparison maths changed no demo's per-tick trace. **Checkpoint 1 (the task check, steps 1 to 8, in full).** Every tree rebuilt at this change first (`boot`, `boot-san`, `video`, `cmp-a64`, `cmp-a64-video` in the aarch64 container; `boot-x64`, `cmp-x64`, `cmp-x64-video`, `gate`, `gate-video` in the x86_64 one; `ref-i686`, `cmp-i686`, `cmp-i686-video` in the i686 ones). *LP64-006 task 5, the equivalence runner and its 38 cases (2026-11-21). Commit "Add the equivalence runner, its 38 cases and the two settings profiles" (`scripts/port/lp64_equiv.py`, `lp64_equiv_compare.py`, `lp64_equiv_cases.py`, `lp64_equiv_profile.py`, `lp64_equiv_expected.txt`, `test_lp64_equiv.py` and `test_lp64_equiv_compare.py` (new), `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_streams.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_equiv_streams.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play_run.py`, `port/src/port_simtrace.c`, `port/include/port_simtrace.h`, `src/game/ramromreplay.c`, `scripts/port/test_simtrace.c`, `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, `AGENTS.md`, this inventory, the LP64-006 plan's new section "Amendments during Task 5" and the plan's LP64-006 row). The task was planned as tools only, but the controller's ruling on demos changed game C after all. That change is harness-only: `PORT_PLAY_HARNESS` is 0 in a 32-bit video build, and `compare_win32.py commits 1c777fc WORKTREE` says `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`.* **The runner.** `lp64_equiv.py run --rom ROM --set SETS [--profile default|all] [--video [--draw [--shots TICK]]] [--repeat N] [--jobs N] [--only NAMES] [--maths-off] [--timeout-scale F] [--env NAME=VALUE] [--saves DIR] --output DIR EXECUTABLE` runs each case's streams into `DIR/runK`. Each case prints `CASE: RAN (T ticks, S shots)` or `CASE: FAIL (runK: reason)`, and the run ends with `OK: N of N cases ran` and `OK: N of N cases agree with themselves`; `equiv.json` records the run, written after the self-agreement check, with each case's verdict: whether it ran and whether it agreed with itself. It refuses an executable that does not log `ge: compare: on` (with `--maths-off`, `ge: compare: on (libm)`). `--env` refuses the variables the runner sets: `GE_LOCKSTEP`, `GE_FIXEDTICK`, `GE_NOSLEEP`, `GE_SIMTRACE`, `GE_GFXDIGEST`, `GE_GFXDIGEST_NODRAW`, `GE_AUDIO_LOCK`, `GE_AUDIO_CAPTURE`, `GE_SEED` and `GE_IRONSIGHTS_FONTS`, plus the video and folder variables with `--video`. `compare --streams S[,S] [--expect FILE] DIR...` compares each later folder's run 1 with the first's and prints the first difference by field. It refuses (exit 2) a folder whose runs failed or did not repeat: a record of one run (`--repeat 1`), a compared case that did not run or did not agree with itself, or no verdicts at all (an `equiv.json` from before they were recorded). Without that refusal, two builds that crashed at the same tick would have been reported as identical. `sensitivity` runs `stage-dam` with `GE_SEED` 1 and 2 and requires every stream to differ. The comparing code is in `lp64_equiv_compare.py`; `lp64_equiv.py` remains the entry point (ruling 4). `lp64_equiv_expected.txt` holds only its format: no exception is recorded yet. `lp64_play_run.py` gained a `Display.ini` (the profile's `midas.ini`) and `run_case(..., maybe_saves)`, which copies a saves folder into the run folder. **The cases (`lp64_equiv_cases.py`).**
- `demos`: the 14 demos, paced as `lp64_play.py` runs them.
- `solo`: the 20 missions and Cuba in lockstep, with `GE_CHEATS=invuln`, `GE_PLAYLOG=1` and a generated route of 3,900 ticks.
- `mp`: `temple-4p`.
- `menus`: `walk`, from boot to Dam, the watch's five tabs, the abort and back to the title.
- `reload`: `dam-twice`.
- `saves`: empty until Task 13.

The ticks of `walk` and `dam-twice` were measured on `cmp-a64` and pinned on 2026-11-21 at 1c777fc. `stepped(NAME)` gives a case's steps again so they can be measured anew. **The controller's rulings in this task** (the plan's "Amendments during Task 5" has the figures that caused them):
1. A route with fire needs `SHOT_FLOOR` = 15 shots and `moved`, not the plan's 30. Most missions start with a pistol that fires once a trigger window, so the first route measured 28 or 29 for most cases, 20 for frigate and 140 for caverns. The unarmed bunker2, archives and `temple-4p` need `moved` only (`ge: play: weapon 1`, the fists). Cuba, which has no player control, needs its stage load and frame limit only. Each case's count is recorded in `MEASURED_SHOTS` as a figure, not judged.
2. The routes sidestep; they do not turn. A headless replay acts on `P` records only (`port/src/inputrec.c`), and nothing in a `P` record turns Bond. Measured on `cmp-a64`, Dam in lockstep, each input held from tick 1300 to 1600: stick X at -80 moved Bond sideways, from (20167.4, 16892.6) to (19881.7, 17526.0); C-left left him still; his facing stayed 90.3 in every run. So the plan's C-button turn legs became sidestep legs: stick X at 80, left or right by the sign of the benchmark's turn list, for 45 ticks, with no `M` record and no C button (`route_uses_pad_records_only`). Each lockstep case keeps one facing for its whole run, and the 14 demos are the cases that turn. Turning in a lockstep route would need an `M` record or a look-stick field that headless replay acts on; that is game C in input recording and was left out of this task.
3. A demo's stream is its playback. Paced demos repeat, but `timer` and the trace's length follow the host's pace: in the first Step 4, ten of the 14 demos differed from themselves, in `timer` only within their playbacks. In harness builds a `T` line now ends in `demo=K` while a recording replays, K being the recording's tick (`port_simtrace.c`, `port_simtrace.h`). `src/game/ramromreplay.c` gained an include and a seven-line accessor under `#if PORT_PLAY_HARNESS`, `portRamromReplayTick`, which returns -1 when nothing plays. A one-line hook, dropping `static` from `port_demo_ticks`, changed 103 bytes of the 32-bit Windows `.text` (first at 0xf8ed0), so the accessor replaced it. The reader kind `sim-demo` (`lp64_equiv_streams.py`) keys records by K and compares every field except `n` and `timer`. A stream with no `demo=` line is unreadable, and unequal playbacks differ at the first K one of them lacks. The runner compares demos with it, still printing the stream as `sim`, and fails a demo trace with no `demo=` line.
4. Comparing moved to `lp64_equiv_compare.py`.
5. `--profile all` sets `GE_IRONSIGHTS_FONTS=1`, because `font_style=2` loads as Original without it. `--env` refuses it.

*LP64-006 task 6, simulation equivalence (2026-11-21). Commits "Record the 32-bit special-portal walk as Jungle's one difference from the 64-bit builds" and "Record where each case's simulation matches the 32-bit build" (`scripts/port/lp64_equiv_expected.txt`; no game C or C++ changed).* The 38 cases ran on the three comparison builds at 639a047, each brought up to date first with `cmake --build` in its own container (`cmp-i686` in the i686 container under qemu-i386, `cmp-x64` in the x86_64 container under Rosetta 2, `cmp-a64` in the native aarch64 container; each only relinked its build information). Nothing here ran on real x86 hardware. **The reference agrees with itself.** `lp64_equiv.py run --rom /rom/baserom.u.z64 --set demos,solo,mp,menus,reload --repeat 2 --timeout-scale 8 --output build/lp64/equiv/sim/i686 build/lp64/cmp-i686/IronSights` printed `OK: 38 of 38 cases ran` and `OK: 38 of 38 cases agree with themselves` in 427 s of wall time. The same command without `--timeout-scale` printed the same two lines on `cmp-x64` (`build/lp64/equiv/sim/x64`, 221 s) and `cmp-a64` (`build/lp64/equiv/sim/a64`, 215 s). Each lockstep case ran 3,897 ticks (`walk` 2,996, `dam-twice` 5,570) with the same shot counts on all three builds. **What matched.** `compare --streams sim --expect scripts/port/lp64_equiv_expected.txt build/lp64/equiv/sim/i686 build/lp64/equiv/sim/x64 build/lp64/equiv/sim/a64` exits 0 with `OK: 38 cases, 76 streams, 74 identical, 2 as recorded`. Identical on both pairs (i686:x64 and i686:a64): the 14 demos' playbacks; 20 of the 21 `solo` cases, every one but Jungle; `temple-4p`; `walk`; and `dam-twice`. Because `dam-twice` matches, its second Dam load included, Step 3 had no difference to try: on this route the portal fields that the 32-bit build keeps from the first load change nothing the trace records. No 64-bit defect was found. **Jungle** (`stage-jungle`, both pairs, first tick 7, field `rooms`). At tick 7 the 32-bit build has 7 rooms loaded and both 64-bit builds 10. `GE_ROOMLIST=1` names the rooms: the 32-bit portal walk draws rooms 19, 20, 22, 21, 23, 24 and 25, with clipped screen boxes for 21, 23 and 24 (from x=116, 185 and 215). The 64-bit walk adds rooms 16, 17 and 18, and every box is the whole screen. The props first differ at tick 530, the guards at 584 and the random seed at 630. The cause is the 32-bit special-portal walk (`sub_GAME_7F0B37EC`, `src/game/bg.c`), the link-order dependence that the LP64-004 entry "the special-portal walk's end" recorded. The walk stops when its pointer reaches `&g_BgCurrentRoom`. On the N64 that variable follows the 20-byte `specialportalarray`, but both 32-bit links checked place it 4 bytes before the array: the Linux comparison build `cmp-i686` (0x0823e78c against 0x0823e790) and the local Windows build that `compare_win32.py` made of 639a047 (`build/lp64/compare/a`, 0x10337630 against 0x10337634). Both variables are defined in `src/game/bg.c`, so their order is the compiler's, not the linker's choice among objects. The released Windows binary's map was not read. The do-while therefore applies only the array's first record, level entry 3 (Control), which is why Control matches. It never reaches the second record, level entry 17 (Jungle), which marks portals 0x00 to 0x3a `PORTALFLAG_SPECIAL`. The 64-bit walk ends at the array's own end and marks them, as the N64 layout does. The run that removes the cause is a scratch 32-bit comparison build (`build/lp64/equiv/scratch-portal-end`, made from `git archive HEAD` with `scripts/port/lp64_patches/portal-end-32bit.patch`) that ends the walk at the array's own end at both widths. All 38 of its cases ran and agreed with themselves (437 s, `build/lp64/equiv/sim/i686-portal-end`). Its compare with both 64-bit folders printed `OK: 38 cases, 76 streams, 76 identical, 0 as recorded`; against the reference, only Jungle differs, at tick 7. What a player sees: in a 32-bit build with this layout (both builds checked have it), Jungle's 59 portals, all it has, are walked as ordinary portals rather than special ones. The room walk clips through them and draws and loads fewer rooms (7 against 10 at the start), and the guards and props that depend on them part later. A 64-bit build draws them as the N64's data asks. No picture was taken, so whether a player notices missing or popping scenery is not verified. Nothing shipped changes. Whether the 32-bit game should end the walk at the array goes to the owner with this evidence, because that change would alter the shipped 32-bit program.

**With the maths off** (Step 4). `cmp-i686-libm` and `cmp-x64-libm` were configured as the plain trees are, plus `-DGE_COMPARE_LIBM=ON` (Debug, `GE_HEADLESS=ON`, `GE_COMPARE=ON`, and `GE_POINTER_BITS=64` for x86_64), and their logs say `ge: compare: on (libm)`. With `--maths-off` both printed `OK: 38 of 38 cases ran` and `OK: 38 of 38 cases agree with themselves`: i686 in 430 s with `--timeout-scale 8` (`build/lp64/equiv/sim-libm/i686-libm`) and x86_64 in 219 s (`x64-libm`). The folders carry the `-libm` suffix so that their pair, `i686-libm:x64-libm`, keeps its expectation lines apart from the plain pair's. `compare --streams sim --expect scripts/port/lp64_equiv_expected.txt build/lp64/equiv/sim-libm/i686-libm build/lp64/equiv/sim-libm/x64-libm` exits 0 with `OK: 38 cases, 38 streams, 34 identical, 4 as recorded`. Dam and Depot first differ at tick 641 and `dam-twice` at 3156, each in `props`. At Dam's tick 641 the detail lines (`GE_SIMTRACE_DETAIL=630-645`) show an explosion prop (type 7, list index 0, prop slot 267) created that tick, one tick after the route's third trigger window opens: its Y is `c24ad9ac` on i686 and `c24ad9aa` on x86_64, 2 ulp apart, and its X and Z are equal. Jungle differs at 7, the special-portal walk above, and with the walk ended at the array in a scratch 32-bit libm build (`sim-libm/portal-end-i686-libm`) its first difference moves to tick 1481 (`props`). Which function is to blame was shown by scratch comparison builds that put libm's functions back one at a time (`scripts/port/lp64_patches/libm-cosf-scratch.patch` and `libm-cosf-atanf-scratch.patch`, which rename the in-tree definitions so the link takes glibc's). With libm `cosf` and the in-tree `tanf` and `atanf`, the three cases are identical between i686 and x86_64 (`sim-libm/cosf-libm-*`). With libm `atanf` and `cosf` and only the in-tree `tanf`, they are identical as well (`sim-libm/tanf-only-*`). Jungle with that build and the walk ended at the array is identical to the x86_64 build over all 3,897 ticks (`sim-libm/portal-end-tanf-only-i686` against `tanf-only-jungle-x64`). The C library's `tanf` is therefore the callee whose result differs in all four cases. The three lines for Dam, Depot and `dam-twice` are `host:` lines. Each names libm `tanf` alone and the run that isolates it (`sim-libm/tanf-only-*`, `libm-cosf-atanf-scratch.patch`), and says that it was seen only between the emulated i686 and the translated x86_64 builds. Jungle's libm line stays `explained:` for the walk, and its `tanf` part from tick 1481 is worded the same way. The expectation file holds 3 `explained:` lines and 3 `host:` lines (review fix round 1; the first wording, `explained: libm tanf/atanf; removed-by: GE_COMPARE`, claimed more than the runs show). What a player would see: the shipped builds keep libm's `tanf`. A 32-bit and a 64-bit game on different C libraries can therefore place an explosion a few ulp apart, and the two runs part from there; nothing at that scale is visible on its own. These differences were seen only between the emulated i686 build and the translated x86_64 build. Whether real x86 hardware gives the same `tanf` results is not confirmed. **Checks.** Only the expectation file and documents changed, so no play sets ran: the executables are the ones last checked in Task 5. `compare_win32.py commits 639a047 WORKTREE`: `identical in loaded code and data`. Every line of the CI tests step ran in the x86_64 container, each under `timeout 1200`: 80 runs, all exited 0, in 461 s. The combined `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 bash scripts/port/test_buffers.sh` was not run locally, because its sanitized 32-bit half spins under emulation here. It ran instead as `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64 MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1` and `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=32`, and CI runs the combined line after the push. Those runs include the static checks: `lp64_casts.py check` (`OK: 24 truncating casts in 11 files, all allowed`), `lp64_overlays.py check --no-defects` (`OK: 1620 sites, all reviewed`), `lp64_diagnostics.py gate` (357 and 388 files compiled, 0 failed), `narrowing --check` (0), `unprototyped --check` (2 allowed) and `lp64_pointer_types.py check` (122 types as pinned).

*LP64-006 task 7, the picture digest (2026-11-21). Commit "Hash what the renderer is asked to draw, a line a frame" (`port/src/port_gfx_digest.cpp` (new), `port/include/port_gfx_digest.h` (new), `port/src/video.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `scripts/port/test_gfx_digest.cpp` (new), `scripts/port/test_gfx_digest.sh` (new), `scripts/port/test_pointer_bits.sh`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_compare.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_streams.py` and their three tests, `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, `AGENTS.md`, this inventory, the plan's LP64-006 row and the LP64-006 plan's Task 7 amendments). Comparison video builds only: CMake compiles the digest only with `GE_COMPARE` and `GE_VIDEO`, the hook in `videoInit` is inside `#ifdef GE_COMPARE`, and `compare_win32.py commits 8924801 WORKTREE` says `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`. Because no shipped or benchmarked build holds it, the render benchmark rule does not apply; the wrapper asks the GL driver nothing.* **What it writes.** In a comparison video build, `GE_GFXDIGEST=FILE` wraps the backend's `GfxRenderingAPI` table (`portGfxDigestWrap`, called after `set.rapi = &gfx_opengl_api`) in one whose every entry hashes its arguments and then calls the backend's, and writes one line at each `end_frame`: `F n=N tick=T draws=D tris=R vtx=H8 tex=U:H8 state=H8 post=H8`, plus ` demo=K` (the recording's tick, `portRamromReplayTick`) while a recording replays. Each H8 is a 32-bit FNV-1a hash, over 32-bit values, of one part's calls: `vtx` the vertex floats drawn and the retained geometry (hashed once at `retained_build`, then each `retained_draw*` adds that hash with its matrices, fog and lights); `tex` the uploads (U counts them) and, at each draw, the contents of the textures its shader samples (from the interpreter's own `shader_get_info`); `state` depth, viewport, scissor, alpha, samplers, shader ids, tiles, framebuffer selection and clears; `post` the optional passes. Content is hashed, never an address or handle: a shader is its two combiner ids, a texture the hash of its last upload, a retained draw its descriptor's built contents, a framebuffer its creation order. Bookkeeping (queries, shader lookups and info, texture ids made and freed, framebuffer and retained buffer creation) is in no part. That rule came from a measurement: `demo-dam1` first failed to agree with itself in `state`, at the 13th call of a frame (`select_texture`), first because creation-order texture names followed the host's pace before the recording plays, then because the texture cache's free-id pool hands back ids without `new_texture`; naming textures by content and hashing what each draw samples fixed both. An X-macro list (`GFX_DIGEST_ENTRIES`) wraps all 53 entries, and a `static_assert` on the table's size fails the build when the table gains one the list lacks; an entry the backend leaves NULL stays NULL. `GE_GFXDIGEST_NODRAW=1` calls the backend only for what the interpreter reads back or what sets it (shader create, lookup, info and clear; texture ids and filter; framebuffer creation, parameters and ids; clip parameters; `retained_create`, `retained_build`, `retained_destroy`; `start_draw_to_framebuffer`; the frame's own entries) and skips draws, uploads, binds, clears, copies and post passes. `GE_GFXDIGEST_DETAIL=A-B` adds `C n=N k=K entry=NAME part=PART hash=H8` a call in frames A to B. A file that cannot be opened or written stops the run with `ge: FATAL: GE_GFXDIGEST ...`. **The runner.** `lp64_equiv.py run --video` sets `GE_GFXDIGEST` to `CASE.gfx` with `NODRAW=1`, or draws with `--draw`, and fails a run whose `.gfx` is missing or torn (`gfx unreadable: ...`). `lp64_equiv_streams.py` reads `gfx` (frames from 1, a `C` line belonging to the next `F` line, the first differing frame and field named) and `gfx-demo` (a demo's frames keyed by `demo=K`, so the host-paced frames before the recording are not compared). Agreement and `sensitivity` judge `sim` and `gfx`; `snd` is left out until Task 9's sound lock (the `.wav` of two runs of one build differed when measured). `compare` still byte-compares `snd`. **Tests.** `scripts/port/test_gfx_digest.sh` compiles `test_gfx_digest.cpp` with the wrapper against a counting stand-in table at both widths (`harness_widths.sh`); its 13 checks include that one vertex bit changes only `vtx` and one texel only `tex`, that equal bytes at two addresses hash equally, that a recycled texture id is named by its new contents, that NODRAW skips draws and uploads but forwards shader info, that NULL entries stay NULL and every slot is wrapped, and the demo and detail lines. It failed first on the missing header. The Python tests (`test_lp64_equiv_streams.py` 24, `test_lp64_equiv.py` 33, `test_lp64_equiv_compare.py` 11) pass; the new reader tests failed first on `unknown stream 'gfx'`. `test_pointer_bits.sh` checks that the 32-bit comparison video tree compiles the digest and that the headless comparison, plain 32-bit video and 64-bit video trees do not. **Measured** on the comparison video builds (Mesa software GL, offscreen SDL, in containers on an Apple Silicon Mac; nothing ran on real x86 hardware or a GPU). Step 3: `stage-dam` on the commit's `cmp-a64-video` build with `--repeat 2`, without and with `--draw` (`build/lp64/equiv/t7-step3-final-nodraw`, `t7-step3-final-draw`), each printed `OK: 1 of 1 cases agree with themselves`, and the four `stage-dam.gfx` files (3,897 lines) hash to sha1 `0f2a8647...` (`t7-step3-final.sha`): drawing or not changes no line. Step 4: the same case on `cmp-i686-video` under qemu-i386 with `--timeout-scale 10` ran in 46 s of wall time (`t7-step4-i686`), and its `.gfx` and `.sim` are identical to the aarch64 build's over 3,897 lines, an early observation for Task 8. Step 5: `sensitivity --video` printed `OK: sim and gfx differ between seeds` (`t7-sensitivity`). Demos: the 14 demos on the commit's `cmp-a64-video` build with `--repeat 2` printed `OK: 14 of 14 cases ran` and `OK: 14 of 14 cases agree with themselves` (`t7-demos-video-final`). The first Step 3 and demo runs (`t7-step3-nodraw`, `t7-step3-draw`, `t7-demos-video`) predated the wrapper's last edit; the controller reran both on the commit's build, with the same result and, for Step 3, the same sha1, which `t7-step4-i686`'s `stage-dam.gfx` also has. The one-distinct-`demo=K`-a-frame count (`t7-demos-video.counts`) comes from the earlier demo run only. Steps 4 and 5 ran on the commit's builds. **Renderer maths the digest sees.** `gfx_ge_vector_overlay` (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`) computes the HUD arcs and ellipses with `std::cos` and `std::sin` and hands them to `draw_triangles`, so a host difference there would show in `vtx`; the `std::tan` of `gfx_screen_env.inl` runs inside the backend after `env_begin`'s arguments are hashed, so the digest does not see it. 64-bit builds compile with `-ffp-contract=off`; the 32-bit build with `-msse2 -mfpmath=sse`. **Checks.** The plain play sets (`lp64_play.py run --set demos,stages,stops,menus,tours,attract,input` on `build/lp64/boot/IronSights`, aarch64) printed `OK: 146 of 146 cases` in 945 s (`build/lp64/play/t7-plain`), and the video sets with `sound` (`--video --jobs 4 --timeout-scale 4` on `build/lp64/video/IronSights`) printed `OK: 148 of 148 cases` in 3,928 s (`build/lp64/play/t7-video`). In the x86_64 container, `lp64_diagnostics.py gate` compiled 357 and 388 files with none failing, `narrowing --check` found 0, `unprototyped --check` the 2 allowed calls and `lp64_pointer_types.py check` the 122 pinned types (the gate trees are not comparison builds, so they do not compile the digest; `test_gfx_digest.sh` compiles it at both widths with `-Werror`); `lp64_casts.py check` and `lp64_overlays.py check --no-defects` pass. Every line of CI's tests step, each under `timeout 1200`, passed in that container (81 lines, `build/lp64/equiv/t7-ci/summary.txt`), and `hand_gallery.py verify --allow-pending` reports the gallery pending, not failing. The combined `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 bash scripts/port/test_buffers.sh` line was not run locally (it hangs here, the controller's ruling); its two halves were run instead: `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64 MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1` and `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=32`, both passing.

*LP64-006 task 8, picture equivalence, phase A (2026-11-22). Commit "Add the picture comparison tool" (`scripts/port/lp64_equiv_pictures.py` (new), `scripts/port/test_lp64_equiv_pictures.py` (new), `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`, `AGENTS.md`; no game C or C++ changed).* `lp64_equiv_pictures.py` checks drawn pixels beside the picture digest: `shots DIR_A DIR_B` compares each case's screenshot at picture TICK in two `lp64_equiv.py run --video --draw --shots TICK` folders and prints `CASE: identical` or `CASE: N of M pixels differ, largest channel difference D` (exit 1 on a difference, 2 on a missing, unreadable or mis-sized screenshot, which is never counted as a difference); `gallery --rom ROM --output DIR EXECUTABLE` runs the hand gallery's capture mode offscreen with the fixture `midas.ini` and the variables `hand_gallery.py` uses (the module is imported, never edited, and its `generate` is never called), in DIR with its own `HOME` and a copy of the executable that it removes, and writes the 216 captures' pixel hashes to `DIR/gallery.txt` only when all 216 and the completion line were seen; `gallery-compare A B` names each capture that differs and counts them. The rule it serves: equal digests with different pixels are the rasterizer's (recorded with their size), different digests are a defect or an explained difference. Screenshots and hash lists are ROM-derived and stay under `build/lp64/`. `test_lp64_equiv_pictures.py` (six tests, ROM-free, in CI's tests step) failed first with `No module named 'lp64_equiv_pictures'`, then passed. On the comparison builds before phase A's fixes: `gallery` on `cmp-a64-video` wrote 216 captures, 108 of 108 cases repeating their pose between samples, in 323 s; on `cmp-x64-video` the same in 452 s; the two lists differ in 216 of 216 (two llvmpipe builds; informational). The render thread does not move a demo's digest: dam1 on `cmp-a64-video` with `GE_RENDERTHREAD=1` and without gave 453 ticks each, 0 differing (55 s each).

*Commit "Read zero past an odd-width 4-bit texture at 64 bits" (`src/game/image.c`, `scripts/port/test_image_inflate.c` (new), `scripts/port/test_image_inflate.sh` (new), `.github/workflows/windows-release.yml`).* Cause A of the default profile's picture differences: `texChannelsToPixels` (I4, IA4) and `texInflateLookupFromBuffer` (4-bit lookups) pack each row's last pixel of an odd-width image with the value after it, which for the image's last row is one past what the decoder wrote into `texInflateNonZlib`'s stack `scratch`, so that nibble is whatever an earlier, differently deep call left there. Measured with an instrumented scratch copy (`build/lp64/equiv/t8-meas-src`, trees `build/lp64/t8-meas-{a64,x64}-video`, runs `t8-meas-{a64,x64}`): walk's 65 by 65 textures 2598 to 2605 (IA4 and I4, lookup, RLE-lookup and Huffman-blur methods) end each row in such a pair, and the varying byte, offset 2592 of the 2,600 uploaded, is the last row's last pair; Frigate's IA4 textures 1542 and 1543 are 129 wide with odd-width mip levels. The compressed data is not short: in walk and Frigate on both hosts (502 and 408 texture loads) every texture's reads end inside its `romCopy` (`read` at most `copy` in each `t8meas load` line), and every zlib image inflates to exactly its index count, within `scratch2`. Filling `texLoad`'s `compbuffer` moved walk's byte only because a shallower earlier call put that buffer where a later `scratch` lies. A 64-bit build now clears `scratch` at the start of each `texInflateNonZlib` call (inside `#if IS_64_BIT`; the 32-bit program keeps its leftovers, the owner's to change as with the Jungle portal walk (changed by LP64-007 Task 12)), so the value after the image reads zero; whatever still differs from the i686 build there is recorded as an explained difference in phase B. `test_image_inflate.sh` (ROM-free, CI's tests step, both widths) links `image.c` with stubs, dirties the stack, inflates one RLE-coded I4 pixel of 0xA and requires the packed byte to be 0xA0 at 64 bits: on the unfixed `image.c` it failed with `last pixel pair 0xff, want 0xa0`, and after the fix it passes at both widths, the 32-bit half printing the leftover (0xff).

*Commit "Keep the host's clock out of comparison pictures under all options" (`port/src/port_baked_light.c`, `port/src/port_console.c`; both changes only under `#ifdef GE_COMPARE`, so shipped and other builds are unchanged).* Cause B: under `--profile all` every case's `gfx` disagreed with itself on all three builds while its `sim` agreed (i686 2354 s, x64 969 s, a64 907 s, before this commit). Two things on screen followed the host. Baked Lighting (FORK-082) finished on the frame its worker threads' speed picked and printed `Baked Lighting: ready (N vertices, M ms)` with wall-clock milliseconds; with `baked_lighting=0` in a scratch profile the lockstep cases agreed with themselves (`t8-all-nobake-a64` 193 s, `t8-all-nobake-x64` 206 s). A comparison build now waits for the bake at the end of `portBakeLevelLoaded`, so it is ready at the stage's first tick on every host, and its ready line names no time; the unbaked frames stay covered by the default profile, which has Baked Lighting off. With that alone, dam1's digest still parted between runs (`t8-demo-detail2-a64`, three runs with `GE_GFXDIGEST_DETAIL=1-400`, 213 s): the `C` lines name the call, a third `start_draw_to_framebuffer` pass of 33 textured quads (the console's transient top row) drawn in pictures 1 to 261 in two runs and 1 to 262 in the third, because the console times a message's 3 s dwell by `osGetTime`, which in a paced demo follows the host. A comparison build now reads, for that dwell only, a clock that counts the pictures `portConRender` has drawn at a sixtieth of a second each. On the code as committed at the end of phase A ("Number the Explosive Rounds rows as the table has them", built after it), stage-dam, stage-cuba, temple-4p, dam-twice, walk, dam1 and runway1 under `--profile all --repeat 2` printed `OK: 7 of 7 cases agree with themselves` on `cmp-a64-video` (`t8a-c-a64`, 208 s) and on `cmp-x64-video` (`t8a-c-x64`, 213 s), and stage-dam and dam1 printed `OK: 2 of 2 cases agree with themselves` on `cmp-i686-video` (`t8a-c-i686`, 127 s, `--timeout-scale 4`); stage-frigate under all options is left for phase B. Rule kept for any further option of this kind: a stream holds nothing of the host.

Cause C, found and not fixed here: under `--profile all` the aarch64 build's simulation leaves the x86 builds' in 12 solo cases and dam-twice (stage-dam at tick 755: 493,462 random draws on i686 and x86_64, 38 on aarch64). Explosive Rounds (FORK-078) number its blasts 22, 23 and 24 (`port/include/port_explosive_rounds.h`, "after Rare's 22"), but Rare's US table has 21 rows, so `g_ExplosionTypes` holds 24 (0x600 bytes of 64-byte rows in the aarch64 binary): Visual rounds read Bond's damaging Explosive row, Bond's Explosive rounds the guard row (the same data, and his hit marker still showed, since that test compares type numbers), and a guard's round (type 24, logged 581 times in stage-dam with `GE_ROUNDS_LOG=1`, `t8-roundslog-a64`) reads past the table into the next objects, whose bytes differ by host, so its shrapnel count (`explosion.c`'s `numshrapnelbits` loop) is thousands on x86 and a few on aarch64. A float-cast-overflow sanitizer build (`build/lp64/t8-fco-x64-video`, `t8-fco-x64`) named no conversion on that path (its one report was `env.c:496:27`, a float of -44309.2 to `short` in the audio envelope). Moving the three numbers onto their rows (scratch patch `scripts/port/lp64_patches/t8-rounds-table-index.patch`, trees `build/lp64/t8-rounds-{a64,x64}-video`) makes stage-dam's `sim` identical between aarch64 and x86_64 through tick 3,897 (`t8-rounds-{a64,x64}`). It changes what the shipped 32-bit game does (the feature's own defect), so it waited for the owner's ruling, below.
