*LP64-006 task 9, the sound lock (2026-11-22). Commit "Add the comparison build's sound lock and read its recordings" (`port/src/port_audio_lock.c` (new), `port/include/port_audio_lock.h` (new), `port/src/audio_pc.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `scripts/port/test_audio_lock.c` (new), `scripts/port/test_lp64_compare.sh`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_streams.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_compare.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv.py` and their three test files, `AGENTS.md`).* Until now a recording's length and contents followed the host's audio clock (the SDL queue's top-up and trim, or the clock path without a device), so two runs of one build differed. **The lock.** `portAudioLockFrames(field_now)` (`port_audio_lock.h`) answers, in a comparison build with `GE_AUDIO_LOCK` set (read once), the game fields since its last call (0 on the first, never below 0), and -1 without the variable. Without `GE_COMPARE` the header defines it as `(-1)` and CMake leaves `port_audio_lock.c` out, so a shipped `audio_pc.c` compiles the call to today's path: `compare_win32.py commits 925fe12 WORKTREE` printed `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs` (119 s). The pump asks it first, after the synthesizer check; when it answers 0 or more, `portAudioPumpLocked` mixes that many frames of `g_FrameSize` samples (audi.c, 368 at 60 fields a second) and records each through `GE_AUDIO_CAPTURE`, with no device, no queue level, no top-up, trim or clock, and logs `ge: audio: locked to game fields` once. A frame `portAudioPumpForce` asks for (music.c's stop waits, which spin on the sequencer until it stops) is still mixed, ahead of its field, and the next pumps mix one fewer, so frame k of a recording is field k + 1's counted from the lock's first pump (the brief did not cover forced frames; the plan's "Amendments during Task 9" says why). A frame the synthesizer gives no command, or that `portAcmdValidate` refuses, is recorded as silence, so the frame count stays the field count. **The stream.** `lp64_equiv_streams.py` reads `snd` (`read_snd`): a RIFF WAVE, 16-bit PCM, 22,050 Hz stereo, whose data chunk holds the bytes it declares, a whole number of samples, one or more; anything else is unreadable. `first_difference('snd', a, b)` names the first differing sample (the index), its channel, audio frame and field (`R frame=1 field=2`); two files whose common part is equal differ at the shorter one's end (field `length`, values the sample counts). The byte-for-byte fallback in `lp64_equiv_compare.py` is gone: every stream now has a reader. **The runner.** `JUDGED_VIDEO_STREAMS` is `gfx` and `snd`: with `--video --repeat 2` each case's `.wav` must agree with itself, `sensitivity --video` requires `sim`, `gfx` and `snd` to differ between seeds, a video run fails without the line `ge: audio: locked to game fields`, and `compare --streams snd` refuses a folder whose case log lacks it (exit 2). A demo's `snd` is never judged, in self-agreement, sensitivity or compare; the runner prints `CASE: snd not judged: REASON` for each demo and compare `CASE snd PAIR not judged: REASON` (`DEMO_SND_REASON`; measured below, recorded as an amendment). **Tests**, each seen failing before its code: `test_audio_lock.c` (`one_frame_a_field`: fields 5, 6, 6, 9 give 0, 1, 0, 3; `off_without_the_variable`: -1; `off_outside_a_comparison_build`: the header without `GE_COMPARE` gives -1), built twice by `test_lp64_compare.sh` at each width; RED `scripts/port/test_audio_lock.c:14:10: fatal error: port_audio_lock.h: No such file or directory`. `test_lp64_equiv_streams.py` adds `test_snd_names_first_sample_frame_and_field`, `test_snd_reports_length_when_one_is_longer`, `test_snd_that_is_not_22050_hz_stereo_is_unreadable` and `test_identical_recordings_have_no_difference` (RED: `ValueError: unknown stream 'snd'`). `test_lp64_equiv.py` (36 tests) writes real recordings from its stand-ins and adds a recording that is not a WAV, a run without the lock line, a recording that differs from itself (`FAIL: stage-dam snd differs from itself at 1 (R frame=0 field=1, run2)`), a demo's unjudged recording, and sensitivity over `sim, gfx and snd`; `test_lp64_equiv_compare.py` (13 tests) replaces the byte-stream test with a recording difference by sample, frame and field, and adds the refusal of an unlocked recording and a demo's unjudged `snd`. GREEN: `test_lp64_compare.sh` in the aarch64 container prints `test_audio_lock: PASS (64-bit, comparison build)`, `test_audio_lock: PASS (64-bit, without GE_COMPARE)` and `test_lp64_compare: PASS`; the three Python files `OK`. Its runs and the checkpoint are in the next note.

*The comparison and checkpoint 2 (2026-11-22; commit "Lock the comparison build's sound to game fields and compare it": `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_expected.txt`, this note, the plan's "Amendments during Task 9" and its status row).* Hosts, for every figure here: aarch64 native, x86_64 under Rosetta 2, i686 under qemu-i386, all on one Mac in the project's containers, video through SDL's offscreen driver on Mesa's llvmpipe; no real x86 hardware and no GPU. Step 4's runs used trees built at 10:32 to 10:35 from the code of the lock commit, after its last C edit and before its commit, which changed only build stamps; Step 3, the demo measurement, sensitivity and the checkpoint ran on trees rebuilt from the commit (`0878cf4`). *Step 3:* `lp64_equiv.py run --set solo --only stage-dam --video --repeat 2` on `cmp-a64-video` (33 s, `build/lp64/equiv/t9-final/step3-a64`): two byte-identical `stage-dam.wav` files, 11,475,756 bytes (2,868,928 samples, 7,796 frames of 368), SHA-256 `f0dabf2f...8497e`, 130.11 s, peak 14,641, 99.8 percent non-zero; the same file as the run before the commit. *Demos (the brief's ruling 4):* two runs each of dam1 and facility1 (`t9-final/demos-a64`, 51 s; `demos-i686`, 55 s): `sim-demo` and `gfx-demo` identical in all four pairs, the recordings different in three (aarch64 facility1 at 8,814,380 against 8,817,324 bytes; i686 dam1 from sample 1,466,276; i686 facility1 from sample 105,651) and identical in one (aarch64 dam1). Before the commit the same four pairs all differed (`build/lp64/equiv/t9-demos`). In Step 4's runs none of the 14 demos recorded the same sound twice on any build under either profile, 84 of 84 pairs (`t9-final/demo-self-agreement.out`). A demo's fields a recording tick are the host's pace, so its `snd` is not judged (amendment 1). *The pump on idle pumps* (a review's pointer from Task 2): `musicFadeTick` and the pump also run on a lockstep pump that delivers no retrace. Not changed: every lockstep case recorded the same sound twice on every build under both profiles, so it does not matter to the recording; under the lock an idle pump mixes nothing, since no field passes. *Sensitivity* (`t9-final/sensitivity`, 67 s): `OK: sim, gfx and snd differ between seeds`. *Step 4*, 38 cases, `--video --repeat 2 --timeout-scale 4`, each build `OK: 38 of 38 cases ran` and `OK: 38 of 38 cases agree with themselves`, with a `not judged` line for each demo: default (`build/lp64/equiv/snd-default/{i686,x64,a64}`, `.out` beside each) i686 597 s, x86_64 461 s, aarch64 463 s; all options (`snd-all`) 830, 470 and 452 s. i686 and x86_64 ran together, then aarch64 beside the all-options i686 run; the all-options x86_64 run beside that i686 run; the all-options aarch64 run alone. `compare --streams sim,gfx,snd --expect scripts/port/lp64_equiv_expected.txt i686 x64 a64`: default `OK: 38 cases, 200 streams, 192 identical, 8 as recorded`, all options `OK: 38 cases, 200 streams, 190 identical, 10 as recorded` (`compare.out` in each folder); the 28 demo `snd` comparisons print `not judged`. x86_64 against aarch64, without the file: `OK: 38 cases, 100 streams, 100 identical, 0 as recorded` under both profiles (`compare-x64-a64.out`), so `env.c:496`'s out-of-range conversion (Task 8's concern) changes nothing either host records and was not touched. Commit "Read the pool peaks by stage and check them against a budget file" (`scripts/port/lp64_play_peaks.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_play.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_play_peaks.py`, this note).* **The tool.** `lp64_play.py peaks` now reads `DIR/runK/*.log` as well as `DIR/*.log`, so an `lp64_equiv.py` folder's repeats are read. `peaks --by-stage DIR...` keeps each pool's largest use by level and size, one line `POOL LEVEL SIZE PEAK DIR/CASE`, marked ` ABOVE HALF` past half its size. A print belongs to the level of the `ge: load_bg_file levelid=` line logged since the print before it, and to level 0, the front end, when no background loaded in between (the brief's "the last `load_bg_file` line before it" would give the front end's pools, printed at the next stage's unload, to the stage before; over 354 logs of Tasks 9 and 10 every print holding room memory, and no other, had a load since the print before). A line is a pool, level and size, not a pool and level, because one stage gives a pool several sizes: multiplayer tokens and Statue's raise (room memory in levels 22, 27, 32, 34 and 39, the graphics buffer in 24, 27, 32, 34 and 39), the vertex pool by players, and the name `texture pool`, which the stage's pool, the gun's pools and the persistent 4 MB model pool (`objecthandler_2.c`, `portModelTexPool`) share. `peaks --budget FILE DIR...` exits 1, naming the pool and level, when a pool, level and size of the logs is not in FILE (a listed pool and level at another size is named as such), when its peak is above half its size, or when the pool printed an exhaustion line in that level; a line ending ` withheld: REASON` accepts its pair past half by name and is printed as `withheld:`; otherwise it prints `OK: N pool and stage pairs within budget`. **Tests** (`test_lp64_play_peaks.py`, 15, in CI's tests step): the six of the brief, `by_stage_attributes_a_peak_to_the_level_before_it`, `budget_fails_a_pool_past_half`, `budget_fails_an_unlisted_pair`, `budget_fails_a_changed_size`, `budget_passes_at_exactly_half` and `by_stage_reads_run_subfolders`, and three more, `by_stage_gives_a_print_without_a_load_since_the_last_to_the_front_end`, `budget_accepts_a_withheld_pair_past_half_by_name` and `budget_fails_an_exhausted_pool`; before the code the nine failed (`unrecognized arguments: --by-stage`), after it the 15 pass. The game is unchanged by this commit.*

Commit "Report the peaks of the permanent bank, the model rooms and the synthesizer's parameters" (`port/include/port_lp64.h`, `port/src/port_lp64.c`, the new `port/src/port_lp64_synth.c`, `port/src/port_memp.c`, `src/game/gun.c`, `src/game/front.c`, `src/libultra/audio/synthesizer.c`, `src/libultra/audio/synthInternals.h`, `port/src/port_soak.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_peaks.c`, `scripts/port/test_audio_synth.c`, this note).* **Six more pools print a peak line** (Step 2), each at 64 bits only: `permanent bank` (`port_memp.c`, `notePeak`: the permanent bank's cursor after each block and resize, as the stage bank's, held the same way when a block took the rest); `gun room left hand`, `gun room trigger` and `gun room weapon` (`gun.c`, `used_to_load_1st_person_model_on_demand`: after the load into each of the three fixed model rooms, 0x133E0, 0x11DC0 and `D_80032464[hand]` bytes, the image the model loader committed, `get_pc_buffer_remaining_value`, which is its size rounded up to 16 and so fits the room exactly when the image does, every room being a multiple of 16); `wallet room` (`front.c`, `load_walletbond`: the same for `FRONT_WALLET_ROOM`); `synthesizer parameters` (the update records in use times `sizeof(ALParamRoom)` against the pool's, counted by `portLp64SynthParams`, `portLp64SynthParamTake` and `portLp64SynthParamGive` in the new `port_lp64_synth.c`, called from `alSynNew`, `__allocParam` and `__freeParam`). *LP64-006 task 11b, the converted display lists stop growing the high arena (2026-11-23). Commit "Reuse the converted display lists at 64 bits so the high arena stops growing" (the new `port/src/port_gdl_store.c` and `port/include/port_gdl_store.h`, `src/game/objecthandler_2.c`, `port/src/pcsched.c`, `port/src/port_soak.c`, `port/src/port_lp64.c` and `port/include/port_lp64.h` (the pool names), `CMakeLists.txt`, the new `scripts/port/test_gdl_store.c`, `scripts/port/test_buffers.sh`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_peaks.c`, `scripts/port/lp64_budgets.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, this note, the correction to the note above, and the plan's "Amendments during Task 11b").* Hosts: aarch64 native in Docker on the Apple Silicon Mac; x86_64 under Rosetta 2; i686 under qemu-i386; video through SDL offscreen with Mesa llvmpipe; nothing on real x86 hardware or a GPU. **The leak** (Task 11): `portConvertModelGdl` took a new `portAllocHigh` block of `(n * 4 + 96)` commands for every display list of every model load and nothing gave one back. **The fix, at 64 bits only:** `sub_GAME_7F0762E0` converts through `portModelGdlConvert`, and the store behind it (`port_gdl_store.c`) remembers for each block the address of the node record that points at it (`ModelNode.Data`, inside the model's file image). **The lifetime rule:** a block is given back only when a later model load writes its image over that record (`portModelGdlImageLoaded`, called with the image's start and the size `fileSetSize` just committed): the record that held the pointer is then another model's bytes. Nothing else gives a block back, not a stage change and not the bank's reset, which is the per-stage scoping that regressed for the texture pool. A list takes the smallest given-back block that holds its worst case, zeroed first as a new arena block is, and only once every frame handed to the renderer before the give-back is finished (`portGfxFramesSubmitted` and `portGfxFramesFinished`, `pcsched.c`; they differ only while the render thread holds a frame). Two models that are both loaded never share a block. **Who else holds a list's address:** a part node's instance copy (`model.c:6627`), which is of no use once its model's nodes are overwritten (guns are re-made every frame, `gunfire.c:1116`); a frame's display list, which the frame rule covers beside the game's own guards (the bank is reset only at `pendingGfx == 0`, `boss.c:611`; a gun room is reloaded after three hidden frames, `gun.c:968`); the part cache, whose key is the list's address and its vertex base and which never follows the address later: it is emptied at each stage load (`lv.c:984`), and a list that takes a block again in a caller's room (a gun room, the wallet room) makes it forget that list's vertex base (`portPartCacheVerticesFreed`); the light fixture table, which only compares a background hit with a model list's range (`lightfixture.c:600`); and the wallet's in-place edit (`front.c:2575`), applied after each conversion as before. **Kept as before:** the port's arm and grip sources (`port_arm_mesh.c:93`, `port_grip_mesh.c:40`) are loaded once into their own buffers, no model is loaded over them, and their blocks are never given back (nothing a lap); the cuff cache keyed by a list's address (`port_arm_mesh.c:379`) reads only those. A record that ends up under data that is not a model keeps its block until a model is loaded over it. **In a sanitizer build** a block is poisoned from its give-back until it is taken again (`port_poison.h`). **A 32-bit build keeps the leak**: `compare_win32.py commits 7a2a61c WORKTREE` prints `identical in loaded code and data; .buildid differs`, `port_gdl_store.c` is left out of 32-bit builds, and the store would not work there as it stands, since a suspend image (`port_state.c`) restores nodes that point at blocks the store may have handed on, and compiled-in models' nodes are never written over. **Before** (the build at 7a2a61c, `GE_SOAK=all:600:5`, headless): the arena's mapping grew 10,240 KB of resident memory in each of laps 2 to 5, to 63,488 KB, five 2 MB pages a lap, so `ge: smaps:` cannot show less than 2 MB. **After**, by the new line `ge: soak: lap=L high arena used=BYTES added=BYTES lists held=N spare=N bytes=BYTES` (a 64-bit harness build, each lap's end): headless the arena held 6,781,440 bytes after lap 1 (4,473,152 of them the model pool) and laps 2 to 5 added 91,904, 0, 43,904 and 0 bytes (6,917,248 at the end, 10.3 percent of the 64 MB; 628 blocks, 2,378,560 bytes of lists; no mapping's resident size grew in any lap); with video 6,797,696 after lap 1, then 76,672, 0, 0 and 0 (71,827 pictures; the arena's mapping is in no lap's list of grown mappings, `[heap]` moved between 226,624 and 234,068 KB). Over dam and facility alone a lap added 1,100,736 bytes before; a seeded eight-lap run now adds 97,472, 18,048 and then nothing. **What still grows, and why:** the use and the store's bytes rise by the same amount in every lap, so every added byte is a list that found no given-back block large enough. A block comes back only as later loads reach its record, so while a stage loads, the stage before still holds what has not been written over; and laps differ, since guards' heads and bodies are drawn at random (`initguards.c:73`). A traced scratch build (`build/lp64/play/t11b-trace-soak-full`, never committed) named the lists: 620 new blocks in lap 1, 7 in lap 2 (lists of `PmiltruckZ`, `Pchrmp5kZ`, `Pdest_seawolfZ`, `Pdest_exocetZ`, `Pdest_engineZ`, `PtigerZ` and `PshuttleZ`; 82,688 bytes; each larger than the largest block given back so far while 1 to 117 held blocks would have held it) and none in laps 3 to 5; its head models were loaded in some laps and not in others. The store is bounded by what one stage holds while the next loads over it. Giving back whatever lies above the bank's cursor when a model is loaded into it would bound it by one stage alone; it rests on the bank's lifetime and was not taken (a sanitizer build poisons the bank at its reset, `memp.c:304`, so the play sets would report a read that rule forbids, should the owner want it). **Smaller versions measured and dropped:** a block reused only for a list of exactly its size kept adding 20,736 and 26,368 bytes in laps 3 and 4 of a two-stage soak with 70 blocks spare, and a cap at twice the size added 33,216 in lap 5. **No other grower:** `stan.c`'s packed tiles keep one block and take another only for a larger stage; the port's images and the two sources are taken once. **The arena is a measured pool:** `ge: lp64: peak high arena USED of SIZE bytes` (`portAllocHigh` and each model load report it; a fourteenth name, `test_lp64_peaks.c`), and `lp64_budgets.txt` lists it for every stage at 6,917,248 bytes, its largest use in any run here (the end of the headless five-lap soak): `peaks --budget` over the final folders prints `OK: 318 pool and stage pairs within budget`. **Tests:** `scripts/port/test_gdl_store.c` (in `test_buffers.sh`, both widths, plain and sanitized): a second load of a model takes no arena bytes; a block given back is taken by another model's list; a model loaded elsewhere gives nothing back; a longer list takes a new block; a shorter list takes the smallest block that holds it; only records inside the image give back; a block waits for the frames built before; a room's list makes the part cache forget and a bank's does not; the counts; and, sanitized, the poison. RED against a store that behaves as the old converter (`s_ArenaUsed == usedAfterFirstLoad` failed), GREEN at 64 bits plain and sanitized on aarch64 and x86_64 and at 32 bits plain on x86_64; the sanitized 32-bit half does not start under Rosetta (a sanitized 32-bit `hello` hangs the same way) and is left to CI. **Pictures:** the 38 comparison cases with `--video --repeat 2` on `cmp-a64-video` and `cmp-x64-video`, 38 of 38 ran and agree with themselves under both profiles; `compare --streams sim,gfx,snd` against the i686 folders: default 192 identical and 8 as recorded, `--profile all` 190 and 10; x64 against a64 100 of 100 under each profile; the new a64 and x64 folders against Task 11's 100 of 100 each under each profile. `dam-twice` loads Dam, aborts and loads it again: its three streams match Task 11's, and its arena line reads 5,197,312 bytes after the first Dam and 5,353,536 at the end (133,504 for the menus' models, 22,720 for the second Dam). Bunker 1, Caverns, Bunker 1 in one process (`GE_SOAK=bunker1,caverns,bunker1:600:1` in lockstep on `cmp-a64-video`, run as a comparison case): the digest, the trace and the sound are identical to the same run of the build before the change, 2,231 frames, under both profiles and with `room_cache=2`; the second Bunker 1 took no arena bytes (5,518,784 before and after) and starts from the first visit's state (24 characters and 103 props with the same hashes at tick 1), but its frames cannot be compared with the first visit's in either build, because the random seed differs at its first tick. **Final runs** (every tree rebuilt after the last source edit, each paced run alone): `lp64_play.py run --set demos,stages,stops,menus,tours,attract,input` 146 of 146 on `build/lp64/boot` (944 s) and on `boot-san` (1,188 s, the poison live); the video mission smoke on `video-san` 20 of 20 (785 s); the soaks above (1,218 s and 1,370 s). **Per frame:** nothing; the store runs at model loads. **Late loads:** `late_load_audit.py --no-pack --video-driver offscreen` on all 26 stages with the build before the change and with this one, each alone (`build/lp64/late/t11b`): the 20 missions logged the same late events by kind and name (149 to 1,663 a stage); each of the six multiplayer arenas logged one fewer with this build, an 8x12 glyph upload at tick 6 of the legal screen (level 90), which prints the build's number, commit and time (`port_startup.c`): the two executables' differ (605, 3ae837e35 and 12:42 against 606, 7a2a61c7d and 04:24). No stage gained a late load, and no conversion moved: `portModelGdlConvert` runs where `portConvertModelGdl` did. **Checks:** `lp64_casts.py check`, `lp64_overlays.py check --no-defects`, `lp64_diagnostics.py gate`, `narrowing --check`, `unprototyped --check` and `lp64_pointer_types.py check` pass in the x86_64 container, with every other line of the CI tests step there: 84 lines, 0 failed (475 s, on the final tree), `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1 bash scripts/port/test_buffers.sh` run as its two halves (64-bit sanitized, 32-bit plain; the combined line was not run locally, its sanitized 32-bit half hangs under emulation). **Not covered:** no harness run has a frame in flight (the render thread is off at 60 retraces a second and in lockstep) or a part cached under a gun room's list, so the frame rule and the forget are checked by the unit test alone; `room_cache=2` was run for the three-stage comparison only.*

*LP64-006 task 14, the Arm check (2026-11-23). Commit "Compare the aarch64 build with x86_64 stream by stream" (`include/PR/gu.h`, `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` and the new `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe_conversions.h`, `scripts/port/lp64_diagnostics.py`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_diagnostics.py`, a comment in `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_expected.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/port/native_64bit_plan.md`'s LP64-006 row, this note and the plan's "Amendments during Task 14").* Hosts: aarch64 native in Docker on the Apple Silicon Mac; x86_64 under Rosetta 2, so every "x86" result here is Rosetta's emulation of x86, not real x86 hardware; the 32-bit references ran in the i686 containers under emulation; video is SDL's offscreen driver with Mesa llvmpipe, no GPU. **The probe before the fix:** `FTOFIX32(40000.0f)` and `FTOFIX32(-40000.0f)`, read through a `volatile float`, must both be `INT_MIN`. aarch64 failed (`2147483647` and `-2147483648`: `fcvtzs` saturates); the x86_64 container passed at both widths (`cvttss2si` gives `INT_MIN`) (`build/lp64/equiv/t14/red-probe-*.out`). In `guMtxF2L` x86-64 converts with `cvttss2si` and aarch64 with `fcvtzs w, s, #16` (`build/lp64/equiv/t14/conversion-instructions.txt`). **The fix:** on an aarch64 64-bit build `FTOFIX32` gives `INT_MIN` for a product outside [-2^31, 2^31) and for NaN, as x86 does, and stays a constant expression for `gbi.h` (a `_Static_assert` in the probe checks it); it reads its argument three times. x86-64 and 32-bit builds keep their definition: `mtxutil.c` preprocessed with the x86_64 gate tree's command is identical before and after, and differs only in its two `FTOFIX32` lines with the aarch64 tree's (`build/lp64/equiv/t14/preprocess-diff.txt`); `compare_win32.py commits c972f8f WORKTREE`: identical in loaded code and data. Measured instead, natively on Apple Silicon in the aarch64 container: a scratch program (`build/lp64/equiv/t14/bench/`, not committed) links the repository's `mtxutil.c`, preprocessed with c972f8f's `gu.h` and with this one and compiled with the aarch64 video tree's C flags (`-O2 -ffp-contract=off ...`), and times 4,000,000 calls on 4,096 varied in-range matrices, 11 repeats, three interleaved rounds (both give one checksum). `guMtxF2L` takes 4.29 to 4.36 ns a call before (round medians; every repeat 4.21 to 4.67) and 11.56 to 14.50 ns after (every repeat 10.76 to 16.34): about 8 ns more a call, as x86's result costs Arm the fused `fcvtzs w, s, #16` and adds two compares and branches. The machine was not quiet (load average about 9 from other work), which the wider after range shows. A one-compare form (`fabsf(v) < 2^31`, giving the same results, -2^31 included) measured 9.09 to 9.85 ns; it was not taken, since it saves about 3 ns of the 8 and would have needed every run again. Calls a frame were not counted (no counter exists and no game code was added for one); the direct callers are the projection (`src/fr.c`), two in `src/game/bondview2.c`, one a weapon's projection in `src/game/gunfire.c`, and libultra's `gu` builders (`guPerspective`, `guLookAt`, `guRotate`, ...), so at a few hundred calls a frame the price would be a few microseconds of a 16.7 ms frame. `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.c` now requires `INT_MIN` for `FTOFIX32` past range (it accepted `INT_MIN` or `INT_MAX`); with c972f8f's `gu.h` it fails on aarch64 (`build/lp64/equiv/t14/red-address-aarch64-oldgu.out`), and it passes at both widths in the x86_64 container and at 64 bits on aarch64. **The gate:** `lp64_diagnostics.py gate` refuses an entry whose compiler names an aarch64 machine (`-dumpmachine`, asked of the words before the command's first option, with any `--target`; an aarch64 tree's `compile_commands.json` holds the same `/usr/bin/cc` command as an x86_64 one) unless its last `-ffp-contract=` is `off`, and refuses a compiler that names no machine. Unit tests: the refusal, a later `-ffp-contract=fast`, acceptance with the flag, an x86_64 command without it still accepted (as before), and the mute compiler (three failed before the change, `build/lp64/equiv/t14/red-gate.out`; all 44 tests of the file pass after). On real trees: a copy of one `gate-a64` entry without the flag is refused, the same of `gate` is accepted, and the full gate passes on `gate-a64` and `gate-video-a64` (357 and 388 files, `build/lp64/equiv/t14/gate-*.out`). **Out-of-range float conversions:** a scratch aarch64 headless tree with `-fsanitize=float-cast-overflow`, built with c972f8f's `gu.h` so an out-of-range `FTOFIX32` would report as well, ran the play sets (`build/lp64/play/t14-fco`, reports in `t14-fco.reports`; the tree was removed afterwards). No overlay verdict and no record layout changed (the three OP17 lines of `lp64_overlays_reviewed.txt` are reads through the record's own type), so neither the reviewed list nor the probe changed. *For the owner:* `scripts/port/lp64_patches/t16-op17-32bit.patch` (written, not applied) gives OP17 its own map at both widths in `romfile_model.c` and the converter and drops the tests' 32-bit branches; in a scratch tree it passed `test_romconv.sh` at 32 and 64 bits (x86_64 container). **The three reads (Step 3).** `chrGetEquippedWeaponProp(...)->chr` in `chrlvInitActAttack`, `chrlvInitActAttackWalk` and `chrlvInitActAttackRoll`. `test_lp64_typed_chraction.c` calls each with an unarmed guard (the right hand flagged for the first; the other two flag a hand themselves when neither holds a prop), each in a child process so that a fault is a result: at 64 bits the child must return, at 32 bits it must end by SIGSEGV, the inherited read through NULL, so the 32-bit half passes without the guard. Guard: inside `#if IS_64_BIT` each loop's condition also requires the hand's prop, so an empty flagged hand is skipped (not automatic, not a launcher); `chraction.c` now includes `platform_info.h` itself so the guard cannot be silently false. GREEN: `PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` in both containers; under qemu the 32-bit half's three expected faults print `qemu: uncaught target signal 11`. *For the owner:* `scripts/port/lp64_patches/t16-chraction-32bit.patch` (written, not applied) guards at both widths and expects no fault at both; in a scratch tree the test passed at 32 and 64 bits. **The index-0 load (Step 3).** The `stops` set on `build/lp64/boot-san` rebuilt from BASE: `OK: 12 of 12 cases`, no sanitizer report (`build/lp64/play/t16-stops-before`), though each setup stop logs `fileIndexLoadToBank: NO LINKED DATA for file index 0 (bank 4)`. Why, measured with a scratch sanitizer build printing the addresses (`build/lp64/t16-scratch/idx0-src`, never committed; `build/lp64/play/t16-idx0-measure`, the three setup stops): the load allocates the rest of the stage bank (63,662,056 to 64,080,736 bytes), the host check leaves `pc_size` 0, so `resource_load_from_indy` reads `pPayload[0]` and `[1]` at the allocation's end, which is the stage bank's end and the permanent bank's start; the gap is dropped at a bank's end (`port_memp.c`, `gapAfter`), and those two bytes are the first of the permanent bank's live first block (cursor 0x1BEA0 in), `__asan_address_is_poisoned` 0 for both. So no poisoned gap covers the read: it stays inside the pool area and reads two live bytes of the next bank, which no sanitizer can report. The brief bounded the read only when it was reported; the controller then ruled it bounded under decision 10 (ruling 14), in commit "Bound the index-0 load's payload read at 64 bits" (`src/game/ob.c`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_typed_ob.c`, `scripts/port/test_lp64_typed_reads.sh`). `test_lp64_typed_ob.c` (run by `test_lp64_typed_reads.sh`, stubs for the host check, the host load and `decompressdata` only) calls `resource_load_from_indy` with no host file: once with the allocation ending at a page no access may touch, in a child process, and once with 0x11 0x72 just past the allocation. RED at 64 bits (aarch64 and x86_64): `reads nothing past its allocation (ended by 11 ...)`, `does not enter the decompressor` and `loads 0 bytes` failed (`build/lp64/equiv/t16/index0-red-*.out`); at 32 bits it asserts the inherited behaviour, the fault and the decompressor entered with its size, and passed. The fix: after the host check, inside `#if IS_64_BIT`, a `pc_size` of 0 sets the result to 0 and returns before the payload pointer is formed, the size the inherited code gives for a payload without the header; `ob.c` includes `platform_info.h` itself. To keep `ob.c` at the 628-line limit (it was exactly 628, and it has no length exception) the guard is three lines and four of the five blank lines after the function were removed, no other line changing. GREEN: `test_lp64_typed_ob: PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)`, and `test_lp64_typed_reads: PASS`, in both containers. Reach, from the code: `resource_load_from_indy` runs only for a file whose `hw_address` is NULL; at 64 bits `romdataRequireServed` stops a classified file the ROM does not serve, and the table's only unclassified loadable entry is index 0, so the index-0 load is the only caller that reaches the changed lines. Its bank load logs `NO LINKED DATA`; over every t16 play, video and comparison folder that line names index 0 only, in the three setup stops (`stop-citadel`, `stop-complex`, `stop-temple`); an index-0 load through `fileIndexLoadToAddr` logs no such line, but a load by name reaches index 0 only through `fileGetIndex`'s miss, which logs `ge: fileGetIndex MISS` first (`ob.c:556`), and over the same folders those lines name only the three stops' setups (`UsetupcatZ`, `UsetupdishZ`, `UsetuprefZ`, in the 18 logs of `stop-citadel`, `stop-complex` and `stop-temple` and nowhere else; counted at the final review), so the logs too show no other index-0 load by name. Reruns on `boot`, `boot-san`, `boot-x64` and `video` rebuilt from the fix, one at a time: the `stops` set `OK: 12 of 12 cases` on each (`build/lp64/play/t16b-stops-{plain,san,x64,video}`, the last with `--video`), each setup stop still logging `NO LINKED DATA for file index 0 (bank 4)`, no sanitizer report; casts (`24 truncating casts ... all allowed`), overlays (`1620 sites, all reviewed`, `0 defect lines`), gate, `0 narrowings`, `4 unprototyped calls`, `121 pointer-only types`; CI's tests-step lines in the x86_64 container `DONE 97 lines, 0 failed` (`build/lp64/equiv/t16b-ci/`, with fresh LTO logs: `OK: 15 mismatches, all allowed`). By the ruling no other set or comparison was rerun. *For the owner:* `scripts/port/lp64_patches/t16-index0-32bit.patch` (written, not applied) guards at both widths and expects the bounded read at both; in a scratch tree `test_lp64_typed_reads.sh` passed at 32 and 64 bits (x86_64 container). `compare_win32.py commits f60ed4f WORKTREE`: identical in loaded code and data. **The render thread's exit (Step 4).** Where `PORT_PLAY_HARNESS` is 1 (every headless build, every 64-bit video build, comparison builds), `portRenderThreadStop` prints `ge: video: render thread stop: waiting (state pending=P executing=E completed=C)` under its lock after the quit signal and `ge: video: render thread stop: joined` after `SDL_WaitThread`, each flushed on standard output; nothing else in the function changed, and a 32-bit video build compiles neither line. Both also print when a live tick change restarts the thread (`portRenderThreadFollowTick`). `lp64_play.py run --video --env GE_RENDERTHREAD=1` runs a case with the thread on as it stands (the variable is not refused, and mode 1 turns the thread on at tickhz 60; a probe of `menu-files` logged `render thread ON (GE_RENDERTHREAD; tickhz=60)`, both lines and `PASS (750 pictures)`), but it writes a log after the run, so the wait between the lines was measured by a scratch runner that imports the tool's cases, environment, folder set-up, shared executable and judge and stamps each line as it arrives (`build/lp64/t16-scratch/rt_exits.py`). **301 exits** (the `menus` set's 7 cases 43 times, `--jobs 4`, `--timeout-scale 4`, on `build/lp64/video` rebuilt at 11:26 from this code, before only the explicit `platform_info.h` include of `chraction.c`, which changes no 64-bit object since `IS_64_BIT` already reached it (the guard's test passed before the include), 11:28 to 11:49): `counted 301 of 301 runs`, each passing the tool's judge with the thread on, the waiting line and the joined line its last. *LP64-006 task 17 step 3, a pin per kind of run (2026-11-24), on the Mac.* Commit "Pin a headless run's stream apart from a video run's" (`scripts/port/lp64_equiv_compare.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv.py`'s help, `scripts/port/test_lp64_equiv_expect.py`, `scripts/port/lp64_equiv_expected.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, the plan's "Amendments after the final review" item 6, this note). Step 2's finding, that a headless `sim` comparison fails the two Jungle `default` `sim` lines (`i686:x64 jungle default sim` and `i686:a64 jungle default sim`) because their pins hash a video run's stream, is settled by the controller's ruling: a pin is per kind of run. `sha256=HEX` stays the pin of a run made with `--video`; an optional `headless-sha256=HEX`, after it in that fixed order, pins a run made without. `compare --expect` checks the pin of the newer folder's kind (its `equiv.json`'s `video`); a line pinned only for the other kind is judged by its first index, as an unpinned line is, and `compare` prints `note: line N has no pin for a headless run; judged by its first index alone` (or `a video run`); a line with neither pin is judged so without a note, as before. `pins` prints a fresh pin of the folders' kind and keeps the other kind's pin on the line; it still writes nothing. A pin on a line that is not `explained:` is refused (`only an explained line carries a pin`), and so are the two pins in the other order. *Tests first:* `test_lp64_equiv_expect.py` gained a class of ten tests and its five video-pin tests now make their folders with `video: true`; before the code `python3 -m unittest test_lp64_equiv_expect` printed `FAILED (failures=10, errors=1)` (19 tests), after it `OK`, and with `test_lp64_equiv_compare`, `test_lp64_equiv`, `test_lp64_equiv_video`, `test_lp64_equiv_streams` and `test_lp64_equiv_cases` `Ran 101 tests ... **LP64-007 planned and accepted (2026-11-24, nothing built).** The owner accepted all thirteen recommendations of the plan that day; `native_64bit_plan.md`'s "Decisions" lists them. [The plan](scripts/port/native_64bit_lp64_007.md) has thirteen tasks and thirteen decisions for the owner, and is not accepted yet. It was written from six look-ups made on `main` at f04e0a7, in the Mac's containers with x86_64 translated by Rosetta 2 and video drawn by Mesa's llvmpipe through SDL's offscreen driver; no GPU and no real x86 hardware. *How packages are made today:* every push to `main` publishes a release; the `linux` job builds the i686 tarball, AppImage and Steam Deck ZIP in `linux-release.Dockerfile` (Ubuntu 22.04, GCC 11.4, glibc 2.35) with `linux_build.py` and `package_linux.py`, both i686-only (`-m32`, `lib/i386-linux-gnu`, `SENTRY_BUILD_FORCE32`, the `runtime-i686` pin, an ELF32 check, the names); the shipped build type is `Debug`, which `CMakeLists.txt` compiles at `-O2 -g`, as every 64-bit tree so far was. *A 64-bit video tree configured as the shipped build is* (`-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DGE_POINTER_BITS=64 -DGE_VIDEO=ON -DGE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK=OFF`, GCC 13.3, the x86_64 development container): built in 32 s with the usual eleven optionless C++ warnings; a 28.3 MB PIE needing GLIBC_2.38 and GLIBCXX_3.4.32 and, through the container's SDL 2.30.0, 49 libraries; `lp64_boot.py --expect-run --frames 600` printed `OK: ran 600 frames`; `lp64_play.py run --video --set demos` printed `OK: 14 of 14 cases` in 225 s; `package_linux.py` on it stopped at `FileNotFoundError: .../sentry-crash`, and Sentry was off (`ge: crash reporting preference=ON active=0`). *The packages' compiler:* in the unmodified `midas-linux-release` image (GCC 11.4.0, CMake 3.22.1), a 64-bit headless tree built all 360 C objects with 0 errors and 0 warnings, needs GLIBC_2.34 at most, ran 600 frames and replayed 14 of 14 demos in 101 s; the video sources, C++ renderer included, were not compiled there, since that image has only i386 `-dev` libraries. *What a 64-bit build does differently for a player:* the Suspend Points row, its four bind rows and keys say nothing until used; its stops (statuses 4, 5, 6 and `sysFatalError`'s 64-bit messages) only log; `port/crash/reporting_linux.c:163` tags every report `i686`; `PORT_PLAY_HARNESS` is 1 with no CMake switch; the icon cache file is named by the ROM's fingerprint alone, so an i686 and an x86_64 install share it. The Linux signal handler (`port/src/main.c`, glibc `backtrace`) is the same at both widths, so the design's "portable replacement" of the x86 frame walks has nothing to replace outside Windows-only code. The two scratch trees (`build/lp64/ship-probe/`) were deleted after planning. *Not run:* anything on a GPU, a Steam Deck or real x86 hardware; an x86_64 Sentry runtime (none exists yet); the i686 packaging on the Mac (`ldd` on 32-bit files cannot run under Rosetta 2).

Local commit on `main`, not pushed.* Commit "Refuse six kinds of damaged file in the 64-bit converters, and test fix wave C's two paths" (`port/src/romconv_anim.c`, `romconv_seq.c`, `romconv_setup_records.c`, `romconv_font.c`, `romconv_bank_records.c`, `romconv_model_walk.c`, `port/src/animdata.c`, `src/game/initanitable.c`, the three `port/include/port_romconv*.h` headers and `romconv_setup_walk.h`; the fixtures under `scripts/port/test_romconv*`, new `scripts/port/test_romconv_ai_size.c` and `scripts/port/test_romdata_damaged.c`, `scripts/port/test_romconv.sh`; this note; the plan's Task 7 boxes and status row). **The six reads, each bounded in the 64-bit converter only; every bound refuses the file through `portConvRefuse`, so the game stops by name (or, for a text bank, zeroes it) as before:**
1. *An animation's stream length and entries offset* (`portAnimHeadersConvert`, `port/src/romconv_anim.c:130` and `:138`). The converter now also takes the entries image's size (`portAnimStagedEntriesSize()`, `animdata.c`, `ANIM_ENTRIES_SEG_SIZE`; `initanitable.c` passes it to the converter and to its oracle, a mechanical change inside the existing `#if IS_64_BIT` and `GE_LP64_ORACLE` blocks) and refuses a header whose root-motion stream (`stream_offset` plus `frames * unk0c` bits) passes the staged image, or whose frames (`entries_offset` plus `frames` times its frame bytes) pass the entries image. The stock ROM's largest entries end is 0x169EBE of 0x169EC0.
2. *A sequence's address and lengths* (`port/src/romconv_seq.c`; fixed at the Task 7 review). Three bounds:
   - `seqFileHoldsEntries` refuses a count below `NUM_MUSIC_TRACKS` (63, `src/music.h:13`). `portSeqTableLoad` (`port/src/audio_stubs.c`) sizes the table by the file's count, and `musicInit`'s loop (`src/music.c:872`) reads entries 0 to 62 whatever the count, so a shorter table would be read past its end. A count above 63 is safe and merely ignored: those entries are converted and rebased (`musicSeqFileNew`) but never read, because the play functions index the table by the game's track numbers, which are below 63.
   - `seqSequencesInFile` refuses a sequence whose `offset + len` passes the file. The sum is computed in 64 bits, so an offset with bit 31 set no longer wraps.
   - `seqSequencesInFile` also refuses a sequence whose `len`, rounded up to 16, is more than `seqCopyEnd(uncompressed_len)`: the uncompressed length made even in a u16 as `musicInit` does, rounded up to 16, plus 64. `musicTrack1Play` and its two twins (`src/music.c`, around 1005) copy the compressed bytes so that they end at that point from the track buffer's start, so a longer copy would start before the buffer, whichever player plays it. The stock ROM's smallest margin is 112 bytes.
   - What the converter cannot bound is whether the inflated sequence fits its track buffer. `decompressdata` (`src/game/decompress.c:32`) takes no output size and writes as many bytes as the stream holds, so `uncompressed_len` only places the compressed copy. The buffers are `music.c`'s private `TRACK_1_DATA_SEQ_SIZE_BYTES` (6,344), `TRACK_2_...` (2,000) and `TRACK_3_...` (4,000), defined at `src/music.c:154-156`; `musicInit` allocates them at 861-867, tracks 2 and 3 in one 6,000-byte block. Which buffer a sequence reaches is decided at play time by the game, through the track number the stage passes to `musicTrack1Play`, `musicTrack2Play` or `musicTrack3Play` (`src/game/mp_music.c`, `musicGetXTrackForStage`, `musicGetBgTrackForStage`). The stock ROM's largest copy end, 6,176 bytes, fits track 1's buffer; 47 sequences pass track 2's size and 18 pass track 3's, so no single limit holds for a sequence. A check against the largest buffer would need `music.c`'s private constant and would still pass a sequence too long for the player that plays it. This stays in shared code, for upstream.
3. *The end of an AI list* (`aiListEnd`, `port/src/romconv_setup_records.c:78`): the list is walked command by command with chrai.c's `chraiitemsize` (line 91), as the interpreter steps, instead of scanning for an `AI_EndList` byte; an `AI_EndList` byte that is another command's argument no longer ends it, and `AI_PRINT`'s NUL-terminated string is sized there so its scan stays inside the unowned run. The refusal now says "whose AI_EndList command is not before".
4. *A glyph's extent* (`fontGlyphInFile`, `port/src/romconv_font.c:56`, refusal at `:65`): a glyph whose `height` rows of `width` rounded up to 8 bytes pass the file is refused; both are read unsigned, so a negative one is refused. Stock: gothic ends at 0x24A8 of 0x24B0, zurich at 0x3538 of 0x3540.
5. *A wave of an unknown type* (`bankMeasureWave`, `port/src/romconv_bank_records.c:79`, refusal at `:102`): every type's `base + len` is held to the wave table, not only ADPCM and raw 16-bit.
6. *A `G_TEXRECT` tail in a model list* (`texRectTailFollows`, `port/src/romconv_model_walk.c:138`, called at `:185` for 0xE4 and 0xE5): a texture rectangle must be followed, inside the list, by `G_RDPHALF_2` (0xB3) and `G_RDPHALF_CONT` (0xB2), the words `gbi.h` writes and `gfx_pc.cpp` consumes whatever they hold.
**Left in shared code, for upstream** (both widths read them; this task does not edit them): `src/game/model.c`'s `loadAnimationFrame` reads its frame in 16-byte rounded blocks, 8 bytes past the stock entries segment for the last animation, and trusts the descriptor's indices and bit offsets past its stride; `src/music.c` copies a sequence with `ALIGN16(len)` (9 bytes past the file for the stock sequence 62, inside the ROM image), and inflates a sequence into the track buffer of the player that plays it with no output size (item 2 says why the converter cannot bound that; its count and copy start are now bounded there). **Fix wave C's two paths, held by fixtures** (`scripts/port/test_romdata_damaged.c`, 64-bit only, under the sanitizers; it includes `romdata.c` to reach its statics and stubs what it calls): a 0x100-byte ROM serving only the images bank makes `portRomdataSegsApply` stop with "The ROM segment sfxctl is missing; a 64-bit build has no compiled-in copy to read"; a text bank that arrives still 1172-compressed is zeroed by `romdataTextPreprocess`, every byte, with its log line. A copy of each file with the fix undone fails its fixture. **Fixtures and their failure.** One a read (`test_romconv_anim.c`, `_seq.c`, `_setup_checks.c`, `_font_checks.c`, `_bank_checks.c`, `_model_checks.c`), each with an accepted neighbour at the bound; `test_romconv_ai_size.c` stands in for `chraiitemsize` in the setup tests. Before the bounds every new refusal test failed at both widths in the x86_64 container, as a failed assertion: the converters copy without over-reading, so no sanitizer report fired; the setup cases were also failed against a copy with only the walk undone. After: `test_romconv: PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` on x86_64 and `PASS (64-bit)` on aarch64. **Stock ROM untouched.** Oracle (i686, qemu, 3 min 38 s): animation tables 3633, text banks 255, audio banks 42, music sequences 21, textures 2521, fonts 63, models 512, backgrounds 45, collision tiles 47, setup files 54 files, 0 differ each. Mission smoke at 64 bits (aarch64, `--fixed-tick --frames 1800`): plain 20 of 20 (2 min 31 s), sanitizer 20 of 20 (2 min 55 s), no `cannot convert` line and no sanitizer report. `lp64_census.py compare` of the oracle's mission logs and the plain smoke: 20 of 20 missions load the same at both widths. `compare_win32.py commits 9b53983 WORKTREE`: identical in loaded code and data (`.buildid` differs). **Checks.** Every line of CI's tests step in the x86_64 container, 103 passed and none failed (the sanitized `test_buffers.sh` line as its two halves, the 32-bit one without the sanitizer; `hand_gallery.py verify` not run, by the task's rule), among them `lp64_overlays.py check --no-defects`, `lp64_casts.py check`, the diagnostics gate, `narrowing --check`, `unprototyped --check`, `lp64_pointer_types.py check` and `lp64_lto.py check`. Plain aarch64 play sets (`demos,stages,stops,menus,tours,attract,input` on `build/lp64/boot`): `OK: 146 of 146 cases` (17 min). Package check: P1 and P2 exit 0, P2 printing the three package paths; P4 printed `OK: ran 600 frames` and passed 20 of 20 missions (11 min). P3 was not run on the Mac. CI will judge it on real x86_64 once this commit is pushed. The bank refusal was reshaped into one early return (same bound, same two messages) after the aarch64 boot trees were built: the fixtures were rerun on it at both widths in the x86_64 container and at 64 bits in aarch64, and the packaged x86_64 build of P1 holds it; the oracle, smoke and play runs above used the trees built just before. No per-frame work or load changed, so no benchmark or late-load audit applies. **Review fix (2026-11-25, commit "Refuse a sequence bank shorter than the game reads, and a copy that starts before its track buffer").** It adds the count bound and the copy-start bound of item 2, which it rewrites. Their fixtures are in `test_romconv_seq.c`, rebuilt on a 63-entry bank: 62 entries are refused and 63 are accepted; a compressed copy of 81 bytes against 15 uncompressed is refused and one of 80 accepted; and an uncompressed length of 0xFFFF, which the game rounds to 0, is refused. It also adds an accepted-at-the-bound fixture for the animation stream (28 frames of 18 bits from 0xC1, ending at the 0x100-byte image's end). Before the bounds, the three new refusal tests failed at 32 and 64 bits; after, `test_romconv: PASS (32-bit)` and `PASS (64-bit)` (x86_64) and `PASS (64-bit)` (aarch64). Checks on the final code:

  1. *Jungle's special-portal walk.* The 32-bit program walks Jungle's 59 portals as ordinary ones (link order; Task 6). Fix at 32 bits: `portal-end-32bit.patch`. Its price at 64 bits in late loads: the laptop's real-x86 comparison counted 456 room loads at 32 bits against 1,324 at 64 bits over the same 44 rooms (Task 17 Step 2); on the Mac, one Jungle `late_load_audit.py --no-pack --video-driver offscreen --keep` of the native aarch64 video build reported `1324 / 42.9` (room loads / ms, 43 of 44 rooms toured before the mission ended, 1,663 late events), the costliest room load 0.78 ms in its kept `late.txt`; none is among the 25 costliest late events, which are all texture uploads (13.5 to 20.5 ms) (Task 17 Step 3). *Open*: unanswered.
  2. *`image.c`'s scratch buffer.* The 32-bit program packs an odd-width 4-bit texture's last pixel with stack leftovers; the 64-bit one zeroes them (Task 8, cause A). Fix at 32 bits: `t8-zero-stack-buffers.patch`. *Applied* (LP64-007 Task 12, by hand as `#ifndef TARGET_N64`).
  3. *The display-list leak at 32 bits.* A 32-bit build still takes a new high-arena block for every list of every load (Task 11b). No patch: the store does not work at 32 bits as it stands, because 32-bit suspend images and compiled-in models hold list addresses the store would give back. *Open*: no for now (2026-11-24).
  4. *Save-record padding at 32 bits.* The 32-bit program stores whatever memory holds in a folder record's two padding bytes, which the checksum covers; the 64-bit one stores zeros (Task 13). Fix at 32 bits: `save-padding-32bit.patch`. *Applied* (LP64-007 Task 12).
  5. *The envelope's `ratel` conversion on Arm.* A positive overflow would part aarch64 from x86 (none was seen; Task 14). Fix, aarch64 only, never compiled: `t14-env-ratel.patch`. *Open*: no for now (2026-11-24).

That census was taken before the strict batch landed; LP64-006 reruns it on the landed code.

Largest shares at the close, over the plain headless and plain video folders: room memory 68.2 percent (`tour-aztec`), texture pool 53.1 (`soak`, video), music heap 44.0, graphics buffer 40.4, vertex pool 21.5, room memory's largest request 17.6, stage bank 9.5 (`mp-statue-4p`); the figures are in the close note above. Their lengths follow wall time (Task 10), so a length comparison with the 32-bit build waits for LP64-006's capture that does not depend on it.

No GPU, no real x86 hardware. Every judged video pass except the render-thread ones ran with the render thread off (`GE_TICKHZ=60`); a shipped video build runs it by default.
- *The render thread's exit stall.* `watch-inventory` with `GE_RENDERTHREAD=1` stalled once during exit in the fix wave (after the pool-peak lines, before standard output was flushed; `portRenderThreadStop`'s join in `port/src/video.c` is the likely place), killed at 1,080 s and not reproduced in three reruns at the case's frames and one at eight times its frames then; at the close it did not recur in 243 render-thread runs (108 and 27 plain, 79 and 29 sanitizer), `watch-inventory` among them three times, so it was not investigated further; no debugger is in the images and none was installed. Its cause is open.
- *`weapons-dam` varies from run to run* (found at the close): on the plain aarch64 headless executable it failed once of four runs (no shot logged with the dual Spectre, the 29th change, before the 30th), passed in three reruns and on the other executables; its shot counts before that change were 116 to 121 across those runs, so the game's state there depends on the run, as the case's docstring says of its totals. Measured in the close's fix round on the same executable: 10 of 10 runs alone and 11 of 12 under a load of six, so with the full pass and its three reruns 24 of 26 runs passed in all; the one new failure was the same window (change 29 at tick 4578, no shot while the trigger was held from 4620, the M16 at 4698 where passing runs change at 4728). The game's clock follows retraces while the route counts pad reads, so 8 to 12 of 5,100 retraces passed without a game frame and Bond first drew at tick 1158 to 1161; neither figure singles out the failing run. Why the dual Spectre fired nothing there is not found (infinite ammo rules out an empty gun); the first step is logging player 0's gun state at each change and held trigger. A fix to the case or the game reruns the input set on the plain and sanitizer aarch64 and plain x86_64 headless executables and with video. A judge that needs every weapon to fire is exposed to it. The owner accepted this miss against decision 6 on 2026-11-20, so finding its cause is LP64-006's first item, not a condition of LP64-005's close. *Corrected while planning LP64-006 (2026-11-21):* the i686 build misses the case too (2 of 6 runs under load), a later aarch64 failure was at change 13, and changes 29 and 30 are a pair of Golden Guns and the silver PP7 by `src/bondconstants.h`, not the dual Spectre and the M16; the plan's Task 1 starts from that.
